proofs.title: The paged catalog's live links: every bound (group . number) entry is live with its true neighbour and every live number is bound, through commit, withdrawal, redecision and clear; a live number's neighbour read is the table probe
proofs.statement: books/catalog-live-links.lisp + books/catalog-paged.lisp; the subject is the paged catalog's withdrawal and commit executables (fn-cat$p-withdraw-w, fn-cat$p-commit-w), the attached executables of the generic exports fn-cat-withdraw / fn-cat-commit (books/catalog-paged-attach.lisp) called by the served write path (books/owner-batch.lisp, books/index-backing-served-producer-carry.lisp). fn-cpl-okp (every bound key is a live number and its value its NEXT/PREV live neighbour) is kept by the commit's link plan (KEYSTONE fn-cpl-okp-of-commit), the withdrawal's unlink (KEYSTONE fn-cpl-okp-of-withdraw; the r < len c hypothesis proved redundant: fn-cpl-okp-of-withdraw-any-r) and a redecision (fn-cpl-okp-of-redecide). fn-cpl-coverp (every live number is bound) is kept by the same writes (fn-cpl-coverp-of-commit, -of-withdraw, -of-redecide, -of-no-rows). fn-cat$pcorr carries both for both tables; under it the liveness probe IS liveness (KEYSTONE fn-cat$p-livep-is-live: (group . number) bound in NEXT iff live) and a live number's neighbour read is its entry -- bound, a natural, its true neighbour (KEYSTONES fn-cat$p-next-is-probe, fn-cat$p-prev-is-probe); the paged executables have no row scan: the withdrawal's only row reads are its three withdrawal columns and its numbers column (fn-cat$p-withdrawn-of, fn-cat$p-numbers-of; the remainder in the pool is never decoded), every liveness and neighbour question a table probe. Measured (hbox REPL, 10k rows of 2 groups, guards on, loop averages): 2,798 B consed per withdrawal (was 15,031: one full row decode); commit 28,635 B (was 27,127: the numbers walked as a second tree) and +157 B/row retained (the numbers' program). Scope: the logical tables (alists) the stobj's hash tables model; the cost claims are measurements, not theorems. Open: fn-cat-rowsp in fn-cpl-okp-of-withdraw (no counterexample known, weakening not proved). Teeth: tests/acl2/catalog-live-links-tests.lisp (commit-generated tables, positive + okp-removal + natp-r removal + coverage witnesses), tests/acl2/catalog-paged-tests.lisp (probe positive on an executable-built state; Codex r30 F1 corrupted-state: tables erased, the scans answer).

proofs.title: The paged catalog's withdrawals-by-version reader answers the old foundation's ascending list for every withdrawal order: a per-version binary trie whose in-order walk allocates only the answer
proofs.statement: books/catalog-wbv-trie.lisp + books/catalog-paged.lisp; the subject is fn-cpt-list (exec fn-cpt-walk), the executable of fn-cat$p-withdrawn-at, attached to the generic export fn-cat-withdrawn-at (books/catalog-paged-attach.lisp) read by books/served-catalog-view.lisp fn-scv-withdrawn-numbers; its writer fn-cpt-add is called by fn-cat$p-withdraw-w and fn-cat$p-commit-w (the exports fn-cat-withdraw / fn-cat-commit on the served write path). A version's withdrawn rows are a binary trie over row numbers, most significant bit first, leaves counting multiplicity; the writer copies one root-to-leaf path (O(log N) conses, plus one a level of growth), the reader walks high subtree first onto an accumulator (allocation = the answer, recursion depth = the trie depth). KEYSTONE fn-cpt-list-of-add: for a natural s, the trie's ascending list after the add is fn-cpt-insert s of the list before (= fn-cat-insert-asc, fn-cpt-insert-is-insert-asc), so the view's table is the old foundation's exactly (fn-cp-view-of-wbv-push); no distinctness invariant is needed (multiset leaves). Measured (hbox REPL, 10k rows, 9,998 withdrawals at one version, guards on, loop averages of 100 reads): 161,186 B/read for ascending, descending AND scrambled arrival (was 161,186 / 1,029 / 6,084,346 with the sort-on-read reader); withdrawal 15,031-15,058 B (was 14,817: one ~15 KB row decode plus the path); retained 10,006 conses for 9,998 members at depth 14. Scope: the logical tables; costs are measurements, not theorems. Teeth: tests/acl2/catalog-paged-tests.lisp (writer-built buckets in the three orders read through fn-cat$p-withdrawn-at and equal to fn-cat$a-withdrawn-at, the keystone's antecedent and conclusion on the bucket before/after the last withdrawal, natp removal, a labelled walk-order MUTATION).
proofs.progress_note: Lanes paged-catalog-6..8 (8: the trie replaced the sort-on-read reader); hbox REPL-admitted; certification of the lane head pending.

proofs.title: The paged catalog's (group . number)-keyed tables (numbers, live NEXT, live PREV) are dense per-group runs whose every read is the old hash table's lookup: no table of N memberships is rehashed in one commit
proofs.statement: books/catalog-dense-map.lisp + books/catalog-paged.lisp; the subject is the abstract stobj fn-dmap (exports fn-dmap-get/-put/-rem/-clear, exec fn-dmap$c-*), the fn-cat$p-dm field of the paged catalog, called through fn-cat$p-numbers-get/-put (fn-cat$p-group-number, fn-cat$p-numbers-apply in fn-cat$p-tab-commit) and fn-cat$p-lnext-*/lprev-* (fn-cat$p-link, -unlink, -livep, -next, -prev) by fn-cat$p-commit-w and fn-cat$p-withdraw-w, the executables of the generic exports fn-cat-commit / fn-cat-withdraw / fn-cat-group-number attached by books/catalog-paged-attach.lisp. Representation: page (g . floor((n-1)/256)) holds 256 memberships x 3 lanes of u64 words (value + 1; 0 unbound), found through a (group . page index) table and carrying its owner key; an escape table keyed (lane . key) takes what a cell cannot (non-membership keys, values >= 2^64 - 1): the total-semantics fallback, NOT proved empty (a sequence can reach 2^64 - 1: fn-cat$p-count is unbounded), itself an equal hash table that rehashes as it grows. The logical side is exactly three stobj hash tables (get = cdr of hons-assoc-equal, put = cons, rem = hons-remove-assoc, clear = nil), so the paged catalog's view puts lane 0 at the old foundation's numbers position and every simulation (fn-cat$p-commit-w-sim, -withdraw-w-sim, -clear-w-sim, -table-readers-sim) and obligation is the old one at the view. KEYSTONES fn-dm-get-of-put / fn-dm-get-of-rem / fn-dm-get-of-clear (each write changes exactly its own (lane, key); through fn-dm-slot-inj and the owner check fn-dm-pid-own, with no injectivity invariant on the page table) and the extensional correspondence fn-dm-agree (defun-sk over every lane and key), preserved by every export (fn-dmap-*{correspondence}). Measured (hbox REPL, guards on, sb-ext:get-bytes-consed, fn-cat$p-commit-w of real rows in two groups, worst single commit step): numbers+groups+lives step 604,672 / 2,529,776 / 5,059,488 / 10,118,864 B at 8,191 / 32,767 / 65,535 / 131,071 rows before, 32,752 / 32,752 / 62,256 / 88,512 B after; live links 1,265,056 / 5,059,552 / 10,118,976 / 20,237,728 B before, at most 32,752 B after; fn-dmap alone 32,752 B worst at 1k and 84,032 B at 262,144 memberships (dense groups). NOT flat in general: the page table and page array double in one step, Theta(pages) work, and pages are one per (group . 256-block), so G sparse groups make G pages, never freed on rem (Codex r44 F1); a two-level page directory is the open fix, mean 121 B a membership for three puts. Scope: the logical tables; costs are measurements, not theorems; the groups and live-summary tables (one entry a group) and the Message-ID table are not this target. Teeth: tests/acl2/catalog-dense-map-tests.lisp (executed correspondence over two pages, two groups, the escape, a rebinding, a removal and a clear; lane-removal witnesses for fn-dmap-put/rem{preserved}); tests/acl2/catalog-paged-tests.lisp (links exact over the group's numbers: live entries their neighbours, dead numbers unbound; CORRUPTED states by unbinding).

proofs.title: Reachable-state invariant preservation
proofs.statement: Every permitted transition preserves a meaningful invariant from valid initial/reachable states.
proofs.progress_note: Actual finite node traces preserve state and prior bindings; mixed live file/node traces including refusal, known abort and recovery preserve the phase/history relation. The host-called store prepare projection now preserves that relation after observed open across the actual post-open mutators without replaying the appended history per prepare. Provenance, complete runtime guards and physical refinement remain open. BP joint durable/pending sender binding and fixed-Store receiver state/context/decision invariants now hold through actual transitions and arbitrary finite replay; changing-Store composition remains open. CHANGED 2026-09-22 (w31/freeze-3): `fn-snt-relation` (books/store-node-traces) now covers the two publications whose node effect is deferred to `fn-sn-finish` -- `fn-sn-prepare-retention` (`6ab2c783`) and `fn-sn-prepare-identity` (`4bb7bb3d`) -- and the fault arm `fn-sn-recover` grew in `40bb3f74`. Before this it was false of every state those three transitions produce, so `fn-snrt-step-preserves-relation`, `fn-own-step-preserves-relation` and `fn-opc-configured-step-preserves-owner-relation` above it were false with it and no run had said so. What the deferred arm says is weaker than the article arm by design: it carries the replayed node at the reservation's transaction id and the equation between the applied event and the replay of the extended history, and no proposal standing on the live node, because there is none until the directory barrier. PKT-413 adds source-admitted actual replay result projections to the receiver-only full/suffix models on the explicit context-first/no-transit domain; the original model subjects and reach exceptions remain until checker coverage and matching certification are established.

proofs.title: Atomic allocation and stable numbering
proofs.statement: Acceptance publishes all intended local memberships together and never reuses an allocated number for another article.
proofs.progress_note: Atomic logical publication and stable number/binding lemmas; persistent/reclamation integration remains open. OVER THE SERVED PATH (books/owner-numbering.lisp, 2026-09-24): fn-own-served-watermarks-never-decrease -- under fn-own-relation of the configured owner, for any group, any sequence of writer events ((:take), (:begin id), (:store e), (:complete)) through fn-ocfg-step (fn-owner-step, host/owner-host.lisp:209) followed by any connection's outcome installed with fn-ocfg-with-owner (fn-owner-replace-core) leaves the committed view's next local number for that group at least what it was; fn-own-served-local-number-is-never-reassigned -- over the same calls, a (group . number) that names an article of the committed view names an article with the same Message-ID afterwards. The committed view is the archive every reader pins when it opens or advances and reads through fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix (owner-host.lisp:1240). Proof: the view is the replay of a prefix of the durable records and the records only grow (fn-own-step-records-prefix); replaying a longer prefix only conses articles on the front and only raises watermarks; the Message-ID half cites fn-state-has-fresh-local-numbers on the new view. Teeth (tests/acl2/owner-numbering-tests.lisp): witness of two POSTs in fn.letters across a completion (numbers 3 and 4, watermark 3 to 5, 1 and 2 keep their Message-IDs, the advanced reader's GROUP 211 4 1 4 and STAT 3/4 name the new articles); must-fail for the relation on both keystones (the store node's archive wound back to empty: the 240 is still answered, fn.letters 1 is given again and the watermark falls from 3 to 2) and for the holder hypothesis (fn.letters 3 unheld before, held after). The writer-events hypothesis has no tooth: no violating value was found (every other fn-ocfg-step arm keeps the view or refreshes it from an extension of the records), and redundancy is not proved; it is the statement's scope. SCOPE of fn-own-pinned-view-survives-other-post (T6): reader connections only, by design -- a peer connection answers IHAVE/CHECK from the live node (fn-own-conn-live-session), so a POST by another connection correctly changes its 335 to 435; tests/acl2/owner-served-invariants-tests shows it. No peer-connection variant is owed. EVIDENCE: persvati run-20260924T152353Z-e987, manifest planning/evidence/manifests/certify-20260924T152452Z-1758763.json: books/owner-numbering 4.1 s, tests/acl2/owner-numbering-tests 4.3 s, both passed. RESTATED BY control-c3b (2026-09-25), when the committed view began serving the visible state (a cancel withdraws its target from what readers see, books/control-visible.lisp): fn-own-raw-local-number-is-never-reassigned is the former statement over the view's raw list (fn-own-view-raw, the acceptance articles, withdrawn ones included): a (group . number) held there names the same Message-ID after the same calls. fn-own-served-local-number-is-never-reassigned now says a number held in the served (visible) list is held afterwards by the same Message-ID or by nothing (withdrawn); it is never given to another article. The former equality over the served list is false once a cancel executes. fn-own-served-watermarks-never-decrease is unchanged (the visible state keeps the acceptance watermarks). Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-numbering-tests.lisp, both holder keystones with the relation and the held-before must-fails; the fixture has no cancel, so the served keystone's nothing arm has no witness there. Record: planning/evidence/control-c3b-2026-09-25.md. catalog-slice-6 (2026-09-27): P3 (fn-own-pinned-view-survives-other-post, books/owner-served-invariants.lisp) restated under NNT-042: another connection's post leaves a reader's connection record (its pin) and the clock unchanged; the read half holds per framed event for every command that is not a selection (fn-own-other-post-keeps-a-non-selecting-read-step over fn-ocfg-read-step, the host's per-event read); a chunk whose GROUP or LISTGROUP succeeds answers from the fresh view by specification (its witness in tests/acl2/owner-served-invariants-tests.lisp is flipped and labelled). The chunk form for chunks framing no selection is stated in the record and not yet proved.

proofs.title: Reservation and release safety
proofs.statement: Accepted obligations are accounted for and discharge requires the specified predicate over committed authorized evidence.
proofs.progress_note: Finite abstract admission and general release preserve valid ledgers; release preserves independent pins and known identities. P9 over the host-called functions (books/store-node-retention.lisp, 2026-09-24): fn-spc-prepare (host/store-node-host.lisp:472, answered :refused at :475 when it returns its input) returns the live store state unchanged whenever the record's charge exceeds the room the node's retention capacity leaves, with that comparison its only hypothesis; fn-node-prepare does the same; fn-node-prepare-refuses-whatever-retain-admit-refuses is the named equation that makes RET-002's fn-retain-admit-refuses-unaffordable-obligation a statement about the called function (fn-retain-admit's no-op is exactly the inadmissible case, and in that case prepare refuses). fn-sn-finish (store-node-host.lisp:546): every article accepted before a completion is accepted after it on every arm (no hypothesis beyond membership), and an obligation leaves the ledger only when the completed record is a retention release, not an undertaking, matching its id, subject, kind and evidence; Store releases name kind :forward, so no arm releases an article's :archive pin (corollary fn-sn-finish-keeps-every-archive-obligation). Teeth: tests/acl2/store-node-retention-tests.lisp, reachable witnesses from fn-sn-initial through the host's io/prepare/finish (capacity 10, 2 reserved, charge 9 refused and 8 staged; article, undertaking and release arms) and one must-fail per hypothesis; the identity, consumer and topic arms have no concrete witness. Scope: charges are abstract units, not physical bytes; there is no archive-release event in v0, so 'until explicit release' is 'kept' for articles; crash/recover and sweep are not covered here. Authorized/committed evidence validation remains open. M5 transaction budget over the called prepare (books/owner-store-budget.lisp, 2026-09-24): fn-sbud-prepare, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare installs, is the identity when the budget is at most the owner Store's committed record count and is fn-opc-prepare below it; its refusal word is :unaffordable; the budget is the persisted profile's admissibility (fn-sbud-budget-is-the-profile-admissibility) and is fixed at init. Teeth in tests/acl2/owner-store-budget-tests.lisp and tests/acl2/store-budget-tests.lisp; farm manifest certify-20260924T161235Z-2188032. Second count and payload constant removed (books/store-budget-naming.lisp, 2026-09-24): the host names each transaction file from the staged candidate's sequence, fn-sbud-pending-sequence (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-pending-sequence, host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-pending-sequence), through fn-sbud-txn-name, the scan's fn-bs-txn-name; in a record phase of a well-formed kernel that sequence is the committed count (fn-sbud-pending-sequence-is-used) and the name extends the committed namespace to one fn-bs-txn-observation-pairs accepts at sequence used (fn-sbud-pending-name-is-the-scans-next-name). The POST boundary both entries call is fn-sbud-post-boundary over the persisted profile, admitting exactly the payloads at or under the profile's payload field (fn-sbud-post-boundary-refuses-exactly-past-the-profile-bound); the served owner relays :payload-bound as the Store word :refused, whose 441 line is W3's. Teeth in tests/acl2/store-budget-naming-tests.lisp over an owner reached by its own transitions; farm manifest certify-20260924T182844Z-3383029.

proofs.title: Codec and identity preimages
proofs.statement: Accepted values round-trip; deterministic encodings and domain-separated preimages have the specified uniqueness and version boundaries.
proofs.progress_note: The record codec has schemas 1 (bounded acceptance stamp) and 2 (a wide integer field); the stampless schema 0 and its :legacy stamp are deleted (no migrations: fresh deploys at 6.6.0; lane small-rows-2-d3). The combined native image and migration witness remain open. The codec evidence is scoped to its admitted grammars; unknown-record opaque preservation and complete native signature/Store integration are not established by it. The separate hybrid-carrier evidence describes exact-source serialization and its remaining universal round-trip obligation. D27 codec ceilings (packet P2, lane/bounds-p2-ceilings, 2026-09-25): the record codec writes and reads every byte string through the CBOR bounded API at the record width (fn-record-item-encode, fn-record-item-decode, books/records.lisp), so the record is no longer capped by the generic entry's 65,535-octet item; fn-record-impl-round-trip and fn-record-impl-accepted-input-is-canonical keep their statements over it, fn-record-item-stream-bytes-round-trip is the item round trip at any length up to the u32 record width, fn-record-item-encode-is-cbor-encode keeps every record of at most 65,535-octet items byte-identical (the schema-0 golden vector is unchanged), and the seam constraint fn-record-encode-length-bound bounds a record's encoding by fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling of its payload length and group count. Teeth: tests/acl2/records-ceiling-tests.lisp (a 70,000-octet payload and a 460-octet group name round-trip; the generic decoder refuses the u32-headed item; a must-fail per round-trip hypothesis). Scope: the codec ceilings (record 2^32-1, payload 2^32-2^25, 65,535 groups, 460-octet names) are widths, not the operator's bounds; until packet P1 the served bound is the profile's payload field (32,768 in every named profile). Evidence: planning/evidence/bounds-p2-2026-09-25.md.

proofs.progress_note: Fixed-mode framing composition, production event-yield preservation and exact consumed-prefix/suffix accounting are certified. Wildmat DP matches independent anchored semantics. Session-sensitive mode changes and complete protocol/effect refinement remain open. The served path is now the subject: books/served states partition independence of fn-served-step and of the whole reply stream, which is the function tools/run_reader.py calls once per socket read, so the wire pending_subject note is closed for framing. The owner book now certifies in the merged feed/transit batch recorded by planning/evidence/manifests/certify-20260921T051833Z-3941584.json. This does not extend these framing theorems to an unproved owner composition or to Python outbound article rendering; W12 wire-block owns that running-path extension. The W14 cumulative byte-feeder induction now proves successful outbound block source preservation through fn-wire-drive and the actual fn-wire-render-feed-command article arm under the exact served article-start profile. Its hypotheses require positive command profile, the nonempty article arm excluding CHECK/IHAVE/TAKETHIS command prefixes, renderer success, and the article limit no greater than receiver body limit; tests separate each premise. This is not a new proof of later authentication/injection dispatch or durable acceptance. The native counted fast transition is now integrated: fn-served-step-counted-fast-is-reference is certified under the maintained full wire invariant, with a malformed-retained-byte separating witness. Per-read entry checks only the fixed wire spine and scalars. The changed outer fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix-is-full-read correspondence is pending current-source certification; the focused served closure excludes that owner book. See planning/evidence/native-served-fast-path-w26-2026-09-21.md. CLOSED AS STATED 2026-09-22 (w31/freeze-3): `fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix-is-full-read` now certifies with the premise `fn-served-step-counted-fast-is-reference` asks for -- `fn-wire-statep` of the found connection's wire. proofs.title: Conditional crash recovery
proofs.statement: Under the disk model, recovery retains acknowledged commits, may retain complete unacknowledged commits, and exposes no partial transaction.
proofs.progress_note: Arbitrary mixed live/file traces including refusal/abort preserve exact ready-state replay and prior acknowledged records, conditional on the kernel crash model. Observed-image opening uses actual recovery with no fabricated acknowledgements or barriers; zero through two barriers remain gated, the third opens ready (*fn-sf-recovery-barrier-count* 3 since lane open-barriers, 2026-09-27; five before). Host adoption passed the integrated suite; physical byte correspondence, freshness and platform qualification remain separate from these targeted proofs. Receiver logical replay now preserves exact contexts and committed receipt ADUs against a fixed Store. Five actual receiver process-death cuts passed in the 133-test suite; process death is separate from power loss and general FNWF/FNRJ byte/live/replay refinement. Fencing, barrier and retention keystones are unchanged in statement and now run with the whole-state recognizers off the executable path (24 calls to 0 in the store cluster, 10 to 0 in core), carried under mbe instead. Real process evidence: the deploy gate SIGKILLed the server inside an open POST and the acknowledged article reread byte-for-byte after recovery. Byte-level torn writes remain the DESIGN-crash-model-v2 design, which is review finding D4. OPEN AND CHANGED 2026-09-22 (w31/freeze-3): `fn-snrt-new-success-is-actual-matching-durable-completion` keeps its safety conjuncts at full strength for all three arms of `fn-sn-finish` -- a new acknowledgement comes only from `:finish` and only under an enabled completion -- and makes its article-specific conclusions (the bound record, the `fn-node-complete` equation, the committed record) conditional on the acceptance arm, as the keystone it uses already does since `6ab2c783` and `4bb7bb3d` gave the completion record a retention and an identity kind whose node transition is not a completion and whose article accessors name nothing. `fn-sn-known-abort` CHANGED BEHAVIOUR in the same lane: `6ab2c783` gave it a retention arm that left the live node alone, so an aborted retention publication returned a `:ready` state whose node sat one transaction id behind its own durable frontier, which `fn-snt-relation` forbids and `fn-own-idle-node-is-replay` relies on; the arm now advances the node over the id the abort consumes, exactly as `fn-sn-refuse-reservation` does over a refused reservation, and `tests/acl2/store-identity-traces-tests` carries the witness. RESTATED 2026-09-23 (red/bpre): `fn-bprv-history-record-is-node-committed-when-idle` now carries `(fn-record-p record)`: since `6ab2c783` and `346a8f99` a Store history holds retention and statement events beside article records, those install no article under their own name, and `tests/acl2/bp-receiver-evolving-tests` commits a retention undertake on a related `:ready` Store where the old statement is false; the loop keystone `fn-bprv-apply-store-event-keeps-committed` now covers every arm of `fn-replay-apply-record`. `fn-bprv-evolving-invariant-survives-observed-reopen` and `fn-bpr-live-receipt-regenerated-after-restart` now carry `fn-sn-observed-identity-okp` of the image's records, the kernel's own reopen hypothesis since `4857c648`; OPEN: no ground witness separates it under `fn-snt-relation` plus `fn-sf-crash-imagep` (the live prepare checks the identity step, so it may be derivable there), so that hypothesis has no must-fail tooth, and deriving it from the relation would lift it from every kernel reopen guarantee at once. INTERIM 2026-09-24 (BP observed reopen): fn-bprv-observed-reopen-facts, fn-bprv-evolving-invariant-survives-observed-reopen, and fn-bpr-live-receipt-regenerated-after-restart now require fn-sn-observed-topic-okp(records), matching the actual Store observed opener after topic events were added. The existing consumer relation and identity premises do not establish the independent topic replay check; Store tests exhibit structurally valid topic-invalid records, while a counterexample under the full crash-image hypothesis and a reachable-state derivation remain separate obligations. The conditional BP book and dependent test certify at manifests 050516 and 050842. Query: `fn-sn-state` carries the index and the keyring it was computed under as two new fields; `fn-sn-statement-lookup` and `fn-sn-equivocatorp` read the index and nothing else; `host/store-node-host.lisp` `fn-store-sn-statement` and `fn-store-sn-equivocator` call them on the `'fn-store-sn` global, reachable from outside as `run_store.py statement`; and `fn-sn-statement-lookup-is-the-lace-lookup` and `fn-sn-equivocatorp-is-the-lace-equivocator` equate the called function to the projection. Their hypothesis `fn-sn-indexedp` is discharged by a complete reachability chain over every transition that reaches an `f-put-global` of that global. WHY THIS IS NOT YET `certified`: (a) `fn-stx-index-slots-agree` still has no caller -- no served query walks the slot list; (b) A-CRYPTO stands behind every verification, and the only witnesses are under the toy realiser of `tests/acl2/crypto-seam-tests`; (c) the keyring is supplied per invocation and is not carried in the durable configuration history, so a restart forgets it; and (d) `fn-stx-transit-authority-ok` (books/stx-policy) still walks the whole lace per article on the ADMISSION path and has no caller, so D3 is answered at the query and not at admission. Witnesses: `tests/acl2/store-node-index-tests`, a real run of the store transitions from `fn-sn-initial` to `fn-sn-finish` with a signed `FN-Statement` article, with the same run under the empty keyring as the separating witness and a stale-index tooth. Route: planning/lanes/HANDOFF-w11-sn-index.md. CLOSED 2026-09-23 (T4): `fn-sn-finish-preserves-indexedp` no longer excludes the accepted-statement arm. Local replay lemmas establish that a non-nil composite replay from a valid idle node installs exactly one article, its payload equals the decoded composite payload, and `fn-sn-composite-delta` is that article's statement delta; `fn-sn-completion-enabledp` discharges the replay/idle premises. The host-called finish therefore preserves the carried index through retention, neutral identity, accepted composite identity, and ordinary durable acceptance. A reached composite acceptance with a nonempty statement index and a stale-index must-fail tooth are in tests/acl2/store-node-composite-index-tests. The source-book certificate and the pending test certificate are recorded in planning/evidence/store-composite-index-t4-2026-09-23.md.

They replace fn-sn-statement-lookup-is-the-lace-lookup and fn-sn-equivocatorp-is-the-lace-equivocator, stated over the node's article bytes, which carry handles after the flip. The index is the fold of the retained rows' contexts (fn-sn-indexedp over fn-sn-index-of-rows, preserved by every transition in books/store-node-invariants.lisp) and that fold is the wire index of the rows' bytes (fn-rows-index-is-the-wire-index, under fn-rows-contexts-okp, which fn-intern-events-contexts-okp establishes at the intern).
