TEETH (flip-L1-3): tests/acl2/store-node-composite-index-tests.lisp forks the composite run with a held article row at handle 1 (a reachable store holding a composite row and an article row) and asserts both keystones with every hypothesis and both sides of each conclusion non-degenerate (the lookup answers the second statement, the equivocator question is T); hypothesis removals: a stale index (corrupted state; the context invariant still holds) and a mis-paired arena (the arena before the fork's seal; fn-sn-indexedp still holds), each failing both conclusions.

proofs.title: Transit admission is the policy function, and a peer cannot widen it (S4-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-transit-admit-is-fn-pol-admitp: the authority gate on the transit path is fn-pol-admitp over this node's lace and keyring, which is the theorem-subject equation for every policy theorem; fn-stx-peer-batch-cannot-change-policy: if a contact batch contains no statement by the group's authority verified under the local keyring, the policy in force is equal before and after the batch.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: `tests/acl2/stx-transit-tests` CERTIFIES since w10/substrate-2, and the S4-1 witnesses were VACUOUS until it did: the hostile batch's delta was empty because the policy statement's carrier article had a prose body where `fn-stx-payload-for` projects base64. Both carriers are repaired and the deltas are now pinned by their own assertions.

proofs.title: Reconnection never revises admissibility (S5-1)
proofs.statement: fn-stx-commits-of-batch-are-verified-and-well-formed is the carrier obligation and the new work: under a well-formed keyring the commits a batch contributes are well formed and each has a verified statement behind it. On it rest fn-stx-reconnect-never-revises-admissibility, which keeps every fn-me-decide equal across the merge, and fn-stx-reconnect-exposes-the-partition, which makes two commits off a shared base a visible fork rather than a winner.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.note: `books/stx-epochs` CERTIFIES (w10/substrate-2), so the carrier obligation `fn-stx-commits-of-batch-are-verified-and-well-formed` is proved and the three reconnection rows follow it as labelled corollaries of the `books/membership-epochs-invariants` keystones. Its local witness lemma needed a repair, not a weakening: `fn-stx-commits-of-lace-have-witnesses` asked only `fn-lace-p` of the delta and was false; it now asks that every statement of the delta verifies, which `fn-stx-batch-delta` satisfies by construction. Not closed, and w11/node-index found the gap is wider than `no caller`: NO BOOK OUTSIDE THE STX CLUSTER INCLUDES `books/stx-epochs`, and there is no reconnection path in the tree to wire `fn-stx-commits-of-batch` to. That is future feature work, not missing evidence for implemented behaviour (docs/proofs.md, assurance scope). A-CRYPTO stands behind every verification here.

proofs.title: The reader's verdict is the recorded verdict, three-valued (S6-1)
proofs.statement: A durable kind-4 (hybrid acceptance) completion through fn-sn-finish records that event's verdict under its Message-ID; a reader opened after the owner's (:complete) pins that verdict list; and one fn-own-read of HDR :fn-verified <msgid> on an ungated reader connection, framed at its last octet, answers exactly the pinned verdict for the retrieved article, with no keyring consulted. A served NNTP POST (and a local control post or BP application submission) carrying an FN-Authorship carrier takes the transit classification: when ACL2 builds its kind-4 event under the node's current enrollment and that event is the completion record, the owner's (:complete) records its verdict at the POST's Message-ID and a later reader reports it; a present carrier the plan refuses renders its reason as its own 441 line and is never the unsigned arm. On NNTP transit (IHAVE) the same relayed reason renders `437 transfer rejected; ` with the text of that reason's 441 line. fn-stx-reader-verdict-is-the-recorded-verdict (books/stx-reader) is the definition restated and is not a proof event; it is no longer cited. D23: on NNTP transit the same fn-pa-current-plan takes the delivering boundary's carried-source list; it plans :carried only when this node has no keyring snapshot of the carrier's principal and the list names it, and off that arm it is the D02 plan (fn-pa-current-plan-off-the-carried-arm-is-the-d02-plan); the carried kind-4 event binds the received octets and the carrier and records token :carried at keyring generation 0, which replay records without a snapshot and the reader renders `carried HEX`, never `verified`.
proofs.planning_note: Stated in specs/substrate-transport.md section 6 against definitions that do not exist yet; no ACL2 event, and the teeth named there ship with the theorem.
proofs.progress_note: Bounds P4 (2026-09-25): a verdict over a v2 carrier records the evidence tag fn-hybrid-v2, which fn-stxe-keyring-profile maps to the one D09 keyring profile so kind-4 replay and the schema-1 binding accept it (fn-hsig-keyring-profile-of-evidence-tag); verdicts recorded under fn-hybrid-v1 keep their meaning and a v1 record stored by a pre-v2 image reads verified on the P4 image (planning/evidence/bounds-p4-2026-09-25.md). This adds no PRF-026 event. Signed-path (2026-09-25, D27): the kind-4 composite's literal caps (32,768 source, 65,538 record, 196,608 composite) are codec ceilings; a served signed POST's composite is held to the store profile's record field R by fn-sbud-signed-event-boundary, which host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-transit asks through fn-owner-signed-event-boundary before the identity commit, and a composite not formed or past R is refused with its own 441 line (:event, :signed-record); an :ok composite satisfies the publish gate's fn-bs-publication-admissiblep at its framed length. Native: a 60 KiB v1 and a 200 KiB v2 signed POST are accepted, HDR verified and fn_verify exit 0; a tampered v2 is refused by name.

proofs.title: The two durable kinds are one sequence-ordered stream (R5)
proofs.statement: fn-cstr-merge-keeps-every-config-record and fn-cstr-merge-keeps-every-article-record: the merge of the configuration-record file and the transaction journal by the sequence field each record carries holds exactly the records of each file, in order -- the left side walks the merge, the right side walks the input file. fn-cstr-merge-is-sequence-ordered: two sequence-ordered files merge to one sequence-ordered stream, so the two-directory layout loses no ordering information. fn-cstr-ok-merged-replay-ends-in-a-configured-node: a merged replay that reports :ok ends in a fn-cnode-statep state, which carries reserved <= capacity, so every configuration record in the history was admitted at a node that had already replayed the article records before it. Covered scope: finite histories of the two record kinds; no on-disk interleaving is claimed.
proofs.progress_note: books/config-stream certifies (ACL2 8.7, persvati, 2026-09-20). The separating witness in tests/acl2/config-stream-tests is the argument for the decision: one (:set-capacity 1) over a history whose two articles reserve 2, which the configuration-only replay the host runs today accepts and the merged replay refuses with :config-refusal; a raise and a decrease to exactly the reservation total are both admitted, so the merged replay is not refusing every decrease. Open: the host still replays configuration first (specs/reconfiguration.md section 8). No event yet; T2.

proofs.title: Live reconfiguration: what a configuration generation serves, and what a crash recovers (R5, T8)
proofs.statement: fn-ocl-no-reader-observes-a-half-change, over what the host calls (staging through fn-ocfg-step at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-reconfigure-deltas, publication through fn-ocl-publish at fn-owner-reconfigure-complete) and with no hypothesis: every open connection's record, every configuration pin and every served table are unchanged across staging and publication; staging leaves the live configuration where it was; a non-durable verdict changes nothing; a :durable verdict completes exactly the record whose generation the durable write named, appends that whole record to the store's configuration history, publishes what that history replays to, clears the stage and installs the matching posting configuration. The owner itself is not unchanged on the called path (store and posting configuration move). fn-ocl-publish-installs-the-whole-staged-record: under fn-ocl-config-historyp the published configuration is fn-cfg-apply-record of the live configuration and the whole staged record, by fn-ocl-cpr-loop-configuration-is-the-record-fold. fn-ocl-publish-agrees-with-ocfg-complete-on-readers equates the called path with the model event (:complete) on pins, served tables, connection records and the stage. fn-ocl-request-refused-over-a-reader-in-the-group: a group request (fn-ocl-request-deltas, the delta the host no longer builds) for a group some open connection's reader has selected is refused at staging. The model statement follows. fn-ocfg-no-reader-observes-a-half-change: the two owner events a live reconfiguration consists of, (:reconfigure other deltas) then (:complete), leave the owner -- every open connection's record, session and pinned archive, hence every reply -- and every configuration pin exactly as they were; staging leaves the live configuration where it was; and publication moves it to fn-ocfg-published-config of the staged record, the old configuration or fn-cfg-apply-record of the whole record and nothing between; one hypothesis, that a record was staged, the condition under which the host calls (:complete). fn-ocfg-pin-is-stable-without-advance: over any finite fn-ocfg-step event list holding no (:advance id), (:close id) or (:fault id), a pinned connection keeps the configuration it opened at. fn-ocl-crash-at-any-instant-recovers-the-live-generation, over what the host calls (staging (:reconfigure id deltas) and (:close id) through fn-ocfg-step, the durable write, publication through fn-ocl-publish; recovery through fn-cpr-replay of the configuration journal and the Store journal at host/owner-host.lisp:173 in fn-owner-recover), with one hypothesis, fn-ocl-config-historyp (the live configuration is what fn-cpr-replay of the store's own journals recovers): before the durable write the store and both journals are unchanged and replay :ok to the live configuration, which staging did not move; after the write and before publication, a replay of the configuration journal with the staged record appended is either not :ok (the host answers :fault and installs nothing) or recovers exactly the configuration the model's (:complete) publishes, fn-cfg-apply-record of the live configuration and the whole record, at the record's generation; on a :durable publication the installed store's journals are exactly those, their replay is :ok to the published configuration, nothing is staged and the hypothesis holds again, so the statement chains across every later reconfiguration; A-DURABILITY enters as the publisher's :durable meaning the record is in the directory the next open reads. fn-ocl-cpr-replay-ok-is-config-replay-ok relates the called replay to the configuration-only one as a refinement: an :ok of fn-cpr-replay on (configs, events) is an :ok of fn-cnode-config-replay on configs with the same configuration; the converse is false (a configuration journal whose transaction ids descend is accepted by fn-cnode-config-replay and refused :config-txid by fn-cpr-replay; tests/acl2/config-crash-replay-tests), and the called path does not write such a journal (fn-cpo-configure-durable appends only at the Store frontier and only when fn-cpr-replay of the result is :ok). The model statements fn-ocfg-crash-at-any-instant-recovers-the-live-generation and fn-ocfg-config-replay-of-one-more-record (books/owner-config.lisp, over fn-cnode-config-replay, which no host line calls, and fn-ocfg-step (:complete)) stay as model-level lemmas and are not registry events. fn-ocfg-open-pins-the-live-configuration and fn-ocfg-advance-observes-the-live-configuration: under fn-ocfg-statep a new or advanced connection pins the live configuration. fn-native-admin-live-group-delta-is-a-typed-delta: an accepted group create or retire stages one delta that fn-cfg-deltap admits. Covered scope: the owner's configuration and pins; NOT covered: the live node's allocation domain and capacity, which no owner transition moves, so a group created live is published and in the injection configuration but GROUP and LIST ACTIVE answer from the acceptance state's group list and do not show it until a restart (books/owner-config.lisp OPEN item 3); LIST ACTIVE on the wire answers from that list, not from the pin (OPEN item 1).
proofs.progress_note: T8 (2026-09-22): two defects found and fixed in the live arm. (1) fn-ocfg-complete published through fn-cnode-apply-config on the live node, whose domain and capacity no live transition moves, so after one live group create or capacity change every later completion kept the old configuration while the record was already durable (ground witness in tests/acl2/owner-config-tests: the second of two live reconfigurations violated fn-cnode-apply-config's guard); completion now publishes fn-ocfg-published-config, the configuration step recovery replays. (2) host/native-admin-host.lisp passed argv octets as configuration labels, so live group create, group retire and peer remove were refused :malformed-delta; the delta list is now fn-native-admin-plan-deltas. Teeth for every hypothesis in tests/acl2/owner-config-tests and tests/acl2/native-admin-tests. fn-ocfg-list-active-lists-the-pinned-served-table stays proved and is not cited: fn-ocfg-list-active has no host caller. V0-CFG-LIVE on an image is not claimed: its GROUP check needs the domain seam. T8c (2026-09-22): the dabebb84 matrix run showed the live arm faulting the owner on every request, because host/native/admin.lisp read fn-owner-open's integer id through fnn-owner-action (fixed; reproduced and fixed on hbox, planning/evidence/t8c-live-rows-2026-09-22.md), and the control reply losing the owner's fault word to its own stop hook, so the caller saw uncertain (fixed in host/native/control.lisp). fn-native-admin-publication-is-authorized-only-under-the-lock: an accepted publication result, and any result carrying a publication state, implies the lock observation the host passes, which is now the store's own (fnn-admin-lock-observation) and no longer a literal T; teeth in tests/acl2/native-admin-tests. P6 (2026-09-24): the headline is restated over the called path in books/config-owner-publish (fn-ocl-publish, fn-ocl-request-deltas moved from host code); certified on persvati run-20260924T144825Z-3f2c, manifest certify-20260924T144840Z-1413165 (config-owner-publish 4.2 s, its tests 4.2 s). P6 crash replay (2026-09-24): headline 2 restated over fn-cpr-replay, the replay fn-owner-recover calls (host/owner-host.lisp:173), and over fn-ocl-publish, as fn-ocl-crash-at-any-instant-recovers-the-live-generation in books/config-crash-replay; fn-ocl-cpr-replay-ok-is-config-replay-ok relates the two replays as a refinement (the converse is false, with a descending-txid journal); the two fn-cnode-config-replay theorems are model-level lemmas, no longer events. Certified on persvati run-20260924T152028Z-644e, manifest certify-20260924T152041Z-1719002 (config-crash-replay 3.9 s, its tests 3.9 s, config-owner-publish-tests 3.8 s); dependencies run-20260924T150833Z-2987, manifest certify-20260924T150854Z-1605486 (config-owner-publish 4.0 s). Status stays in-progress: no image carrying fn-ocl-publish has run test_native_live_reconfiguration. OCL at open (2026-09-24): fn-orec-recover-installs-ocl-relation (books/owner-recover-ocl) proves, over the composition fn-owner-recover calls (host/owner-host.lisp:186 fn-cpr-replay, :191 fn-cpo-open-observed, :195-201 fn-ocfg-make of fn-own-configure of fn-own-start with fn-oag-post-config), that the installed owner satisfies fn-ocl-relation and fn-scar-view-indexedp under (natp max-conns) and the open's kind :ok, both checked by the host before it installs; the remaining host checks are implied. This discharges fn-ocl-config-historyp, the hypothesis of fn-ocl-crash-at-any-instant-recovers-the-live-generation, at every recovery. Certified on persvati run-20260924T221249Z-f2d3, manifest certify-20260924T221303Z-1169743 (owner-recover-ocl 4.3 s, its tests 4.1 s).

proofs.title: The outbound feed offers exactly the peers in scope, and never a loop (K2, outbound half)
proofs.statement: fn-own-feed-target-is-offerable with fn-own-feed-targets-omit-no-offerable-peer: for a feed table the owner carries, the peers one durably accepted article is offered to are exactly the peers of that table whose own configured record has an outbound half, whose outbound wildmat matches one of the article's own Newsgroups names, whose path-identity the article's Path does not already name, and which is not the peer the article arrived from. fn-own-feed-never-offers-a-loop is the loop-freedom half (RFC 5537 section 3.6) and fn-own-feed-target-is-in-scope the scope half; fn-own-feed-accept-touches-only-its-targets and fn-own-feed-accept-never-enqueues-on-the-origin transport both to the table the owner holds, and fn-own-feed-tick-peer-is-the-feed-tick is the subject rule tying one peer's tick to fn-feed-tick-step on that peer's own feed. Covered scope: one article's octets against one table; the hypothesis is the carried recognizer fn-own-feed-tablep. NOT covered: the statement over fn-own-step and fn-feedp preservation, which is cited from books/peer-feed-invariants and not restated. Over the functions the host calls (books/owner-feed-subject.lisp, 2026-09-24): fn-own-submission-targets-are-feed-targets bounds fn-own-submission-targets -- what host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-submission-intent reaches through fn-own-submission-intent-records, and what fn-own-feed-durable enqueues and fn-own-feed-durable-records journals -- by fn-own-feed-targets (a bound, not an equation: a peer already holding the Message-ID is filtered out); fn-own-submission-never-targets-a-loop is the loop statement over it under the carried recognizer fn-own-feed-tablep; fn-own-transit-outcome-never-enqueues-on-the-origin says the owner fn-owner-transit-outcome installs keeps the origin peer's feed unchanged, whatever the decision and the store word. fn-own-feed-accept has no caller in books/ or host/, so fn-own-feed-accept-touches-only-its-targets and fn-own-feed-accept-never-enqueues-on-the-origin are -sibling theorems and count for nothing on their own; the host-called replacements are fn-own-feed-durable-touches-only-the-submission-targets and fn-own-feed-durable-never-enqueues-on-the-origin. fn-own-feed-targets-omit-no-offerable-peer's recognizer and bound-entry hypotheses are redundant (tests/acl2/owner-feed-tests proves the conclusion from the scope decision alone), so it has one tooth, not three.
proofs.progress_note: books/owner-feed and tests/acl2/owner-feed-tests are CERTIFIED as of 2026-09-20, lane w6/peering-feed-4 (laptop ACL2 8.7, evidence build/lanes/w6-peering-feed-4/build/acl2/certify-20260920T212559Z-13370; the persvati closure run-20260920T211802Z-ba78 reached them for the first time). What unblocked them was books/peer-feed-invariants, which now certifies with no open form. books/owner certifies too. The owner-side statement over fn-own-step is still open, and the reason has moved: books/owner-invariants is open at the :open-peer arm of fn-own-step-preserves-relation, not at the feed. The earlier non-admission explanation above is historical; later frozen owner books certified. W22 integrates the actual host tick/reply/loss/restart projections through owner-feed-port, including an all-or-nothing logical restart fold. Its owned closure and combined source gate are tracked separately; no new theorem over fn-own-step or native outbound socket/timer behavior is claimed from this adoption. Native feed component now carries a connection-table invariant from recovery through put/remove, validates only selected bounded input, and distinguishes handshake rejection from delivery refusal. Owned certification and raw boundary tests are separate from activation/real two-native-node evidence. The shell host-wrapper witness is withheld pending repair of its unconditional success marker.

proofs.title: Provenance is typed, and its wire form is lossless and legacy-compatible
proofs.statement: Every string is an admissible provenance (the :legacy kind), so widening the retention evidence slot from stringp to fn-provp changes no stored value; the rendered form of each typed kind is exactly the string that kind's writer produced before the widening; and a provenance the codec can write is the provenance it reads back from its wire form.
proofs.note: The transit path's DURABLE provenance is not covered: fn-peer-injection-arguments still passes fn-peer-evidence's rendering, and fn-peer-evidence-is-the-legacy-rendering is the equation between the typed record and that string, not evidence that the record reaches the store. books/peer-inbound and books/peer-inbound-invariants have no certificate on dev (blocked on fn-peer-echo-reply-effects-well-formed), so those two events are admitted, not certified, and are not listed here.

proofs.title: AUTHINFO on the served path, and what posting follows (W10)
proofs.statement: fn-auth-gated-command-is-refused-and-not-performed: with authentication required and no authenticated subject, a restricted command's step submits nothing, never offers article mode, leaves the session unchanged and its whole effect list is the single 480 line (RFC 4643 section 2.2). Its seven hypotheses each have a violating value in tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp; the two syntactic ones it used to carry were removed on 2026-09-22 because no value violates them while the restricted-keyword hypothesis holds (fn-auth-restricted-keyword-is-a-keyword-token). fn-auth-post-without-permission-is-not-offered and its lift fn-auth-step-post-without-permission-is-not-offered: a connection whose posting allowance is false is answered by this book and never offered 340, so no body can follow and no submission can leave; fn-auth-postingp is the authenticated principal's credential flag, so a principal enrolled without it is refused 440 however permissive the pinned injection configuration is (RFC 3977 6.3.1.1). fn-served-dispatch-of-a-refused-post-leaves-the-wire-in-place carries that to the served dispatcher: the wire is not switched into article mode and the read carries no submission. fn-auth-pass-before-user-is-482 and fn-auth-failed-pass-leaves-the-session-unauthenticated are two of the three RFC 4643 section 2.3.2 codes, each with the session unchanged or cleared. The third is stated over the called function: fn-auth-step-protected-only-refuses-authinfo-before-tls says that while the operator's policy is protected-only and the connection carries no TLS layer, an AUTHINFO command line -- USER or PASS, any arguments, configured name or not -- is answered 483 and nothing else happens: the session is the one the command arrived on, so no name is cached and no subject is installed, no submission leaves, and the secret is never compared because the branch that would compare it is not reached. Its eight hypotheses each have a violating value in the teeth book. The label half of the same channel: fn-auth-starttls-is-not-advertised-under-tls-on-any-connection, fn-auth-authinfo-is-not-advertised-once-authenticated-on-any-connection and fn-auth-authinfo-is-not-advertised-before-tls-under-protected-only are over fn-auth-capability-lines-for-peer, which is the list fn-auth-command puts in the 101 block for EVERY connection and not only a reader's, and fn-auth-step-capability-block-unfolds-to-the-peer-aware-lines is the named unfold equating that list to what fn-auth-step emits; fn-auth-starttls-is-not-advertised-without-a-certificate is the reader-facing instance of the first. Those three say what a client is OFFERED; they do not state anything about the octets fn-nntp-multi renders the list into. fn-auth-pass-accepts-only-a-checking-secret says the accepting branch ran fn-authsec-checkp against the stored verifier; it does NOT say a wrong secret fails, which is A-CRYPTO. Covered scope: one served connection over a pinned archive and a pinned AUTHINFO configuration. The subject of the lifts above is fn-auth-step, a sibling the host does not call: books/served.lisp:617 fn-served-dispatch calls fn-auth-step-pinned, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at reaches through fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix. P1 is stated over that called function and over fn-served-dispatch, each 480 and 483 statement proved from the fn-auth-step keystone and the bridge fn-auth-step-pinned-agrees-with-auth-step-on-handled-command: fn-auth-step-pinned-gated-command-is-refused-and-not-performed (seven hypotheses, the 480 keystone's) and fn-served-dispatch-of-a-gated-command-is-480-and-changes-nothing, which says that on a served connection whose policy requires authentication and which has no subject, a restricted command within the command and argument bounds leaves the whole connection (wire framing, session, pinned archive and indexes) equal to the one it arrived on and its only effect is the 480 line; fn-auth-step-pinned-protected-only-refuses-authinfo-before-tls (eight hypotheses) and fn-served-dispatch-of-authinfo-on-a-clear-connection-is-483-and-changes-nothing, the same for AUTHINFO on a clear connection under protected-only, whose only effect is the 483 line, so no name is cached and the secret is never compared; fn-auth-step-pinned-post-by-a-principal-without-the-flag-is-440, an authenticated principal whose credential lacks the posting flag is answered 440 to POST with the session unchanged and no submission; and fn-auth-step-pinned-post-by-a-principal-with-the-flag-is-delegated, one whose credential carries the flag and whose principal is the subject has its POST handed unchanged to fn-auth-delegate-pinned, where the pinned injection configuration still decides. Each has its hypotheses dropped one at a time under must-fail with an evaluated counterexample in tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp (keystones 11 to 17). Covered scope: one dispatched command event; the chain from fn-served-dispatch to the host read is fn-own-read-is-served-step-on-pinned-prefix and fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix-is-full-read. OB-AUTH-FOLD is fn-auth-fold-step-has-no-local-submission: if the served connection is valid, its pinned credential policy grants posting to no principal, and no local POST body is pending, every effect of the complete fn-served-step read excludes fn-inj-injectedp; fn-auth-fold-step-preserves-safe-connp carries those conditions between reads. Separately authorized fn-peer-submissionp transit remains possible, as the reachable AUTHINFO plus TAKETHIS witness shows. The invoked subject is fn-served-step, reached by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at through fn-own-read; fn-own-read-is-served-step-on-pinned-prefix is its named correspondence.
proofs.progress_note: Historical W10 local admission and cache-origin limitations are superseded for the frozen03 closure and source-pinned native-auth continuation by their archived certification/build evidence. The native AUTHINFO startup receiver passes scoped live wrong-password/correct-password and reader-versus-peer cases. These results do not establish independent-client interoperability, native protected transport, or complete physical adapter correspondence. Native principal administration has scoped ACL2 and actual replacement/recovery evidence; public CLI composition remains open. The existing salted SHA-256 verifier is preserved without a password-hardening or secrecy theorem claim. Lane t7/auth-teeth, 2026-09-22: the events above are curated for the first time and tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp is the teeth book, with a reachable non-degenerate witness for each keystone and one must-fail per hypothesis for the 480 gate (seven) and the 483 refusal (eight), plus separating witnesses for the three capability labels. OB-AUTH-FOLD now proves the local-submission exclusion through the served byte fold in books/nntp-auth-fold.lisp, with a reachable transit counterexample to the prior no-any-submission claim. Two of K1's four hypotheses (fn-served-connp and the not-handshaking one) are proof-support and have no must-fail, because K1 restated without them reaches an open case, a session that is fn-auth-sessionp but not consistent with its connection's archive. The 483-before-TLS and 281-after-STARTTLS behaviour on a deployed image is tools/node_probe.py's row and has not been run on one. K2 follow-up teeth isolate the no-pending-POST premise with a forged but fn-served-connp no-posters state after an actual 340 offer; it submits locally and is unreachable from a no-posters open under the preservation theorem. fn-served-connp is a structural carried connection invariant, not a separate permission test or a runtime whole-store scan.

proofs.title: The recovery window's crash images are kernel-admissible and risk no acknowledged record
proofs.statement: In the recovery window -- the phases between a process replaying what it scanned from the view and completing its five recovery fences -- a crash may drop the record the replay read, because that record's directory entry is the entry operation a dead process left pending; and it may roll the frontier back, because the pending entry operation may be the allocator rename instead. fn-sf-recovery-crash-imagep admits exactly those two images and no other, each gated by an empty success history, the frontier arm additionally by a record list that leaves the reserved txid unused, and the two exclusive of one another; every image it admits is produced by fn-sf-image-crash with the same frontier, records, :replaying phase and success history; and an acknowledged pair of the pre-crash state names a record of EVERY image it admits, both rolled-back ones included.
proofs.note: Decisions D14-b (lane w10/kernel-freedom, the record arm) and D14-c (lane w11/bytestore-k2, the frontier arm K2f). The recognizer is a SECOND one: fn-sf-crash-imagep is unchanged and stays the reliance predicate that fn-own-reopen gates on and every reopen theorem takes as a premise, because widening it is false for the composition -- an owner reopened on an image is a recovery-window state whose own success history is empty while its ledger names records earlier processes acknowledged, and which of a state's records are fenced is a fact about the byte store's pending list, not about the kernel state. The counterexample is mechanized in tests/acl2/owner-tests.lisp (the owner half) and tests/acl2/store-observed-traces-tests.lisp (the kernel half). This target retires the open row K2r of specs/crash-model-v2.md; crash-model-v2 K2, whose conclusion this predicate is, remains open on the byte side, and what it waits on is now only K1's three remaining scan clauses: the frontier sub-case K2f is modelled, so K2's STATEMENT is true of every image the platform can leave in the window.

proofs.title: A clock the host contradicts is dropped, and the refusal is not an article verdict
proofs.statement: fn-own-observe answers exactly one of :observed, :refused and :invalid, and the host reports that word rather than inferring one from a state comparison. On a related owner a :refused reading names a host contradiction -- the monotonic counter went backwards, has-wall changed, or a widened error bound moved the earliest admissible true time back -- and never merely a reading that did not move, because a reading equal to the one held is admitted. A refusal leaves the owner with no clock, and with no usable injection reading fn-nntp-post-step emits no submission and answers `441 posting failed; this server has no usable clock reading', which is a different constant from every article verdict the step can give. DATE additionally uses the supplied current reading: fn-served-step-date-any-session-ignores-pinned-reading equates the effects of the host-called fn-served-step over an exact DATE CRLF at a clean command boundary for arbitrary session/archive/config/index fields and two arbitrary accept-time observations; fn-served-step-date-uses-current-reading gives the exact current-clock response on a reachable fresh reader, including missing/no-wall refusals. The current observation is an input, not a proof of clock accuracy or host freshness.
proofs.note: Decision D10-a, lane w11/clock-seam. Keystones fn-own-observe-refusal-names-a-contradiction (books/owner-invariants.lisp) and fn-post-without-a-clock-refuses-with-the-clock-line (books/nntp-post.lisp), with fn-own-observe-outcome-is-one-of-three and fn-own-observe-outcome-decides-the-clock-by-definition named for what they are and cited by :use. Teeth are evaluated in tests/acl2/owner-tests.lisp (the served-path second post on one connection, the same-reading collision, the clock 441 with an empty queue, DATE 503, and one-event recovery) and tests/acl2/nntp-post-tests.lisp (one must-fail per hypothesis). OPEN under this target: two submissions inside one millisecond still share a generated Message-ID, because fn-clock-later-observationp is non-strict; separating them needs the owner to remember the reading it last minted under and is not done here. t42 (current DATE): the served post dispatchers and unrestricted catalog dispatcher select the current owner-supplied injection observation for DATE and NEWGROUPS year parsing. The prior DATE-503 witness did not establish this on an already-open connection. See books/served-date-current.lisp and tests/acl2/served-date-current-tests.lisp for the served-step clock-independence witness scope; native same-connection >61-second regression is tests/test_native_owner.py::NativeOwnerTests::test_date_on_connection_older_than_a_minute_is_current. Certification and native execution of these changed bytes are pending liaison validation. NEWNEWS two-digit-year parsing still shares its pinned horizon input and remains open; no no-miss claim is added.

proofs.title: A reopened journal answers for a work what the pre-crash machine would have, and says which works it recovered
proofs.statement: fn-bp-work-status-of-restart: under fn-bp-statep, the :restart transition a reopen runs changes the boundary answer for one work id by fn-bp-work-status-after-restart and by nothing else -- an attempt that was in flight is marked :restart-observed, while :absent, :outstanding, :receipted, a retryable status and :delivered are fixed points. fn-bp-replay-work-status-is-the-pre-crash-status-restarted lifts that to fn-bp-replay-journal, the predecessor interpreter for the original FNWF kinds: when the replay succeeds, fn-bp-work-status of the installed image is fn-bp-work-status-after-restart of fn-bp-work-status of the trace of the initial state over fn-bp-durable-events, the journal's denotation without that trailing restart. Provenance is separate and also ACL2's: fn-bp-work-origin-at-open-is-recovered-or-absent says that against the id list fn-bp-work-ids records at open, every work the image holds reads :recovered and every other id reads :absent; fn-bp-durable-enqueue-after-open-reads-enqueued says this session's durable enqueue of an id that list does not name reads :enqueued. So a work recovered from a cut and a work enqueued after the reopen, which share the status :outstanding, are distinct at the boundary. fn-bprl-replay-work-status-is-durable-status-restarted covers fn-bprl-replay-journal over the release-aware FNWF language: if replay succeeds, the installed work status is the one-restart status of the exact ACL2 release-aware interpreter folded over its durable records. fn-bpiw-reopen-after-live-recovery-is-the-live-image-restarted covers the recovery outcome in the ION-overlay journal the host now opens: if fn-bpiw-replay-journal opens a journal and fn-bpiw-apply accepts a :recovery outcome on the opened image, then fn-bpiw-replay-journal accepts the journal with that outcome appended (so the history gate admits what the live gate admits), and its installed BP image is fn-bp-restart of the live image and its ION state is the live one.
proofs.note: Lane w11/workflow-replay, book books/bp-workflow-replay-status.lisp, teeth in tests/acl2/bp-workflow-records-tests.lisp. The subject of the first two keystones is what host/workflow-host.lisp:63 (fn-workflow-work-status) calls; of the last two, what host/workflow-host.lisp:73 (fn-workflow-work-origin) calls on the list host/workflow-host.lisp:8 records. Certified on hbox, run-20260921T005523Z-05dc, build/acl2/certify-20260921T005528Z-1361353. Before the ION extension, the native workflow host called fn-bprl-replay-journal, which also interprets :undertake and :release; fn-bprl-replay-work-status-is-durable-status-restarted certifies that successful predecessor path, with an extended reachable journal and a malformed-suffix must-fail tooth in tests/acl2/bp-release-tests.lisp (persvati manifests certify-20260923T173933Z-2312844.json and certify-20260923T174038Z-2322911.json). The earlier fn-bp replay theorem remains scoped to its original record language. The :enqueue kind hypothesis of fn-bp-durable-enqueue-after-open-reads-enqueued has a constructed rather than a reached tooth, and the test book says so: fn-bp-prepare-attempt only prepares an attempt for a work the image holds, so the composed machine reaches no :attempt pending over an image that holds none. Current scope correction (2026-09-24): host/workflow-host.lisp fn-workflow-install-replay now calls fn-bpiw-replay-journal, whose mixed FNWF stream includes :ion-route and :ion-observed. The two certified single-record structural projections in books/bp-ion-workflow.lisp do not yet lift the work-status theorem through that complete replay. A named actual-caller correspondence with a reachable mixed-history witness remains open; predecessor certificates do not discharge it. Hence the target is in-progress, while its existing component theorems remain intact. Replay fence (lane ion-replay-fence, 2026-09-24): fn-bpiw-replay-records now reconstructs the unrecorded reopen fence before a :recovery outcome (fn-bpiw-replay-fence, books/bp-ion-workflow.lisp), as fn-bp-replay-records does; before it, a journal holding a recovery outcome could not be reopened and the history preflight refused every recovery outcome (planning/evidence/m4-app-receipt-2026-09-24.md finding 4). The keystone's subject is fn-bpiw-replay-journal, called by host/workflow-host.lisp:13 (fn-workflow-install-replay) and :107 (fn-workflow-preflight-history), against fn-bpiw-apply as host/workflow-host.lisp:112 (fn-workflow-apply-record) calls it; book books/bp-ion-workflow-replay.lisp, teeth in tests/acl2/bp-ion-workflow-replay-tests.lisp (reachable enqueue, attempt and ION-carrying cuts; must-fail without the recovery-outcome and live-acceptance hypotheses; the open-success hypothesis has no separating witness because a failed open's image holds no fence, and the test book shows that refusal). Scope: one recovery outcome applied right after an open; the general live-suffix correspondence across later records is not claimed, and a live re-attempt of a :restart-observed attempt without a journaled retry request is refused by the history (the must-fail witness), which is the host's intended gate. Evidence: planning/evidence/ion-replay-fence-2026-09-24.md.

proofs.title: The frame integrity trailer has one owner, and the host's framing is the model's
proofs.statement: fn-frame-trailer (books/frame-trailer.lisp) is the only definition of the 32-octet frame integrity trailer in the tree: it is fn-frame-digest, realised through books/crypto-attach.lisp by fn-blake3-stobj (books/blake3-stobj.lisp, the buffer computation; SHA-256 up to store format 9), which fn-blake3-stobj-is-blake3 equates to the definition fn-blake3 (books/blake3.lisp) on every object, and it answers :bad rather than a digest for an argument that is not an octet list. For any magic, version, kind and payload in fn-frame-inputp, the byte string a host builds by asking ACL2 for the protected prefix, asking ACL2 for the trailer over it and concatenating the two is fn-frame-seal of those fields; and handing that byte string back to fn-frame-decode with the trailer re-derived over the frame's own fn-frame-protected-prefix answers fn-frame-ok of the fields that went in. The same two statements hold for the store instance the bridge executes, over fn-frame-store-protected and fn-frame-store-decode. Collision and preimage resistance are A-CRYPTO and are not claimed: the attachment introduces no axiom and the seam's constraints are shape only.
proofs.note: Lane w11/one-owner. Keystones fn-frame-protected-plus-trailer-is-seal, fn-frame-decode-of-host-framing and their store instances fn-frame-store-protected-plus-trailer-is-seal and fn-frame-store-decode-of-host-framing, all in books/frame-trailer.lisp. Subject-to-host: the host lines that call fn-frame-trailer are tools/frame_bridge.py FrameSession.trailer (called by seal and digest_of), host/native/io.lisp fnn-trailer (called by fnn-seal and fnn-digest-of) and tools/run_owner.py Acl2Owner.trailer (called by feed_frames and feed_replay_frame); each replaced a separate SHA-256 in that host. Teeth in tests/acl2/frame-trailer-tests.lisp: 25 assert-events, including two FIPS 180-4 vectors, the exact store prefix and trailer octets, the :bad boundary arm, and one violating value per clause (a magic whose third octet is 300 for the shape clause keystone 1 needs, a max-payload of 2 for the bound clause keystone 2 needs, and a non-octet record for the store instance). Byte identity with the deleted host copies was cross-checked outside ACL2 against CPython hashlib.sha256 at 32, 4096, 32768, 262144 and 1048576 octets. NOT closed by this target: fn-frame-digest's collision resistance, and the marshalling cost of sealing a 4 MiB staged inbound bundle through the decimal-octet bridge. Lane rep-sha256 (D27 boundary 3, 2026-09-25): the executable digest is fn-sha256-stobj, SHA-256 over a word stobj (books/sha256-stobj.lisp), attached in crypto-attach under fn-sha256-stobj-is-sha256; fn-sha256-stobj-is-sha256-of-octets is its instance on octet lists and fn-sha256-of-string-is-sha256-of-octets covers the string entry the host sha256 verb calls (host/native/io.lisp, the verb; the host SHA-256 twin fnn-sha256 is deleted). Teeth in tests/acl2/sha256-stobj-tests.lisp: the FIPS vectors through both entries, the padding boundaries against the list model, a must-fail and a separating witness for the string theorem's stringp; the keystone has no hypothesis. No statement of an existing theorem moved.
proofs.progress_note: Both books certified with tools/certify_books.py on the laptop (ACL2 8.7, SBCL 2.6.8), evidence dirs above. The four keystones and the 25 assert-events all pass. What the target does NOT establish: collision or preimage resistance of SHA-256 (A-CRYPTO, unchanged by the attachment); and the old tools/run_feed.py driver has since been deleted. W12 feed-durability owns the remaining FNFD envelope/recovery decisions in tools/feed_wire.py and their host adoption; that extension is separate from these trailer theorems.

proofs.title: Prefix and lower-frontier recoverability of a replayed history
proofs.statement: A history that replays successfully leaves an IDLE node whose next txid only moves forward, so dropping its last record leaves a history recoverable at the same frontier, and a history whose txids are all below a bound is recoverable AT that bound. Those are the two facts fn-sf-history-recoverablep needs beyond a successful replay -- together they are fn-replay-advance-okp -- and on them every image the platform may leave in the recovery window is replayable at its own frontier and the host's reopen entry succeeds on it.
proofs.note: Lane w11/bytestore-k2, packet 2. fn-sn-replay-loop-append already gave ok(whole) implies ok(prefix); what was missing, and what blocked lane w10/kernel-freedom's first widening at fn-snt-admissible-crash-image-is-recoverable, is that the prefix node is idle with next-txid at most the frontier. The acknowledged-record half of crash-model-v2 K4 is NOT restated over the wider predicate: on both rollback arms the arm's own (null (fn-sf-successes s)) and a member-equal success hypothesis are contradictory, so the restatement would be fn-sn-acknowledged-record-survives-observed-reopen with two vacuous arms. fn-sf-recovery-admissible-image-facts carries that guarantee over every arm instead. Claimed as PRF-033 before merging dev at 81ae082 and RENUMBERED: w11/clock-seam and w11/workflow-replay had taken 033 and 034, and w11/one-owner 035, while this lane held an older dev. Host tie (books/store-open-bridge.lisp, k4-bridges lane): the cited keystones stay the registry events; fn-cpo-open-observed-is-sn-open-observed-on-the-kernel and fn-cpo-open-observed-succeeds-exactly are the named theorems relating them to fn-cpo-open-observed, which host/store-node-host.lisp:159 and host/owner-host.lisp:193 call. Corollaries (the host's subject, not registry events): fn-sn-recovery-admissible-image-reopens -> fn-sn-recovery-admissible-image-reopens-of-host-open (added hypothesis fn-sob-configured-openp).
proofs.progress_note: Certified over an older digest; `store-node-traces`, `store-observed` are red at their current digest per `green_check` (2026-09-22); T0 re-establishes them.

proofs.title: Checkpoint validation refuses a non-journal prefix
proofs.statement: Checkpoint validation binds a checkpoint to exactly one prefix and refuses a prefix that is not an ordered journal interval below the checkpoint frontier: fn-cpc-validp implies the checkpoint is fn-checkpoint-capture-value of that prefix at its frontier, and a prefix with any record whose recorded generation is not its transaction id is refused for every checkpoint and configuration offered with it.
proofs.progress_note: Certified over an older digest; `checkpoint-codec` are red at their current digest per `green_check` (2026-09-22); T0 re-establishes them. fn-cpc-validp accepted a prefix that fn-checkpoint-capture refuses as :history until 2026-09-21, because fn-replay carries a record generation into the node transitions without comparing it with the txid and validation compared only replay results. The journal-interval clause is now in the recognizer. Open, and not claimed here: fn-cpc-validp has no host caller, so these are properties of a sibling API to the served restore path (host/checkpoint-host.lisp calls fn-checkpoint-restore, which tests the condition itself). `fn-cpc-validp` has no caller; the served restore path is `host/checkpoint-host.lisp` to `fn-checkpoint-restore`; v1 checkpoint adoption.

proofs.title: The BPv7 bundle codec inverts, and what fn authors another implementation accepts
proofs.statement: For every bundle satisfying fn-bpb-bundlep whose encoding is within the caller's transfer bound, fn-bpb-decode of fn-bpb-encode is that same bundle and nothing else (fn-bpb-decode-of-encode), resting on the one-block round trip fn-bpb-decode-block-of-encode-block, the fold over the block sequence fn-bpb-decode-blocks-of-encode-blocks and the primary block's half fn-bpb-scan-primary-of-encode; every accepted input yields a bundle (fn-bpb-decode-yields-bundle) and an input over the bound is refused before any octet is examined (fn-bpb-decode-refuses-overlong-input). Over those, the node's two ends: what fn-bpn-send puts on the wire is a bundle (fn-bpn-send-bundle-is-a-bundle), and a peer that accepts what fn-bpn-send authored recovers exactly the ADU that was sent (fn-bpn-receive-of-send-carries-the-adu), under the receiver's own configuration and transfer limit. The covered scope is a whole bundle with at most *fn-bpb-max-blocks* canonical blocks plus the payload block; fragments, BPSec and status reports are outside it.
proofs.note: Lane w11/bp-node, 2026-09-21; the codec keystones are lane w10/dtn-3's. All seven named theorems are in books/bp-bundle-invariants.lisp and books/bp-node.lisp, both certified (hbox run-20260921T005707Z-8672 and run-20260921T021131Z-1eb0). Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-bundle-tests.lisp and tests/acl2/bp-node-tests.lisp, including the 32-block boundary and the refusal one past it, the three distinct outcomes, and a node configured for a 16-octet transfer refusing a bundle a larger node accepts. The EXTERNAL check is *bpb-dtn7-0-21-0*: 132 octets dtn7-rs 0.21.0 authored, which fn decodes and re-encodes byte for byte (planning/evidence/bp-dtn7-w11-2026-09-21.md). OPEN under this target, and recorded rather than weakened: fn-bpb-decode-blocks-are-canonical-by-construction and fn-bpb-accepted-input-is-canonical-by-construction were REMOVED by w10/dtn-3 after a rewriter runaway with three cures measured and none stopping it, so 'every accepted input re-encodes to itself' is NOT proved for a whole bundle -- it holds of dtn7-rs's captured vector by evaluation only. The native outbound lifecycle now calls fn-bpn-step in books/bp-node-machine.lisp, with source-pinned runtime evidence. This codec target does not cover its persistence, restart or obligation-preservation contracts; PRF-045/046 track those still-open obligations.

proofs.title: Every connection the owner opens carries the operator's AUTHINFO policy, and its greeting says what that policy allows
proofs.statement: fn-served-peer-and-reader-open-under-the-same-policy: the AUTHINFO configuration pinned into a connection the owner resolved to a peer record (fn-served-open-peer) is the same value pinned into a reader connection opened under that policy (fn-served-open), so no decision in books/nntp-auth.lisp -- the credential fn-auth-authinfo searches, the AUTHINFO and STARTTLS labels fn-auth-capability-lines emits, the 480 gate fn-auth-gatedp applies and the posting allowance fn-auth-postingp computes -- can answer one way for a client the owner resolved as a peer and another way for the client beside it. fn-served-open-peer-pins-the-configuration is the field-level half: the pinned value is the argument, coerced by fn-auth-open-session to fn-auth-open-config only when it is not a configuration. fn-auth-step-preserves-the-config is what makes those two statements about the CONNECTION and not only about its open: for any session and any wire event, with no hypothesis at all, the step's session carries the same fn-auth-session-config -- not a login, not the handshake, not a delegated reader command and not a command books/nntp-auth.lisp does not answer writes that field. Every decision in that book reads it, so the policy a client meets on its hundredth command is the one pinned before the connection opened. Covered scope: the OPEN transition for the first two, and one step for the third; the fold over a whole read is OB-AUTH-FOLD's. The subject is what host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open-peer calls through fn-own-open-peer, which tools/run_owner.py Owner.accept_nntp calls for every accepted socket whose source address matches a peer record. Second half, the same value read where a client first sees it: fn-served-open-greets-200-exactly-when-the-connection-may-post says the greeting the open emits is RFC 3977 section 5.1.2's 200 exactly when the pinned injection configuration allows posting AND fn-auth-postingp of the session just built is true -- which is the conjunction fn-auth-command hands fn-nntp-capability-lines for the POST label and the one fn-auth-postingp decides 340 against 440 and 480 by. fn-served-open-greeting-agrees-with-the-post-label states that over the octets a client sees, and is named for what it is: a corollary of the keystone and a local unfold of fn-auth-capability-lines, doing no work of its own. Covered scope: the OPEN transition. It says nothing about the greeting a connection would deserve LATER, after a 281 changes the allowance; RFC 4643 section 2.2 sends the client back to CAPABILITIES for that, and fn-auth-authinfo-is-not-advertised-once-authenticated is the only statement fn has about the block after a login. After the open: fn-auth-step-pinned-login-installs-the-credential-posting-flag says that for any wire event, a step of the host-called fn-auth-step-pinned that takes a session with no subject to one with a subject leaves a posting allowance (fn-auth-postingp) equal to the posting flag of the credential enrolled under the session's cached name; covered scope: one step.
proofs.note: Lane w11/auth-live, decided by measurement and not by inspection. fn-served-open-peer pinned the literal (fn-auth-open-config) while fn-served-open pinned the operator's, and the owner resolves a connection to a peer by SOURCE ADDRESS alone, so on a box where a configured peer is reachable on loopback every client was opened without the operator's policy: AUTHINFO PASS answered 481 with the secret just written, CAPABILITIES carried no AUTHINFO line and POST was never gated. Both theorems are FALSE of that definition. The live before/after is planning/evidence/auth-live-2026-09-21.md and the boundary test is tests/test_auth.py ServedCredentialTests, which starts the node with `bin/fn run` over an fn.toml and writes the peer record, because no test that starts tools/run_owner.py directly can reach this. The greeting half is a second defect the same measurement found: fn-served-greeting read the injection configuration alone, so a connection under [auth] required = true greeted 200 and then answered POST 480, where section 5.1.2's MUST is 201. It takes the opened session now. Lane t7/auth-teeth, 2026-09-22: teeth in tests/acl2/nntp-auth-teeth-tests.lisp. proofs.title: A host fault costs one connection, and the fourth outcome says so
proofs.statement: fn-own-fault (books/owner-fault.lisp) is the owner's host-fault transition. For any owner and any connection id: the faulted connection is no longer found; every connection with a different id is EQUAL to what it was, so every later step over it has the same input it would have had; a submission in flight for the faulted id, and a pending transaction held by it, are cleared, with no hypothesis that the connection was still open, while a submission in flight for a DIFFERENT id is untouched; the store, the committed view and the completion ledger are unchanged; and the octets the faulted connection receives are RFC 3977 section 3.2.1's 403 and are not the reply octets of fn-nntp-post-outcome for any session and any completion, including that function's own malformed-session 403 -- so the fault is a fourth outcome, distinguishable on the wire from accepted, refused and uncertain.
proofs.note: Lane w11/owner-survival. CLAIMED as PRF-035 and renumbered to PRF-040 on merging dev: 035 had already gone to w11/one-owner's frame trailer, 036 to w11/bytestore-k2, 037 to w11/checkpoint-validator, 038 to w11/bp-node and 039 to w11/auth-live, all inside one evening. Keystones fn-own-fault-keeps-every-other-connection, fn-own-fault-clears-the-faulted-submission and fn-own-fault-reply-is-not-a-post-outcome (books/owner-fault.lisp), with fn-own-fault-closes-the-faulted-connection, fn-own-fault-keeps-another-connections-submission, fn-own-fault-releases-the-faulted-transaction and fn-own-fault-is-not-a-store-event beside them. Teeth are evaluated in tests/acl2/owner-tests.lisp on the same witness the served POST scenario builds (*own-taken*: connection 4's submission in flight, reader 3 open), including one violating value per hypothesis and the relation holding after a fault. The host side is tests/test_owner.py OwnerSurvivesAFaultTests, which injects an unexpected exception on one connection and asserts the other is still served. TEETH (tests/acl2/owner-fault-tests.lisp, 2026-09-24): every owner-fault event above has a reachable witness on *own-taken*, and one must-fail per violable hypothesis: fn-own-fault-keeps-every-other-connection 1 (other = id), fn-own-fault-clears-the-faulted-submission 1 (the in-flight submission is another connection's), fn-own-fault-keeps-another-connections-submission 1 (it is the faulted connection's), fn-own-fault-releases-the-faulted-transaction 1 (a reader faults while connection 4 holds the transaction; the review had found no violating value). REDUNDANT HYPOTHESES: the (fn-own-inflight o) hypothesis of fn-own-fault-clears-the-faulted-submission and of fn-own-fault-keeps-another-connections-submission can never be violated usefully -- with nothing in flight the slot stays empty -- and the test book proves both conclusions without it (oft-clears-the-faulted-submission-needs-only-the-id, oft-keeps-another-connections-submission-needs-only-the-id). The statements keep the hypothesis; removing it is a later decision. fn-own-fault-closes-the-faulted-connection, -is-not-a-store-event and -reply-is-not-a-post-outcome have no hypothesis and carry a witness only. EVIDENCE: persvati run-20260924T152544Z-e3c9, manifest planning/evidence/manifests/certify-20260924T152627Z-1775721.json: tests/acl2/owner-fault-tests passed, 4.0 s (books/owner-fault unchanged). OPEN under this target: nothing states that the HOST calls fn-own-fault at every point where it can fault -- the boundary's coverage is a code property, not a theorem -- and tools/run_reader.py has no such boundary at all. Native host calls fn-owner-fault through fnn-owner-serialized/fault-service, but at checkpoint 76901c1 also stops the service for unexpected serious conditions. The logical single-connection theorem does not establish native service survival; that actual-host obligation remains open. Shared-core failure and uncertain persistence require a global fence and are not justified as connection-local faults by this theorem.

proofs.title: Every byte-level crash image of a related store scans, and scans to an image the file kernel admits
proofs.statement: fn-bs-store-crash-image-scans (K1): for every byte store related to a file-kernel state and every image fn-bs-crash-imagep admits of it, the scan tools/run_store.py performs at open -- the config entry and its integrity check, the frontier entry and its decode, the contiguity of the transaction namespace, and the record list -- returns :ok and not any of its four :fault values. No trailer assumption is used: an authority inode is fenced before any name points at it (D1) and is never overwritten (D2), so the only freedom a crash has over the authority namespace is whether the last entry operation landed. fn-bs-store-crash-image-is-kernel-admissible (K2): what that scan reads is an image fn-sf-recovery-crash-imagep admits, which outside the recovery window is the reliance predicate fn-sf-crash-imagep and inside it is that plus the two rollback arms of D14-b and D14-c -- the record the replay read and has not re-fenced, and the allocator rename that the fourth recovery barrier has not drained. fn-bs-store-recovery-is-a-kernel-crash (K3): fn-sf-image-crash at that image reproduces its frontier, its record list and the :replaying phase. fn-bs-crash-image-consumer-replay-ok: from the maintained E2 completed-prefix relation fn-csi-full-relationp, K2 and the platform crash-image arms, the exact scanned record list strictly replays the consumer projection, including recovery rollback. fn-bs-crash-image-reopens: the host reopen entry fn-sn-open-observed succeeds on every such image whose identity and topic histories replay (fn-sn-observed-identity-okp and fn-sn-observed-topic-okp), with E2 consumer replay derived rather than assumed. fn-bs-acknowledged-record-survives-byte-crash (K4): under the same maintained and observed conditions, an acknowledged outcome names a reopened record. K-sweep: fn-bs-staging-unlink-keeps-relation-and-scan, an unlink in :staging at any name and with any outcome keeps the byte relation to the same kernel state and keeps the scan; fn-bs-recover-sweep-keeps-relation-at-every-cut, every pair of fn-bs-recover-sweep-program's run (every recovery-stage-unlinked cut) is that kernel state with a related byte state and the original scan; fn-bs-sweep-round-keeps-every-cut-reopenable, over the names fn-sn-sweep-round returns (host/native/io.lisp fnn-sweep-staging via fn-store-sn-sweep-round), every identity- and topic-replayable crash image at every cut of the sweep reopens and the kernel state is the one before the sweep. The sweep's rounds (books/store-sweep.lisp): fn-sn-sweep-rounds-collect-every-orphan, with the kernel gate open and a positive observation bound, a staging directory of N unheld staging names ends :done and empty for every N; fn-sn-sweep-rounds-keep-every-name-they-may-not-remove; fn-sn-sweep-rounds-end-done-or-refused, the loop ends :done or :refused and :refused means more than one observation of names remains and that observation removes nothing. K5 scan-record form: fn-bs-stable-prefix-retained-by-byte-crash, under the same byte/kernel relation and modeled crash-image premise, retains the durable decoded record list as a prefix and bounds the scanned list to at most one additional record. K6 partial raw-frame form: fn-bs-k6-actual-record-linked-input-has-exact-frame proves that a well-formed byte state, ACL2-valid record input, fresh staging key, and absent final name at the file-fence cut make the actual P-RECORD linked cut point that final name at the new fenced inode containing the complete supplied frame; the modeled surviving-name crash image at both the actual linked and record-attempted cuts now reads exact raw octets and the decoder returns the candidate; the related-input trace derives no-prior-operation and final-name absence at the file cut for typed Store events; the actual pair-10 whole-list scanner result is now proved conditionally on relation of that pair, while universal relation preservation remains K0. Under a related ready byte/owner input, typed successor frontier frame and fresh staging name, the actual failed P-FRONTIER pair 12 of fn-bs-run is an EIO byte cut for each modeled pending-root-entry choice; the host-called configured-owner :store/:io error observation fences the Store projection while retaining fn-bs-store-relation. The :apply choice makes the candidate durable, while :drop keeps the old frontier. The actual configured-owner retention prepare event, built from the live owner sequence and txid plus host text octets, stages that exact event on the prepared branch and leaves a reserved Store unstaged on refusal. Served-entry byte relation and physical filesystem qualification remain separate obligations.
proofs.note: K1/K2 in byte-store-scan and K3/K4 in byte-store-keystones concern every modeled crash image of an already related byte/kernel state. The reopen subject is fn-sn-open-observed, called by host/store-node-host.lisp; native process startup reaches that entry through its wrapper. K4 additionally assumes maintained consumer completed-prefix consistency and observed identity and topic replay. The topic condition is not yet derived for every modeled byte crash image by the maintained Store relation; a valid physical FNST topic-anchor image after consumer bootstrap separates it from identity and consumer replay. Its recovery-window instances are vacuous because there are no current-process successes there; fn-bs-crash-image-reopens covers that window without a success premise. The identity condition has a kernel witness; its distinct byte-level premise witness remains missing. Framed metadata, a nonempty bootstrap/publication trace and a physically framed registration-before-bootstrap counterexample exercise the other composition boundaries. proofs.title: The inbound transit decision the served path reaches is the model's, over the node the owner holds now (K2 loop, K3 duplicate)
proofs.statement: fn-peer-loop-is-refused: an article whose Path already names this node's path-identity is never accepted through transit, and fn-peer-transfer leaves the node. fn-peer-history-is-have-at-offer and fn-peer-history-is-refused-at-transfer: a Message-ID in the history is :have :history at the offer and is never accepted at the transfer. The subject rule (AGENTS.md rule 1) is closed in two halves: fn-peer-ihave-of-a-held-message-id-is-435-and-no-article and fn-peer-check-of-a-held-message-id-is-438-and-no-offer-outstanding say the reply octets fn-peer-command emits ARE that decision and that the connection does not enter article mode, and fn-own-read-offers-against-the-live-node says the node the served path supplies is fn-sn-node of the owner's own store. The host line is host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at -> books/owner.lisp fn-own-read for the offer, and host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-decide -> fn-peer-decide-transfer for the transfer. Covered scope: one connection's offer and one article's transfer against one node and one pinned peer record; the hypotheses are the connection facts the decision needs before it reaches its history arm. NOT covered: the peer record is still the one the connection opened with, so a (:set-peer ...) delta reaches the transfer decision and not the offer decision; and fn-peer-decide-transfer emits no :date-future or :no-clock, because the tree has no certified RFC 5322 date-time reader. EXTENSION (lane friend-blockers, 2026-09-27, the stranger rehearsal's stops): PKT-711: KEYSTONE fn-peer-full-store-is-a-retry-code: a full Store's :unaffordable answers IHAVE and TAKETHIS 436 (retry class), never 437/439; IHAVE's line names the reason.
