proofs.title: A control article is filed only in control.<verb>, or refused, over the filing plan every ingress calls
proofs.statement: fn-ctl-control-article-is-filed-only-in-control: for every received octet string that fn-ctl-classify-octets classifies (:control VERB ARGS), fn-pa-filing-plan RECEIVED GROUPS DOMAIN (books/peer-authored-accept.lisp; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-control-filing-buffer calls its buffer twin (books/article-buffer.lisp fn-ars-filing-plan-is-reference) and host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-filled calls that first, for served POST, bound submission, NNTP transit and BP transit, and host/native/hybrid-control.lisp fnn-hybrid-control-author calls fn-owner-control-filing itself for the local signed-author path) either files the article in exactly one group, its filing group fn-ctl-filing-group VERB, which is "control" or begins "control." and is a member of DOMAIN, or refuses it :control-not-filed; the ingress's own GROUPS (the names its Newsgroups field gave) are never the answer unless they are that group. fn-ctl-classify-reads-only-the-control-field: inserting any field F whose name is neither control nor supersedes anywhere in a field list leaves fn-ctl-classify-fields unchanged. fn-ctl-cmsg-subject-is-ordinary: an article whose parsed fields have no Control field is filed in GROUPS unchanged by fn-pa-filing-plan, whatever its Subject, Newsgroups or Also-Control. Covered scope: the filing decision; the host's use of the filed groups is a transcribed stub test (tests/native_peer_authored_accept_raw.lisp) and the native cases of the evidence file. A signed control article is filed the same way (the :control-signed refusal was removed 2026-09-25 by lane control-c3 when the signed record binding came to name the filing group; PRF-084).
proofs.progress_note: Lane control-c1 (2026-09-25), packet C1 of planning/design-2026-09-25-control-messages.md. Teeth in tests/acl2/control-tests.lisp: reachable witnesses (a cancel naming fn.test with control.cancel configured is filed in control.cancel; without it, refused; a cmsg Subject article and a .ctl/Also-Control article keep fn.test), must-fail per hypothesis (an ordinary article is filed outside control; a Control field or a Supersedes field inserted changes the classification; a signed control article is not filed). 2026-09-25 (control-c3): the signed record binding names the filing group, so a signed control article is filed; fn-ctl-unsigned-control-filing-by-definition became fn-ctl-control-filing-by-definition without its carrier hypothesis.

proofs.title: A held bundle is offered only to the routed hop, over the step the host calls; unrouted bundles stay held and are reported; the decision is deterministic in the table
proofs.statement: fn-bpnp-step-offers-only-the-routed-hop: for a routed :session event (:session PEER S t MRU OBS (:via HOP ANNOUNCED TABLE)) to fn-bpnp-step (host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-foundation-step, from host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bpnode-forward-session), a :persist-attempt effect is for the row the arrival-order scan chose, and fn-bprt-next-hop of that row's own destination EID text over TABLE and live set (HOP) is HOP, the route fn-bprt-hop-route is a member of TABLE whose pattern matches the destination and whose boundary is HOP, and ANNOUNCED is the octets of that route's enrolled EID. fn-bpnp-step-unrouted-bundle-stays-held-and-is-reported: if the issued operation is not uncertain, no row the table routes to HOP is ready, the scan over every held row is ready and no route in TABLE matches that row's destination, the step's only effect is (:forward-no-route ARRIVAL HOP :no-route) and the held list is unchanged. fn-bprt-next-hop-deterministic-in-the-table: two tables whose routes matching DEST are the same set give DEST the same answer. fn-bprt-next-hop-names-a-live-matching-route: a boundary answer is the boundary of a live matching route in the table. Covered scope: the 7-field routed :session arm and the :resume arm with VIA scan only the rows the table routes to HOP (PRF-103); a :session open or :resume without VIA offers nothing; LIVE is the single session's hop.
proofs.progress_note: Lane bp-routing (2026-09-25). Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-route-tests.lisp: a reachable witness (the bp-node-forward-retry fixture's held transit to dtn://bp-dest/, routed to relay, proposes the attempt) and must-fail cases for an unlisted hop, a wrong announced EID, a prefix route to another boundary, the route present (no report), and tables whose matching sets differ.

proofs.title: Bounds join: an article the profile admits is a record it publishes; the group-name ceiling is the label width; a refused operator article names the profile bound
proofs.statement: fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record (books/byte-store-frame.lisp): under a profile a store runs under (fn-bs-profile-admittedp), every record whose payload is at most the article field A and whose group count is at most G encodes (fn-record-encode) to at most the record field R; it rests on fn-record-encode-length-bound and the validity relation R >= fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling A G (:max-record-octets-below-the-article-record in fn-bs-profile-validp, which the host calls through fn-bs-profile-init-verdict, host/store-host.lisp:385, fn-profile-upgrade-verdict, :429, and fn-bs-profile-admittedp at install, host/owner-host.lisp:219). The format-7 translation takes G and the group name at the codec ceilings and R as the larger of H/T and the article record of (A, G). fn-cfg-labelp-of-record-group-name (books/config.lisp): every group name the record codec admits is a configuration label, the one statement relating *fn-record-max-group-name* and *fn-cfg-max-label*. fn-native-control-refusal-status-is-a-refusal (books/native-control.lisp): the control word for a refused operator submission (:article-exceeds-profile-bound for the injection reason :oversize, else :refused) is in the FNCT reply vocabulary and of class refused; host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-control-submit-serialized calls it through fn-native-control-host-refusal-status. Covered scope: record encodings under a valid profile; the frame :blob width (131,072) and the owner's per-octet recursion at take are not covered.
proofs.progress_note: Lane bounds-join (2026-09-25). Teeth in tests/acl2/byte-store-frame-tests.lisp: a tight witness (R equal to the article record of its (A, G)); one refusal by name per argument of the relation; a concrete counterexample per hypothesis (a non-profile reads R = 0 while an empty record encodes to 70 octets; 196,609 payload octets in one group; six 256-octet groups at A). config-tests: a 256-octet group name is a 256-octet label; a 257-octet string is not a label. native-control-tests: the named status survives the sealed reply and exits 1; :uncertain and :fault are not refusals.

proofs.title: BP journal rotation: recovery from a selected held-row checkpoint equals recovery over the whole history, and every publication cut leaves one authority
proofs.statement: fn-bpnr-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover (restated for N16-F1, lane bp-n16-prod): for every authority plan0 that is not damaged, whose ordered received-final rows replay :ready, the projection ck1 of that replay (a checkpoint), E the epoch field of the recovery event over plan0 and the rows, and the file of the checkpoint the rotation publishes, fn-bpnr-rotation-checkpoint ck1 E (operation frontier (E . 0), the rotation's own id; what fn-bpnp-rotate-step's effect carries and host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-publish-generation writes): fn-bpnr-recover-auto-event (the event fnn-bps-open passes to fn-bpnp-step) over that file with no later rows names epoch E + 1 with the old replay at frontier (E . 0) and row count 0, so no operation after the reopen reuses the rotation's id; over later rows that start after (E . 0) it equals the event over plan0 and the concatenated rows with field 5 set to the later rows' count. fn-bpnr-rotation-crash-recovers-old-or-new: at every phase of the publication driver fn-bpnr-publish-action/-step/-outcome (followed by fnn-bps-publish-generation) and for either outcome of an atomic rename, the visible selection file is the old or the new one, before the rename may have been issued it is the old one, and under the new one recovery with no rows is the reopen event above. fn-bpnp-rotate-step-proposes-only-own-projection: a proposal carries fn-bpnr-rotation-checkpoint of the state's own projection, from a quiescent state, and its file exists. fn-bpnr-retirement-cut-keeps-open-view: when the root's selection file selects G and no other name the open reads is retired, the open's view (selection plan, selected directory, the other names) after any prefix of fn-bpnr-retire-ops (the removal program host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-retire-generations runs step by step: older generation directories and killed rotations' staged selections) equals the view before it; fn-bpnr-retired-names-never-the-selected-directory. fn-bpnr-checkpoint-decode-of-octets: every file fn-bpnr-checkpoint-octets writes decodes to its checkpoint. Covered scope: one atomically renamed kind-19 file; the chunked kinds 19 plus a manifest kind, the :quiesce event and the empty new-generation premise are not modelled; the removal model is a name-to-entry alist, not K0's byte store; the codec runs on octet lists (no D27 concrete twin); a killed rotation's unselected new-generation directory is kept (never reused). Natural rotation (lane bp-rotation, 2026-09-27; books/bp-node-rotation-due.lisp): host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bps-rotate-when-due, called at the open of bp-node serve and dispatch (fnn-bps-open-node), drives fn-bpnrd-due-rotation-event's answer. fn-bpnrd-due-rotation-event-by-definition: it answers (:rotate G CK) exactly when the profile is a profile 3, the recovered generation's record count has reached its rotation threshold and the state is quiescent, with G above the selected generation and CK the checkpoint of the open's recovery event (the event `bp-node checkpoint` drives). fn-bpnrd-due-rotation-preserves-recovery: when the open drove the host's recovery event (fn-bpnr-recover-auto-event over ROWS0 and a non-damaged PLAN0 whose replay is :ready, with a clock-domain decision appended), the machine state is at that event's epoch E, and fn-bpnp-rotate-step proposes the due event's publication, the published checkpoint read back at the machine's depth budget recovers with no later rows epoch E + 1 with the old replay at frontier (E . 0) and row count 0, and over later rows that start after (E . 0) the event over PLAN0 and the concatenated rows with field 5 set to their count. The state/epoch premise is a hypothesis (the recovery arm's installation of the epoch is not restated). The publication and retirement programs are the operator rotation's, so the crash and retirement keystones above cover every cut of it. In-serve rotation (lane bp-retention-leftovers): host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bps-serve-rotate-when-due asks fn-bpnrd-serve-rotation-due-p between sessions (threshold reached at a safe point: nothing issued, no pending image, no outbound session), recovers in place under the locks the serve holds (host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-reopen-in-place), drives the open-time decision's rotation and reopens in place. KEYSTONE fn-bpnrd-rotation-keeps-every-held-family: for every state the machine rotates from, a proposed publication's file reopens (no rows) :ready with exactly that state's held rows, handoffs and arrival frontier at frontier (E . 0).
proofs.progress_note: Lane n16-rotation (2026-09-25), spec bp-node-machine 3.6 slice E, trace N16. Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-node-counterexamples-tests: the positive trace through fn-bpnp-step, must-fails for a damaged plan0, absent octets and an unready prefix (recovery keystone) and a visible new file before the rename (crash keystone). Certified in hbox runs run-20260925T044146Z-230d, run-20260925T050214Z-702e and run-20260925T051528Z-15c2. Lane bp-n16-prod (2026-09-25): N16-F1 repaired (the published checkpoint's frontier is the rotation's own id; the recovery keystone restated with the event's epoch), and old generations retired by an ACL2 program whose every prefix is a model crash point; teeth in tests/acl2/bp-node-counterexamples-tests (N16 section, over real kind-5 rows) and tests/acl2/bp-node-retire-tests. Lane bp-rotation (2026-09-27, F7): natural rotation by a profile threshold at a node verb's open; teeth in tests/acl2/bp-node-rotation-due-tests (reachable witness over N16's real rows through fn-bpnp-step with a clock-domain decision; must-fails for later rows at the rotation's id, and corrupted-state witnesses for the publication and epoch premises); tests/test_bp_fragment_node_native's rotation test runs on production and developer images with no developer cut.

proofs.title: Open from an exact-state Store checkpoint equals the full open
proofs.statement: fn-sn-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover: for every configuration history, frontier, record prefix P and suffix Q, (fn-sco-open (fn-sco-capture configs P) configs frontier Q) equals (fn-cpo-open-observed configs frontier (append P Q)), with no hypothesis; fn-sco-open is what the host calls at open when a checkpoint verified (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-recover-from-checkpoint) and fn-cpo-open-observed is the full open (fn-store-sn-recover). Built from one append lemma per fold of fn-cpo-open-observed: fn-cpr-loop-append (configuration and node fold, paused at the prefix end), fn-replay-identity-append (and fn-replay-identity-append-of-true-lists, which asks only true lists: the fault is sticky), fn-cpe-projection-replay-append, fn-th-prefix-project-append, fn-cei-build-append; the history recognizer runs over the carried record list. fn-sco-extend-of-capture (one hypothesis, a true-list suffix): the next checkpoint is the extension. fn-sco-capture-of-later-configs: a configuration whose txid is above every covered record does not change the capture. fn-scc-decode-segments-of-segments: the FNSC segments decode to the value, for every tree whose program and record count fit the u64 header fields. fn-bs-scp-program-crash-is-old-or-new: at every cut of the publish program the checkpoint name is the old file, absent, or the new octets. fn-bs-read-ranges-concatenate: consecutive range reads concatenate under A-HOST-EXCLUSIVE-READ. Owner (2026-09-25, lane owner-checkpoint-open): fn-owner-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover, with no hypothesis: the owner fn-ock-recover-extended installs from (fn-sco-extend (fn-sco-capture configs P) configs Q) is the owner fn-ock-recover-full installs from the full open of P ++ Q (the composition fn-orec-recover-installs-ocl-relation is stated over: the Store open, the configuration replay, fn-own-start's archive, views, trie and ledger, fn-own-configure, fn-ocfg-make) or :fault on both; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-recover-extended calls fn-ock-recover-extended on both paths (fn-owner-recover-from-checkpoint over the decoded checkpoint and the suffix, fn-owner-recover over the empty capture and the whole history, fn-ock-recover-from-empty-capture-is-full). fn-ock-recover-installs-ocl-relation carries fn-ocl-relation and fn-scar-view-indexedp to what is installed on either path. Publication: fn-ock-next-checkpoint-is-the-capture (no hypothesis: a record that is not a Store event faults the identity fold stickily, fn-replay-identity-append-of-true-lists, so the extension over a prefix holding one is still the capture; the admitted-history hypothesis was proved redundant, PKT-192) and fn-ock-published-checkpoint-opens-to-the-full-open: what the owner publishes is the capture of its whole history and opens, over any later records, to the full open; fn-ock-not-due-keeps-the-checkpoint-open: until fn-ock-publication-duep (twice the suffix reaches K) the durable checkpoint is the one a restart selects. Replay carries the node invariant: fn-cpr-apply-event-preserves-cnode-statep (no hypothesis beyond non-refusal) and fn-cpr-loop-preserves-cnode-statep; fn-cpr-apply-event and fn-cpr-loop test a refusal by NIL on the executable path. Recovery-lag policy (2026-09-26, lane checkpoint-pipeline-5, PKT-583 (b), gpt-6's review section 2): fn-ock-publication-next (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-sco-due) decides :due, :idle, :blocked, :inflight or :coalesce; fn-ock-one-publication-in-flight: while one publication is in flight (the count it captured) the decision is never :due and the rule's observation is the one coalesced request; fn-ock-publication-next-decides-by-the-rule: with nothing in flight it is fn-ock-publication-duep at the frontier given unless a recorded deferral blocks; fn-ock-finish-binds-the-captured-prefix: the next checkpoint's sequence is the count the capture was handed (fn-owner-sco-publication-done records it as the durable S, never the count at the finish); fn-ock-fast-path-within-k-by-definition: K is the fast path's threshold at fn-sco-select, the full replay past it (the honest fallback; not a guaranteed maximum suffix). RECORDS FLIP (lanes checkpoint-arena, checkpoint-arena-2, 2026-09-27; books/store-checkpoint-arena.lisp, -load.lisp, -writer.lisp): the file carries the ARENA run first (the canonical payloads, batched, framed and chained like every run), then the four tables of the capture of the CANONICAL rows. fn-intern-events-is-intern-at (no hypothesis) and fn-intern-events-arena-is-payloads (the intern not refused, the arena a true list): the open's intern is the counter intern fn-scka-intern-at and its arena the canonical payloads. fn-scka-load-of-written-file: a plan whose segments are the arena run of PS followed by the tables' runs of the capture of RECORDS loads (fn-scka-load: fn-scka-open-run, the host's fn-scka-seal-n calls, which are one loop by fn-scka-seal-n-compose, fn-scka-finish) to those tables with the arena exactly PS. fn-scka-recover-from-checkpoint-is-full-recover (hypothesis: the whole history interns): from the capture of a prefix's canonical rows and its canonical arena, the recover over the suffix is the full recover of the whole history from the emptied arena, extension and arena; fn-scka-recover-rows-rii-is-recover-rows: the composition the host runs (fn-intern-events, then fn-rii-sco-extend) is that recover. fn-scka-write-run-is-run-segments (hypothesis: the batches sum to the payload count): the octets of the host's arena-run steps (fn-scka-write-step) are the run segments of the live rows' canonical payloads, for any buffer contents. fn-scka-next-checkpoint-is-capture: the owner's next checkpoint (its base extended over the canonical rows of the rows after it, handles from the base's payload count) is the capture of the canonical rows of all of them.
proofs.progress_note: Open items: K0 coverage of the publish program's :root rename and :root fsync (fn-bs-k0-step-inputp admits neither; the profile program has the same gap); the whole-file statement over the host's range loop; the publication keystone's history hypothesis has no must-fail (the identity fold's fault is absorbing); the pack, compaction and export verbs still re-encode the covered prefix's octets after a checkpoint open (fn-store-sco-prefix-octets; the owner's open no longer does, checkpoint-arena-2) and the Store open and the owner open each replay the suffix.

proofs.title: Control authority requires a verified principal and a covering grant; a withdrawal record is decided once and serves no view that holds its cancel
proofs.statement: fn-ctl-authorize-requires-verified-verdict: an :execute from fn-ctl-authorize VERDICT VERB GROUPS ROWS (books/control-authority.lisp) has verdict token :verified with a 32-octet principal. fn-ctl-authorize-requires-a-covering-grant: under :execute, for every GROUP of GROUPS, fn-ctl-covering-row is a member of ROWS whose principal is the verified one, whose verb is VERB and whose namespace pattern covers GROUP. fn-cfg-grant-control-admissible-iff: fn-cfg-delta-reason admits (fn-cfg-grant-control NS P VERB) iff NS is a namespace pattern, P 64 lowercase hex characters and VERB is cancel. fn-ctl-revoke-changes-decisions-not-records: when every cancel entry's txid is below the first appended configuration record's, fn-ctl-journal-withdrawals ENTRIES (append CONFIGS MORE) equals fn-ctl-journal-withdrawals ENTRIES CONFIGS. fn-ctl-cancel-executes-only-for-author-or-authority: a withdrawing fn-ctl-withdrawal-effect W T-GROUPS T-VERDICT means the target's verdict names W's principal, or W's scope is nonempty and covers every one of the nonempty T-GROUPS. fn-ctl-target-is-never-visible-beside-its-cancel: an article targeted by a record of WS whose cause is among ARTICLES and whose effect withdraws is not in fn-ctl-visible-articles ARTICLES WS VERDICTS. fn-ctl-pinned-view-keeps-its-archive: a record whose cause is absent from ARTICLES leaves the visible articles unchanged. fn-ctl-visible-is-arrival-order-independent: (T C . REST) and (C T . REST) serve the same articles. fn-hsig-signed-control-record-lists-its-filing-group: fn-hsig-carried-record-metadatap SOURCE RECEIVED RECORD (books/hybrid-store.lisp; a conjunct of the schema-1 and carried replay bindings replay's identity step calls, and required by the native constructor fn-hsig-authorized-carried-submission-event-base that host/native/hybrid-control.lisp and host/native/owner.lisp reach) with SOURCE classified (:control VERB ARGS) implies the record lists exactly (fn-ctl-filing-group VERB). fn-hsig-malformed-control-binds-no-record: a source classified :malformed binds no record. fn-ctl-visible-add-is-visible and fn-ctl-visible-extend-is-visible (books/control-visible.lisp): when the carried list equals fn-ctl-visible-articles OLD WS VERDICTS, the incremental list after one new article (resp. a batch DELTA) equals fn-ctl-visible-articles of (A . OLD) (resp. (append DELTA OLD)); an ordinary article costs one pass over WS, an executed cancel one pass over the visible list. fn-ctl-refresh-visible-is-visible (books/control-visible.lisp; called by fn-own-refresh, books/owner.lisp, which every owner step at an idle store runs): when the carried visible list equals fn-ctl-visible-articles OLD WS OLD-VERDICTS and NEW has distinct Message-IDs, fn-ctl-refresh-visible NEW OLD OLD-VISIBLE WS2 OLD-VERDICTS VERDICTS equals fn-ctl-visible-articles NEW WS2 VERDICTS, WS2 being fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawals NEW OLD WS VERDICTS RECORDS CONFIGS (the records fn-ctl-withdrawal-plan decides for each cancel or superseding article the refresh first publishes, under fn-ctl-config-at of that article's own acceptance-record txid in the Store records RECORDS over the configuration journal CONFIGS). fn-ctl-articles-withdrawals-is-the-journal: the rebuild the refresh runs at a discontinuity (start, reopen) equals fn-ctl-journal-withdrawals over the archive's entries (TXID CAUSE VERDICT TARGET). fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawals-is-the-journal (called by fn-own-refresh with the Store's records and fn-sn-config-history): when the carried records are the journal of the old archive under the old Store records R0, verdicts V0 and configuration journal C0, every withdrawing article of the old archive has its acceptance record in R0, the verdicts grew by at most one pair for a Message-ID outside the old archive, and the configuration records appended since carry txids above every old entry, the refresh's records over the grown inputs are the journal of the new archive under them: the live decision is recovery's. fn-ctl-withdrawal-plan-record-is-bound: a record names its cause, its target (a cancel argument or a Supersedes field, fn-ctl-article-target), the verified principal, the principal's cancel grants and the generation. fn-ctl-visible-state-statep: the visible state of an acceptance state is one. Supporting (not registry events; teeth are the owner tests' relation witnesses): fn-own-refresh-preserves-relation and fn-own-conn-serves-a-projection (books/owner-invariants.lisp), the restated K1 holds after every refresh; the committed view's archive is fn-ctl-visible-state of its prefix under the records and verdicts it carries, and a connection's archive is that prefix's state with a subsequence of its articles. Covered scope: the served view and every connection pinned after a withdrawing article's refresh, records decided at each article's own txid live and at recovery alike, Supersedes under the cancel's rules. Served answers (control-c3e; subject fn-nntp-archive-command-pinned, books/nntp.lisp, reached from fn-own-read through fn-served-step and fn-served-dispatch; the control pin is the fourth slot of the group pin, the owner connection's fn-own-conn-control set from fn-own-view-control at open and advance): fn-nntp-423-withdrawn-is-a-withdrawn-holder, when the pin's withdrawn list is fn-ctl-withdrawn-articles RAW WS VERDICTS, a `423 withdrawn' answer names an article of RAW holding the number that the view does not serve and the pinned archive holds nothing at that number; fn-nntp-withdrawn-holder-answers-423-withdrawn, the converse for ARTICLE/HEAD/BODY/STAT with one number argument and a selected group; fn-nntp-430-withdrawn-is-a-withdrawn-article and fn-nntp-withdrawn-article-answers-430-withdrawn, the same by Message-ID under the pinned trie's correspondence with the archive; fn-nntp-hdr-fn-control-is-the-status, `HDR :fn-control <msgid>' answers one line whose item is fn-ctl-control-item of fn-ctl-control-status (the kernel, over the trie by fn-ctl-served-status-is-control-status) of the article with that Message-ID, served or withdrawn, or 430, or 503 when the item would not be a clean field; fn-nntp-hdr-fn-control-executed-means-withdrawn, an executed status names a target RAW holds and the view does not serve, withdrawn by the record the article caused. fn-own-read-archive-command-is-the-pinned-dispatcher (books/owner-control-read.lisp; host line host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at): one read framing one archive command line answers that dispatcher's reply over the connection's archive, trie, buckets and control pin whenever the reply offers no article; fn-own-related-conn-control: under fn-own-relation a connection's control pin has W = fn-ctl-withdrawn-articles of its pinned prefix under the pinned records and its archive serves that prefix's visible list (fn-own-control-okp in fn-own-conn-okp; the view carries W = fn-ctl-subseq-diff of its raw and visible lists, refreshed by fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawn). Kernel (books/control-served.lisp): fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawn-is-withdrawn (now for any RAW), fn-ctl-number-withdrawn-is-a-withdrawn-holder, fn-ctl-msgid-withdrawn-is-a-withdrawn-article, fn-ctl-executed-status-means-withdrawn, fn-ctl-owed-status-means-not-held. Not covered: the owner-level lift has no teeth book yet (no reachable owner witness nor must-fail per hypothesis for fn-own-read-archive-command-is-the-pinned-dispatcher); the owner relation does not carry the journal equality nor the configuration-txid fact it rests on (records appended later have larger txids); the txid lookup walks the Store records (no Message-ID-to-txid index); a view with an empty group index pins no control, so it answers the plain 423/430 (a view serving no article). PKT-575 (PRF-256): fn-ctl-cancel-executes-only-for-author-or-authority gains the disjunct `the record's principal is :node` (the operator's withdrawal). After the records flip (flip-L8-2) the refresh reads a withdrawing article's target and Cancel-Key entries from its row's control fact in the Store's history (fn-ctl-article-plan; fn-hf-control-of-held-facts-of and fn-ctl-control-of-fields: the fact is the readers over the row's bytes), and fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawals-is-the-journal's hypotheses are: the carried records are the journal of the old archive, the verdicts grew by at most one pair for a Message-ID outside it, no configuration record was appended or every appended one comes after every entry, and the history grew by the new article's rows only (fn-ctl-history-grows-by-p); records made before their target arrived are resolved to its locks by the refresh (fn-ctl-resolve-tlocks), as recovery reads them. proofs.title: Owed receipts leave from bp-node serve: the contact offers exactly the queued receipt job on its route
proofs.statement: fn-bpnp-receipt-contact-offers-the-queued-job: over the called fn-bpnp-step on (:base E), where E is fn-bpnp-receipt-contact-event of the node state and the peer (the event host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bpnode-send-receipts asks for after each fnn-bpnode-queue-outboxes in bp-node serve), for a well-formed base, a non-nil event and a journal token below *fn-bpn-machine-max-records*, the one effect persists the :attempting record of the first :queued job for that peer and the pending success effect is that job's :cl-send with its route, peer, key and wire. fn-bpnp-receipt-contact-event-needs-a-queued-job: the event is non-nil exactly when the peer is an EID, nothing is issued, no delivery is uncertain, the base is neither fenced nor pending and a :queued job for the peer exists. fn-bpnp-uncertain-receipt-transfer-keeps-the-job-owed and fn-bpnp-receipt-reoffer-after-uncertain (spec 4.3.2): an uncertain base transfer is connection-local; over the called fn-bpnp-step it proposes only the durable :requeued :uncertain record, keeps the job :attempting until that is durable, fences nothing and emits no release, receipt-prepare or :forwarded; once durable the job is :queued again with its own identity and the receipt contact event opens for its peer again. Only an uncertain publication fences. Covered scope: the decision, the offer and the uncertain transfer's outcome; a connect that produces no socket reads :failed and requeues the same way. The host's exit scope (serve and dispatch continue; bp-contact tick answers exit 3) is host reporting over these effects. Open: 'offered once per contact' is not an ACL2 statement over the host loop (fnn-bpc-drive-contact stops at the first transfer or outcome that is not :accepted and the durable :attempting record takes the job out of :queued; the latter is witnessed in the test book, not proved over a driver).

proofs.title: The running owner's status report is the offline report of the same state, and its pages join to it
proofs.statement: fn-nls-live-report-is-the-offline-report: for every KIND (status, pins, peers, obligations), profile, configured owner OC and observation, when the carried octet sum CACHE is valid for the records of OC's Store (fn-sbud-octets-cache-validp) and no connection is open (no pin in fn-ocfg-pins), (fn-nls-live-report kind profile oc cache obs) equals (fn-nls-offline-report kind profile (fn-own-store (fn-ocfg-owner oc)) (fn-ocfg-config oc) obs); the owner reaches fn-nls-live-report through fn-native-live-status-host-answer (host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-status-answer), once per request and the offline command reaches fn-nls-offline-report through fn-native-live-status-host-offline (host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-live-report). fn-nls-client-step-of-owner-reply: for every octet REPORT whose length is a uint32 and every client prefix ACC of it (with, past the first page, the report's total and digest), the client's step on the owner's page from (len ACC) is :done REPORT, or :next with the strictly longer prefix of one more chunk; fnn-control-live-status folds pages through fn-nls-client-step. fn-nls-page-of-buffer-is-reply: for every REPORT and OFFSET, (fn-nls-page (fn-nls-buffer report) offset) equals (fn-nls-reply report offset), with no hypothesis; fn-nls-buffer is the report as one string with its frame digest and fn-nls-page answers a substring of it (the D27 twin of the page). fn-nls-client-step-of-owner-page: the client-step keystone with the same hypotheses over the page the owner answers, (fn-nls-page (fn-nls-buffer report) (len acc)). fn-nls-cached-buffer-of-put: for a positive offset, the buffer the owner looks up for KIND after storing BUFFER for KIND is BUFFER; fn-native-live-status-host-answer renders anew at offset 0 and otherwise pages from the stored buffer. fn-nls-nat-is-the-decimal-digits: for every natural N, (fn-nls-nat N), which renders every number of the report, is a nonempty run of decimal digits whose value under fn-nntp-decimal-value is N. Supporting: fn-nls-reply-decode-of-encode, fn-nls-request-decode-of-encode, fn-nls-open-of-seal. fn-nls-report-of-query-kind-is-query-report: for every administrative plan, the status-path report of the kind fn-native-admin-result-report-kind names -- the kind host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-execute-admin passes to fnn-operator-status-once for an accepted `peer list' or `control list', live (fn-nls-live-report) or offline (fn-nls-offline-report) -- is fn-nls-query-report of the plan over the same configuration (fn-native-admin-query-report, or books/account-list.lisp fn-acct-kinds-list-report for `account list'), so `control list' renders the authority rows (fn-cfg-authorities), `peer list' the peers and `account list' the accounts slot; supporting: fn-native-admin-control-report-empty-iff-no-rows (the listing is empty only over no grant row). Covered scope: the rows are rendered, not parsed back (qual-e747dbcc A3).
proofs.progress_note: Answering changes no state by signature (the host wrappers return one value and no state), not by a theorem. The multi-page join trusts the frame digest to name one report (A-CRYPTO): a report that changes between pages restarts the join, at most 8 times. The owner pages from a string buffer rendered once per request (fn-nls-page); the renderer and the FNLS frames are still octet lists (their D27 twin is open). The open= line names each process's own open, the offline orphan listing is the reader's own observation, and the checkpoint-file line is each answering process's lstat at the request. The words (the history-marker word, checkpoint-file, open-cost) are tests, not theorems; the live and offline reports share them through fn-nls-report. Q10c source continuation: consumer show selects the consumer-only report, with FNLS plain code 13. Clean scoped source roots passed native-live-status-tests 153/153 and control-evidence-tests 84/84, including the plan/report and any-request roundtrip teeth. Matching native consumer-identity module and committed certification remain runner-owned.

proofs.statement: On every Store event (fn-store-event-p), fn-evc-field-by-shape at 0, 1 and 2 equals fn-store-event-sequence, -txid and -generation, and fn-evc-class-by-shape names exactly the recognizer that holds (fn-record-p, fn-store-retention-event-p, fn-stxe-p, fn-stxk-p, fn-stxa-p, fn-cpe-eventp, fn-th-topic-eventp); each reading is O(1) and looks at the head and at most ten conses (books/store-events-carried.lisp, ten keystones, :rule-classes nil). The carried accessors fn-evc-* are the references in the logic and these readings in execution, guard fn-store-event-p, which a history record carries under fn-sn-statep (fn-ccar-seek-finds-a-store-event). The commit the host calls reads the completion record through them: fn-ccar-own-finish-is-own-finish (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish-submission) and fn-ccar-ocfg-complete-is-ocfg-step-complete, fn-ccar-ocfg-complete equal to fn-ocfg-step of (:complete) for every configured owner with no hypothesis (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish, the completion of identity, retention, consumer and topic events: the signed POST). The feed intent's Path is parsed once at take and carried: fn-icar-submission-targets equals fn-own-submission-targets under fn-icar-carryp (host fn-owner-submission-intent and fn-owner-submission-resolution).

proofs.title: The octet buffer abstracts to the octet list
proofs.statement: fn-octets (books/octets-stobj.lisp) is an abstract stobj whose logical value is the octet list and whose executable is a resizable (unsigned-byte 8) array with a fill count. The abstraction relation fn-octets$corr (the array's first FILL cells read in order are the list, the fill count is within the array, the concrete object is well formed) is established by the creator (create-fn-octets{correspondence}) and preserved by every export, and every export's executable step equals the list operation on the abstraction under the export's guard: fn-octets-get{correspondence} is nth, fn-octets-put{correspondence} is update-nth, fn-octets-append-octet{correspondence} is append of one octet (through the array's doubling resize), fn-octets-list{correspondence} is the list read tail-recursively, fn-octets-from-list{correspondence} is the list written; each with the guard theorem and the logical preservation ACL2 requires. The derived readers a codec twin reads the buffer with are their take/nthcdr terms over the logical value, under the hypothesis that the value is a true list, which every buffer value is: fn-oct-slice-list-is-take-nthcdr, fn-oct-prefix-equalp-is-list-prefixp (a prefix test against the list-model shape fn-inj-strip has, not take, which pads with nil past the end), fn-oct-suffix-equalp-is-equal. Every executable function is guard-verified. The host fills the array from the byte vector of a socket read in raw Lisp (host/native/io.lisp fnn-octets-fill: reserve, one replace, the count; A-HOST) and calls the buffer entries with the live stobj (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt). Bulk exports (lane octets-bulk, 2026-09-27): fn-octets-append-back{correspondence} is the octet-by-octet back copy fn-oct-back-copy (each appended octet the one OFF back when it is appended, so a run longer than OFF repeats, as an LZ match) executed as one reservation and one forward array loop; fn-octets-get-word{correspondence} is fn-oct-word-at (K octets as a little-endian natural; seven unrolled reads at K = 7); fn-octets-append-word{correspondence} is append of fn-oct-word-octets (a fixnum loop below 2^56, the octet-list write above); fn-oct-word-octets-of-word-at is the round trip that makes a word copy between two buffers the copy of the octets (a defabsstobj export cannot name a second buffer).
proofs.progress_note: Consumers on the buffer: the existing-article test and the prepare of the served POST (fn-pbb-same-articlep-is-pb-same-articlep, host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action-buffer and fn-owner-prepare-buffer). Since 2026-09-25 (pbb-d32) the buffer twin reads a recipe v3 record (D32, a supplied Path): the source is a description (K A B) of buffer positions, st[K..A) then st[B..) with the AGENT! insertion cut out, found by the index Path scan (fn-pbb-path-scan-is-inj-path-scan, fn-pbb-unsplice-at-is-inj-unsplice, fn-pbb-source-index-is-inj-source-of) and compared in place (fn-pbb-range-match-is-equal-of-append, fn-pbb-desc-equalp-is-equal); the agent of a v3 record is read from its block (fn-pbb-block-agent-is-pb-block-agent, fn-pbb-path-agent-is-pb-path-agent). Open: the payload digest over the buffer needs a SHA-256 reader by index (books/sha256-stobj.lisp, a third message reader beside the string and list readers); the chunk read (fn-owner-chunk) and the accumulated body are the owner's logical state (wave C); the record encoder, the frame and the article parser over the buffer are boundaries 7 to 9 of planning/design-2026-09-25-representation.md. A-HOST dropped from this row's assumptions (lane audit-fixes, keystone-audit G3-9, 2026-09-27): no theorem of the row takes fn-assume-host-report or fn-assume-host-events (books/assumptions.lisp) as a hypothesis, so the citation was decorative (AGENTS.md: the theorems that use a named assumption mention it). The host's honest I/O remains the trust boundary these theorems sit inside, not a hypothesis of them.

proofs.title: Frame blobs have per-schema widths; the control socket carries an article up to the profile's A
proofs.statement: D27, packets PKT-008/009. The frame field grammar (books/frame-fields) has a spec form (:blob . W), 1 <= W <= 2^32-1, beside :blob (131 072, the node's own fields); fn-frame-field-parse-of-octets-wide-blob (books/frame-invariants) is its round trip, and fn-frame-fields-octets-within-width: a record whose values satisfy SPECS encodes to at most (fn-frame-specs-width SPECS) octets, which is the journal encoders' guard bound (books/frame-journal, with the FNWF and FNRJ tables proved within their payload caps). The FNCT request's article field is (:blob . *fn-record-max-payload*) and its group-list field the encoded list at the record's group ceiling (books/native-control). KEYSTONE fn-native-control-request-within-profile-frame: for naturals A and G, every request encoding (fn-native-control-request-encode, which the client calls through fn-native-control-host-request-encode in host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-submit) whose article is at most A octets and whose group list has at most G names is at most (fn-nctrl-max-frame-for A G) octets; fn-native-control-request-within-read-bound gives the same under fn-nctrl-read-bound-for, the bound the owner reads a control connection under (host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-handle-client, computed once at fnn-control-start from the carried profile's A and G through fn-owner-control-profile-bounds and fn-native-control-host-read-bound, or fn-native-hybrid-control-host-read-bound = fn-nhctrl-read-bound-for when hybrid control is built in, which covers both, fn-nhctrl-read-bound-covers-both). The owner's injection decision then refuses an article past A as article-exceeds-profile-bound (PRF-016's boundary). Covered scope: the request encoder and the read bound; the frame decoder's cons walk and the ACL2 octet lists at runtime are D27's representation work, not this target. The FNRJ request-context blobs (a Store record and a request ADU at 131 072), the app journal's record count and aggregates, and the history pre-check figures (PKT-011) are open. EXTENSION (lane downstream-requests, 2026-09-27; Mini/DREGG's PKT-codex-003): the local signed-author request (books/native-hybrid-control.lisp, kind 5, `hybrid-author`) carried only a v1 source (at most 65,535 octets, *fn-hsig-v1-max-source*), so a v2 source that the served POST accepts was refused on the control socket. Its source field is now (:blob . *fn-nhctrl-max-source*), the frame's u32 payload less the other four fields (4,294,963,388; fn-nhctrl-max-payload-is-the-frame-width), and fn-nhctrl-author-request-covers-every-storable-article: *fn-article-max-octets* < *fn-nhctrl-max-source*. The read bound no longer reads the codec width: fn-nhctrl-read-bound-for A G = max(fn-nctrl-read-bound-for A G, 42 + the widest key request, fn-nhctrl-author-frame-for A = 42 + 3,907 + min(A, max-source)). KEYSTONE fn-native-hybrid-control-author-request-within-read-bound: (implies (and (natp a) (<= (len source) a) (not (equal request :bad))) (<= (len request) (fn-nhctrl-read-bound-for a g))) for request = (fn-native-hybrid-control-author-encode generation source ed ml path), which host/native/hybrid-control.lisp fnn-command-hybrid-author calls through fn-native-hybrid-control-host-author-encode; the owner's bound is computed at host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-start through fn-native-hybrid-control-host-read-bound. Teeth: tests/acl2/native-hybrid-control-tests.lisp (a 65,536-octet source round-trips; a 300,000-octet source at A = 300,000, G = 0 is formed, within the hybrid bound and past the ordinary one, and decodes to itself; the hypothesis-removal witness at A = 1,000). Native: tests/test_native_hybrid_author.py test_v2_source_through_hybrid_author (191,283 octets accepted, its resend DUPLICATE, served with its acceptance-time verdict; a carrier past A refused ARTICLE-EXCEEDS-PROFILE-BOUND). That case found the route injecting under the codec's payload bound (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-live-post-config was fn-owner-post-config at *fn-record-max-payload*), so a carrier past A passed injection and the owner's admission (fn-own-control-decision, :control-invalid) refused it with no name; fn-owner-live-post-config is now the owner's installed configuration (fn-own-config: the profile's A and header limits), so the carrier arm's :oversize is the named word.
proofs.progress_note: Certified: runs 22ae (538 passed) and 2f56 (exit 0) on persvati, e8e4 on hbox (image closure, 198 passed); native operator post of 131 073 and 290 000 octets under A = 300 000 accepted, 300 001 refused by name (planning/evidence/bounds-blob-2026-09-25.md). Open: the FNRJ receipt blobs and app-journal counts (PKT-010 remainder), the pre-reservation figures (PKT-011, blocked by fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-verdict, PRF-072), and the octet lists at runtime on this path (D27 representation).

proofs.title: Content reclamation removes only unheld payload bytes and every history decision reads the same afterwards
proofs.statement: fn-rcl-reclaimable-is-no-obligation-names-it: (fn-rcl-reclaimable rule now h verdicts article) (the standing verdict fn-rcl-standing-verdict, which reads no payload; the tombstone test is the caller's on the octets it holds: the record's own payload in fn-rclp-rewrites-p, the arena in fn-rcl-verdict-in, the payload in the octet model fn-rcl-verdict, fn-rcl-verdict-reclaimable-by-definition) equals: rule not keep-forever and a rule, the rule permits the article's stamp at now, no authorship verdict other than :absent (fn-rcl-verdict-heldp), and no obligation of (fn-rcl-obligations h) -- reader pin, consumer cursor, undelivered feed to a live peer, BP obligation -- names the article; no hypothesis. fn-rclp-event-never-touches-a-held-article (of the per-record rewrite the host calls, fn-rclp-event: host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-log-reclaim-event; shared with PRF-119): if an obligation names the record's article, or its verdict needs its payload, or the rule is keep-forever and the expiry policy has not expired it, the rewrite returns the same octets (the in-memory model's fn-rcl-reclaim-never-touches-a-held-article, fn-rcl-reclaim-if-permitted the identity, stays in books/store-reclaim.lisp, uncited: no host verb drives that transition). fn-rcl-reclaim-keeps-the-duplicate-history: fn-acceptedp of every Message-ID is unchanged, no hypothesis. fn-rcl-reclaim-keeps-every-binding and fn-rcl-reclaim-keeps-the-numbering: groups, memberships, pin, stamp, per-group next numbers, next txid and pending unchanged; every other article unchanged. fn-rcl-reclaim-preserves-statep: under fn-statep. fn-rcl-prepare-commutes-with-reclaim: under fn-statep, fn-accept-prepare after reclaiming equals reclaiming after fn-accept-prepare. fn-rcl-existing-action-after-reclaim: for an article M present and not already a tombstone, the D25 verdict fn-rcl-action-over (the host entry fn-store-existing-action is it over alpha, fn-store-existing-action-is-the-verdict-over-alpha) for every Message-ID, submission and groups is unchanged, or SHA-256 collides on the compared pair, or the submission names another agent under which the removed payload gives back a source. fn-rcl-config-rule-after-retention-set: under fn-rcl-rulep, the rule read after fn-cfg-apply of fn-rcl-rule-deltas is the rule, on any prior value. fn-nntp-reclaimed-article-answers-reclaimed: fn-nntp-article-response on an article with a usable identifier and a tombstone payload answers 423 (number or current) or 430 (Message-ID) article reclaimed. fn-rclb-same-articlep-is-rcl-same-articlep: under fn-octets-p (the buffer's recognizer), the buffer comparison fn-rclb-same-articlep, which the native owner's buffer verdict fn-pidx-existing-action makes (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action-buffer, fn-owner-prepare-buffer), equals the list comparison fn-rcl-same-articlep; the list sites call fn-store-existing-action (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare, fn-owner-existing-action; host/store-node-host.lisp prepare and fn-store-sn-existing-action). The store-shaped twins fn-rcl-existing-action and fn-rclb-existing-action, which compared with the held handle, were retired (PKT-860, entry-guards-2). fn-nntp-over-by-msgid-answers-reclaimed: for a Message-ID token naming a held tombstone, fn-nntp-over-response (called by fn-nntp-archive-command) answers 430 article reclaimed; fn-nntp-over-current-answers-reclaimed: with a selected group and a current article that is a tombstone, 423 article reclaimed. fn-nov-lines-indexed-skip-a-reclaimed-article (subject of fn-nntp-over-range-indexed, the pinned OVER/XOVER range) and fn-nov-lines-skip-a-reclaimed-article (unpinned): the lines over NUMBERS equal the lines over NUMBERS without a tombstoned article's number. fn-nntp-newnews-scan-lists-only-live-articles: every Message-ID fn-nntp-newnews-scan lists is that of an article that is not a tombstone; no other hypothesis. fn-rcl-store-holders-hold-behind-a-lagging-consumer: while a registered consumer's acknowledgement is below the committed frontier, no article numbered (n >= 1) in a served group is reclaimable under fn-rcl-store-holders, for every rule, clock and verdict list. fn-rcl-absent-verdict-contributes-nothing: when fn-stx-verdict-of-octets of a payload under any keyring is :absent, fn-stx-delta of that payload is nil under every keyring, so an :absent verdict holds nothing; with fn-sn-finish-records-the-acceptance-verdict (the recorded verdict is fn-stx-verdict-of-octets of the payload) and fn-rcl-tombstone-contributes-nothing (fn-stx-delta of any payload satisfying fn-rcl-tombstonep is nil under every keyring), reclaiming such an article leaves the statement index every later open derives unchanged. fn-rcl-tombstone-refused-at-carrier-form: every payload satisfying fn-rcl-tombstonep gets (:refused :article) from fn-pa-carrier-form, which the host calls over the octet buffer as fn-owner-peer-carrier-form-buffer (host/owner-host.lisp; fn-ars-carrier-form-is-reference) in host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-filled before any Store call, on every served ingress (POST, IHAVE, TAKETHIS, peer and BP transit, bound submissions); no other hypothesis. Its keystone lemma fn-rca-nul-first-octet-is-not-an-article: an octet string whose first octet is 0 does not parse (fn-article-parse), no other hypothesis. Not covered: the developer image's store post (host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-post), which prepares a raw payload file without an article check. PKT-844 (lane bp-retention-leftovers): each article is in exactly one retention class, fn-rcl-class-in (books/store-reclaim-holders.lisp): :reclaimed (tombstone), :signed (an authorship verdict other than :absent names it: every kind-4 composite, served key statements among them), :reclaimable, :held (a holder), :kept (the rule keeps it). proofs.title: Queued base jobs are offered only to their routed hop, each at most once per contact; the routed session scans only routed rows and the ungated forms offer nothing
proofs.statement: The host asks fn-bpnj-contact-next: host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bpc-drive-contact calls fn-bpnjc-contact-next, equal to fn-bpnj-contact-next by fn-bpnjc-contact-next-is-the-head-scan (books/bp-node-job-cursor.lisp), before every offer of a base contact (bp-service run/resume, bp-obligation request, bp-contact tick, bp-node serve's fnn-bpnode-send-receipts), and drives its event through fn-bpnj-step (fnn-bps-foundation-step). fn-bpnj-contact-offer-is-the-routed-hop: when it answers an offer with routing (:table TABLE) in force, the offer names fn-bpnj-select's job, queued, for the peer and not yet offered on this contact; OFFERED gains its key; fn-bprt-send-decision over TABLE answers :send on the job's durable route (the contact port of the boundary fn-bprt-next-hop chooses among the boundaries with a contact) and the EID the host passes as the expected TCPCL peer is the decision's, so a job the table routes nowhere is never offered. fn-bpnj-contact-offers-each-job-at-most-once: along any sequence of states the host consults it at, threading OFFERED, the keys one contact offers are distinct and none was offered before. fn-bpnj-contact-offers-while-a-ready-job-remains: while the gate is open and any queued job for the peer is ready, the answer is an offer, so a held or already offered job never ends the contact. fn-bpn-apply-record-keeps-forwarded: no lifecycle record returns a :forwarded job to :queued, so a job queued again after its offer had a transfer that was not accepted. fn-bpnp-step-session-offer-is-the-scan-choice: a routed :session proposes the row the arrival-order scan chooses among the held rows the table routes to its hop. The direct branch helper fn-bpnp-routed-rows-skip-an-unrouted-row is not a cited keystone; the original composed no-blocking obligation remains open at this evidence boundary; a :session open or :resume without VIA offers nothing. Covered scope: queue-time routing is host-driven through fn-bprt-job-route and a job is not queued without a route; a table change after queueing holds the job (:route-changed) and a durable re-route record is open; verbs without a Store keep the queued address; the contact host is loopback.
proofs.progress_note: 2026-09-30 coordinator assurance correction: the demand-driven ledger normalizer exposes fn-bpnp-routed-rows-skip-an-unrouted-row as a direct branch equation. It is no longer cited as a keystone. The original routed-session no-blocking obligation remains; its complete composed host-step argument and literal witnesses must be established independently of this helper. Existing contact-selection keystones retain only their stated scopes. The BP owner separately owns the helper rename and matching source admission.

proofs.statement: fn-sco-store-open-of-extended-capture: over the capture of any prefix P extended over any Q (P = NIL is the full path), the open fn-sco-store-open computes is (fn-cpo-open-observed configs frontier (append P Q)), and when it is :ok its configuration fold is (fn-cpr-replay configs (append P Q)); host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-open-extended calls fn-sco-store-open on both paths (fn-store-sn-recover over the empty capture, fn-store-sn-recover-from-checkpoint over the decoded checkpoint) and tests the kind, which is fn-sn-open-okp by fn-sco-finalize-okp-is-kind-ok. fn-ock-install-of-store-open-by-definition: fn-ock-install over that pair is fn-ock-recover-extended of E, so PRF-083's owner keystone holds of host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-recover-from-store-open (native owner.lisp fnn-owner-recover-core), with no second extension. fn-sco-thaw-of-freeze: for every checkpoint of the right shape, thawing the file's value (the count in the record slot, the records read back out of the event index) gives the value; fn-sco-freeze-of-capture-carries-the-count: a capture of at most 2^32 records is written with its count; fn-ock-published-segments-decode-to-the-checkpoint composes it with the FNSC round trip under the codec's tree and width hypotheses (host fn-store-sco-decode thaws; fn-store-sco-publish-octets and fn-ock-publication freeze). fn-ock-publication-is-the-capture-at-the-capture-point (hypothesis: an admitted history): the publication the owner runs outside its mutex over the values captured under it (fn-owner-sco-capture, native fnn-owner-publish-captured) is the capture of the captured history. The linear :exec paths equal the unchanged :logic definitions with no hypothesis: fn-ks-distinctp-is-nodupp, fn-ks-subsetp-is-subset-logic, fn-no-duplicatesp-is-ks-nodupp, fn-subsetp-is-ks-subset-logic, fn-article-listp-is-shape-and-distinct-msgids, fn-node-binding-listp-is-shape-and-distinct, fn-retain-no-duplicatesp-is-no-duplicatesp; fn-cnode-statep reaches them through fn-node-statep in fn-sco-cpr-resume, fn-sco-cpr-finish and fn-sco-finalize-from.
proofs.progress_note: Open: the Store state still holds the record list (fn-sf-records; a commit appends to it, store-files.lisp), so the kernel does not yet carry a count; fn-node-articles-have-archive-bindingsp and fn-articles-freshp are still quadratic in the whole-node recognizer; the covered prefix's octets are still re-encoded for fnn-open-live-store's callers; two hypotheses have no must-fail (the :ok hypothesis of the Store open's replay conjunct and the admitted-history hypothesis of the publication keystone) and the 2^32 bound of fn-sco-freeze-of-capture-carries-the-count has no reachable counterexample. proofs.title: Key succession and revocation over the acceptance plan: the owner's key-statement executor, the :revoked token and its replay binding
proofs.statement: Over fn-pa-current-plan (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-peer-carrier-plan, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-transit), which now takes TRANSITP and has a fifth outcome :revoked: while a principal's newest snapshot is its tombstone no plan for it is :ok on any path (fn-pa-no-ok-plan-for-a-revoked-principal, fn-pa-revocation-leaves-no-ok-plan), and on NNTP transit a carrier under keys once enrolled is :revoked at the tombstone's generation, elsewhere refused :local-enrollment (fn-pa-revoked-principal-on-transit-is-revoked-at-its-tombstone); fn-pa-revoked-event exists only with both primitive observations verified and is the composite replay's revoked branch admits at those snapshots (fn-pa-revoked-event-binds-the-arm-and-both-observations), and replay admits a :revoked composite exactly when its generation names a tombstone of that principal (fn-osp-replay-admits-a-revoked-composite-exactly-at-its-tombstone), leaving the keyring unchanged, as the carried composite does (fn-osp-*-composite-keeps-the-keyring). Over the key-statement executor fn-ks-plan / fn-ks-execute (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-plan / -event, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-key-statement after a :verified kind-4 commit): a statement acts only on its own stored :verified verdict with a keys grant covering its groups (C2's fn-ctl-authorize), so a :carried or :revoked statement never changes a keyring; the verdict's generation was the principal's current enrollment and a succession's old key is that enrollment's; the PoP is a D09 signature by the new keys over the statement's Message-ID and old key with both observations verified; after the succession's kind-3 event the new keys are selected and any other key set, the old one included, is refused :local-enrollment; after a revocation's no plan is :ok. The executor runs after every durable kind-4 composite that carries a statement, :carried and :revoked included, once the statement's own barrier returned (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-statement-committed; PRF-310), and a Store refusal of the key change leaves the article accepted and is reported as such (transit detail :key-change-refused; log line `key-statement ... refused`). The crash cut between the statement's commit and its change's is a model crash point: the open's recovery (fn-ks-recover; host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-key-statement-recover over the newest record, through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-pending) reaches from the cut exactly the uninterrupted acceptance under the recovery's rows and observations (fn-ks-recover-completes-the-cut) and, after an acceptance that acted, changes nothing under any rows or observations (fn-ks-recover-after-an-acting-acceptance-changes-nothing); executing a statement whose change is already the newest snapshot yields nothing (fn-ks-execute-is-idempotent). The verb keys is grantable (fn-cfg-grant-control-admissible-iff over *fn-cfg-control-verbs* = (cancel keys)). The rendered item for :revoked begins `r`, never `v` (fn-stx-verified-item-first-octet-names-the-token), and token code 5 round-trips. The next generation is ACL2's (fn-hl-next-generation; control kinds 7 and 8). Evidence is never rewritten: a kind-3 completion keeps every stored verdict (fn-hls-finish-snapshot-keeps-historical-verdicts, existing) and a kind-4 one conses its own (fn-hls-finish-kind4-verdicts, existing).
proofs.progress_note: Open: no native run (no image was built on hbox for these bytes); a crash between the statement's kind-4 commit and the executor's kind-3 commit leaves the statement accepted and unexecuted (no model crash point, no recovery re-run); a refused kind-3 commit surfaces as the transit attempt's refusal after its kind-4 committed; fn_verify.py does not render :revoked; the served path (NNTP POST, BP transit) never reports :revoked by design (TRANSITP nil). A-HOST dropped from this row's assumptions (lane audit-fixes, keystone-audit G3-9, 2026-09-27): no theorem of the row takes fn-assume-host-report or fn-assume-host-events (books/assumptions.lisp) as a hypothesis, so the citation was decorative (AGENTS.md: the theorems that use a named assumption mention it). The host's honest I/O remains the trust boundary these theorems sit inside, not a hypothesis of them.

proofs.title: Invitation binding: accept enrols only a bound invitation; confirm consumes a pending invitation this node issued exactly once and enrols only the acceptance that consumed it
proofs.statement: fn-pinv-accept-step-enrols-only-a-bound-invitation: a (:enrol EVENT) from fn-pinv-accept-step SEQ TXID GEN RECEIVED OBSERVED-ML ED ML SNAPSHOTS (books/peer-invite.lisp; called by host/native/peer-invite.lisp fnn-pinv-owner-accept) has EVENT = fn-hl-enroll-event at fn-hl-next-generation SNAPSHOTS of the carrier's principal P and key set K, P not already enrolled with K, and fn-pinv-bound-document-p: fn-hsig-authorize-at over the carrier decoded from RECEIVED and the two primitive observations, the body has the invitation kind line and names P, the Ed25519 and the ML-DSA-65 key of K (fn-pinv-body-names-p, a line of the body), and fn-prin-genesis-bindsp P (Ed25519 || ML-DSA-65) TOKEN. fn-pinv-issue-plan-records-the-signed-invitation: an :issue delta is fn-cfg-issue-invitation of the body's nonce, the verified principal and the invitation's authored-source identity, the nonce keying no row. fn-pinv-confirm-consumes-only-a-pending-named-invitation: a (:consume DELTA) from fn-pinv-confirm-plan (called by fnn-pinv-owner-confirm) has a bound acceptance, the row its nonce keys pending, naming the body's Inviter-Principal and Invitation-Source-Id, and DELTA = fn-cfg-consume-invitation of the nonce, the acceptor and the acceptance's source identity. fn-pinv-confirm-step-enrols-only-the-consuming-acceptance: an (:enrol EVENT) from fn-pinv-confirm-step (called by fnn-pinv-owner-enrol-confirmed) has a bound acceptance, the row consumed (state 1) by exactly its principal and source identity, P not enrolled with K, and EVENT the kind-3 enrolment of P and K. fn-pinv-consumed-stays-consumed-across-replay: a consumed invitation stays consumed through fn-config-replay-loop; fn-pinv-consumed-refuses-consumption: fn-cfg-delta-reason refuses every :consume-invitation of it; fn-pinv-consumption-consumes. fn-pinv-confirm-after-its-consumption-enrols: after the consuming delta is applied (the crash point before the kind-3 record) the same acceptance's plan is :enrol; fn-pinv-confirm-step-never-enrols-twice. Covered scope: the owner's three steps and the configuration admission and replay; the peer record is still `peer add`; the crypto primitives are A-CRYPTO.

proofs.title: The NEWNEWS pull feed advances its cursor past a round only when every listed Message-ID drew 235, 435 or 437 from the local node, and a crash mid-round recovers the cursor that round asked with
proofs.statement: Over the functions host/native/pull-service.lisp calls (fn-pull-begin, fn-pull-step through fn-pull-step-pair, fn-pull-close, fn-pull-replay over fn-pull-journal-scan): closing a round moves the cursor only if the round ran to its end and every Message-ID its NEWNEWS listed has a 235, 435 or 437 answer, the new instant being the peer's DATE less one second (fn-pull-close-advances-only-past-a-fully-answered-round; per id fn-pull-unanswered-id-holds-the-cursor); an answer is recorded only by a local reply and is that reply's own code for the article in hand (fn-pull-step-answers-only-from-the-local-node); no step changes the round's cursor or journals anything (fn-pull-step-keeps-the-cursor-and-journals-nothing) and every NEWNEWS it sends names the round's cursor instant (fn-pull-step-newnews-names-the-cursor); if the FNPL journal replays to the owner's cursor, it replays after the begin, after any events and after the close to that cut's cursor (fn-pull-journal-is-the-cursor-at-every-cut), so the round begun after a crash asks the dead round's instant (fn-pull-recovery-asks-the-dead-rounds-newnews). The schedule starts only a due, idle peer and spaces rounds by the operator's interval (fn-sched-pull-due-is-due-and-idle, fn-sched-pull-started-is-not-due, fn-sched-pull-finished-waits-its-interval). That the peer lists again what it listed for the same instant is RFC 3977 7.4's NEWNEWS semantics, not proved. Restated 2026-09-26 by PRF-165 (PKT-213): the cursor carries PENDING (per-id consecutive 430 counts) and fn-pull-close-advances-only-past-a-fully-answered-round / fn-pull-unanswered-id-holds-the-cursor now admit an id the peer answered 430 for BOUND consecutive complete rounds; PRF-165 states them.
proofs.progress_note: Native (hbox, SCN-058): a second fn node, INN 2.7.4 nnrpd and a SIGKILL mid-round then the same NEWNEWS all pass. Open: the pull client has no TLS arm (a TLS transport is not pulled); a remote 430 for a listed id holds the cursor until the peer stops listing it; the cursor lives in <store>/pull/*.fnpl (FNFD envelope and phase machine), not a Store transaction record. proofs.title: The operator's configuration is ACL2's: [alerts]/[ops] rows, the rendered configuration, missions and their store profiles, the SIGHUP log reopen, and file-first on the bound commit route
proofs.statement: fn-native-config-show-round-trip: for every configuration C that fn-native-config-show-wfp admits, fn-native-config-load -- the loader fn-native-operator-run (host/native-operator-host.lisp:19) reads fn.toml through -- of fn-native-config-show-octets C, the text `operator CONFIG show' prints and a mission writes, is (:accepted C); the [alerts] and [ops] rows are part of C. fn-native-config-load-renderable: every configuration fn-native-config-load accepts satisfies fn-native-config-show-wfp (the parser's values are parsed-shaped and each field's normalization keeps its bound), so fn-native-config-show carries no run-time check; with the round trip, fn-native-config-loaded-show-round-trip: the rendering of every loaded configuration loads back as itself. fn-native-mission-profiles-valid and fn-native-mission-store-opens-with-its-profile: for each of small-community, relay and archive, the mission's profile request resolves to an admitted profile, and the frame `init' writes for it (fn-bs-config-frame-for-profile, host/store-host.lisp fn-store-metadata-config-frame) decodes at every later open to exactly that profile (under A-CRYPTO through fn-bs-config-decode-of-encode). fn-native-operator-run-init-under-a-mission: under a configuration naming a mission, an accepted init plan's profile is the mission's request. fn-olr-reopen-iff-requested: fn-olr-decide, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-log-reopen answers host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-maybe-reopen-log with, reopens exactly when a log path is configured and a SIGHUP arrived since the last one handled, and every counted request is then handled. fn-obc-commit-only-after-filing: fn-obc-commit-gate, which fnn-owner-complete-bound-submission asks (through fn-owner-bound-commit-gate) before any commit callback, answers :commit only when fn-pa-filing-plan files the article in exactly the committed groups; with C1's keystone a control article then commits only in its filing group (fn-obc-control-commits-only-in-its-filing-group). Covered scope: that the host calls the callback only on :commit, and swaps the log descriptor under the log mutex, is host code measured natively, not proved.

proofs.title: BP outbound fragmentation: every fragment the send plan answers fits the peer's Transfer MRU, reassembles exactly to the parent's payload with no data cap, and restores the parent
proofs.statement: The subject is fn-bpfs-plan WIRE MRU (books/bp-fragment-send.lisp, logic mode, guard-verified), which host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-send-effect calls after SESS_INIT with the session's negotiated Transfer MTU (fn-tcl-negotiated-transfer-mtu). fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-fit-mru: when the plan answers (:fragments W1 ... Wn), every Wi is at most MRU octets (the chunk is MRU minus 8 minus the encoded length of the empty fragment at the largest offset; fn-bpfs-fragment-length-bound over fn-bpfs-fragment-primary-length-shift and the payload block's exact length). fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-reassemble-exactly: the decoded views of the Wi draw the decoded parent's payload exactly on the reassembly canvas fn-bpf-canvas at the parent's ADU offset (0 for a whole parent, its own offset for a fragment parent) and all carry the parent's total, for every payload length and fragment count (no data cap). fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-restore-parent: every Wi decodes to a bundle with the parent's extension blocks and ADU key and the fragment flag, and a whole parent's fragment primary unfragments to the parent's primary. fn-bpfs-plan-fragments-reassemble-within-caps: for a whole parent of at most *fn-bpf-max-length* (65538) octets cut into at most *fn-bpf-max-fragments* (64) pieces, the receiver's executable reassembler fn-bpf-reassemble answers (:ok payload). Covered scope: the sender's base-job send path (bp-service run and the bp-node send of queued jobs through fnn-bps-send-effect); held-transit forwarding (the :session arm's MRU wait) does not fragment; the receiver's reassembler and held-row recognizers keep the 65538 x 64 caps; one job attempt covers all fragments (no per-fragment custody records); the plan runs on octet lists (no D27 concrete twin).
proofs.progress_note: Lane bp-n16-prod-2 (2026-09-25), PKT-061. Productionizes spike/bp's :program fn-bpfs-plan. Teeth in tests/acl2/bp-fragment-send-tests: witnesses at MRU 300 and 400 over a real 1000-octet bundle, a fragment parent at ADU offset 500 of 3000, a 70000-octet ADU (above the receiver cap) and a 100-fragment cut (above the fragment cap); must-fails for dropping the 8-octet head reserve, for each keystone without :fragments, and for each cap hypothesis of the within-caps corollary.

proofs.title: Peering composed: the confirm's one configuration record consumes the invitation and configures the peer; a declined key statement is decided at reopen under the configuration in force at its txid; the admission verdict names its class
proofs.statement: fn-pinv-confirm-record-configures-the-issued-invitations-peer: a (:configure DELTAS) from fn-pinv-confirm-record-plan RECEIVED INVITATION OBS ED ML INVITATIONS SNAPSHOTS PEERS (books/peer-invite.lisp; host/native/peer-invite.lisp fnn-pinv-owner-confirm calls it through fn-pinv-host-confirm-record-plan) has fn-pinv-confirm-plan :consume, the row pending, the invitation of kind invitation whose authored-source identity is the row's, the confirmed peer fn-cfg-peerp with auth (:principal ACCEPTOR) and a name no peer of PEERS has, and DELTAS = (consume-delta, fn-cfg-set-peer-delta peer). fn-pinv-confirm-record-fold-consumes-and-configures: over fn-cfg-apply V GEN STAMP DELTAS (the fold fn-cfg-apply-record runs when the owner completes the publication) the invitation row is consumed by exactly this acceptor and acceptance source identity, the peers table holds exactly the peer's rows under its name, and (not enrolled) the next confirm plan is :enrol. fn-ks-reopen-is-blind-to-later-configuration and fn-ks-a-decline-replays-as-a-decline: fn-ks-recover-recorded (the open's recovery; host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-key-statement-recover with AT-OPEN, rows from host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-rows = fn-ks-statement-rows with AT-OPEN; no policy switch) decides the pending statement under fn-ctl-config-at its own txid, so configuration records later than the statement change nothing, and a statement whose plan declined is left as the acceptance left it. fn-ks-recorded-recovery-completes-the-cut: when every configuration record precedes the txid and the journal replays, the recorded recovery of the cut is the uninterrupted acceptance under the live grants. fn-pcb-admission-verdict-names-its-class: the verdict is one of :unsigned :carried :malformed :cryptographically-invalid :unenrolled :unsupported-profile :verified; :verified iff the plan is :ok under both verified observations; :carried iff the D23 arm; a present carrier is never :unsigned. Not covered: pull over TLS (packet 8), the observation determinism the decline theorem assumes (A-CRYPTO), fn-pcb-admission-verdict has no host caller yet (its classes are the transit refusal detail's plus :carried/:verified).

proofs.title: A resend of an accepted source after its withdrawal or reclamation is answered from the Store (duplicate or conflict), never prepared as a fresh acceptance, and is served a 441 line
proofs.statement: Over the decision the host calls at POST (fn-rclb-existing-action, host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-existing-action-buffer from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt; fn-rcl-existing-action, fn-owner-existing-action from fnn-owner-attempt-transit): for a string Message-ID held in the Store's article list, both answer :duplicate or :conflict after fn-sn-finish of that Store, whatever the completed record (fn-vj-a-completion-keeps-a-held-message-id-answered; a cancel that withdraws the target is accepted by such a completion, and the owner's carried commit is fn-sn-finish by fn-ccar-sn-finish-is-sn-finish), and for any Store whose article list is fn-rcl-reclaim-state of an acceptance state holding it (fn-vj-reclamation-keeps-a-held-message-id-answered); while the resend is the connection's in-flight submission with no completion consumed, fn-own-outcome renders the duplicate or the conflict 441 line for it (fn-vj-a-held-message-id-is-answered-441). The host returns the word before fnn-advance-frontier and fn-owner-prepare-buffer, so no number is allocated (host control flow, observed natively, not a theorem). The same source being :duplicate rather than :conflict after reclamation is fn-rcl-existing-action-after-reclaim with its SHA-256 collision disjuncts. RECORDS FLIP (flip-books-residue, 2026-09-27): the three keystones are stated over fn-store-existing-action (books/store-intern.lisp) for every arena: the host's decision after flip-L6 on both entries (the buffer path through fn-pidx-existing-action-is-store-existing-action); fn-rclb-existing-action and fn-rcl-existing-action are the wire-view specifications. The same source after reclamation over the entry is fn-sr-a-retry-after-reclaim-is-already-stored (PRF-117).

proofs.title: The record producers the node runs stay inside the widths the profile admits, discharging the width hypothesis of fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record
proofs.statement: fn-sn-prepare-stages-a-narrow-article-record (books/record-width-producers.lisp): if CHARGE is at most 2^32 - 1 and fn-sn-prepare stages the record fn-sn-article-record builds (the result is not the input state), that record is not fn-record-widep: sequence, txid and generation are within u32 because the file machine stages only the reserved txid (frontier - 1), generation = txid and sequence = the committed count, and every file state holds a u32 frontier with strictly increasing committed txids below it (fn-sf-prepare-record-stages-u32-coordinates, fn-sn-prepare-stages-u32-coordinates); the stamp is below 2^32 by fn-record-stamp-of-observation (fn-sn-article-record-stamp-and-charge). The charge premise is discharged by the charge gate: fn-sbud-post-boundary answers :ok only for a u32 charge (fn-sbud-post-boundary-admits-a-u32-charge), and fn-post-admitted-article-record-is-within-r composes the boundary verdict :ok under PROFILE, the producer and the prepare into the conclusion of fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record: the staged record encodes within the profile's R, so the publish gate's record check (host/store-host.lisp fn-store-publication-admissibility, asserted by host/native/io.lisp fnn-publish) never refuses it. The BP ingress producer: fn-bpi-staged-record-is-narrow (policy charge u32 by fn-bpi-policy-p). Host calls: host/store-node-host.lisp and host/owner-host.lisp call fn-sn-article-record and then the prepare (fn-spc-prepare, equal to fn-sn-prepare by fn-spc-prepare-equals-specification-under-relation; fn-pcar-sbud-prepare, equal to fn-sbud-prepare by fn-pcar-sbud-prepare-is-sbud-prepare), after the boundary (host/native/io.lisp fnn-post-boundary; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-post-boundary); the boundary and the prepare are separate host calls, so the composition is over the host's order, stated, not one ACL2 function. Not covered: the signed composite (kind 4) and the peer-carried event producers, which carry their own R check (fn-owner-signed-event-boundary). Packet 1 (decided): the history gate charges an article its own figure, fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling of its payload length and group count (fn-sbud-article-figure, books/store-budget-article.lisp). fn-sbud-article-verdict-keeps-history: if fn-sbud-article-verdict-at PROFILE USED BYTES-USED PL GC is :admissible and RECORD is narrow with at most PL payload octets and GC groups, then fn-profile-replay-within-boundp PROFILE (+ BYTES-USED (len (fn-record-encode RECORD))): the bound the next open checks per file (host/native/io.lisp fnn-durable-records through host/store-host.lisp fn-store-profile-replay-within-bound). Host: host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-article-verdict (native store post, before reservation). fn-sbud-prepare-under-article-budget-keeps-history: a fn-sbud-prepare that staged under fn-sbud-article-budget-for PROFILE BYTES-USED RECORD kept the history within H; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare and fn-owner-prepare-buffer pass that budget with the owner's carried committed octets (fn-owner-record-octets) to fn-pcar-sbud-prepare (= fn-sbud-prepare). fn-post-admitted-article-keeps-history composes the store-post sequence with PRF-123's keystone. fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-article-verdict: an upgrade keeps every article verdict (the figure does not read the profile). PKT-250 (the composition over the owner's two host calls): fn-prwo-owner-post-record-is-narrow-within-the-profile (books/post-record-width-owner.lisp) is stated over exactly the ACL2 functions the served POST calls in order -- fn-pak-post-admission (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-post-boundary, asked by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt), then fn-sn-article-record, fn-apc-intern-row-at and fn-ppc-pout-prepare-article-cat (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-buffer; the host seals only on its :prepared word): under a carry whose verdict is its profile's (fn-pvc-carryp), a boundary :ok over the payload length and group count, and a :prepared word for the interned row of the record, the profile is admitted, the record is narrow and its payload and group count are within A and G; fn-prwo-owner-post-record-is-within-r composes it with fn-bs-profile-admits-every-article-record (the record encodes within R). No join, view or relation hypothesis: the catalog's duplicate answer may be any value. Host-side facts not in the statement: the boundary and the prepare read the same owner (the owner's lock), the boundary's lengths are the prepare's (fnn-owner-attempt passes (length payload) and (length codes), the buffer is filled from the same payload and fn-store-groups-from-codes resolves the same codes).
