proofs.title: A chain of packs reconstructs the history: contiguous digest-linked links compose one prefix, compaction extends it over the uncovered suffix, the open over the walked chain answers the history, reclaim and publication cuts keep it
proofs.statement: Over the functions host/checkpoint-host.lisp calls for host/native/checkpoint.lisp (fnn-pack-walk, fnn-pack-extend-chain, fnn-pack-recover-records, fnn-pack-retire-older-generations): fn-ccc-links-okp-composes-a-prefix (a walked chain is BOUNDARY exact Store events from sequence 0 under the newest frontier); fn-ccc-capture-extends-the-chain (fn-ccc-capture-link from the chain's boundary, frontier, generation and digest yields a link that, consed on, is again a chain whose records are a prefix of the history and strictly longer; the old chain is its tail); fn-ccc-capture-link-succeeds (it succeeds on a valid suffix); fn-ccc-chain-reconstructs-the-history (fn-ccc-observe-chain over the decoded chain and an observation holding, for every sequence from some N at or below the chain's boundary to the end of H, the record H holds there answers (:ok H frontier) when the chain's records are a prefix of H and the suffix is valid: no reclaimed file is needed, and the served view replays exactly these records); fn-ccc-reclaim-preserves-reconstructed-history (PRF-073 over a chain); fn-ccc-retire-plan-keeps-the-chain; fn-ccc-publication-crash-walks-old-or-new-chain (under the marker-old-or-complete-candidate and files-kept facts of the pack program, the walk reads the old chain or the new link on it); fn-ccc-links-count-within-boundary (walk fuel T suffices); fn-cverb-pack-decision-capture-succeeds restated over the chain capture. Joined with the reclamation work (pack-chain-join, 2026-09-26): fn-rclp-reclaiming-pack-is-a-first-link (books/store-reclaim-pack.lisp; when fn-rclp-decide answers :reclaim, the summary it hands host/native/checkpoint.lisp fnn-pack-publish-generation is, through fn-ccc-link-of-summary, a valid first link with no predecessor whose boundary is the selected chain's coverage and the whole committed history); the compact verb's temporary-space figure is the next link's (fn-cverb-pack-fits-the-disk, PRF-129). The between-links cut (pack-chain-link, lane pack-chain-cut): fn-ccc-chain-program is fnn-pack-extend-chain's link as a program (:publish, :select, then the cut); fn-ccc-chain-link-cut-walks-the-extended-chain (at the Nth cut the state is the selection's, from the lemma fn-ccc-chain-cut-state-is-previous-state that a :cut leaves the preceding step's state; the marker names link N and the walk from it reads links N..1 on the chain selected before, when the host's chain names each predecessor, its generations are distinct and its entries are the host's triples); fn-ccc-chain-link-cut-reopens-to-the-history (the reopen there answers the history under fn-ccc-chain-reconstructs-the-history's hypotheses over that chain).
proofs.progress_note: Retired 2026-09-27 (lane flip-cleanup, 2026-09-27; design 2026-09-27 storage-log section 9 row 5, log-recovery's section 6 continuation): its subject was deleted with the pack layer: the pack chain (books/checkpoint-pack-chain.lisp) and its host wrappers (host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-checkpoint-chain-*) had no native caller since PKT-838 deleted fnn-pack-walk and the pack verbs; the books and tests are gone. What covers the property now: the record log's open over its segments and the checkpoint (PRF-270). Before: Lane bounds-p5 (2026-09-25). Open: the link codec round trip is executed, not proved; the crash keystone is stated under the pack program's two facts, not composed with fn-cpp-crash-selects-old-authority-or-complete-candidate by a theorem. Lane pack-chain-cut (2026-09-26, PKT-459): the between-links cut pack-chain-link is a model program cut (fn-ccc-chain-program) with its K0-shaped state theorem and its crash keystones (fn-ccc-chain-link-cut-walks-the-extended-chain, fn-ccc-chain-link-cut-reopens-to-the-history); the chain's links-okp at the cut is a hypothesis, not composed from the per-link captures (PKT-460).

proofs.title: A control article is offered to every peer whose outbound wildmat matches its Newsgroups names or its filing group, and an ordinary article's feed scope is unchanged
proofs.statement: fn-own-submission-offers-a-control-article-under-its-newsgroups-and-filing-group: for an owner O with a submission in flight whose octets classify :control (fn-own-feed-control-of, equal to fn-ctl-classify-octets whenever the article parses: fn-own-feed-control-of-is-the-filing-classification), a peer NAME of the feed table (fn-own-feed-tablep, fn-own-feed-entry-of) with an outbound half whose wildmat matches a group of the article's Newsgroups (fn-own-feed-groups-of) or its filing group (fn-ctl-filing-group of the verb), whose path-identity the Path does not name, which is not the origin and whose queue does not hold the Message-ID, is a member of fn-own-submission-targets O (books/owner-feed-subject.lisp; the host's intent calls it through fn-icar-submission-targets, equal to it, at host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-submission-intent, and the durable enqueue fn-own-feed-durable through fn-own-outcome, fn-own-control-outcome and fn-own-transit-outcome). fn-own-submission-target-of-a-control-article-is-in-its-scope: every target of a control article matches its base groups, its Newsgroups names or its filing group. fn-own-sub-feed-groups-of-an-ordinary-article: a submission whose octets do not classify :control has exactly its base groups. Not covered: the pull side (NEWNEWS serves by the filed group), the receiving node's acceptance of the cancel (PRF-097/C3's), RFC 5537 section 5.3's advice that a cancel's Newsgroups equal its target's (the author's, not checked).

proofs.title: The operator's `keys redecide MSGID` decides a stored key statement as a new acceptance under the grants in force at its own txid, repeats nothing at the next open, and is refused by name for a Message-ID that names no stored statement or a statement already acted; and the transit refusal class the owner prints is the seven-class admission verdict's refusal arm
proofs.statement: Subject fn-ks-redecide / fn-ks-redecide-plan / fn-ks-redecide-event (books/key-statements.lisp), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-key-statement-redecide-find/-plan/-event compute over the owner's Store records, keyring snapshots and live authorities rows, called by host/native/keys.lisp fnn-keys-owner-redecide under the owner mutex (control request 12, `operator CONFIG keys redecide MSGID`). (1) fn-ks-redecide-decides-under-the-configuration-at-its-own-txid: when every record of the journal CONFIGS is at or before TXID and CONFIGS replays, the redecide under the replay's authorities (the live rows the host passes) equals the redecide under fn-ks-redecide-rows TXID CONFIGS (fn-ctl-config-at the redecide's own txid). (2) fn-ks-reopen-after-a-redecide (no hypotheses): the open's recorded recovery fn-ks-recover-recorded of the redecided state, under any journal and any coordinates, is the redecided state when the redecide committed a kind-3 change and the recovery of the unchanged state otherwise, so PRF-124 and PRF-140 carry over. (3) fn-ks-redecide-of-no-stored-statement-is-refused-by-name and fn-ks-redecide-of-an-acted-statement-is-refused-by-name: the plan is (:refused :not-a-key-statement) / (:refused :already-acted) and the state is unchanged. (4) fn-ks-redecide-of-an-unacted-statement-is-its-acceptance-decision: for a stored statement that has not acted, the plan and kind-3 event are fn-ks-plan and fn-ks-execute of it, so the PRF-098 keystones over them apply. (5) fn-ks-a-redecide-that-acted-is-refused-the-second-time: after a redecide that acted, when the statement's verdict generation precedes the keyring's next generation, the same MSGID is refused :already-acted under any grants. The record is the kind-3 change itself at the redecide's coordinates (no re-filed composite, no new record kind, no cut). Teeth: tests/acl2/key-statements-tests.lisp section PRF-166 (decline, later grant, redecide at a later txid; one must-fail per hypothesis; the generation hypothesis's removal is a CORRUPTED-STATE witness). Not covered: live rows = replay of fn-sn-config-history is the owner's maintained relation (P6/PRF-028 (certified again at the current digest since c7072ddc: served-path-scale's manifest certify-20260926T123813Z-1816946 covers its thirteen theorems), not proved here; the host-to-model link of fnn-keys-owner-redecide is by construction (it calls the named functions), as PRF-098. (6) fn-pcb-admission-verdict-refusal-arms-are-the-refusal-class (books/peer-carriage.lisp, PKT-240, no hypotheses): fn-pcb-verdict-refusal-class of fn-pcb-admission-verdict equals fn-pcb-refusal-class on every input; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-refusal-class, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-transit-class inside fnn-owner-attempt-transit, computes the former. Witnesses for all seven verdicts in tests/acl2/peer-carriage-tests.lisp.

proofs.title: The consumer count is the operator's profile field 9: the served registration refuses exactly past it and the table stays within it
proofs.statement: The consumer registration the owner serves (fn-cp-register-within, called by books/consumer-owner-local.lisp fn-col-register from host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-register with MAX = fn-store-profile-max-consumers of the carried profile, host/store-host.lisp) is (:refused :max-consumers) iff fn-cp-register answers :write and the table already holds (nfix MAX) entries, and is fn-cp-register's answer otherwise (fn-cp-register-within-refuses-exactly-past-the-operator-bound, no hypothesis). From a table of at most MAX entries, applying any non-register event or the served decision's write keeps at most MAX (fn-cp-apply-preserves-consumer-capacity); Replay re-runs the validity decision fn-cp-register, not the admission bound, and a store keeps the profile it was opened under (D34; no migrations): when every :register the open's replay applies (fn-cpe-projection-replay nil RECORDS 0, books/config-observed.lisp, books/checkpoint-auxiliary.lisp) is one fn-cp-register-within under the opened profile's max-consumers (field 8, *fn-bs-profile-field-names*) writes in the state the replay has reached (fn-crb-registers-within), the replayed table holds at most max-consumers entries (fn-crb-replay-keeps-the-consumer-bound, PKT-370; a live completion's one fn-cpe-projection-step: fn-crb-projection-step-keeps-the-bound). OPEN JOIN (Codex r36 L1): no producer theorem yet shows that the persisted history the host writes satisfies fn-crb-registers-within (every committed register came through fn-col-register under the same max-consumers); a log written under another bound, or by a foreign or corrupted writer, is not bounded at replay (the teeth's replay-reachable removal).
proofs.progress_note: Open (PKT-435): field 7 has no served reader and the group-name width is 256; the checkpoint generation names (PKT-168 (1)); PKT-183's contiguity lemma and credential-file bound; the FNFD payload fit. A-HOST dropped from this row's assumptions (lane audit-fixes, keystone-audit G3-9, 2026-09-27): no theorem of the row takes fn-assume-host-report or fn-assume-host-events (books/assumptions.lisp) as a hypothesis, so the citation was decorative (AGENTS.md: the theorems that use a named assumption mention it). The host's honest I/O remains the trust boundary these theorems sit inside, not a hypothesis of them.

proofs.title: One fn-wide outcome classification and one ACL2 code map: every native command exits code(classify(f, x)), the seven classes' codes are disjoint and fixed, a fence is the only 3 in every family, NO-STORE and the clock-undecided decode are refusals, and CONFLICT is a refusal that keeps every earlier FNCT octet
proofs.statement: books/outcome-class.lisp: *fn-outcome-codes* maps :accepted 0, :refused 1, :fenced 3, :fault 4, :usage 5, :interrupted 6, :not-connected 7; fn-outcome-code reads it. fn-outcome-code-separates-the-classes: distinct classes have distinct codes. fn-outcome-code-table-by-definition: the seven codes are (0 1 3 4 5 6 7). fn-outcome-code-is-fenced-iff-fenced: over classes, the code is 3 exactly for :fenced. Families: host conditions (fn-outcome-of-host-condition, called by host/native/io.lisp fnn-exit-code-for; the +fnn-exit-*+ constants are fn-outcome-code of their classes): fn-outcome-host-condition-fences-iff-indeterminate. Operator (fn-native-operator-exit-code = fn-outcome-code of fn-native-operator-outcome-class, called through fn-native-operator-host-result-exit-code by host/native/operator.lisp): fn-native-operator-exit-is-fenced-iff-uncertain; fn-native-operator-absent-store-is-refused now concludes exit (fn-outcome-code :refused), 1. Control (fn-native-control-status-exit-code, called by the operator post and hybrid clients): fn-native-control-exit-is-fenced-iff-uncertain; topic control fn-thlc-outcome-class. BP (fn-bprc-exit-code is fn-outcome-code; host fnn-bp-exit-code, fnn-bps-exit-code, fnn-tcl-exit-code): fn-bprc-run-exit-code-is-fenced-iff-fenced; bp decode (fnn-command-bp-decode renders fn-bprc-decode-exit-code): fn-bprc-decode-never-fences, the clock-undecided verdict exits 1. CONFLICT (PKT-246): :conflict appended to *fn-nctrl-statuses*; fn-native-control-conflict-is-a-refusal: for an owner control result in the admitted range, the completion status (fn-native-control-completion-status, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-complete-bound-submission for the operator post and hybrid-author) is :conflict only for an owner refusal of D25's :conflict word, it classes :refused and exits 1, and any other word passes the result through; fn-nctrl-conflict-keeps-every-earlier-octet: each status of *fn-nctrl-statuses-before-conflict* is sealed exactly as the enumeration before :conflict seals it. The round trip of :conflict and the older decoder's :bad are executed witnesses (the seal's digest is A-CRYPTO's constrained function in proofs).

proofs.title: A signed article naming a group this node does not serve is refused by name at the signed-author ingress, a served one proceeds unchanged, and every refusal of that ingress carries its word; and the Store open refuses a control record a pre-C1 image filed under its Newsgroups by name, never a fault
proofs.statement: fn-hsig-injected-carrier-unserved-group-is-refused-by-name (books/hybrid-store-injected.lisp, KEYSTONE): for a signed source whose carrier the injecting agent admits under some served group list G1 (fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets non-nil under (fn-inj-make-config allow agent G1 max)) and a list of group names G2 (fn-inj-group-namesp), under G2 with the same agent, bound and clock: when every group the admitted decision names is in G2, fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets is the same octets and fn-hsig-injected-carrier-reason is nil; otherwise the octets are nil and the reason is :unknown-group. Its lemma fn-inj-decide-served-groups-choose-only-unknown-group states the same over fn-inj-decide. The host (host/native/hybrid-control.lisp fnn-hybrid-control-author) calls fn-hsig-injected-carrier-octets with the owner's live post configuration (fn-owner-live-post-config, the served groups of the configuration) and, when it is nil, answers (fn-nhc-author-refusal :carrier (fn-hsig-injected-carrier-reason ...)); fn-nhc-author-refusal-names-an-unserved-group: that word is :unknown-group exactly for the reason :unknown-group; fn-nhc-author-refusal-is-a-named-refusal: every word of every arm (enrolment, source fields, carrier, filing, event) is a control status whose class is :refused and whose exit code is 1. The owner of the unserved-group decision is the injection decision (fn-inj-decide's :unknown-group arm, reached through fn-hsig-injected-carrier-plan), not fn-own-control-decision: the carrier arm refuses before the bound submission, so the fnn-fault at the group-code lookup is not reached for an unserved group. Not covered: the decision of which groups a node serves (the configuration's); the operator post's refusal words (unchanged). PKT-444 (1), books/store-open-pre-c1.lisp: fn-sopc-pre-c1-control-record-p recognizes a schema-1 kind-4 composite whose signed source C1's classifier calls a control article, whose record lists exactly the source's Newsgroups and not fn-hsig-source-filed-groups (what a pre-C1 image filed). KEYSTONE fn-replay-identity-step-never-admits-a-pre-c1-control-record: from any context the identity step (books/replay.lisp, unchanged) answers a context that is not :ok at the same cursor. KEYSTONE fn-replay-never-faults-on-a-pre-c1-control-record, over fn-sopc-classified-open (the function host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-open-extended calls on every open, full replay and checkpoint): when the identity fold of the prefix is :ok and the next record, at its own sequence, is such a record, the open of the history is (:refused :pre-c1-control-record TXID MSGID); fn-sopc-checkpoint-open-names-what-the-full-open-names carries it to the checkpoint open. KEYSTONE fn-sopc-classified-open-is-the-open-without-a-pre-c1-record: on a history with no such record the classified open is fn-sco-store-open, the open before. The host renders fn-sopc-refusal-text and exits 1 (fnn-store-open-refusal). Not covered: what repairing such a store means (ember's, PKT-444); a pre-C1 malformed control record (still the generic fault, PKT-457); schema-0 composites (no stored source to classify).

proofs.title: A signed POST's identity prepare and a signed-entry lookup cost what the request costs, not what the history holds: the prepare stages without replaying the appended history, and the BP receiver's Message-ID lookups read a maintained index
proofs.statement: Part 2, the incremental identity prepare. host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-identity (called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-identity-commit for every signed POST's kind-4 composite and every keyring snapshot) installs fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity, whose store step fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity stages through fn-spc-stage-record: the specification's candidate predicate without fn-sf-history-recoverablep over (append records (list event)) (O(N*L) per signed POST, PKT-223). fn-spc-related-identity-candidate-is-recoverable (books/store-prepare-correspondence.lisp): in a :reserved state satisfying fn-snt-relation, a candidate the prepare's gate has applied to the live node (consp (fn-replay-apply-record node event)) leaves the appended history recoverable at the frontier (by fn-snt-deferred-preparation-outcome). KEYSTONES fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity-is-sn-prepare-identity-under-relation: (fn-snt-relation s) implies (fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity s event) = (fn-sn-prepare-identity s event); fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity-is-ocfg-step-under-relation: (fn-own-relation (fn-ocfg-owner oc)) implies (fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity oc event) = (fn-ocfg-step oc (list :store (list :prepare-identity event))). The premise is the article prepare's (fn-opc-prepare-equals-owner-event-under-relation): fn-own-relation conjoins fn-snt-relation, established at observed open and preserved by the owner transition family. They replace the hypothesis-free equalities of carry-kind, which held only because the function replayed. Cites PRF-117 (the D23 source decision) and fn-sr-a-signed-retry-is-already-stored (a signed retry is the D25 duplicate) unchanged: the verdict the prepare stages is the specification's. Part 1, the Message-ID index. The Store's derived event index (fn-sn-event-index, books/consumer-event-index.lisp) is a pair: the sequence trie and a Message-ID trie from each Message-ID to the article records the history commits under it (a plain record, or the record a kind-4 composite carries, decoded once when added: fn-cei-event-article), in history order. fn-cei-put extends both halves, so fn-sn-io's record-directory append (the one transition that grows the history) maintains it and every open's fn-cei-build establishes it. KEYSTONE fn-cei-msgid-records-of-correspondence: (stringp msgid) and (fn-cei-correspondencep index events) imply (fn-cei-msgid-records msgid index) = (fn-cei-article-records-for msgid events), the fold over the history; the correspondence is the maintained relation fn-ceis-indexedp (books/consumer-event-index-store-invariants.lisp: the index is fn-cei-build of the Store's history in every phase; fn-ceis-relatedp is its crash-tolerant weakening), established by fn-sn-initial (fn-ceis-initial-indexed) and preserved by fn-sn-io (fn-ceis-io-preserves-indexed: the record-directory append extends the index by the appended event), the five prepares, finish and recover. fn-bpaj-indexed-records-are-the-walk (books/bp-native-app-fast.lisp), the refinement lemma: under fn-ceis-indexedp the index answer is fn-bpaj-record-for-msgid's walk. fn-bpaj-record-lookup-fast, fn-bpaj-transit-record-lookup-fast and fn-bpaj-store-record-accepted-fast (host: host/bp-receipt-journal-host.lisp fn-bprj-request-action through fn-bpaj-dispatch-fast; host/bp-native-app-host.lisp fn-owner-app-plan-install and fn-owner-app-record) read the index; their -is-checked equalities carry fn-ceis-indexedp as refinement lemmas. Part 3, the relation carried at the host's live owner (books/owner-store-indexed.lisp, lane signed-history-index-2). KEYSTONE fn-osi-open-installs-indexed-store, no hypothesis: the owner host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-recover-extended installs on every open path (fn-osi-open: fn-ock-recover-extended of the extended checkpoint; through fn-owner-recover-from-checkpoint-equals-full-recover, fn-ock-install over fn-cpo-open-observed, whose opened Store carries fn-cei-build of the history it read) has an indexed Store. fn-osi-host-step-keeps-indexed: every owner host/owner-host.lisp installs (fn-ocfg-step for every owner event but the kernel crash, which the host never issues; fn-rcon-ocfg-io; the carried prepares fn-pcar-sbud-prepare and fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity; fn-ccar-ocfg-complete; fn-ccar-own-finish; fn-ocl-publish; fn-own-configure; fn-osb-install; fn-own-with-feeds; fn-own-transit-outcome; fn-acar-own-outcome; fn-ocfg-open, -open-peer, -read-step, -fault, -observe; fn-exp-open; fn-scar-ocfg-read-tls-prefix) keeps it. KEYSTONE fn-osi-live-owner-store-is-indexed, no hypothesis: the Store of every owner the host reaches from its open by those transitions (fn-osi-live-store) is indexed; host/native/bp-app.lisp fnn-bpapp-accept-locked binds exactly that Store (fn-owner-app-bind-receipt-store) before each fn-bprj-request-action. fn-osi-live-dispatch-fast-is-checked and the live store-record, lookup and transit-lookup equalities hold over it with no index premise, and PRF-132's keystones are stated over it. Retires PKT-223, PKT-291 item (2) and PKT-330 item (3). RETIREMENT (lane history-columns-3, 2026-09-27): the store node's event index (field 13) is retired: fn-sn-io no longer extends it and every open puts nil. Its readers read the history stobj fn-hist (books/history-columns.lisp) under R (books/history-columns-relation.lisp fn-hist-of-storep); the host refreshes the stobj before each read (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-host-hist-sync; KEYSTONE fn-hist-refresh-is-the-history: a whole load after an open, else the sync of the rows committed since, answers the history). fn-ceis-indexedp, fn-ceis-relatedp and books/consumer-event-index-store-invariants.lisp are deleted; owner-store-indexed keeps its host-step model without the index theorems.

proofs.title: HDR :fn-enrollment over the host-called read is the pinned keyring view's enrollment of the recorded verdict's principal
proofs.statement: fn-own-read-hdr-fn-enrollment-is-the-pinned-enrollment (books/owner-enrollment-read.lisp): for a read of owner connection ID of O whose octets frame nothing before the last and whose last octet frames exactly the command line `HDR :fn-enrollment <msgid>` (the fn-octl-reader-hyps reader premises, one Message-ID argument that is an octet list), on a connection with buckets whose pinned Message-ID trie holds that Message-ID, (car (fn-own-read O ID OCTETS)) is the one-line HDR reply `0 ITEM` with ITEM = fn-enr-item of the connection's pinned verdict for that Message-ID (fn-stx-reader-lookup over fn-own-conn-verdicts) against the connection's control pin (fn-own-conn-control), whose keyring slot is the view's fn-own-view-keyring. fn-enr-item (books/nntp-enrollment.lisp) names the verdict's 32-octet principal and the state of its newest snapshot in that keyring (fn-hl-current-for-principal, fn-hl-history-row): active when the row is :active at the verdict's generation, retired when :active at another generation, revoked when the row is the tombstone; unenrolled with no snapshot; none no-keyring-view / no-record / no-principal otherwise (fn-enr-item-of-an-enrolled-principal). Host line: host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-handle-chunk -> host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at -> fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix = fn-ocfg-read (fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix-is-full-read) -> fn-own-read. Supporting: fn-nntp-hdr-fn-enrollment-is-the-pinned-enrollment (the pinned dispatcher's arm), fn-nntp-enrollment-hdr-response-is-the-pinned-enrollment, and fn-own-reader-opened-after-completion-pins-the-finished-keyring (a reader opened after the owner's (:complete) pins the keyring fn-sn-finish produced, with fn-hls-finish-identity-current-enrollment the chain from a durable kind-3 record).

proofs.title: An invitation code redeems at most one account, once, across a crash: the accounts slot keeps a redeemed row the same row, the redeem plan stages only an admitted delta and resumes as already redeemed, and a redeemed account's credential is in the connection's snapshot
proofs.statement: Over the configuration the owner replays at open (fn-config-replay-loop; the records fn-owner-reconfigure-complete publishes through fn-ocl-publish), a code's redeemed row in the tenth slot (books/config.lisp fn-cfg-accounts) is the same row, or that row's tombstone once an account delete names its login, after every later acceptable record (fn-acct-bound-row-succeeds-across-replay; per admitted delta list fn-acct-bound-row-succeeds; restated by lane public-node-2 from the row's equality, which account delete falsifies), and fn-cfg-delta-reason refuses a redeem of a redeemed digest unless it carries exactly that row (fn-acct-redeemed-refuses-another-redeem). The redeem plan fn-acct-redeem-plan (books/accounts.lisp; a pure function of the configuration value, the stamp, the code, the login, the password, the host's salt observation and whether the snapshot already names the login) plans :redeem only of a delta the configuration admits at every generation and ledger, which redeems the code under that login with the verifier fn-authsec-enrol computes (fn-acct-redeem-plan-is-admitted-and-redeems); after that delta is applied the same code, login and password plan (:already-redeemed) under any later stamp, salt and snapshot (fn-acct-redeem-plan-after-its-redeem-is-already-redeemed: the crash after the publication's root barrier and before the reply); another login is (:refused :account-redeemed) (fn-acct-redeem-plan-refuses-another-login); an unknown code plans neither (fn-acct-redeem-plan-of-an-unknown-code-stages-nothing). The row keeps the verifier as text and fn-acct-text-verifier-of-verifier-text is the representation's round trip. The connection's credential snapshot fn-auth-config-with-accounts (books/nntp-auth.lisp; host-called through books/owner-config.lisp fn-ocfg-open from host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open, and fn-ocfg-open-peer from fn-owner-open-peer) is a configuration, keeps the operator's credential for a login auth.toml names, and otherwise finds the redeemed row's credential (the login's local principal fn-acct-local-principal, the row's verifier, posting); composed with fn-auth-step-principal-login-binds-exactly-the-unique-match (cited) a redeemed account's 281 installs exactly that principal. The wire (friends-accounts-2), over fn-auth-step-pinned (the dispatcher books/served.lisp fn-served-dispatch calls, reached by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at through fn-own-read, and by the owner's re-entry fn-owner-account-outcome, host/native-admin-host.lisp, through fn-ocfg-read-step): XREDEEM before a TLS layer on a protected-only listener answers 483 and changes nothing (fn-auth-step-pinned-xredeem-before-tls-is-483); after 381, XREDEEM PASS PASSWORD answers nothing and holds the session (handshakingp, so the served fold stops) with exactly the cached code, login and password and no subject (fn-auth-step-pinned-xredeem-pass-holds-for-the-owner; a hold binds nobody and keeps the role, fn-auth-step-redeem-hold-keeps-the-role); a holding session answers the owner's (:account-outcome WORD) 281 exactly when WORD is :bound, else 482, and leaves the hold (fn-auth-step-pinned-redeem-outcome-answers-the-word). An event no client's octets made (fn-auth-client-eventp false: books/wire.lisp's framer emits only :command, :article and :reject) on a session not holding for the owner's word gets no reply and no submission (fn-auth-step-pinned-host-event-answers-nothing), and, unless it is the host's :tls-established or :sasl-context, leaves the session unchanged (fn-auth-step-pinned-stray-event-changes-nothing): an owner outcome arriving after the hold ended was answered 501 by the reader step, a syntax error the client never caused (lane compress-8). The owner's plan (host/native-admin-host.lisp fn-acct-host-owner-redeem-stage, run by host/native/admin.lisp fnn-owner-account-redeem under the owner mutex inside fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked) is fn-acct-redeem-bounded-plan over the live configuration: where fn-acct-redeem-plan redeems, it redeems exactly while the credential table is under the profile's max-credentials, else (:refused :account-credential-bound) (fn-acct-redeem-bounded-plan-refuses-exactly-past-the-operator-bound); the word fn-acct-redeem-word is :bound only for a resume or a :redeem whose publication answered :accepted, i.e. after fn-owner-reconfigure-complete installed the durable record (fn-acct-redeem-word-is-bound-only-after-a-durable-redeem); an unknown code stages nothing and is refused (fn-acct-redeem-word-of-an-unknown-code-is-refused); after its redeem is published the same request is (:already-redeemed) and :bound under any later stamp, salt, snapshot, count and bound (fn-acct-redeem-bounded-plan-after-its-redeem-is-bound: the crash cut FN_ACCOUNT_TEST_STOP_AFTER_PUBLISH). Source extension PRF-1123 supplies the full-result command framing and held-prefix bridge at fn-served-step; fn-own-read-is-served-step-on-pinned-prefix is the existing owner effect boundary under fn-own-relation. Native region-consumption and account-outcome persistence remain separate. Not covered: that a guessed code finds no row is the crypto seam's preimage resistance (A-CRYPTO); P6's publication theorems are PRF-028 (certified again at the current digest since c7072ddc: served-path-scale's manifest certify-20260926T123813Z-1816946 covers its thirteen theorems). EXTENSION (lanes public-node-2 and -3, 2026-09-27): `fn operator CONFIG account delete LOGIN` (books/native-admin.lisp, host host/native-admin-host.lisp) stages config delta code 27 (:account-delete), which tombstones the login's redeemed rows (mark 7: digest and login kept, verifier dropped) and withdraws nothing (fn-acct-delete-apply-unfolds). KEYSTONE fn-acct-delete-is-admitted-exactly-when-held-and-unobligated: admitted exactly when the login is well formed, held, and no signing binding, moderator role or consumer binding names it. KEYSTONE fn-acct-delete-keeps-the-login-taken. KEYSTONE fn-auth-config-with-accounts-after-an-account-delete-offers-only-the-operators-credential: every later snapshot offers only auth.toml's credential under that login. The owner's bounded plan counts the table itself (PKT-399): fn-arc-redeem-plan (books/account-redeem-count.lisp) derives TAKENP and USED from the connection-independent credential table fn-auth-config-with-accounts (auth.toml's credentials, then the live value's redeemed accounts, fn-auth-account-creds: mark 1 only, so pending invitations and login-to-principal bindings are not counted), and, under fn-auth-configp, where the unbounded plan redeems it refuses :account-credential-bound exactly when auth.toml's credentials plus the redeemed accounts reach (nfix BOUND), and is the unbounded plan otherwise (fn-arc-redeem-refuses-exactly-past-the-operator-bound). MODEL-LEVEL until the host rewire: host/native-admin-host.lisp fn-acct-host-owner-redeem-stage still passes (len creds) itself; it calls fn-arc-redeem-plan after stage 0.

proofs.title: The cheaper committed-history marker programs PKT-079 and PKT-143 allow are refused by the contract they would refine: the deferred marker leaves A <= M <= D, and an unfenced or in-place marker is refused by the byte model's discipline and its crash images
proofs.statement: Over the history model of books/store-history-required.lisp (the host-called decisions fn-hmr-open-verdict and fn-hmr-catch-up, host/native/io.lisp fnn-check-history-marker and fnn-recover's catch-up; the marker written by fnn-mark-committed at host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-publish-prepared) and the byte programs of books/byte-store-marker-program.lisp (fnn-mark-committed's syscalls): fn-hmr-deferred-commit is the step in which a live process answers success for record COUNT while the marker still counts COUNT (the marker of commit n renamed under commit n+1's reservation, the brief's shared later barrier). fn-hmr-deferred-commit-leaves-the-invariant: from any state satisfying fn-hmr-invp with a live process, the step leaves a state that does not satisfy it (A = COUNT+1 > M = COUNT). fn-hmr-deferred-commit-admits-a-lost-answered-record: from the same state, K = COUNT is below the answered prefix and (fn-hmr-open-verdict profile marker K) is (:admitted :marked K): the negation of fn-hmr-open-refuses-below-every-answered-record's conclusion, so a lost newest record that a client holds a 240 for is admitted by the next open. fn-hmr-deferred-commit-is-not-caught-up: D31 case (2) does not cover it, the catch-up over the shortened history writes nothing. The byte candidates fn-bs-marker-unfenced-program (the stage's fsync folded into the record's staging barrier: a fence drains one inode, so the marker's stage is unfenced) and fn-bs-marker-in-place-program (one overwrite of committed-history.json and one fsync) are refused executably: the model's discipline D1 (fn-bs-links-only-fencedp) rejects the first and D2 (fn-bs-never-overwrites-authorityp) the second, and on the K5 fixture a crash image of each (a garbled unit of the pending write, fn-bs-tear-write) holds a marker that is neither the old nor the new one: the open of a store that lost nothing refuses it, :history-short-of-marker 23 or :marker-damaged, so fn-bs-marker-crash-after-barrier-is-new and fn-bs-marker-crash-open-stays-admitted are false of them. fn-bs-marker-program stays the served program; its cost is seven barriers per commit, measured in the record; the one sound sharing (the next reservation renamed under the marker's root barrier before the acknowledgement) is a file-kernel and K0 change, PKT-441.
proofs.progress_note: Retired 2026-09-27 (lane log-recovery-2, PKT-838; design section 9 row 3): the marker programs it compared (books/byte-store-marker-candidates.lisp, books/byte-store-marker-program.lisp, books/store-history-required.lisp) were deleted with the per-file layout; a format-9 store has no marker (M := D). Before: Lane publish-program (2026-09-26, dev 17ff24aa). Certified on persvati (ACL2 8.7 w25 acl2-literal, 2 jobs, 300 s): run-20260926T102908Z-0df7, manifest certify-20260926T102932Z-378295, the book passed and the test book failed on a wrong witness (one garble selector for an eleven-unit write: the fixture's unit is 4 octets); run-20260926T103449Z-fa4d, manifest certify-20260926T103516Z-444060, the repaired test book passed; no book over 10 s. Teeth: a reachable history (open, one acknowledged commit, the deferred commit) asserting every hypothesis and conclusion of the three theorems, beside the served step at the same point (invariant kept, the open refused); the live hypothesis removed (a state that is not live: the identity step, the invariant kept, K not below A, a marker behind the history caught up); the invariant removed as corrupted-state witnesses (a marker above the history: the deferred step lands on the invariant and the open at K refuses; a marker behind: caught up). The byte refutations are ground images on the K5 fixture (byte-store-k0-marker-tests' pair): admissible choices, the observation neither old nor new, the open's refusal by name, and the served program's image at the same cut for contrast. Not claimed: a general theorem over the unfenced program's crash images (the ground counterexample refutes the universal claims); any program of the served path changed; the sound sharing (PKT-441).

proofs.title: The operator's daily verbs decide starting, stale and the exit scale in ACL2: health's code never overlaps the seven outcome codes, a held lock where an owner would listen is starting, and an offline control verb runs offline exactly when the lock was seen free
proofs.statement: books/native-health.lisp: fn-nh-exit-code-is-zero-or-past-the-outcome-codes: for every V, (fn-nh-exit-code V) is 0 or at least 19, and it satisfies fn-outcome-codep (books/outcome-class.lisp, reading *fn-outcome-codes*) exactly when it equals (fn-outcome-code :accepted); host: fnn-operator-execute-health (host/native/operator.lisp) returns fn-native-health-host-exit of the rendered report, which is fn-nh-exit-code (fn-nh-report-exit-of-render). fn-nh-exit-code-cases (exported): with at most eight outcomes the code is in (0 19 20..27). fn-nh-fence-of-starting-iff: with no clone fence and a route that did not reach an owner, fn-nh-fence-of is :starting exactly when the lock is :held and an owner would listen, and a free or absent lock is never fenced; host: fn-native-health-host-fenced from fnn-operator-health-report. fn-nh-fence-of-route restated over the fourth observation. books/native-control.lisp fn-native-control-liveness-decides: the offline executor starts (fn-native-control-liveness-offlinep) exactly when the lock was observed :free or :absent, the decision is :stale exactly when a socket node is present and the lock is free or absent, and it is one of :live :stale :offline :held; host: fn-native-control-host-liveness from fnn-operator-execute-admin, which removes a :stale node under the control-path lease (fnn-control-remove-stale-offline) and refuses :held without starting the executor. Continuation (operator-daily-2): books/native-health.lisp fn-nh-starting-clears-on-listening (PKT-454): fn-nh-health-step, the host's whole decision for one health invocation, is (:fenced :starting) exactly when no clone fence is present, the lock is :held, an owner would listen and the route is :offline; with the socket present and the owner answering, the same lock, fence and listener give (:answered OCTETS) and no fence; host: fn-native-health-host-step from fnn-operator-health-report. books/native-control-reason.lisp fn-native-control-printed-reason-is-the-decisions (PKT-453 (a)): for every FNCT status the client's step (fn-native-control-reasoned-client-step of fn-native-control-reasoned-reply-read) on the reasoned reply the owner sealed (fn-native-control-reasoned-reply-encode STATUS REASON) is (:status STATUS (fn-nctrl-reason-word REASON)), and for a refusal that named a reason the printed detail (fn-native-control-reply-detail) is fn-nctrl-reason-word of it; host: fnn-control-handle-client seals it (fn-native-control-host-reasoned-reply-encode) with the reason fnn-owner-control-submit-serialized (fn-owner-operator-refusal-reason) or fnn-owner-live-admin-serialized (the plan's reason or fn-owner-reconfigure-reason) answered; fnn-control-reasoned-exchange steps and fnn-operator-execute-post / fnn-operator-execute-admin print the detail (fnn-operator-status-detail).

proofs.title: Pull liveness: a peer's 430 for a listed id is an answer of the class unavailable; the round goes on, the id holds the cursor for at most BOUND consecutive complete rounds and is dropped, logged, exactly at the bound; the counts are durable in FNPL
proofs.statement: Over the functions host/native/pull-service.lisp fnn-pull-round calls (fn-pull-session-step through fn-pull-session-step-pair, fn-pull-session-close, fn-pull-session-close-effects; books/peer-pull-session.lisp) and fnn-pull-journal-open / fnn-pull-journal-append call (fn-pull-journal-scan with its committed offset, fn-pull-records-replay, fn-pull-cursor-envelope; books/peer-pull.lisp). A peer's 430 to the round's ARTICLE for a listed id is an answer of the class unavailable: the round records the id, reopens the local transit connection (:reopen-local) and goes on with the remaining ids. fn-pull-session-step-marks-unavailable-only-on-the-peers-reply: a host step that changes the unavailable ids is a (:remote . octets) event after the preamble, in phase :article, and adds exactly the article in hand. fn-pull-session-close-advances-only-past-a-fully-answered-round (PRF-100's keystone restated; its conclusion strengthened per id, not weakened): if the host's close moves the advance count, the round is :done, every listed id drew 235/435/437 from the local node OR was answered 430 by the peer in this round with its consecutive count reaching the bound, the new instant is the peer's DATE less the overlap, and PENDING is nil; fn-pull-close-advances-past-all-answered-when-nothing-is-unavailable keeps PRF-100's conclusion verbatim for a round with nothing unavailable, and the old form is a must-fail witness in tests/acl2/peer-pull-tests.lisp. fn-pull-session-unavailable-id-is-retried-below-the-bound: an id unavailable with 1 + its count below the bound leaves the instant and advance count where they were (so the peer lists it again: RFC 3977 7.4, not proved) and a complete round journals its count as exactly one more; fn-pull-session-complete-round-past-the-bound-advances: a complete round in which every unavailable id reached the bound advances and clears PENDING, the log naming each id whose count reached the bound in that round (dropped exactly at the bound, never before). fn-pull-records-replay-is-the-replay: the records the open scans back from a journal of cursor appends (one :pull-unavailable frame per PENDING entry, then the committing :pull-cursor frame) fold to exactly fn-pull-replay's cursor, so fn-pull-journal-is-the-cursor-at-every-cut (PRF-100, cited, its statement over the four-field cursor) holds of the on-disk journal; fn-pull-records-replay-ignores-an-uncommitted-tail: unavailable records whose cursor record never became durable change nothing (and the scan truncates them). BOUND is the peer row pull-unavailable-rounds (`peer pull NAME SECONDS ROUNDS`), else the local policy *fn-pull-default-unavailable-rounds* = 5: a work bound on re-listing, not a data cap. Trusted, not proved: that the peer lists again what it listed for the same instant (RFC 3977 7.4).
proofs.progress_note: A-HOST dropped from this row's assumptions (lane audit-fixes, keystone-audit G3-9, 2026-09-27): no theorem of the row takes fn-assume-host-report or fn-assume-host-events (books/assumptions.lisp) as a hypothesis, so the citation was decorative (AGENTS.md: the theorems that use a named assumption mention it). The host's honest I/O remains the trust boundary these theorems sit inside, not a hypothesis of them.

proofs.title: The two-node consumer exchange: the receiving node's stored event keeps the carrier's authored source and both signatures, and the served poll report is the event's exact encoding or a named :oversize refusal
proofs.statement: (a) The subject is fn-pa-authorized-event, which host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-transit's :ok arm calls through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-peer-carried-event for NNTP and BP transit and served POSTs. fn-osp-authorized-event-keeps-the-carried-source-and-signatures (books/owner-signed-post): whenever it forms an event, fn-pa-carrier-form of the received octets is :ok; the event's authored source is exactly the carrier's source (nth 1); its article record is exactly fn-record-encode of the record over the received octets (so the stored projection holds the carrier); and fn-hsig-authorize-at holds of the carrier's source version, principal, keys, source and signatures (nth 4) with the host's primitive observations: the two signatures the verdict authorized are the carrier's. The hop-local Path may differ between nodes; the source and signatures may not. (c) The subject is fn-col-poll-report (books/consumer-owner-local), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-poll serves. fn-col-poll-report-fits-or-refuses-by-name (books/consumer-owner-local-progress): a non-page or empty page is fn-col-poll's answer unchanged; a page whose encoded report satisfies fn-ncl-poll-event-bytesp is (:poll cursor report) with the event's exact encoding (fn-col-poll-report-octets: fn-stxa-encode, or fn-rcon-record-encode-impl for a legacy record); a page whose report is octets longer than *fn-stxa-max-octets* is (:refused :oversize). fn-col-poll-report-is-a-page-or-a-refusal: never a write, so an oversize article leaves the position unchanged. (b) PKT-256's CORRUPTED-state witness for fn-cp-ack-writes-only-a-forward-declaration-in-scope's frontier premise and (d) PKT-262's witness (a consumer registered after an article polls it first: intended) are teeth in tests/acl2/consumer-owner-local-progress-tests. Not claimed: that the :oversize antecedent is witnessed concretely (it needs a report above 4,294,966,940 octets, reachable only for a profile whose record bound R exceeds *fn-stxa-max-octets*; PKT-467); an explicit skip past an oversize article (PKT-466); anything about the Python consumer (an external client whose lock, resend and correlation are its own bookkeeping under CNS-003); BP carriage (PKT-333 phase 2).

proofs.title: A login's signing binding is a row of the configuration the owner publishes live: at start and on `principal bind|unbind' the configuration binds every login as the credential file does, an open session is decided under the table its connection pinned, a connection opened after the publication under the published table, and the verb says `applied' only after the owner published
proofs.statement: Subject fn-lb-ocfg-gate (books/login-binding-live.lisp), called over the octet buffer by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-login-gate-buffer (fn-ars-lb-ocfg-gate-is-reference) from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-attempt-served; fn-lb-sync-plan, called by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-login-bindings-plan from host/native/auth.lisp fnn-native-auth-publish-bindings (at start in fnn-native-auth-install and on control request 14 in host/native/login-bindings.lisp), whose delta lists are staged by fn-owner-reconfigure-deltas and published by fn-owner-reconfigure-complete (fn-ocl-publish) through fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked. (1) By definition (fn-lb-ocfg-gate-unfolds, not cited) the host's verdict is fn-lb-owner-gate (PRF of books/login-binding.lisp; its keystones apply) with the policy of the live configuration and the binding table of the in-flight submission's connection pin. (2) The delta (books/config.lisp :login-binding, code 17, rows (LOGIN PRINCIPAL-HEX "" 2) of the accounts slot): fn-lb-binding-delta-binds-the-login binds exactly the given principal (nil unbinds), fn-lb-binding-delta-keeps-other-logins leaves every other login, fn-lb-binding-delta-is-admitted is admitted against every configuration for a bindable login and a 32-octet principal. (3) fn-lb-sync-binds-file-logins-as-the-file-does-and-keeps-account-bindings: when the plan is :ok, applying its deltas binds every login as the credential file's table does, except a redeemed account the file does not name, whose binding stays as the configuration holds it (PRF-388); fn-lb-pairs-deltas-set-exactly-their-logins is the fold; fn-lb-pairs-deltas-ignore-the-record-coordinates lets the host's records of at most 64 deltas compose. (4) fn-lb-a-publication-keeps-every-open-connections-table (no hypotheses): staging and publishing any change leaves every connection's pinned table; fn-lb-an-open-session-is-decided-under-its-pinned-table: over any owner trace that does not re-pin the connection, the gate decides its submission under the table pinned before the trace. (5) fn-lb-a-connection-opened-after-a-publication-is-bound-anew: with nothing staged, a durable publication of the binding deltas (the owner's history relation before, fn-ocl-config-historyp; no stale pin at the fresh identifier after, which fn-ocfg-statep implies) and a connection opened next, that connection's table binds every login the deltas name as the file does and every other as before. (6) fn-native-auth-admin-effect-word-applied-only-when-published (fn-native-auth-admin-effect-word-restart-unless-no-owner, restated with the owner's answer, stays its PRF's): `applied' only when the lock was not seen free or absent and the owner answered :accepted. Teeth: tests/acl2/login-binding-live-tests.lisp (a witness per keystone asserting every antecedent; one must-fail per hypothesis; the gate witness is login-binding-tests' constructed owner, the publication witness config-owner-live-tests' replayed ground owner) and tests/acl2/native-auth-admin-tests.lisp. Not covered: that the owner's live configuration is its history's replay across every publication (the maintained relation; PRF-028 (certified again at the current digest since c7072ddc: served-path-scale's manifest certify-20260926T123813Z-1816946 covers its thirteen theorems); the host's reading of the credential file (bounded transport, as before).

proofs.title: A relay serves every admitted BP neighbour at once: bp-node serve binds one listener per transport-bp boundary row that admits a session and a session on a bound listener is admitted under exactly that row; held transit is dispatched to the neighbour the route table names for its own destination and one pass offers a held row on at most one session
proofs.statement: Over the functions the host calls. LISTENERS (host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-command-bp-node now binds the current owner configuration through fn-owner-bplc-recover/begin and fn-bplc-owner-listener-ports; fn-bplc-owner-listener-ports-refines-the-configured-listener-set (PRF-1075) equates this actual projection to fn-bpaj-listener-ports under carried configuration validity; fnn-bpnc-accept-loop accepts only its installed stable listener generation; each session's admission is fn-bpaj-session-principal inside fn-bpaj-tcpcl-ingress-result, host fn-owner-bp-tcpcl-ingress): fn-bpaj-listener-session-is-admitted-under-its-row: for PORT in (fn-bpaj-listener-ports CFG) and an EID ANNOUNCED, the session principal on (:tcp4 127.0.0.1 PORT 127.0.0.1) is (:admitted NAME GEN) for the listener's boundary NAME when ANNOUNCED is NAME's unique transport-bp EID, else (:refused :eid-mismatch): never :ambiguous-peer or :no-trust-profile. fn-bpaj-admitted-session-arrives-on-a-bound-listener: an admitted session on a positive port arrived on a port in the set. fn-bpaj-listener-ports-are-distinct. DISPATCH (fnn-bpnode-dispatch-one's :progress event with fn-bpnp-host-routes = (:table TABLE), through fn-bpnj-step to fn-bpnp-step and fn-bpnp-progress-step): fn-bpnp-progress-dispatch-names-the-routed-hop: when the step proposes :persist-dispatch, the record applies (:ready), its peer (written into the row's next-hop slot 11 by fn-bpnp-dispatched-held) is an EID, and its text is the EID of the route fn-bprt-outbound-choice selects for the named row's own destination (a :hop; the route is a live matching one by the carried fn-bprt-next-hop-names-a-live-matching-route); fn-bpnp-table-route-peer-is-the-routed-hop. proofs.title: The open's freshness and archive-binding checks, the admission's identity test and the refresh's group index run in one pass, each equal to its unchanged logical definition
proofs.statement: Four linear executions of whole-state checks, each equal to the unchanged :logic definition. fn-articles-freshp-is-one-pass (books/acceptance.lisp, no hypothesis): (fn-fr-freshp articles) = (fn-articles-freshp articles); fn-fr-freshp folds the articles once with a hash set of the memberships seen, checking each article against the earlier ones (disjointness is symmetric: fn-fr-disjointp-commutes), and is the :exec branch of fn-articles-freshp. fn-node-articles-have-archive-bindingsp-is-indexed (books/node.lisp, no hypothesis): (fn-nab-articles-boundp a b p) = (fn-node-articles-have-archive-bindingsp a b p); the bindings and pins are indexed once in two hash tables, the first element with a key kept (the linear searches' answer), and it is the :exec branch. Both run inside fn-statep and fn-node-statep, which the host reaches at every Store open through fn-sco-store-open's fn-sco-finalize-from test (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-open-extended; fn-sn-open-observed's tests are carried), at every reader open through fn-nntp-projectionp and fn-own-reader-context's fn-peer-open-session (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open -> fn-ocfg-open -> fn-own-open), and at each BP acceptance check (fn-bpi-node-record-committedp). fn-retain-known-id-scanp-is-known-idp (books/retention.lisp, no hypothesis, iff): fn-retain-admissiblep's :exec walks the pins and releases for the identity instead of consing their identity lists; reached from fn-node-prepare on every POST and every replayed acceptance. fn-gidx-refresh-is-build (books/owner.lisp; hypothesis: the old index is (fn-gidx-build old-articles) or NIL, which fn-own-view-okp carries): (fn-gidx-refresh buckets old new) = (fn-gidx-build new); fn-own-refresh installs it, so a refresh after one acceptance puts the new article's entries into the old index instead of rebuilding it; fn-own-refresh-preserves-relation (books/owner-invariants.lisp) holds unchanged. The executed functions reach none of fn-all-article-memberships, fn-memberships-conflictsp, fn-pair-memberp, fn-node-find-binding, fn-retain-find-id, fn-retain-obligation-ids or member-equal (asserted over the callee closure in the test book). fn-retain-ids-disjointp (books/retention.lisp, codex t36, 2026-10-02): fn-retain-statep's pin/release disjointness conjunct is this enabled mbe wrapper, :logic exactly (not (intersection-equal pin-ids release-ids)); its :exec fills a local fn-keyset hash set with the release ids and looks up each pin id when there are 8 or more releases (fn-retain-ks-disjointp-is-disjoint, no hypothesis), else walks (fn-retain-ks-disjointp-walk-is-logic); since lane generators-2 (2026-10-03) fn-retain-ks-disjointp is a def-keyset-check declaration (books/def-keyset-check.lisp), its fill, scan, wrapper, walk and both bridges generated. Scope: O(P+R) time; allocates a temporary keyset of O(R) per call (~44 MB @R=100k); measured on hbox at P=R=100k: the old conjunct 144.7 s, the whole new recognizer 0.065 s per call (planning/evidence/retain-disjoint-2026-10-02.md).

proofs.title: A friend whose keys succeeded since genesis is peered under its current keys: a peering document binds a principal this node's keyring holds only by its current enrolment (the genesis identity otherwise), and the confirm of a current acceptor completes at its consumption; `peer list' shows the carriage budget an older reader still parses past; the transit log names the admission verdict beside the class; `account list' names a binding row
proofs.statement: Subject fn-pinv-document (books/peer-invite.lisp) under the owner's keyring (fn-owner-hybrid-snapshots), reached through fn-pinv-issue-plan, fn-pinv-accept-record-plan / fn-pinv-accept-step and fn-pinv-confirm-record-plan / fn-pinv-confirm-step, which host/peer-invite-host.lisp wraps for host/native/peer-invite.lisp fnn-pinv-owner-issue, fnn-pinv-owner-accept, fnn-pinv-owner-confirm and fnn-pinv-owner-enrol-confirmed. (1) fn-pinv-document-binds-a-known-principal-only-at-its-current-keys: when the keyring has a generation for P (fn-hl-current-for-principal), a document that passes is signed by exactly P's current enrolment (a superseded key set is refused `not-current-keys`, a revoked P `revoked`). (2) fn-pinv-document-of-a-current-enrolment-is-accepted: every other check passing and P's current enrolment the carrier's key set, the document is (:ok SOURCE P K) with no genesis condition; a never-succeeded principal enrolled at its genesis keys is the instance. (3) fn-pinv-document-of-an-unknown-principal-is-the-genesis-decision: a principal with no generation is decided exactly as under the empty keyring (the genesis identity, `genesis`). (4) fn-pinv-an-enrolling-accept-is-the-clis-plan: whenever the owner's accept step enrols, the accept plan under the empty keyring (the accepting CLI's fn-pinv-acceptance-source) is the owner's. (5) fn-pinv-confirm-step-current-only-for-the-consuming-current-acceptor and fn-pinv-confirm-of-a-current-acceptor-completes-at-its-consumption: the confirm step answers (:current), enrolling nothing, only for a bound acceptance whose row this acceptance consumed and whose principal is current at its keys, and does so right after that consumption. (6) books/native-admin-peer-budget.lisp, the report fn-native-admin-query-report (host/native-admin-host.lisp fn-native-admin-host-query-report, `peer list`) and fn-nls-report (:peers) serve: fn-native-admin-peer-budget-decode-reads-the-configured-budget, fn-native-admin-peer-extra-decode-reads-past-the-budget (over clean rows the older reader reads the same values and leaves the budget words), fn-native-admin-peer-budget-row-octets-extends-the-older-line. (7) fn-pcb-transit-refusal-detail-is-the-class-and-the-verdict (no hypotheses; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-refusal-class from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-transit-class) with books/owner-log.lisp fn-olog-detail-fields (by definition, not cited): the transit log's `detail=CLASS verdict=VERDICT`. (8) fn-acct-list-word-is-pending-only-for-a-pending-row (books/account-list.lisp, served by books/native-live-status.lisp for `account list`). Not claimed: that the keyring's succession is honest (a key statement's admission, PRF-098); an invitation from a succession-era inviter unknown to the invitee (it is refused `genesis`: no succession chain travels with the document); the POST reply naming a refused key change (PKT-473).

proofs.title: A control reply that cannot carry its value refuses by name: profile validation refuses a record bound the consumer poll reply cannot carry, and the live-status reply names a report its u32 total cannot say
proofs.statement: (a) PKT-467, the coordinator's ruling (D27: profile validation, representation and format evolution agree). The subject is fn-bs-profile-validp / fn-bs-profile-admittedp (books/byte-store-frame), which host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-upgrade-profile reaches through fn-hmr-upgrade-verdict / fn-profile-upgrade-verdict and `init` through host/store-host.lisp fn-store-profile-init-verdict (fn-bs-profile-init-verdict); every open through fn-store-profile-admittedp. fn-bs-profile-invalid-reason answers :max-record-octets-above-the-poll-reply when R exceeds *fn-stxa-max-octets* (4,294,966,940: the Store frame's u32 less the kind-6 poll reply's 9 header and 346 cursor octets, the inequality fn-ncl-poll-event-bytesp checks). fn-bs-profile-valid-record-fits-a-poll-reply: for any value, fn-bs-profile-max-record-octets is at most *fn-stxa-max-octets*, and every payload fn-bs-publication-admissiblep admits (the gate host/store-host.lisp fn-store-publication-admissibility asserts for host/native/io.lisp fnn-publish) is within it. fn-col-poll-report-of-an-admitted-payload-fits (books/consumer-owner-local-progress): a page whose event encoding is such an admitted payload is served by fn-col-poll-report (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-poll) as that page, not :oversize. fn-bs-profile-v1-valid-stays-valid (books/byte-store-profile-v1) now carries R <= *fn-stxa-max-octets*, and fn-bs-profile-v1-valid-above-the-poll-reply-is-refused-by-name says the window it excludes is refused by the new name: together they characterize which saved profiles still open. (b) The subject is fn-nls-page over fn-nls-buffer (books/native-live-status), which host/native-live-status-host.lisp fn-native-live-status-host-answer answers for host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-status-answer, and fn-nls-client-step, which host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-status folds pages through. fn-nls-page-refuses-exactly-past-the-total-width: for an octet report and any offset, the client's step on the owner's page is (:refused :report-past-the-total-width) exactly when the report is longer than 2^32-1 octets; the refused reply's existing chunk field carries the word (no layout change). Not claimed: that the served store's events re-encode to at most R (the :oversize arm stays as the named refusal for a store holding an event past its own R; PKT-470); that a live-status report is bounded before it is rendered (the render is whole, octet lists: PKT-470, hot-path-checker's class); a concrete witness of either past-the-ceiling antecedent (each needs 2^32 octets; the hypothesis teeth are proved symbolically). (c) [retired by format 10: the saved-profile window refusal and the repair are gone with format 9; every format-10 profile satisfies the arm at its writing] PKT-471, the coordinator's decision (a named refusal at open, never translation-at-open). The subject is fn-spo-config-open (books/store-profile-open), the open host/native/io.lisp fnn-metadata-config-decode calls through host/store-host.lisp fn-store-metadata-config-open on every open (fnn-load-config from fnn-acquire: owner start, store recover, inspect, checkpoint, status, the offline health). fn-spo-open-of-a-saved-format-8-profile-opens-or-refuses-by-name: for every profile the format-8 encoder saved under the relation before PKT-467 (fn-bs-profile-v2-validp, frozen; fn-bs-profile-valid-is-v2-valid and fn-bs-profile-v1-valid-is-v2-valid include the current and the pre-P6 saved profiles), the open of its frame (fn-spo-saved-frame) is (:opened VALUES) when R <= *fn-stxa-max-octets* and (:refused :max-record-octets-above-the-poll-reply) otherwise, never (:rejected), the host's fault; the host prints ACL2's line (fn-spo-refusal-text) at exit 1. fn-spo-config-open-refuses-only-what-the-old-open-rejected: a refusal is never a frame fn-bs-config-decode decoded, so every store the open opened before opens the same. The repair is a separate verdict, fn-spo-repair-verdict, which fnn-command-upgrade-profile reaches through fnn-command-repair-profile on that refusal (fn-profile-upgradep is unchanged, so every fn-profile-upgrade-keeps-* theorem is unaffected): fn-spo-repair-admits-exactly-the-lowering-to-the-width: over any saved profile's frame the verdict writes exactly when the saved R exceeds *fn-stxa-max-octets* and the target is (:current ((4 . *fn-stxa-max-octets*))), what `store upgrade-profile --max-record-octets 4294966940` parses to, and the written frame opens as the saved profile with R lowered and every other field kept (fn-spo-repaired-keeps-every-other-field). Not claimed (PKT-486): that the repair's open under the lowered profile names a store holding a committed record above the lowered read bound (it would fault on the read bound; no such record is constructible below 4 GiB); a native crash witness of the repair path (it writes through the upgrade's byte program, fn-bs-profile-program-crash-is-old-or-new).

proofs.title: A peer's configuration rows and the checkpoint generations are data bounded by the profile or by their records: 1,024 rows is a work bound per delta, and the generation allocator refuses exactly at the profile's capacity
proofs.statement: Rows: an :add-peer-rows delta for an existing peer with keyed rows is refused by fn-cfg-delta-reason exactly when it carries more than *fn-cfg-max-rows* rows (fn-cfg-add-peer-rows-refuses-exactly-past-the-work-bound); applied, the group is the old group less repeated rows followed by new rows, with internal invitation receipts stripped from the affected peer and no bound on its length (fn-cfg-add-peer-rows-extends-the-filtered-group); any well-formed delta adds at most *fn-cfg-max-rows* rows to the peers slot and a delta list at most that times its length (fn-cfg-apply-delta-adds-at-most-the-work-bound, fn-cfg-apply-adds-at-most-the-work-bound); the deltas the host publishes for `peer carries` / `peer budget` (fn-pcb-extend-deltas, through fn-native-admin-plan-deltas-over from host/native-admin-host.lisp fn-native-admin-host-apply and fn-native-admin-host-owner-reconfigure) apply as the whole-group :set-peer extension (fn-pcb-extend-deltas-apply-as-the-extend-delta), so PRF-099's budget keystone carries. Generations: on a gap-free checkpoint namespace fn-cpp-next-generation is :exhausted exactly when CAPACITY names are retained and is the count otherwise, for CAPACITY within the uint32 width (fn-cpp-next-generation-refuses-exactly-at-the-profile-capacity); CAPACITY is max-transactions + 1 of the opened profile (host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-checkpoint-generation-capacity). proofs.title: A POST reads the committed count, record octets, completion debt and carriage usage without walking the history: the count is the Store's derived event index's, the three caches advance through that index, and each equals its fold under the maintained index relation
proofs.statement: Subjects, each called by host/owner-host.lisp: fn-sbud-count (books/store-budget.lisp) from fn-owner-publication-verdict, fn-owner-prepare and fn-owner-prepare-buffer (the budget fn-cvec-article-budget-for is handed), fn-owner-record-octets, fn-owner-record-debt, fn-owner-carried-usage and fn-owner-install-profile; fn-sbud-bytes-carried from fn-owner-record-octets (reached from the verdict, both prepares and fn-owner-headroom); fn-sbud-headroom-carried from fn-owner-headroom; fn-scf-debt-carried (books/store-carried-folds.lisp) from fn-owner-record-debt; fn-scf-usage-carried from fn-owner-carried-usage (fn-owner-peer-carried-relay-event). The maintained relation is fn-ceis-indexedp (the Store's derived event index is fn-cei-build of its committed history), established at every host-called open and preserved by every owner transition the host installs with no hypothesis (PRF-144 fn-osi-live-owner-store-is-indexed). The index now counts its puts (books/consumer-event-index.lisp, index = (SEQ-TRIE MSGID-TRIE . COUNT)); fn-cei-count-of-correspondence: under the correspondence the count is the history's length, so fn-sbud-count-is-used-by-definition: under fn-ceis-indexedp, fn-sbud-count = fn-sbud-used = (len records). fn-sbud-lookup-of-correspondence: under the correspondence and a history within the uint32 sequence space, fn-cei-get k is the k-th record. fn-sbud-octets-advance-is-the-suffix-fold / fn-scf-debt-advance-is-the-suffix-fold / fn-scf-tally-advance-is-the-suffix-fold: advancing over sequences k..len-1 through the index is the fold over (nthcdr k records). Keystones: fn-sbud-bytes-carried-is-the-fold (fn-ceis-indexedp and fn-sbud-octets-cache-validp: the carried octets are fn-sbud-bytes-used), fn-scf-debt-carried-is-the-record-debt (fn-ceis-indexedp and fn-cvec-debt-cache-validp: fn-cvec-record-debt), fn-scf-usage-carried-is-the-projection (fn-ceis-indexedp and fn-pcb-cache-validp: read at any evidence, fn-pcb-usage), fn-sbud-headroom-carried-is-headroom-at (fn-ceis-indexedp). fn-sbud-octets-cache-valid-after-commit keeps the stored (COUNT . SUM) valid as the history grows; fn-owner-install-profile stores the fold once at open. The logical model is unchanged: fn-sbud-used stays len and fn-sbud-bytes-used the fold; the host calls the named carried functions (an mbe would put the relation in the guard, which the :program host would evaluate). No Store transition encodes a record (the index holds the event, not its length; the octets take one record's length per record committed since the last query). Teeth: tests/acl2/store-carried-folds-tests.lisp over the live owner's Stores across a commit (owner-store-indexed-tests' *osi-before*/*osi-after*), constructed indexed Stores for a non-zero debt and usage, a removal witness per hypothesis (the crash image or a constructed stale index for the relation; a CORRUPTED cache for validity); tests/acl2/consumer-event-index-tests.lisp for the count. Not covered: the prepare's candidate test still takes len and the last cons of the history (fn-pcar-candidatep, pointer walks, PKT-474); the operator status and health reports still extend by len/nthcdr and fold the debt (PKT-474).

proofs.title: The executed BP CRC-32C and exclusive-or are the bitwise definitions: fn-bpp-crc32c-scan runs a table-driven scan and fn-bpp-xor runs logxor under a mask, each proved equal to the bitwise body every codec theorem reasons about
proofs.statement: books/bp-primary.lisp. fn-bpp-xor-is-masked-logxor (hypotheses (natp a), (natp b)): (fn-bpp-xor a b k) = (logand (logxor a b) (+ -1 (expt 2 k))), the :exec body of fn-bpp-xor's mbe, for every k (a k that is not a natural gives 0 on both sides). fn-bpp-crc32c-scan-table-is-scan (hypotheses (natp crc), (fn-cbor-octet-listp xs)): (fn-bpp-crc32c-scan-table crc xs) = (fn-bpp-crc32c-scan crc xs), where fn-bpp-crc32c-scan-table, the :exec body of fn-bpp-crc32c-scan's mbe, advances the register an octet at a time by one lookup in *fn-bpp-crc32c-table* and a shift, and the logical body advances it eight bitwise register steps (fn-bpp-crc32c-octet). The table is a defconst evaluated from fn-bpp-crc32c-octet at every octet value, and fn-bpp-crc32c-table-agrees checks all 256 entries by evaluation inside the proof. Both keystones are used by the guard proofs of the mbe functions (verify-guards fn-bpp-xor, verify-guards fn-bpp-crc32c-scan), so the executed bodies are what the guard-verified host path runs. Host lines: host/bp-node-host.lisp calls fn-bpn-send (the authoring path: fn-bpb-encode, fn-bpb-block-crc, fn-bpp-crc-octets, fn-bpp-crc32c) and fn-bpb-decode (fn-bpn-host-authored-retry; the decoder's CRC check computes the same fn-bpp-crc-octets). proofs.title: The served read's reply is written from a range of the octet buffer, and that range is the reply the served machine decided
proofs.statement: fn-served-reply-to-buffer-is-the-reply (books/served-reply-buffer.lisp; keystone): for every EFFECTS and buffer, the answer OKP of (fn-served-reply-to-buffer effects fn-octets) is (fn-srb-effects-octetsp effects) (every (:reply octets) effect carries an octet list), and when OKP holds the buffer's length is (len (fn-served-reply-octets effects)) and its range [0, len) read by fn-oct-slice-list is (fn-served-reply-octets effects). fn-served-reply-to-buffer-refusal-keeps-the-buffer: when OKP is false the buffer is unchanged. The subject is guard-verified (guard t) and conses nothing per octet: the buffer is cleared and each reply effect's octets are written by one fn-octets-append-list export call. No host function calls it any longer: since HST-023 (PKT-644) the served reply is rendered off the owner mutex by fn-splan-window (books/served-plan.lisp, PRF-248; host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-write-plan), whose windows reuse this book's fn-srb-effect-octets, and fn-owner-reply-buffer and fn-owner-chunk are deleted. This result stays as the model of the one-shot buffer write, not a served-path claim. The array's cells are the stobj's logical value by PRF-087's abstraction relation (fn-octets$corr). The exposure's observation is unchanged: fn-exp-observe-effects already reads the effects (PRF-161).

proofs.title: The served read the host calls over the octet buffer is the reference list read: fn-owner-chunk-span -> fn-scar-ocfg-read-span reads the range by index and equals fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix over the range's octets, and the wire read is fn-wire-feed-proper over the slice
proofs.statement: Subject fn-scar-ocfg-read-span (books/served-span.lisp), called by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-handle-chunk (which fills fn-octets from the socket vector with fnn-octets-fill and calls fn-owner-chunk-span with the range [0, len), no fnn-octet-list on the read path). KEYSTONE fn-scar-feed-span-is-feed-counted (no hypothesis): the served buffer fold fn-scar-feed-span, reading the range's bytes by fn-octets-get, equals the carried list counted fold fn-scar-feed-counted over (fn-oct-slice-list i end fn-octets), byte for byte. fn-scar-ocfg-read-span-is-read-tls-prefix: for natural i, end the span read is fn-scar-ocfg-read-tls-prefix over the slice. KEYSTONE fn-scar-ocfg-read-span-is-reference-under-ocl-relation: under the configured owner's relation (fn-ocl-relation) and its view trie's correspondence, the span read is fn-ocfg-read-tls-prefix over the slice, the reference read the list path already establishes (fn-scar-ocfg-read-tls-prefix-is-reference-under-ocl-relation). fn-scar-ocfg-read-span-keeps-store and fn-scar-ocfg-read-span-preserves-node-premise: the read leaves the store and its node premise. Every executable function is guard-verified (fn-scar-feed-span-consumed-is-natural). The executable (PKT-479, lane input-loop): fn-scar-step-span-core runs (mbe :logic fn-scar-feed-span :exec fn-scar-scan-span); books/served-scan.lisp fn-scar-scan-span dispatches once per framed event and books/wire-scan.lisp fn-wire-scan runs the wire machine a line at a time (the run of ordinary octets found by index, consed once onto line-rev; a whole line inside the read, from an empty retained line, built forward from the buffer by fn-wscan-slice-onto and handed to fn-wire-after-line, one cons per octet instead of two (lane input-loop-2); CR, LF, refusals and limits through fn-wire-feed-byte). KEYSTONE fn-scar-scan-span-is-feed-counted (no hypothesis): the event scan IS fn-scar-feed-counted over the slice; KEYSTONE fn-wire-scan-is-span-fold (no hypothesis): the line scan IS the octet fold fn-wire-span-fold, hence fn-wire-feed-proper over the octets it consumed (fn-wire-span-fold-is-feed-proper). Teeth: tests/acl2/served-scan-tests.lisp. Since the catalog slice (step 8) the host-called read is books/served-catalog-chain.lisp fn-scr-ocfg-read-span (equal to fn-scar-ocfg-read-span under fn-scr-owner-catalogp, fn-scr-ocfg-read-span-is-scar-ocfg-read-span); its core fn-scr-step-span-core runs (mbe :logic fn-scr-feed-span :exec fn-scr-scan-span), the same event scan with the catalog carried to the dispatcher (lane catalog-scan). KEYSTONE fn-scr-scan-span-is-feed-span (no hypothesis): that scan IS the catalog chain's byte fold on every connection and range. proofs.title: The committed event catalog abstracts to the list of held records; its cross-field invariants are established by the creator and preserved by every export; alpha of intern is the identity on the wire record
proofs.statement: fn-cat (books/catalog.lisp) is an attachable abstract stobj whose logical value is the list of held records (books/catalog-record.lisp: the wire tuple's eleven positions with the payload a natp handle into fn-arena, the byte facts, the context, the numbers and the withdrawal), oldest first, and whose executable is the indexed tables (rows by sequence, a Message-ID hash table, a (group . number) hash table, a group table of row count and next number, the octets total). fn-cat$corr states once that the count is the length, the rows below it are the list, every bound Message-ID looks up to its ascending sequences and every row's Message-ID is bound, every bound (group . number) names the first row binding it and every row's numbers are bound, every bound group maps to its row count and one past its high and every row's groups are bound, and the octets cell is the sum. The creator establishes it (create-fn-cat{correspondence}) and every export preserves it (fn-cat-commit{correspondence}: the numbers assigned one past each group's high, every table advanced without a walk; fn-cat-withdraw{correspondence} and fn-cat-redecide{correspondence}: a same-key row replacement keeps every table; fn-cat-clear{correspondence}), as defabsstobj-missing-events prints the obligations. fn-cat-intern-list-materializes: the held record the intern builds from a wire record W, materialized by handle from the arena the intern sealed, is W (alpha of intern is the identity; fn-cat-intern-is-intern-list equates the buffer intern, hypothesis-free). fn-hf-body-lines-of-is-nov-body-line-count-by-definition: the body line count column is fn-nov-body-line-count's value over fn-nntp-split-article and fn-nntp-crlf-lines. Keystones over the opened view: fn-cat-commit-keeps-rows, fn-cat-commit-new-row, fn-cat-commit-binds-fresh-numbers, fn-cat-visible-at-withdrawn (a row withdrawn at version W is visible to a version V exactly when V <= W). NOT in this target: the relation's establishment at open (entry 2 of design 1.5) and at a checkpoint. catalog-slice-2 wrote books/catalog-relation.lisp (fn-cat-history-relation, the load fold fn-cat-load, fn-cat-load-establishes-relation and the preservation by withdraw, redecide and the completion); every event was admitted in the persvati REPL session but the book is RED at certification (fn-cat-wire-list-of-redecide: the session held the delta book's redecide lemmas, which the relation book does not include), so it is not a root and none of it is claimed here (PKT-585, the continuation's first action).
