proofs.title: The committed delta equals the refresh: the view's incremental application of the one article a completion installs is fn-own-refresh's view on every projection (fn-view-apply-is-refresh); on the catalog, a commit leaves every pinned version unchanged and puts the row's article on top of the new version, and a withdrawal at version W leaves every version at or below W and removes the target from every later one
proofs.statement: The pinned view is a VERSION that a successful GROUP or LISTGROUP advances to the owner's committed view and that no other command moves (NNT-042, specs/nntp.md; gpt-6's wave-5 review section 1). PROVED over the machine the host calls (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span -> books/served-span.lisp fn-scar-ocfg-read-span -> fn-scar-dispatch = fn-served-dispatch, fn-scar-dispatch-is-served-dispatch): (1) fn-served-step-pin-is-old-or-live: after any read a served connection's pin (archive, verdicts, Message-ID trie, group buckets, control pin, pin identity) is either what it was or the live view's (fn-served-live-pin of fn-served-conn-live), and the live view is untouched, for every connection and every octet list; (2) fn-served-successful-selection-is-the-repinned-dispatch: on a GROUP/LISTGROUP line whose reply is 211 (fn-served-selectedp) the dispatch IS fn-served-dispatch-core over fn-served-repin of the connection (the fresh view with the command's own selection effects); (3) fn-served-failed-selection-keeps-the-connection: when the reply is not 211 the result connection is the input connection with only its wire framing state replaced (previous view and cursor unchanged); (4) fn-served-repin-preserves-connp: the re-pinned connection is a connection (its re-selected reader session is consistent with the live archive: fn-served-reselect keeps the group when the live view has it and sets GROUP's own cursor); (5) fn-own-read-preserves-relation / fn-own-read-step-preserves-relation restated with the two cases (the read-back fn-own-finish-read takes the pin from the served connection; the view case is fn-own-conn-okp-of-view-pin, the :advance argument); (6) fn-ocl-read-preserves-historical-relation with fn-ocl-own-read-survivor-has-history: the configured owner moves the connection's configuration pin with the view (fn-ocfg-with-read-owner, fn-own-read-repinned). fn-view-apply-is-refresh as first registered (the delta application equals the owner's refresh under fn-cat-owner-relation) is NOT proved: it needs the retrieval arms over the catalog (7b) and R at the host's entries (step 8). fn-crf-apply-article resolves the records naming the new article to its row's locks (fn-ctl-resolve-tlocks), as fn-own-refresh's cons arm does (flip-L8-2).

proofs.title: Completion by token and the shared transition: fn-cat-complete commits the pending PreparedCommit's row at its expected position with no history search and refuses a stale token or a mismatched expected by name; fn-sn-finish-held over the held record and its context is fn-sn-finish on the article arm; the ARTICLE interval preserves its context and coherent recovery resolves retained snapshots; the pinned view is a version
proofs.statement: books/catalog-commit.lisp. fn-cat-complete-by-token: for a PreparedCommit PENDING (fn-pc-p), TOKEN its token and its EXPECTED the catalog count, (fn-cat-complete token pending fn-cat) commits the row (fn-cat-at expected C') = (fn-cat-assign held C), the count is expected + 1, the pending is cleared and the result is the :article delta of that row (fn-delta-of-row); fn-cat-complete-stale-refused and fn-cat-complete-expected-mismatch-refused: a token that is not the pending's, or an expected that is not the count, is refused by name and nothing changes; fn-cat-abandon-clears, fn-cat-abandon-stale-refused; fn-cat-token-of-abandoned-attempt-is-stale: a token from an abandoned attempt cannot complete the next attempt when the txids differ (the txid is consumed per attempt; the test book shows equal txids let it through). fn-sn-finish-held-is-finish (KEYSTONE, the shared transition): for a store S (fn-sn-statep), W its completing record (fn-sn-completion-record, kept as the meaning), W an article record, H a held record with (fn-held-wire h bytes(W)) = W (alpha), bytes(W) the node's pending bytes, and CTX the context of bytes(W) under S's keyring and generation, (fn-sn-finish-held s h ctx) = (fn-sn-finish s): the finish with the record supplied and the verdict and identity delta from the context, no walk of the history, no read of the bytes. fn-sn-finish-held-refuses-a-stale-context: a context whose generation is not the store's leaves the store unchanged. fn-sn-context-fixed-between-prepare-and-finish: outside :replaying and when the completing record is not a key snapshot, fn-snrt-step, fn-sn-io, fn-sn-finish, fn-sn-finish-held and fn-sn-with-configuration preserve the keyring and generation; fn-sn-set-keyring leaves the keyring whenever it leaves the generation. Durable snapshot completion publishes the accepted snapshot; recovery derives its table and generation from the supplied replay snapshots, so neither is an unconditional old-keyring frame. fn-sn-recover-keeps-coherent-context requires fn-snh-recovery-context-coherentp: the source table and generation resolve its retained snapshots, and these snapshots equal actual identity replay of the retained history. books/catalog-context-recovery.lisp proves fn-osr-ready-establishes-catalog-recovery-context: the unchanged full fn-osr-retainedp at :ready establishes that coherence, without assuming source/recovered keyring equality. Literal ARTICLE and nonempty snapshot-recovery witnesses, reachable omission witnesses at snapshot completion and post-publication crash, and a corrupted same-generation/different-table witness distinguish these cases. fn-sn-set-keyring-advances-the-generation remains unreachable-in-composition: no native host line calls it. books/catalog-delta.lisp: fn-cat-apply-delta-step-bounded (a step touches at most its quantum of rows); the delta grammar, its one-shot application and its resumable form are defined and guard-verified, and that the resumable run under any quanta equals the one-shot application is OPEN (not proved in this lane's budget; the ground check in the test book passes by computation and is not a proof); fn-view-cancel-after-target: a cancel of a row committed when the count is W withdraws it at W, a reader at version V with target < V <= W still sees it, a reader at W + 1 does not. The composite (kind 4), retention, consumer and topic arms keep fn-sn-finish over the event; the equation with fn-own-refresh's view is PRF-202. fn-osr-ready-crash-recovery-keeps-catalog-context composes full retained readiness with every fn-sn-crash image choice and actual fn-sn-recover: crashed identity context is coherent and recovered keyring/generation equal the original. Coherence is established, not assumed as recovered equality. Readiness removal is refuted by a reachable published-before-finish snapshot, and full-carry removal by a ready corrupted generation. This is a model image/recovery dependency, not the physical canonical writer/load/owner installation boundary.

KEYSTONE fn-auth-step-pinned-answers-500-to-a-keyword-help-does-not-list: for every AS, LINE, ARCHIVE, INDEX, VERDICTS, CONFIG, OBSERVATION and INJECTION, if (fn-auth-sessionp AS), AS is not handshaking TLS, its peer session awaits no transit article, its POST session awaits no body, its reader session is open (openp = t), (fn-nntp-command-inputp LINE), the first token of LINE is a keyword token, the arguments are within RFC 3977 section 3.1's bound, and (not (fn-nntp-served-keywordp keyword)), then (fn-auth-step-pinned AS ... (list :command LINE)) has effects (fn-auth-single AS "500 command not recognized"), no submission, and session AS. fn-auth-step-pinned is the dispatcher books/served.lisp fn-served-dispatch calls for every framed command line (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-serve-client -> fn-own-read -> fn-served-step -> fn-served-feed -> fn-served-dispatch). fn-nntp-served-keywordp is membership (RFC 3977 section 3.1 case-insensitively, fn-nntp-keywordp) in *fn-nntp-served-command-table*, 28 keywords in six rows; fn-nntp-served-keywordp-unfolds writes it out as the disjunction the dispatchers test. fn-nntp-help-renders-the-served-command-table-by-definition: (fn-nntp-help SESSION) = (fn-nntp-multi SESSION "100 help text follows" (fn-nntp-help-table-lines *fn-nntp-served-command-table*)). proofs.title: LIST NEWSGROUPS and LIST MOTD show exactly the descriptions and message the connection's pinned configuration holds, set by a live :set-group-description record (code 20) that changes only the name it keys
proofs.statement: Over the served step the host runs (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at -> fn-served-step), a framed LIST NEWSGROUPS [wildmat] line answers fn-nntp-list-newsgroups-described over the pinned archive's groups and the descriptions of the connection's posting configuration's listing (fn-served-step-list-newsgroups-is-the-described-listing), and LIST MOTD answers fn-nntp-list-motd over that listing's message (fn-served-step-list-motd-is-the-configured-message); a description is sent when it is non-empty printable ASCII and otherwise the (no description) marker, and with no listing the reply is the marker listing of before (fn-nntp-described-lines-of-no-descs). The listing of the posting configuration books/owner-agent.lisp fn-oag-post-config builds (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-post-config; installed by fn-ocl-publish after each published record) holds, for a group G, G's description in the configuration's eleventh slot exactly when G is served and has one (fn-oag-description-of-the-listing), and the node's message lines (fn-oag-motd-of-the-listing). Over fn-cfg-apply-delta (replay and live staging), the :set-group-description delta for NAME makes NAME's description its pieces concatenated (fn-cfg-description-after-set-is-its-pieces), leaves every other name's text (fn-cfg-description-after-set-of-another-name), makes the node's message (NAME "") its lines (fn-cfg-motd-after-set-is-its-lines), and no other kind touches the slot (fn-cfg-descriptions-of-other-kinds); fn-cfg-delta-reason refuses a name that is neither "" nor a live group (:no-such-group, by definition) and admits only the delta's own printable rows (fn-cfg-admitted-description-rows-are-printable). The reader listing is not an input of the injection decision (fn-inj-decide-ignores-the-listing).

proofs.title: The process heap is the store profile's figure: an accepted figure holds every store the profile admits and fits the observed machine; a profile the machine cannot hold is refused by name
proofs.statement: RE-MEASURED (lane reservation-figure, 2026-09-27): the figure's terms are the runtime's today. STATE: fn-heap-arena-octets is the paged arena (arena-offheap stage 1): USED + one 256 KiB page + 32 octets a page, never 3 USED (a named parameter lane arena-offheap-3 replaces with its cache bound; the keystones use only fn-heap-arena-octets-monotone); 48 N of handles; 2 N (12,288 + 320 G): the measured live state a record less its payload after per-record-state (the log kernel holds a COUNT) and catalog-columns (8 to 10 KB a record posted or reopened, plus 1.3 KB for realistic Message-IDs), where 5,120 was below the measurement. OPEN: since log-open-stream (PRF-283) and rm2-format9 the open reads one log entry at a time and the full replay takes each record into a 1 MiB chunk (*fn-heap-open-chunk-octets* = *fn-srs-chunk-octets*): fn-heap-store-open-octets (profile ou on) = 2 x 16 x 2 x (chunk + R) + 2 OU (the checkpoint suffix's vectors) + 2 x 1,024 ON; the 64 OU of list copies and 16 KiB a record are gone (the scale preset's open 49,152 -> 2,655 MB). The explosion of `init --profile scale --max-transactions 1048576 --max-article-octets 4096' (reservation 41,961,201 MB) is the membership product 2 x T x 320 x G at G = 65,535 (the scale preset's, the codec ceiling): nothing but G bounds a store's memberships (the history budget charges an article its payload, books/store-budget-stored.lisp), so it is the admitted worst case, not a double count; at G = 16 the same profile's state is 35,633 MB (tests/acl2/heap-reservation-tests.lisp pins both). STATUS: books/heap-reservation.lisp fn-heap-status-decide, called by host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-print-store-line (`operator CONFIG status' and `health'), is the launcher's run reservation over the store on disk; KEYSTONE fn-heap-status-decide-is-the-launchers-run-reservation: (equal (fn-heap-status-decide profile core nursery observations observed) (fn-heap-reserve-operation-decide :run profile core nursery observations (fn-heap-reserve-run-connections bound) observed)) for every owner bound. Before, status printed connection-budget's launch figure (fnn-heap-decision, now removed): 39,519 MB where the launcher reserves 4,662 MB for the mission's top rung on 123 GiB. Figures (core 389 MB, 64 MiB nursery): small 1,924 -> 1,232 MB at its bounds, its first run 672 -> 997 MB (up: the measured record state); development 7,934 -> 7,506; scale 221,127 -> 173,021. Record: planning/evidence/reservation-figure-2026-09-27.md. RE-DERIVED (lane reservation-after-flip, 2026-09-27; supersedes the list figure below for every command): since the records flip the served state is the payload arena, so books/heap-store-figure.lisp models what a process holding a store of USED payload octets in N records needs, having opened an input of OU octets in ON records, at the collector's TRIGGER: fn-heap-store-need = DYN + 3 USED (the arena's byte array, doubling, old copy live during a resize) + 48 N (handles) + 2 N (5,120 + 320 G) (each record's retained small objects and group memberships, twice for the collector; measured 3.5-4.8 KiB and 0.25 KiB) + 2 x 16 x 2 OU + 2 x 16,384 ON (the full replay's transient: the recovery decodes the records as octet lists; measured about 54 B per octet and 34 KiB per record) + 2 x 16 x (R + 3 HDR) + 2 x fn-ock-capture-budget (the request in flight and both buffers) + 2 TRIGGER. DYN is the image's dynamic content: CORE is the image observation (FILE . DYNAMIC) (host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-image-observation), a natural CORE being the whole file as before. TRIGGER is fn-heap-nursery-trigger (d nursery) = max(8 MiB, min(cap, d/16)), which host/native/io.lisp fnn-gc-nursery-octets now calls; the figure fn-heap-store-figure-octets = fn-heap-with-nursery (the base, nursery), the least D of three candidates with D >= base + 2 trigger(D) (fn-heap-with-nursery-holds-the-trigger, for every D at least the figure). OBSERVED (the probe's (OCTETS . RECORDS) of the store's history files, transaction files counted; host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-history-observation) bounds the open's input (fn-heap-open-octets-bound, -records-bound; H and T when NIL); the state stays at H and T since a run grows the store. KEYSTONE fn-heap-store-figure-holds-every-store: (implies (and (natp d) (<= (fn-heap-store-figure-octets profile core nursery observed) d) (<= (nfix used) (nfix H)) (<= (nfix n) (nfix T)) (<= (nfix ou) (fn-heap-open-octets-bound profile observed)) (<= (nfix on) (fn-heap-open-records-bound profile observed))) (<= (fn-heap-store-need profile core used n ou on (fn-heap-nursery-trigger d nursery)) d)). fn-heap-figure-octets is the unobserved store figure; KEYSTONE fn-heap-decide-admits-every-store-the-profile-admits now concludes that store need (ou <= H, on <= T) within the decision's megabytes and those within the machine. fn-heap-operation-decide sizes EVERY command by the observation (:init by the empty store, fn-heap-operation-observation) and the offline verbs by the larger of their list copies and the store figure; KEYSTONE fn-heap-operation-decide-holds-the-store (every action; the member hypothesis removed after proving the weakened theorem). heap-reservation: the threads are 12 fixed + 2 I/O loops + 16 control clients whatever the connections (fn-heap-thread-count; host fnn-mux-thread-count calls it), the core outside the dynamic space is the core file (fn-heap-core-file); fn-heap-reserve-decide-holds-every-thread-the-node-runs drops (natp connections); init judges the first run of the empty store it makes (fn-heap-reserve-first-run-decide). The small preset: 1,662 MB at its bounds on the production image (1,736 on the image-floor core), 583 MB for the run of an empty store and 791 MB for the 1,000-post store (dev before: 824 MB for all); 925 and 1,133 MB in all with 30 threads (before 1,316). fn-heap-small-profile-run-fits-a-small-machine replaces -fits-a-small-machine (the nursery hypothesis removed after proving the weakened theorem). Record: planning/evidence/reservation-after-flip-2026-09-27.md. books/heap-figure.lisp. fn-heap-decide (profile core nursery observations) is the host-called subject: host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-decision calls it, from fnn-command-heap (the `heap -- ARGV` probe the installed packaging/fn runs before it execs the command with --dynamic-space-size MB) and fnn-heap-print-store-line (the line `operator CONFIG status` and `health` print). The figure fn-heap-figure-octets = CORE + NURSERY + 2 x 16 x (2H + R) + 2 x fn-ock-capture-budget(profile), in SBCL megabytes rounded up (fn-heap-mb-of); the machine is fn-heap-machine-octets, the least positive observation. KEYSTONE fn-heap-decide-admits-every-store-the-profile-admits: (implies (and (fn-bs-profile-admittedp profile) (equal (car d) :heap) (<= used (fn-bs-profile-max-history-octets profile)) (natp core) (natp nursery)) (and (<= (+ core nursery (* 32 (+ used used R)) (* 2 (fn-ock-capture-budget profile))) (* 2^20 (fn-heap-decision-mb d))) (<= (* 2^20 (fn-heap-decision-mb d)) (fn-heap-machine-octets observations)))) with d = (fn-heap-decide profile core nursery observations): for every history of USED octets within H (the store budget's bound, fn-sbud-verdict-at), the image, the nursery, the lists at sixteen bytes per octet with the collector's copy, and both checkpoint buffers fit the megabytes passed, which fit the machine. (natp used) was removed after proving the weakened theorem. fn-heap-decide-refuses-exactly-past-the-machine: for an admitted profile and an observed machine the decision is (:heap MB WORD MACHINE-MB) when MB x 2^20 <= machine and (:refused :machine-cannot-hold-profile MB MACHINE-MB) otherwise; fn-heap-decision-exit-code-of-a-refusal: a refusal exits 1 (outcome-class :refused). The small preset (*fn-heap-small-request*: the development base with T 16384, H 8 MiB, R 196608, G 16, K 128) is admitted and fn-heap-small-profile-fits-a-small-machine: with core <= 512 MiB and nursery <= 64 MiB it is accepted on every machine of at least 1536 MiB (OpenBSD's default datasize); (heap-figure's fn-heap-init-request and its two theorems are retired from this row, 2026-09-27: no host line calls it; init's choice is books/heap-reservation.lisp fn-heap-init-decide.) Scope: the 16 B per octet is the octet-list representation's cons (rep-wave-d section 1.2); the second history copy is the open's transient; the model states retained octets, not SBCL's allocator, and the native case measures VmHWM against it. EXTENSION (lane image-floor, HST-017): books/heap-reservation.lisp fn-heap-reserve-decide (profile core nursery observations connections), the subject host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-reservation calls from fnn-command-heap, is fn-heap-decide's decision and, when that accepts an admitted profile, the stack (fn-heap-stack-kib: the constant *fn-heap-stack-octets*, 1,024 KiB, since lane served-line-iterative made the served path's stack need independent of the article: least 142 KiB for 16 lines, 2,000,000 lines and one 4 MiB line; the per-line term 512 KiB + 40 x (floor(A/2) + 1024) is retired) and THREADS = connections + fn-native-control-max-active-clients + 12; the whole HEAP + CORE + THREADS x (STACK + 4 MiB) is refused by name (:machine-cannot-hold-threads) past the machine. KEYSTONE fn-heap-reserve-decide-holds-every-thread-the-node-runs: (implies (and (fn-bs-profile-admittedp profile) (equal (car r) :heap) (natp connections)) (and (equal (fn-heap-decision-mb r) (fn-heap-decision-mb (fn-heap-decide ...))) (<= (+ connections clients 12) threads) (<= *fn-heap-stack-octets* (* 1024 stack-kib)) (<= (+ (* 2^20 mb) (nfix core) (* threads (+ (* 1024 stack-kib) 4 MiB))) (fn-heap-machine-octets observations)))); fn-heap-reserve-decide-refuses-exactly-past-the-machine and -keeps-heap-figures-refusals. Scope: the stack constant rests on a measurement of compiled frames on SBCL 2.6.8 (served-line-iterative's record section 5; image-floor's section 4), pinned by tests/test_native_image_floor.py's stack witnesses, not a theorem about frames. INIT (PKT-582, in the shape of gpt-6's wave-5 review s.8): fn-heap-init-decide (request core nursery physical limits budget-octets sizing-octets), called by host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-init-decision (from operator.lisp fnn-operator-execute-init, which prints fn-heap-init-report-line, and from the heap probe through fnn-heap-init-request), sizes within an explicit budget: the least of the physical memory less the OS's reserve (a quarter, at least 512 MiB), each limit the process runs under (RLIMIT_DATA, RLIMIT_AS, every cgroup memory.max) and FN_INIT_BUDGET_MB. A request naming no capacity field (a bare init, every mission) takes the development candidate when the budget holds its whole reservation at the default max-connections, else the small candidate (conservative; never scale); FN_INIT_SIZING=largest takes the first of scale, development, small; the request's own fields are laid last and never lowered, and each candidate is fn-heap-article-held of the preset under them: R raised to the article record of its A and G and H to at least R, as the preset derivation does, so a request's article bound never makes a candidate invalid (lane fix-line-stack, 2026-09-27: batch AR's candidates laid A over development's R, and `init --max-article-octets 8388608' was refused invalid-init-profile). fn-heap-article-held-holds-the-article-record: (implies (and (fn-bs-profile-requestp request) (not (equal v0 :bad))) (and (equal (car q) (car request)) (not (equal v :bad)) (<= (fn-record-encoded-octets-ceiling A G) R) (<= R H) T, A, G unchanged, H and R never lowered)) over the values v of q = (fn-heap-article-held request) and v0 of request; KEYSTONE fn-heap-article-held-meets-the-article-relations: under requestp, a non-:current preset and well-formed fields, the resolution of the held request is neither (:invalid :max-history-octets-below-max-record-octets) nor (:invalid :max-record-octets-below-the-article-record). When none holds it, init refuses by name (init-budget-cannot-hold-profile). Any other request (a named preset or capacity field) is the operator's: written as named, never resized, the decision's HELDP (nth 6) saying whether the budget holds it (fn-heap-init-decide-honors-the-operators-request; -sized-init-is-held: a capacity-free init is always held). The subject is fn-exp-open, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-exposure-open calls at every accept (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-serve-client) through fn-ocar-exp-open (equal to it under the configured owner's relation: fn-ocar-exp-open-is-exp-open-under-ocl-relation, books/owner-open-carried.lisp), over the limits fn-owner-exposure-limits reads with fn-exp-limits from the owner's LIVE configuration value and the owner's bound. KEYSTONE fn-exp-open-refuses-exactly-at-the-capacity: under the run's bound, fn-cfg-limits-withinp and the failed-login rule not refusing the address (fn-exp-auth-refusesp), fn-exp-admit-decision is exactly (:refuse busy-400 1) when the owner holds the capacity or more, else (:refuse address-400 2) for an address outside the trusted range at its per-address limit, else :admit; fn-exp-open-refusal-is-a-400-and-opens-nothing (PRF-161) makes a refusal the named line (`400 too many connections; try again later', RFC 3977 section 5.1.1) with nothing opened. proofs.statement: books/peer-transit-forms.lisp over the functions the served path calls. fn-peer-check-and-ihave-answer-one-offer-decision: for one connection state and one well-formed Message-ID, the code fn-peer-command answers to IHAVE and to CHECK are fn-peer-offer-code's IHAVE and CHECK images of the same fn-peer-decide-offer decision, so CHECK's code is the RFC 4644 section 2.4 form of IHAVE's RFC 3977 section 6.3.2 code (238/335, 438/435, 431/436). fn-peer-takethis-and-ihave-answer-one-transfer-verdict: for every transfer decision and durable completion, fn-peer-transit-outcome-effects renders TAKETHIS's code as the streaming form of IHAVE's (239/235, 439/437, 436/436; 436 after TAKETHIS is fn's local policy, RFC 4644 section 2.5 names 400) and closes exactly when IHAVE's does. fn-peer-transfer-submission-differs-only-in-form-unfolds: the transfer arm hands the owner the same (peer, Message-ID, octets) whatever the form. fn-peer-step-pinned-keeps-outstanding-offers-within-the-peer-bound: no served event raises the connection's outstanding 238 count above the larger of its value and the peer record's inbound max-inflight (D27: a pipeline past the bound is 431). books/feed-connection.lisp fn-fc-mode-stream-unsupported-falls-back-to-ihave: a 500 or 501 answer to MODE STREAM (RFC 3977 section 3.2.1) makes the same connection ready with streaming off, security and credential kept, and records no stop; books/owner.lisp fn-own-feed-connect-in-ihave-form-offers-ihave, -sends-the-bare-article and fn-own-feed-connect-in-stream-form-offers-check: after a connect in the :ihave form the feed offers the IHAVE line and sends the bare article, after a streaming connect to a streaming record it offers CHECK. Not claimed: that a real peer's code means what the RFC says (the INN lab measures that), nor a CAPABILITIES-driven choice of form (RFC 4644 section 2.3 prefers CAPABILITIES; fn asks MODE STREAM).

(fn-sct-file-octets (fn-sct-table-programs tables (fn-sco-event-index next)) seg s))): the octets of the host's steps (fnn-checkpoint-write-steps loops on fn-ockp-step until fn-ockp-donep; fn-ockp-run is that loop in the logic, answering :fuel when the fuel ends before the four tables), at ANY batch size and ANY segment size, from ANY initial buffer contents (fn-ockp-initial-state starts the residue at the buffer's fill), are the file the tables codec specifies whenever the loop completes with :ok. From fn-ockp-run-is-the-remaining (the residue invariant: what remains of a state is the run K from the residue [W, fill) and the rows not yet encoded, framed from INDEX with the chain at PREV, then the runs after it; each step's frames are exactly the difference: fn-ockp-batch-writes-the-remaining, split on the four tables), fn-ockp-cut-frames-is-cut (the buffer's cut is the list's cut), fn-ockp-chunks-of-append-cut, fn-ockp-frames-of-append, fn-ockp-encode-batch-is-rows-program and fn-ockp-counts-are-chunk-counts. proofs.title: The BP kind-19 checkpoint read from an octet buffer by index is the list decoder: the reopen after a rotation decodes the same checkpoint and refuses the same files, in linear work
proofs.statement: books/bp-node-rotation-buffer.lisp. fn-bpnrb-selection-plan (the host-called entry: host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-selection-plan, called by fnn-bps-open, copies the selected generation file's bytes into fn-octets-bp, an abstract stobj congruent to fn-octets, one byte per octet) reads the file by index: fn-bpnrb-decode-range checks the head, reads the u64 payload length from eight cells, checks the frame trailer over the prefix (fn-frame-trailer of fn-bpnr-checkpoint-prefix of the payload cells, built once) and runs the tree decoder fn-bpnrb-dec, which carries an index (a counted run is its cells copied once, fn-bpnrb-slice-acc; a u64 is eight cells). KEYSTONE fn-bpnrb-checkpoint-decode-is-decode, hypothesis-free: (equal (fn-bpnrb-checkpoint-decode budget x) (fn-bpnr-checkpoint-decode x budget)) -- the same checkpoint on every file the list decoder takes, nil on every file it refuses, so fn-bpnr-checkpoint-decode-of-octets (PRF-081's round trip) and PRF-081's recovery keystones are about what the host executes. fn-bpnrb-selection-plan-is-selection-plan, hypothesis-free: the entry equals fn-bpnr-selection-plan over the buffer's value. fn-bpnrb-dec-is-dec: over an octet buffer, the index decoder on the cells [i, end) is fn-bpnr-dec on that slice, with the rest of the slice being the cells from the returned index. The bounded-step foundation (gpt-6's review 2026-09-26 section 2: the checkpoint pipeline's discipline for the BP checkpoint): fn-bpnrb-mstep, the recursion as an explicit machine over (position, goals, value stack); fn-bpnrb-mrun, one quantum of at most Q steps stopping once B octets are consumed, returning the exact continuation; fn-bpnrb-mrun-all-of-dec-goal (the machine run from a decode goal is fn-bpnrb-dec's result followed by the remaining goals) and fn-bpnrb-mrun-all-of-mrun (a quantum keeps the whole run: resuming from its continuation reaches the same answer; a refused quantum is a refused run). These are NOT host-called yet: the host still calls fn-bpnrb-selection-plan in one call (0.55 s at 11.4 MB); the stepped entry and its keystone are the continuation's (LANEDUMP). Every executable function is guard-verified (asserted :common-lisp-compliant in the test book). Why: the list decoder's u64 and counted reads re-established true-listp of the whole remaining input per token (fn-bpnr-read-u64, fn-bpnr-read-counted), so the reopen after a rotation was quadratic in the file (sb-sprof: 99.9 percent of samples in TRUE-LISTP, 722 s for an 11,418,801-octet file of 1,311 held rows). What it does not say: the held rows' wires remain octet lists in the checkpoint value (the replay's representation); the trailer digest is computed over a list of the prefix (the constrained fn-frame-digest has no buffer-range twin); the list decoder remains the specification and the rotation's writer (fn-bpnr-checkpoint-octets) is unchanged.

proofs.statement: books/catalog-number-index.lisp, over the generic fn-cat. fn-cnx-freshp (every later row's number in a group this row is numbered in is absent or larger) holds of the creator and of clear and is preserved by commit, by withdraw and redecide under their guards (fn-cnx-freshp-of-commit, -of-withdraw, -of-redecide, -of-create-and-clear, stated over fn-cat$a-* with no stobj; fn-cnx-freshp-of-cat-writers over the exports). Under it a number is bound by at most one row (fn-cnx-number-seq-unique), and KEYSTONE fn-cnx-view-seq-is-walk: fn-cnx-view-seq group n v (one probe of the (group . number) table, one row read, one visibility test) equals fn-cat-view-number-find group n count v (books/catalog-view.lisp: the walk of the rows visible at version v, newest first) for every non-nil n; KEYSTONE fn-cnx-view-range-is-walk: fn-cnx-view-range group low high v (the numbers low .. min(high, next - 1) ascending, one probe each) equals fn-cnx-walk-range group low high v, the walk per number over low .. high unclamped (a number past the group's high names no row). Hypothesis-free but for the invariant (and n non-nil for the lookup).

proofs.title: A contact's drain reads each job once from a per-peer cursor and answers exactly what the head-restarting scan answers
proofs.statement: fn-bpnjc-contact-next (books/bp-node-job-cursor.lisp; host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bpc-drive-contact before every base offer, and fnn-bpnode-send-receipts in host/native/bp-node.lisp) reads the job list from the cursor (F C HELD) the host threads between asks. fn-bpnjc-contact-next-is-the-head-scan (keystone): under fn-bpnjc-contact-relp (unique job keys; no job ahead of C ready on this contact; HELD the first held job ahead of C; every offered key ahead of C) its answer equals fn-bpnj-contact-next's, so PRF-120 and PRF-079 describe it. The relation is established at the contact's opening from the peer's frontier (fn-bpnjc-open-establishes-the-relation; fn-bpnjc-frontierp: every job ahead of F is another peer's or :forwarded/:expired), kept by each offer for the next ask (fn-bpnjc-offer-keeps-the-relation) and by an evolution of the jobs ahead of the cursor between asks (fn-bpnjc-evolution-keeps-the-relation; fn-bpnjc-offered-record-evolves: a lifecycle record naming an offered key, or a :queued append, is one). fn-bpnjc-drain-is-the-head-drain (keystone): along a contact's asks, threading OFFERED and the cursor, with the jobs evolving between asks (fn-bpnjc-evolving-p), the answers are the head scan's, ask for ask. fn-bpnjc-drain-visits-are-linear (keystone, work): the positions all asks examine plus the start are at most the length of the last job list asked at; an offer advances at least one (fn-bpnjc-ask-position-bounds). The frontier: fn-bpnjc-contact-close advances it over settled jobs and keeps every peer's (fn-bpnjc-close-keeps-the-frontiers); every lifecycle record keeps every frontier (fn-bpnjc-lifecycle-record-keeps-the-frontier). Covered scope: base job offers. Not covered: that every served event changes the base jobs only by fn-bpn-apply-record (the drain takes the evolution as a hypothesis); the machine's own per-offer work (find-job, replace-job) stays linear in the job's position (PKT-653).

proofs.title: The served path's per-line and per-octet-of-line folds run as loops: serving and posting an article uses a control stack independent of its line count and line length
proofs.statement: Three keystones, each with no hypotheses, each the :exec of an mbe whose :logic is the unchanged recursive definition, so the guard proof makes the loop the executable the host runs. fn-nntp-stuff-lines-iter-is-stuff-lines (books/nntp-session.lisp): (fn-nntp-stuff-lines-iter lines) = (fn-nntp-stuff-lines lines), the dot-stuffed CRLF block of every multi-line reply (ARTICLE, HEAD, BODY, OVER, HDR, LIST), built by a tail-recursive accumulator (fn-nntp-stuff-lines-onto) turned round once. fn-post-body-octets-iter-is-body-octets (books/nntp-post.lisp): (fn-post-body-octets-iter lines) = (fn-post-body-octets lines), the POST's article reassembled from the wire's (:article lines) event. (The fourth, fn-wire-list-length-onto-is-list-length, is retired from the citation since lane chunked-body: the served article line is held in the packed store and fn-wire-after-line charges it in constant work, fn-wire-partial-len, PRF-922.) fn-hf-crlf-count-onto-is-crlf-count (books/catalog-record.lisp, lane line-stack 2026-09-27): (fn-hf-crlf-count-onto bytes inline 0) = (fn-hf-crlf-count bytes inline), the body line count the committer's intern decides once per article (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-buffer-arena-action -> fn-owner-prepare-buffer -> fn-apc-intern-row-at -> fn-apc-held-facts-of -> fn-hf-body-lines-of); the recursion it replaced added one after its recursive call, a frame per body line, and stopped the owner on a 2,000,000-line POST at 1 MiB of stack. The recursions they replaced took one control-stack frame per article line (stuff-lines, post-body-octets) or per octet of one line (fn-inj-append inside post-body-octets, fn-wire-list-length); the profile admits a line as long as the article (fn-wire-article-line-limit), so each was a remote stop. Host chain: host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-handle-chunk -> host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span -> fn-scar-ocfg-read-span, whose wire fold (fn-wire-feed-span -> fn-wire-feed-byte -> fn-wire-after-line) calls fn-wire-line-cost, whose served POST (fn-nntp-post-step-pinned -> fn-nntp-post-step) calls fn-post-body-octets, and whose retrievals (fn-nntp-article-response) call fn-nntp-stuff-lines. Scope: a measured constant, not a theorem about frames: the native witness posts, serves, reopens and serves articles of 2,000,000 lines and of one 4 MiB line at 1 MiB of control stack per thread on both images.

Teeth: tests/acl2/served-line-iterative-tests.lisp (reachable witnesses, the composed BODY reply, served-size witnesses of 2,100,000 lines and of one 20,000,000-octet line through the compiled executables, labelled MUTATION witnesses refuted on ground instances). proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-bpaj-store-record-accepted-fast (books/bp-native-app-fast.lisp), reached per request from host/bp-native-app-host.lisp fn-owner-app-submit and fn-owner-app-record and host/bp-receipt-journal-host.lisp fn-bprj-apply, fn-bprj-preflight and fn-bprj-request-action (native: host/native/bp-app.lisp, host/native/workflow.lisp); fn-bpaj-record-lookup-fast and fn-bpaj-bpr-accept-request-fast, now called by host/bp-receipt-host.lisp fn-bpr-host-accept and host/bp-receive-host.lisp fn-bpreq-existing-record in place of their deleted host walks. fn-bpaj-node-record-committed-carriedp is fn-bpi-node-record-committedp without its fn-node-statep conjunct; KEYSTONE fn-bpaj-node-record-committed-carriedp-is-committedp: under (fn-node-statep node) alone they are equal. fn-bpaj-store-record-accepted-fast-is-checked keeps its statement (fn-sn-statep and fn-ceis-indexedp give fast = fn-bpr-store-record-acceptedp) through fn-bpaj-sn-statep-carries-node-statep. proofs.title: A peer named by a DNS name: the dial resolves only RFC 1123 names, each attempt, and the TLS check a transport selects is the configured name under a pinned anchor or the system's public roots
proofs.statement: books/peer-host.lisp over the functions the host calls. fn-peer-dial-target-decides-the-path (no hypothesis; host host/native/io.lisp fnn-peer-connect, called by host/native/feed-service.lisp fnn-feed-dial and host/native/pull-service.lisp fnn-pull-round): the target is exactly one of (:address A) with A the four octets fn-native-config-ipv4-address spells and the host not a name, (:resolve HOST) with HOST exactly the configured text, an RFC 1123 section 2.1 name of at most 253 octets of letters, digits, hyphen and dot and not an IPv4 literal (fn-peer-host-name-is-not-an-ipv4-literal), or (:refused :host-syntax) for anything else. fn-peer-tls-verification-selects-one-check (no hypothesis; host fnn-feed-enable-tls and the pull's (:tls NAME TRUST) effect in fnn-pull-round): the answer is :verify or :refused only; a :verify names exactly the configured server name, which is a host, sends SNI exactly when it is a DNS name (fn-peer-tls-verification-sni-is-never-a-literal, RFC 6066 section 3), and selects the system roots iff the trust is :system-roots and a pinned file iff it is a C string; a string host name with a well-formed trust is always :verify. fn-peer-tls-select-named-default (peer add, books/native-admin-peer.lisp fn-native-admin-peer-plan-base): a named host given `-` `-` is checked against its own name under the system roots; fn-peer-tls-select-numeric-host-needs-a-name-by-definition; fn-peer-tls-select-is-a-check: every selection is one fn-peer-tls-verification accepts, the roots exactly when the anchor word is `-`. The peer record admits (:tls MODE NAME :system-roots) (books/peer-config.lisp fn-cfg-peer-transportp, row n = 1), the pull plan reads it (books/peer-pull.lisp fn-pull-security-of-rows, books/peer-pull-session.lisp fn-pull-tls-securityp), and invitations carry only hosts (books/peer-invite.lisp fn-pinv-hosts-okp). Not claimed: DNS authenticity, the system bundle's trustworthiness, OpenSSL's hostname check, IPv6 peers, inbound source-address peers after renumbering. EXTENSION (lane friend-blockers, 2026-09-27, the stranger rehearsal's stops): Stop 10: `fn redeem HOST[:PORT] CODE LOGIN [--tls] [--cafile PEM]` (host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-redeem) runs XREDEEM for a friend; fn-redeem-step decides each step from the reply code, fn-peer-tls-verification the TLS check, fn-redeem-text every line. KEYSTONE fn-redeem-done-only-on-281-after-the-password. EXTENSION (lane public-node-3, 2026-09-27, the OpenBSD rehearsal's finding 8): a connection that never opens or ends (host fnn-command-redeem: fnn-os-error, fnn-tls-io-error, socket and name-service errors, a close or 30 s silence in fnn-redeem-read-line) is fn-redeem-lost at its stage, and the exit code is fn-outcome-code of fn-redeem-outcome-class. KEYSTONE fn-redeem-lost-is-fenced-and-server-answers-are-not: every lost outcome is :fenced (exit 3), (:uncertain :password) exactly after the password, (:unreachable STAGE) before it; a final step outcome ((:done) or (:refused WORD)) is :accepted exactly on the 281 after the password and :refused otherwise. Not claimed: that the server did not bind the account when the connection ended after the password (it is uncertain, and said so).

proofs.title: A Store opens only on the filesystem its record names, is refused by name otherwise, and its owner's start is refused by name when it requires durable storage on a mount that observably disables it
proofs.statement: books/store-mount-identity.lisp. The record is an FNMI frame of five u16-length fields (fsid, type, mount point, source, policy); KEYSTONE fn-smid-record-decode-of-seal: the host's fnn-seal of fn-smid-record-protected, read back with ACL2's trailer over its protected prefix, decodes to the record (under fn-smid-recordp). KEYSTONE fn-smid-mountinfo-step-preserves-best-okp: the Linux mountinfo fold only ever selects a mount that contains the store root's resolved path. KEYSTONE fn-smid-recorded-store-opens-iff-same-filesystem: a store whose record was written from observation OBS (fn-smid-record-plan) opens under an observation OBS2 exactly when fn-smid-same-filesystemp holds (type and mount point equal; fsids equal where both are reported, else sources equal). KEYSTONE fn-smid-moved-mount-point-is-refused-by-name: when the root now resolves under another mount point the open answers (:refused :filesystem-changed RECORDED OBSERVED). KEYSTONE fn-smid-absent-record-is-refused: no record, no open, whatever is observed. fn-smid-open-verdict-opens-only-on-a-match. KEYSTONE fn-smid-start-refused-iff-required-and-unsafe (PKT-648): on its recorded filesystem, the owner's start is refused as :storage-not-durable exactly when the policy is 1 and fn-smid-unsafe-reason (nobarrier, barrier=0, tmpfs, ramfs) holds, else it starts. KEYSTONE fn-smid-rebound-store-opens: after rebind-filesystem under an observation, an open under it opens. fn-smid-refusal-text-is-nil-exactly-for-open / -for-start: the host prints a refusal exactly when the verdict is not (:open) / (:start). KEYSTONE fn-smid-open-decision-is-the-verdict: the host's open decision fn-smid-open-decision is fn-smid-open-verdict wherever a record is present or the root holds no config.json; KEYSTONE fn-smid-empty-root-is-refused: no record and no config.json is refused whatever is observed; KEYSTONE fn-smid-unrecorded-store-never-starts: a store with no record (made before the record) opens offline with a warning (fn-smid-unrecorded-warning) and is never started; fn-smid-refusal-text-is-nil-exactly-for-an-open-decision. Host subjects: fn-smid-open-decision and fn-smid-start-verdict (host/native/io.lisp fnn-check-filesystem-identity, from fnn-acquire and host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-install), fn-smid-mountinfo-step and fn-smid-linux-observation / fn-smid-statfs-observation (fnn-filesystem-observation), fn-smid-record-plan (fnn-record-filesystem-at-init), fn-smid-rebind-plan (fnn-command-rebind-filesystem), fn-smid-refusal-text, fn-smid-durability-warning. NOT in this target: that statfs and mountinfo report the truth (A-HOST); ZFS sync=disabled and volatile write caches (not observable); the record replacement's crash cuts as a byte-model program (PKT-671). EXTENSION (lane friend-blockers, 2026-09-27, the stranger rehearsal's stops): PKT-820: fn-smid-same-filesystemp compares type and fsid where both fsids are reported (mount point and source are not compared: the shipped systemd unit's ProtectSystem=strict + ReadWritePaths bind view shows /var/lib/fn as its own mount point), and type, mount point and source where either is unreported. KEYSTONE fn-smid-same-fsid-view-opens: a store recorded under OBS opens under OBS2 with the same type and the same nonzero fsid, whatever its mount point and source. KEYSTONE fn-smid-other-filesystem-is-refused-by-name and fn-smid-other-fsid-is-refused-by-name: another filesystem (known fsids differ) is refused (:filesystem-changed RECORDED OBSERVED). KEYSTONE fn-smid-unreported-fsid-moved-mount-is-refused-by-name: with an unreported fsid another mount point is refused. KEYSTONE fn-smid-rebind-outside-opens-inside: a rebind run outside the unit cures the unit's open. They replace fn-smid-moved-mount-point-is-refused-by-name (retired: the mount point is no longer the identity where the fsid is known).

proofs.title: A served connection's memory is named and a node refuses, by name, at start and at every live change, a connection capacity the machine cannot hold beside the store's heap figure, the core and the fixed threads; every connection fn-exp-open admits under an accepted capacity, trusted sources included, fits the machine
proofs.statement: books/connection-budget.lisp. The subjects are fn-cbud-run-decide, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-connection-budget calls once per run after recovery and before listen (host/native/mux.lisp fnn-mux-budget-install, from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-run), and fn-cbud-deltas-refusal, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-reconfigure-deltas calls before any live reconfiguration is staged (native-admin, peer-invite and auth all reach it), over the host's observations (the machine: heap-figure's fn-heap-machine-octets; the core's length; the fixed threads, 12 + 2 I/O loops + the control clients; the thread control stack) and the store's profile (heap-figure's fn-heap-figure-octets is the base's heap; the profile's largest article A sizes the connection). The per-connection figure is fn-cbud-conn-octets: a heap part (the connection record, its input of two reads of the largest size a served step may read (fn-cbud-step-read-octets, called by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-read-octets from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-refresh-read-octets under the owner mutex after the exposure install and after every served step; host/native/mux.lisp reads into one buffer per I/O loop of that size: 512 octets under a step rate, fn-cbud-step-read-octets-under-a-rate-by-definition, so exposure-steps-per-second keeps its meaning in octets; 4 KiB without one (the measured trade between steps and the owner mutex hold: planning/evidence/input-loop-2-2026-09-27.md), fn-cbud-step-read-octets-is-bounded; the figure holds two, fn-cbud-read-covers-the-step; lane input-loop-2), the one reply of the STATED WORKLOAD -- the largest article rendered, 2A + 1,024 -- and the parser's command line as an octet list, 32 octets per octet; the body of an article in flight is PRF-377's pool) and a native part (kernel socket buffers; the TLS session when a context is loaded); the record, kernel and TLS constants are measurements (tests/test_native_mux.py pins the resident cost). fn-cbud-bound-holds-its-connections: when the base (the store's heap figure, the core, the threads with their stacks and 4 MiB of runtime each) fits the machine, the base plus n connections at the whole per-connection figure fits for every n up to fn-cbud-bound; fn-cbud-bound-is-the-most: one more does not. The resident heap is at most the process's dynamic space, so fn-cbud-resident-octets of n connections is min(dynamic, figure + n x heap part) + the rest of the base + n x native part, and fn-cbud-limit is the larger of fn-cbud-bound and the dynamic space's bound (the whole dynamic space plus each connection's native part). KEYSTONE fn-cbud-limit-holds-its-connections: when either way holds the base (fn-cbud-base-fitsp), the resident figure of every n up to the limit is within the machine; fn-cbud-limit-is-the-most: of limit + 1 it is not. KEYSTONE fn-cbud-run-decide-holds-the-capacity: an accepted run (:hold L) has capacity <= L, L the limit, and the resident figure of capacity connections within the machine; fn-cbud-run-decide-refuses-exactly-past-the-limit: it refuses exactly when the capacity passes the limit or the base does not fit. KEYSTONE fn-cbud-admitted-connections-fit-the-machine: under PRF-211's hypotheses, when the live capacity is within the limit and the base fits, an admission (fn-exp-admit-decision = (:admit)) with nconns held leaves the resident figure of nconns + 1 within the machine; the trusted range exempts no connection from the capacity (fn-exp-open-refuses-exactly-at-the-capacity). KEYSTONE fn-cbud-deltas-refusal-keeps-the-machine-held (lane tls-handshake-budget-2, with PRF-986's term): the run holds its observations and the handshake slots it charged (fn-cbud-run-held); a delta list the refusal passes is the run's decision re-made on those observations with the applied configuration's capacity and the larger of the held slots and its own tls-handshakes-in-flight, so the resident figure of the new capacity, with L x *fn-cbud-handshake-scratch-octets* of handshake scratch in the base's rest (native memory, outside the dynamic space; fn-cbud-handshake-octets when a TLS context is loaded), is within the machine; lowering L never lowers the charge while the run lives; refused by name, :handshakes-exceed-memory when the capacity alone holds under the held slots, :connections-exceed-memory otherwise. Lane zero-copy-commit (2026-09-28): fn-cbud-launch-decide and its theorem are gone (no caller since lane reservation-figure); the body of an article in flight left the per-connection heap part (the parser term is the command line only) for the store figure's pool of article credits, admitted by the served read (PRF-377). Not claimed: replies larger than the stated workload's (range OVER/LISTGROUP) until replies are rendered in windows (PKT-644); the measured constants as theorems; that the probe sees the live capacity (it cannot: PKT-644).

proofs.title: A restricted reader session is served the store with its excluded groups absent, and no reply can depend on what an excluded group holds
proofs.statement: books/nntp-auth.lisp fn-auth-delegate-pinned (called by fn-auth-step-pinned, which books/served.lisp fn-served-dispatch calls per framed line; the carried twin books/served-carried.lisp fn-scar-auth-delegate-pinned, which host/owner-host.lisp reaches through fn-scar-ocfg-read-tls-prefix, calls the same view functions) delegates over (fn-auth-view-session, -archive, -index, -config): for a reader session whose login's rule (fn-auth-access-text over the pinned listing's fourth element) has READ text R and a projected session, the archive is fn-gac-restrict-state R (books/group-access.lisp), the index fn-gac-restrict-index R built from its articles, the session fn-gac-deselect R; otherwise each is its argument (fn-auth-view-when-unrestricted). KEYSTONES (books/group-access.lisp): fn-gac-restrict-state-is-a-projection (fn-nntp-projectionp preserved); fn-gac-restrict-index-corresponds (fn-gidx-pin-correspondencep of the rebuilt index); fn-gac-restrict-state-groups-are-readable (every group of the view is readable under R and a group of the store); fn-gac-restrict-articles-memberships-readable and fn-gac-restrict-index-withdrawn-are-readable (every article of the view and of its withdrawn list names only readable groups and memberships); fn-gac-restricted-article-is-held (the view holds Message-ID M exactly when the store holds an article M with a readable group); fn-gac-restrict-absent-groups (NO ORACLE: for a store fn-statep and any R2 admitting every group R admits, restricting to R2 then R is restricting to R). The served relation: fn-gac-deselected-consistent / fn-gac-consistent-back and fn-auth-view-consistent / -back carry fn-auth-session-consistentp and fn-gidx-pin-correspondencep into and out of the view, so fn-auth-delegate-pinned-preserves-consistentp and fn-auth-step-pinned-preserves-consistent-session hold for restricted sessions. Local policy (INN readers.conf); RFC 3977 section 4.2 wildmats.

proofs.title: A moderated group: an unapproved article is never visible in it, a moderator's approved article is, and an Approved field from anyone else is refused by name
proofs.statement: fn-cfg-set-group-moderation-sets-the-moderation (books/config-invariants.lisp, KEYSTONE): an admitted (fn-cfg-set-group-moderation NAME QUEUE ADDRESS LOGINS) (code 23, `group moderate`) applied by fn-cfg-apply-delta makes fn-cfg-group-moderation of NAME (QUEUE ADDRESS LOGINS), or nil for --off, and leaves every other group's unchanged. Over fn-post-gated-decision, the served POST's decision (books/nntp-post.lisp, called by fn-nntp-post-step; host line host/reader-host.lisp fn-reader-chunk through books/served.lisp): fn-post-unapproved-article-is-never-in-a-moderated-group (KEYSTONE): an ordinary article with no Approved field is never committed with a group whose status in the connection's configuration is moderated (it is forwarded as an RFC 5537 section 3.5.1 method-1 envelope into the queue group, or refused :moderation-unavailable); fn-post-moderator-approved-article-is-committed (KEYSTONE): with Approved and every named moderated group :approver on the connection, the decision is the injection's (committed into the moderated groups); fn-post-forged-approval-is-refused-by-name (KEYSTONE): with Approved and some named moderated group not :approver, the decision is the refusal :approval-not-moderator (441 by name). fn-mod-session-entries-approver-iff-moderator (books/moderation.lisp): on the owner-installed status list (no :approver entries), a connection's view marks group G :approver exactly when its login is one of G's moderators (books/nntp-auth.lisp fn-auth-moderation-config, called by fn-auth-delegate and fn-auth-delegate-pinned). fn-post-submission-is-the-decision-or-its-envelope with fn-mod-envelope-msgid-is-not-a-generated-id keep fn-post-distinct-injection-clocks-give-distinct-identities unconditional. Relay: fn-peer-transfer-never-stages-an-unapproved-moderated-article (books/peer-inbound-invariants.lisp, KEYSTONE) over fn-peer-transfer, the owner's transit port: a transfer that changes the node stages the article in a group moderated under the configuration only when the article carries Approved (fn-peer-decide-transfer's :unapproved-moderated refusal; RFC 5537 sections 3.6 item 6, 3.7 item 5). Queue privacy (PKT-658): fn-own-submission-targets-of-a-queue-by-definition and fn-own-feed-durable-never-enqueues-a-queue (books/owner-feed-subject.lisp, KEYSTONES) over fn-own-submission-targets and fn-own-feed-durable (host fn-owner-submission-intent and the outcomes): a submission naming a moderation queue group of the owner's posting configuration has no target and leaves the feed table unchanged; fn-auth-view-hides-the-queue-from-a-non-moderator (books/nntp-auth.lisp, KEYSTONE) over fn-auth-view-archive, the store fn-auth-delegate-pinned serves: for a projected reader connection whose login moderates none of the groups a queue serves (or has not authenticated), the view holds neither the queue group nor an article filed in it (group-access's READ rule with the queue hidden, fn-gac-readablep's :hide form; fn-mod-hidden-queues). The operator's `moderation list GROUP` (PKT-657) renders the queue's envelopes held/approved/rejected (books/control-evidence.lisp fn-cev-moderation-report; FNLS frame kind 3 code 10); The operator's verbs (PKT-657, books/moderation-verbs.lisp, host host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-moderation-plan calling fn-mvb-plan, fn-mvb-plan-unfolds): fn-mvb-approve-commits-the-held-article-approved (KEYSTONE) over fn-mvb-approve: a planned submission has LOGIN a moderator of a group the envelope queues for, the envelope held, the octets the envelope's proto-article with `Approved: LOGIN` first, fn-post-gated-decision under LOGIN's moderation view injecting them under the planned Message-ID and groups, and the operator path (fn-own-operator-decision, the (:operator-submit ...) event the host steps) injecting them too; fn-mvb-only-a-moderator-approves-or-rejects (KEYSTONE): a LOGIN that moderates no group the envelope queues for gets a refusal from approve and reject (:not-a-moderator by name when the envelope exists); fn-mvb-reject-withdraws-the-held-envelope (KEYSTONE): a planned rejection is the node's withdrawal (PRF-256) of exactly the held envelope. After the records flip the held envelope is an archive article whose payload position is an arena handle: fn-mvb-plan and fn-mvb-approve take the arena (host fn-owner-moderation-plan passes it; only read) and fn-mvb-held-article reads the envelope's octets through it (fn-nntp-article-bytes; lane matrix-reds, PKT-850: before, approve parsed the handle and answered envelope-malformed); fn-mvb-held-article-is-the-model-body-by-definition (the representation bridge; a restatement by definition, so not cited as a keystone): the held body is the body of the envelope's octet model fn-nntp-article-alpha. Teeth over a flipped archive in tests/acl2/moderation-verbs-tests.lisp (the envelope at handle 0; an empty arena refuses envelope-malformed; a pre-flip octet payload approves the same).

proofs.title: A local consumer bound to an account is served only events of a group the account reads, only with the account's credential, and otherwise exactly as the consumer poll and ack; an unbound consumer is unchanged
proofs.statement: books/consumer-bound.lisp. Subjects: fn-cbind-poll and fn-cbind-ack (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-bound-poll / -bound-ack, reached from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-consumer-local-serialized for local-control codes 7 and 8), fn-cbind-plain-poll and fn-cbind-plain-ack (fn-owner-consumer-local-poll / -ack, codes 5 and 1). The binding is the accounts slot's mark-6 row (books/config.lisp fn-cfg-consumer-bind, delta code 24) of the latest configuration; the credential check is fn-auth-checkp over fn-auth-config-with-accounts (the table AUTHINFO reads); the rule is group-access's read pattern (fn-gac-pattern / fn-gac-readablep). KEYSTONES: fn-cbind-poll-delivers-only-readable-events (a bound poll that answers a page: the consumer is bound, the password checks, the answer is fn-col-poll-report's, and the selected event's article has a group readable under the account's rule); fn-cbind-poll-is-the-consumer-poll-or-a-refusal and fn-cbind-ack-is-the-consumer-ack-or-a-refusal (every bound answer is the unbound consumer's own or a refusal, which writes nothing, so PRF-116's page-is-a-read, forward-ack-in-scope and repeated-ack-no-op guarantees hold over the delivered subsequence; an ack that is not refused had the binding, the credential and a readable query); fn-cbind-plain-poll-of-an-unbound-consumer-is-the-consumer-poll and fn-cbind-plain-ack-of-an-unbound-consumer-is-the-consumer-ack (an unbound consumer's plain answer is today's; a bound consumer's is (:refused :bound)). Local policy; no RFC requirement. RECORDS FLIP (flip-bridge, 2026-09-27): the Store retains held rows and fn-col-poll-report refuses a held article row :report, so the polls read the payload through the arena: fn-cbind-poll-over and fn-cbind-plain-poll-over (books/consumer-bound.lisp) over books/history-fold-refinement.lisp fn-col-poll-report-over carry KEYSTONES 1, 2 and 4 (fn-cbind-poll-over-delivers-only-readable-events, fn-cbind-poll-over-is-the-consumer-poll-or-a-refusal, fn-cbind-plain-poll-over-of-an-unbound-consumer-is-the-consumer-poll) and equal the arena-free polls whenever the selected event is no held row (fn-cbind-poll-over-is-poll-unless-a-held-row). Host: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-consumer-local-poll and -bound-poll still call the arena-free forms (a REQUEST to the host lane to pass the live arena); until then a bound or plain poll that selects an article answers (:refused :report). The acks read no payload and are unchanged. Q10c reporting extension: fn-acct-consumer-lines-are-the-list-lines-of-the-consumer-rows proves that consumer show prints exactly the account-list lines of mark-6 consumer rows, in order, omitting every other kind. The actual host-called fn-nls-report composition is fn-nls-report-of-query-kind-is-query-report (PRF-089), with the consumer plan selecting :consumers and the query rendering fn-acct-consumers-list-report. The plain FNLS report code is 13, following the shared evidence/query codes 8..12. Source proof and matching native validation remain distinct.

proofs.title: The refused-offer memory is bounded, evicts oldest-first, and answers an offer with the refusal the parse of a remembered transfer gives
proofs.statement: books/refused-offers.lisp, books/peer-inbound.lisp, books/peer-refused-offers.lisp, books/owner.lisp. The memory (Message-ID . reason) pairs, newest first, is recorded by the owner at a transit outcome (books/owner.lisp fn-own-transit-refused under fn-own-transit-outcome, the :transit-outcome event host/owner-host.lisp steps) only for a refusal whose reason the octets decide, and the reason recorded is recomputed from the in-flight octets (fn-peer-refused-record: fn-peer-intrinsic-refusal, the arms of fn-peer-decide-transfer that read only the octets and the offered Message-ID); it is re-pinned into every peer session per read (fn-own-conn-live-session) and read by the offer arm of fn-peer-decide-offer after the history test (and its served twins fn-pix-decide-offer, fn-pgc-decide-offer). KEYSTONES: fn-rof-record-within-capacity and fn-rof-record-keeps-a-bounded-memory-bounded (D27: never longer than the operator's refused-offer-capacity, default 4096); fn-rof-record-at-capacity-evicts-the-oldest; fn-peer-decide-transfer-refuses-what-the-octets-refuse (for any node and clock, a peer with an inbound half, a well-formed Message-ID and octets within the peer's size: the transfer decision is the octets' refusal); fn-prof-run-is-sound (every Message-ID a memory built by the record step holds names a transfer of it whose octets drew exactly the remembered reason); fn-prof-offer-answer-is-the-reparse (an offer of a held, not-yet-accepted Message-ID is refused for that reason, and the remembered transfer's own decision on this node from this peer is the same refusal). Not persisted (in memory only; a restart costs one re-parse per refused article and changes no answer). A future date and a missing Path are never remembered: the first depends on the clock, the second on the operator's relay-require-path. Lane log-leftovers (2026-09-27, PKT-858): fn-peer-decide-offer-answers-the-memory holds outside the disk-slow posture (hypothesis (not (fn-peer-shed-p session))); the owner's memory built from transfers never holds the posture's entry (fn-prof-run-keeps-no-posture), so fn-prof-offer-answer-is-the-reparse is unchanged.

proofs.title: A relayed article dated beyond the operator's skew, with an unreadable date, with a malformed Path, or (when required) with no Path, is refused by name
proofs.statement: books/relay-checks.lisp and books/peer-inbound.lisp fn-peer-decide-transfer (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-decide calls it; the reply is fn-peer-transit-outcome-effects' 437/439 with fn-peer-reason-text). RFC 5537 section 3.6 step 2: :date-future when the Injection-Date (or, absent, the Date) read by fn-rck-date-instant (RFC 5322 section 3.3 with the section 4.3 obsolete forms) is more than fn-rck-skew seconds after the clock reading; the skew is the operator's relay-date-skew limit row, at most 86400 (fn-rck-skew-within-the-rfc; the admin word is refused above it, fn-rck-limit-valuep), 86400 without a row; without a usable clock the check does not decide and fn-peer-transfer defers :no-clock. Section 3.6 step 4: :date-syntax for a date field that is not a date-time, :path-syntax for a Path present once that is not RFC 5536 section 3.1.5's grammar (fn-rck-path-wellformedp), :no-path for a missing Path when the operator's relay-require-path is 1 (default 0: fn's own authored submissions carry no Path, PKT-674). Theorem subject: the concrete witnesses of tests/acl2/transit-hygiene-tests.lisp through fn-peer-decide-transfer and the keystone fn-peer-decide-transfer-refuses-what-the-octets-refuse (PRF-235) for the octet-decided reasons.

proofs.title: The outbound feed offers an article only to peers whose Distribution filter admits the article's Distribution
proofs.statement: books/owner-feed-subject.lisp over fn-own-submission-targets (books/owner.lisp; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-submission-intent calls fn-own-submission-intent-records, which names it, and the durable enqueue fn-own-feed-durable folds it): KEYSTONE fn-own-submission-targets-respect-the-distribution, every target's filter (fn-own-feed-dists-of, the wildmat of its outbound-distributions row, set at fn-own-feed-reconfigure, fn-own-feed-dists-of-reconfigure) admits the in-flight article's Distribution (fn-own-feed-distributions-of, RFC 5536 section 3.2.4, case-folded) under fn-own-feed-distribution-admitsp; KEYSTONE fn-own-submission-targets-keep-an-admitted-peer, the filter removes nothing else (a peer the scope decision names, whose filter admits the article and whose queue lacks the Message-ID, is a target); books/owner-feed.lisp KEYSTONE fn-own-feed-distribution-targets-member (the filter is exactly the decision). The PKT-400 keystone fn-own-submission-offers-a-control-article-under-its-newsgroups-and-filing-group gains the distribution literal. RFC 5537 section 3.6 paragraph 2; local policy: no filter feeds everything, no Distribution is world, a malformed Distribution matches no filter.

proofs.title: A cancel's authority is exactly a granted signed canceller or the poster: an unsigned cancel or Supersedes withdraws its target exactly when one of its RFC 8315 Cancel-Key entries opens one of the target's sha256 Cancel-Locks; the octets the owner stores for an account's POST carry exactly one Cancel-Lock keyed by that account under an HKDF purpose key, outside the D25 source
proofs.statement: Withdrawal (unchanged): over fn-ctl-refresh-withdrawals / fn-ctl-journal-withdrawals, the record of a cause withdraws a target exactly when the cause names another target and either a verified principal P signed it or P's grants cover its groups, or no principal is verified and a Cancel-Key K of the cause has Base64(SHA-256(K)) among the target's sha256 Cancel-Locks (fn-ctl-withdrawal-authority-is-exactly-signer-or-poster; fn-ctl-verified-cause-ignores-its-keys). Stored octets: books/owner-served-invariants.lisp fn-own-sub-stored-octets CFG SUB RING (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-take; the completion gate compares the same function): for a served submission by account A (fn-own-sub-account, recorded by fn-own-finish-read from the session subject) with a key ring installed (fn-ns-ringp), unsigned and with no poster Cancel-Lock, the stored octets are `Cancel-Lock: sha256:Base64(SHA-256(K))` CRLF, then on a cancel `Cancel-Key:` with one key per retained epoch, then the injected octets unchanged, K = Base64(keyed-BLAKE3(key, hex(A) || MSGID)) with key the BLAKE3 derive_key purpose key of the current epoch (context fn/cancel-lock/v2, material the root and the node identity; HMAC-SHA256 under HKDF-SHA256 up to store format 9, RFC 8315 section 4 leaving the MAC's hash to the agent) (fn-own-stored-octets-carry-the-account-lock, fn-cl-served-payload-writes-one-account-lock). D25: the projection fn-cll-skip that books/poster-bytes.lisp reads both compared payloads through gives the injected octets for every ring and account (fn-own-stored-octets-keep-the-injected-octets, fn-cl-served-payload-projects-to-the-injected-octets, fn-cll-skip-of-the-generated-lines), so a same-source retry by any account or key epoch is :duplicate and a different source :conflict at fn-rcl-existing-action (fn-cld-a-retry-by-any-account-or-epoch-is-already-stored, fn-cld-a-changed-source-is-a-conflict-whatever-the-account). Rotation: a cancel's keys open a lock made under any retained epoch (fn-cl-ring-keys-open-every-retained-lock). Exactly the account's key opens its lock up to the stated collision (fn-cl-account-key-opens-exactly-its-lock). Derivation: distinct info labels are distinct derive_key contexts (fn-ns-purpose-inputs-separate-by-definition); the key file round-trips (fn-ns-file-parse-of-render). Not theorems: that the written line parses back as the entry (teeth on parsed stored octets); that another account's key opens nothing (a SHA-256 collision of two keyed-BLAKE3 outputs under a key the forger does not hold: about 2^-128 per chosen pair); keyed-BLAKE3 and derive_key pseudorandomness. PKT-575 (PRF-256): the plan's first arm is the node's own authority (fn-ctl-node-authorizesp: a configuration row (CAUSE TARGET REASON 1) the operator wrote), and the keystone's right side is `the node authorizes CAUSE for TARGET, or` the signer/poster condition; the effect answers :node for such a record. RECORDS FLIP (flip-books-residue, 2026-09-27): the held payload is an arena handle; the subject is fn-store-existing-action (books/store-intern.lisp), which the host calls after flip-L6 at fn-owner-existing-action, fn-owner-prepare and host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-existing-action, and at fn-owner-existing-action-buffer through fn-pidx-existing-action (fn-pidx-existing-action-is-store-existing-action); the held-payload hypothesis reads the bytes under the held handle through the arena the verdict reads (fn-handle-bytes). The pre-flip statements over fn-rcl-existing-action equated a handle with octets and were vacuous on a flipped Store. After the records flip (flip-L8-2) the target's Cancel-Lock entries are its row's control fact, carried by the record as TLOCKS (fn-ctl-w-with-tlocks) and read by fn-ctl-withdrawal-effect's key arm; the keystone is stated over the plan resolved to TLOCKS.

proofs.title: store import and operator init publication (P-IMPORT, P-INIT-PUB): a crash or an ambiguous rename/barrier outcome leaves no store at ROOT or the complete imported (init: complete empty) store, never replaces an unrelated destination, and recovery classifies by what it observes
proofs.statement: books/store-import-publication.lisp fn-bs-imp-program-crash-is-no-store-or-the-complete-store: for a fresh process (nothing pending), an existing parent directory, distinct STAGE and ROOT names and plan files inside the staged tree, at every pair of every run of fn-bs-imp-program under any well-formed syscall outcomes (fn-bs-imp-outcomesp: :ok or an error pair, including (errno . :issued) renames and failed barriers with torn landings) and every crash choice, ROOT's durable entry is its old one (none, or an unrelated destination untouched), or -- only when ROOT was absent -- the staged directory with every subdirectory named and every plan file named and durable with exactly its octets. fn-bs-imp-classify-by-what-is-known: fn-bs-imp-classify over the two observable names answers :no-store/:not-published only when ROOT is absent and :store-present/:publication-uncertain only when ROOT is the complete staged tree. Host: host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-store-import (through fnn-staged-publication) writes the program step for step (cuts +fnn-import-model-cuts+, renameat2 RENAME_NOREPLACE on Linux) and calls fn-bs-imp-classify before writing and after an error at or after the rename. operator init's plan is PRF-268's (books/store-init-log-publication.lisp fn-bs-init-log-program, the same program with the record log's plan and init's cut names from books/store-init-publication.lisp *fn-bs-init-pub-cut-names*); fn-bs-init-pub-admission (host: fnn-command-init-published, called by operator init) proceeds only when neither ROOT.init-* nor ROOT is present. Host: fnn-staged-publication is the one transcription for both. Scope: the ordinary open between staged-durable and the rename is its own program (P-RECOVER) and is modelled here as the cut import-validated; OpenBSD has no renameat2: import and init hold an exclusive flock on ROOT.lock for the whole program and re-check ROOT's absence under it before rename(2); a process ignoring the lock that creates an empty directory at ROOT in that window is the documented residual.

proofs.title: The record log's scan reads back a well-formed log exactly, and a torn append scans to the old history, the new record, or a forgery
proofs.statement: books/store-log.lisp (the storage-log design's prototype, planning/design-2026-09-27-storage-log.md section 5.2). An entry is an FNLG frame whose payload is the previous entry's trailer (32 octets, the chain) and the committed record's octets, padded with zeros to the write unit (fn-lg-entry); a log is the chained entries of a record list from a genesis trailer (fn-lg-log); the scan reads complete chained entries from the front and answers (records . aligned-end) (fn-lg-scan). fn-lg-scan-of-log-append: for (fn-frame-digestp prev) and (fn-lg-recordsp records max), the scan of (append (fn-lg-log records prev unit) x) is (append records (car (scan x from the log's last trailer))) with the log's length added to the consumed count; fn-lg-scan-of-log: alone, exactly (cons records (len log)): the frontier is the last complete entry's end. fn-lg-torn-variant-len: a torn variant of a write (fn-bs-torn-variantp, the byte model's crash of the one pending write) is no longer than the write. fn-lg-scan-of-torn-entry: for a record within max and a torn variant OBSERVED of (fn-lg-entry prev record unit), the scan of OBSERVED is (nil . 0), or (cons (list record) (len entry)), or (fn-lg-forgeryp observed prev max frame): the first slice validates as a chained frame and is not the written one, the event A-CRYPTO-TRAILER excludes (SHA-256's collision figure, about 2^-128, quoted pessimistically). fn-lg-scan-of-log-then-torn-entry: the composition over a log followed by a torn append. The shift lemma (a crash of an aligned append to a NON-EMPTY inode) and the A-CRYPTO-TRAILER corollary are lane log-core's (planning/briefs-wave5/w6-log-core.txt).

proofs.title: The header limits of one article are the operator's: the parse under a profile's limits admits exactly the headers within them and refuses the next by name, and readers parse under the ceiling so raising a limit never changes an admitted article
proofs.statement: For any limits WIDER under which OCTETS parses, fn-article-parse-under OCTETS LIMITS is that same article exactly when the input's header census (fields, physical lines, octets before the blank line, read by the parser's own line scanner) is within LIMITS, and otherwise a refusal whose code is :header-fields-limit, :header-lines-limit or :header-octets-limit (fn-article-parse-under-admits-exactly-the-limits); by instance a success is within its limits (fn-article-parse-under-within-its-limits) and a success under LIMITS is the same article under any wider limits (fn-article-parse-under-raised-limits-agree). fn-article-parse, which every reader of a stored or received article calls, is the ceiling limits' instance (fn-article-parse-is-the-ceiling-limits-by-definition). For an input the reading parser admits, fn-article-census-refusal of the census against LIMITS is NIL exactly when the parse under LIMITS admits it (and then equals the reading parse), and otherwise a limit's name while that parse refuses by a limit's name (fn-article-census-refusal-is-the-parse); fn-inj-decide (books/injection.lisp, called by the served POST through the owner's configuration, whose header limits host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-served-post-bound takes from the opened profile's fields 15 to 17, fn-bs-profile-header-limits) refuses by exactly that census refusal. The parse's work under any limits is bounded by fn-article-parse-under-work-budget (fn-article-parse-under-work-input-bound). PKT-660 (the coordinator's default): the peer transfer decision the host calls, fn-peer-decide-transfer-under (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-decide, with the owner's limits fn-own-config-header-limits), admits a relayed article exactly when the parse of the octets it would store (fn-peer-relayed-octets) under the limits admits them, and otherwise refuses by a limit's name (437/439) where fn-peer-decide-transfer wanted or deferred (fn-peer-decide-transfer-under-admits-exactly-the-limits), and wants only what fn-peer-decide-transfer wants (fn-peer-decide-transfer-under-wants-only-what-transfer-wants); the owner's BP transit delivery fn-own-bp-transit-submit-result submits only within the limits and is refused past them (fn-own-bp-transit-submits-only-within-the-limits, fn-own-bp-transit-refuses-past-the-limits); the owner's control delivery fn-own-control-decision (BP application and CLI articles) injects only within the limits and past them refuses by a limit's name (fn-own-control-decision-injects-only-within-the-limits, fn-own-control-decision-refuses-past-the-limits-by-name).

proofs.statement: books/bp-handoff-report.lisp over books/bp-node-foundation.lisp. fn-bpah-persist-delivery-step's durable answer is (:delivery-answer :durable D), D the kind-7 record's disposition; fn-bpah-handoff-report (host/native/bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-drive-effects prints exactly its word for every :delivery-answer that fnn-bps-foundation-step returns) is :durable exactly for an accepting disposition and :refused for a refusing one. KEYSTONE fn-bpah-handoff-report-is-application-disposition: after fn-bpah-deliver-result-step records the application's STATUS and issues kind 7 ((car e1) = :persist-delivery), the report of fn-bpah-persist-delivery-step's answer to that publication is a member of (list (fn-bpah-disposition-report STATUS) :uncertain), and with RESULT :durable and the record applying to the held list it equals (fn-bpah-disposition-report STATUS). fn-bpah-persist-delivery-reports-the-record (hypothesis-free) and fn-bpah-persist-delivery-reports-exactly state the same for the publication step alone; fn-bpah-disposition-report-durable-is-accepting: the report is :durable iff the disposition is accepting. fn-bpnf-step-deliver-result-is-step and fn-bpnf-step-persist-delivery-is-step: the foundation dispatcher fn-bpnf-step routes the host's two events (host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-bpnode-dispatch-one) to these steps. proofs.title: The executed BP CRC-16/X.25 is table-driven and equals the bitwise definition every bundle theorem reasons about
proofs.statement: books/bp-primary.lisp. fn-bpp-crc16-scan executes (mbe :exec) fn-bpp-crc16-scan-table: per octet, c = (logand (logxor crc x) 65535) and the next register (logand (logxor (ash c -8) (fn-bpp-crc16-table-ref (logand c 255))) 65535), the 256-entry table *fn-bpp-crc16-table* evaluated from fn-bpp-crc16-octet at every octet value by the defconst (it cannot drift). KEYSTONE fn-bpp-crc16-scan-table-is-scan: (implies (and (natp crc) (fn-cbor-octet-listp xs)) (equal (fn-bpp-crc16-scan-table crc xs) (fn-bpp-crc16-scan crc xs))), the guard proof of fn-bpp-crc16-scan. The octet step is checked at every one of the 65,536 16-bit registers by evaluation inside the proof (local fn-bpp-crc16-step-agrees), so the logical definitions, and every theorem about fn-bpp-crc16, fn-bpb-encode and the bundle codec, are unchanged. Host: every block CRC the node computes (fn-bpb-encode-block-with-crc, the decoders' checks) through fn-bpp-crc16; the reassembled whole bundle's encode in fn-bpnf-family-plan (bp-service.lisp fnn-bps-fragment-progress -> fn-bpnf-family-next, and the kind-18 publication). Why: sb-sprof over the receiver that reassembled and delivered a 1 MiB fragment family: 77 percent of CPU in fn-bpp-crc16-scan's bitwise steps (FLOOR 25.8 percent self, FN-BPP-CRC16-BIT 37 percent cumulative); a 1 MiB CRC now takes 0.06 s in the REPL.
