proofs.title: The owner holds its ledger as a snoc-list: the commit appends one pair in O(1), and the take, the outcome and the host's finish read its length in O(1)
proofs.statement: books/owner.lisp (post-alloc-3). The owner record's ledger field holds a snoc-list (books/snoc-list.lisp; a plain list, nil included, represents itself: fn-sl-list-when-plain); fn-own-ledger reads the list back (fn-sl-list of fn-own-ledger-field) and fn-own-make takes the FIELD, so a transition that keeps the ledger passes the field through and fn-own-ledger-of-fn-own-make reads (fn-sl-list FIELD), which fn-sl-list-of-fn-own-ledger-field names back as the ledger. fn-own-ledger-count (O(1) on a snoc form) is the length for every owner (fn-own-ledger-count-is-len); fn-own-take-submission's mark and fn-own-completion-consumedp read it through mbe (logic unchanged). KEYSTONES (no hypothesis): fn-rix-own-complete-enabled-ledger-field (the completion the host calls puts the pair on the field with fn-sl-snoc: one cons) and fn-rix-own-complete-enabled-ledger (the ledger it represents is the old one with the pair appended); fn-sl-list-of-fn-sl-snoc (PRF-275) for every value. Host subjects: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-finish-submission -> books/owner-refresh-indexed.lisp fn-rix-own-finish -> fn-rix-own-complete -> fn-rix-own-complete-enabled; fn-owner-finish -> fn-rix-ocfg-complete (the same completion) and compares fn-own-ledger-count before and after. Before: the commit copied the ledger (fn-ag-append), 16 B x POSTs-since-open per POST, and the take and the outcome walked it for its length. Local policy (D27: bound work, not data); no RFC requirement.

proofs.title: A POST's profile admission is decided once per open and carried
proofs.statement: books/store-profile-carried.lisp (post-alloc-3). The carry pairs the Store profile with its admission verdict (fn-pvc-make, written once by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-install-profile; NIL at the recovery reset); fn-pvc-carryp: the verdict is fn-bs-profile-admittedp of the profile it names (no owner state, so no owner step falsifies it; fn-pvc-carryp-of-make, fn-pvc-carryp-when-atom); a reader uses the verdict only for the profile the carry names and decides afresh otherwise. Local policy; no RFC requirement.

proofs.title: The carried obligation-id set is a path-compressed id trie, updated by the retention delta
proofs.statement: books/post-retain-carried.lisp (post-alloc-3). The carry's set is a path-compressed id trie whose leaves are the ledger's own id strings (fn-rit-put, fn-rit-hasp; fn-rit-hasp-of-put holds for every node). fn-prc-carryp is fn-prc-set-okp: every pin and release id is in the trie and every string stored in it is a known id; fn-prc-set-okp-is-knownp: the trie then answers exactly fn-rii-knownp of the ledger it names. fn-prc-refresh keeps the carry for the same ledger, applies the retention delta (releases consed on the carried ones; pins = new pins over the carried ones less released ones: fn-prc-delta, fn-prc-set-okp-of-delta) and rebuilds only otherwise (fn-prc-set-okp-of-build); fn-prc-carryp-of-refresh. KEYSTONE unchanged: fn-prc-sbud-prepare-is-pidx-sbud-prepare (the prepare host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-buffer installs is PRF-191's fn-pidx-sbud-prepare under fn-prc-carryp), through fn-prc-admissiblep-is-admissiblep. host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-install-extended builds the carry at every recovery (fn-prc-refresh of nil). Local policy; no RFC requirement.

proofs.title: The open streams the transaction files: the numbered chunk checks each file's sequence in its one decode, and the unframe answers the payload without copying it
proofs.statement: Subjects, called by the host: fn-srs-checked-decode and fn-srs-unframe (books/store-recover-stream.lisp sections 5 and 6). host/native/io.lisp fnn-recover-full-replay (fnn-recover: every full-replay open, the store verbs and the owner start) reads the transaction files a chunk at a time as the replay takes them (fnn-recover-file-chunks): each file unframed by fnn-unframe-list, which sends the file as its protected prefix and its trailer to host/store-host.lisp fn-store-unframe-split (fn-srs-unframe), then the chunk of (FILE-NUMBER . RECORD) pairs to fn-srs-checked-decode, then its value to the guard-verified fn-srs-intern-step unless it answered :sequence (the host faults, as the per-file check did). KEYSTONE fn-srs-checked-decode-is-the-per-file-check: for every numbered chunk, fn-srs-checked-decode is :bad when a record does not decode, otherwise :sequence unless every record's sequence (fn-srs-record-sequence, which host/store-host.lisp fn-store-record-sequence is) is its file's number, and otherwise the decode of the chunk's records. fn-srs-checked-step-is-the-step: the host's two calls over a numbered chunk are fn-srs-step over its records, so PRF-261's fold keystone carries over. KEYSTONE fn-srs-unframe-is-the-frame-decode (no hypothesis, guard-verified subject): fn-srs-unframe of PREFIX and TRAILER is fn-frame-store-decode of their concatenation with fn-frame-trailer of PREFIX, which is what fnn-unframe computed for the whole file and its digest; on a well-formed frame its payload is PREFIX's own tail (no copy). Scope: the full-replay path without a selected pack (with one, the history is fnn-committed-history's and goes over in chunks by PRF-261); the open now answers the record count, and the verbs that need the records read them with fnn-history-records, which on a format-9 store reads the record log (fnn-log-history-records: the log kernel's committed records) and on format 8 the per-file layout (lane rm2-format9).

proofs.title: The owner's prepares decide the served groups themselves, and the carried owner invariant holds across every owner prepare the host calls, the deferred publications' order and the known abort
proofs.statement: books/owner-prepare-served.lisp and books/owner-prepare-served-ocl.lisp. The host's article prepare is fn-psrv-prepare (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-buffer and fn-owner-prepare): fn-prc-sbud-prepare when fn-psrv-event-servedp of the live configuration and the record, the owner unchanged otherwise (fn-psrv-prepare-refuses-unserved, fn-psrv-prepare-when-served); the refusal word is fn-psrv-refusal-kind (:refused for an unserved group). The host makes no served test. fn-psrv-event-servedp equals the configured replay's fn-cpr-event-servedp at the configuration (fn-psrv-event-servedp-is-cpr-event-servedp). KEYSTONES, each with fn-lgoc-invariantp (PRF-286) as the only hypothesis unless named: fn-psrv-prepare-preserves-invariant (plus fn-prc-carryp and the two carried index premises of PRF-191/PRF-242; no served hypothesis), fn-psrv-prepare-identity-preserves-invariant (fn-owner-prepare-identity: fn-psrv-prepare-identity tests a signed composite's article groups), fn-psrv-prepare-retention-preserves-invariant and fn-psrv-prepare-consumer-preserves-invariant ((:store (:prepare-retention/consumer E)) through fn-ocfg-step), fn-psrv-prepare-topic-preserves-invariant (fn-owner-prepare-topic: fn-psrv-prepare-topic, which is (:store (:prepare-topic E)) where the consumer projection admits E, fn-psrv-prepare-topic-is-ocfg-step-when-admitted), fn-psrv-known-abort-preserves-invariant ((:store (:known-abort))), fn-psrv-rcon-io-preserves-invariant (every record file observation of any staged record) and fn-psrv-log-order-preserves-invariant (fn-olr-ocfg-order whatever is staged). Store level: fn-psrv-deferred-stage-preserves (a deferred candidate staged at the reservation keeps fn-cst-relation and fn-cstp-carriedp), fn-psrv-deferred-record-dir-preserves-relation, fn-psrv-known-abort-preserves. The bridge to the budget gate: fn-psrv-prepare-is-sbud-prepare-when-served (under the carry's recognizer and PRF-191/PRF-242's carried view premises, the host's prepare of a served record is fn-sbud-prepare). The standalone Store's POST (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-prepare) calls fn-psrv-store-prepare-next (books/store-prepare-served.lisp), which stages only a record whose groups the configuration serves (fn-psrv-store-prepare-next-cases).

The retired-group witness (control-quanta-2's *lgt-r-prepared*) is refused by the host's prepare with the invariant kept. The topic prepare's projection-refused branch has no reachable witness (argued, not proved: the proposal's sequence is the carried topic counter, which the invariant keeps at the Store's next). FINDING: the plain signed composite (fn-stxa-p, what fn-owner-prepare-identity admits and fn-pcb-carried-event returns) is never staged: fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity admits only the row (fn-hstxa-p); witnessed in the same book. Certified hbox certify-20260927T145853Z-4012905. The host's identity entry is now fn-oiis-prepare-identity (books/owner-identity-served.lisp: signed-post's interned row, then this target's served test; the plain-composite finding above is fixed by that intern). Its teeth: tests/acl2/owner-identity-served-tests.lisp -- *ois-staged* (reachable: the wire composite of the signed fn.test article at the arena's count, staged as the candidate row, invariant before and after, completed by order and finish), the retired fn.test composite refused by name (owner unchanged, invariant kept; fn-oii-ocfg-prepare-identity alone stages it and breaks the invariant), the WIRE value where the row is expected (not staged; its served test passes whatever the groups), and *ois-bad* (corrupted-state: invariant dropped, row staged, conclusion fails). Certified hbox certify-20260927T152733Z-10493 (with owner-prepare-served-events-tests). the index and carry premises of the article prepare keep PRF-191's and post-alloc-2's teeth.

proofs.title: A configuration request refused before its record is written is un-staged by ACL2, so the configuration lock does not outlive the refusal
proofs.statement: books/owner-prepare-served.lisp fn-psrv-unstage, called by host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-reconfigure-unstage from host/native/admin.lisp fnn-owner-live-reconfigure-locked on the three pre-publication refusals (fn-oclc-live-authorizep refused, fnn-admin-authorize's candidate open refused, the immutable publisher's :refused); an uncertain publication or a fault keeps the stage and fences. KEYSTONE fn-psrv-unstage-preserves-invariant (hypothesis fn-lgoc-invariantp): the result carries the invariant, has the same owner (so the same Store and durable state: a process death on either side of the un-stage recovers the same history), configuration and pins, and nothing staged. Before it, a refused request left the record staged and fn-ocfg-step refused every :begin and :take (every POST) until a restart.
proofs.progress_note: Lane prepare-served (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27). Teeth: control-quanta-2's *lgt-stale* refuses :begin before and admits it after.

proofs.title: The served ARTICLE reads the article's bytes once and builds its reply in one pass, equal to the specified reply
proofs.statement: Lane gate-regress (2026-09-27): fn-rcompat-article-reply (books/nntp-reader-compat.lisp; reached from the served step through fn-nntp-archive-command-pinned, host/native/io.lisp fnn-reader-chunk's fn-served-step) executes fn-rcompat-article-reply-exec: one read of the article's bytes through the arena, the served reply over the served octets by fn-nntp-article-response-of-bytes, whose ARTICLE arm is the one pass fn-nntp-block-rev (RFC 3977 3.1.1 framing validated and each line dot-stuffed onto a reversed accumulator), and the stored reply's session decided by fn-nntp-response-okp-of-bytes without allocating. Over the live arena the exec is the specified reply (fn-rcompat-article-reply-exec-is-the-reply, hypothesis fn-arena-p); the pass is fn-nntp-crlf-lines then fn-nntp-stuff-lines then .CRLF over octet lists (fn-nntp-block-rev-is-the-block); fn-nntp-article-response is the of-bytes response over fn-nntp-article-bytes (fn-nntp-article-response-is-of-bytes); a response's session moves exactly when okp holds (fn-nntp-response-of-bytes-session).

proofs.title: The owner's identity prepare stages the row the intern makes of a signed composite, and seals its article's payload only when the Store took it
proofs.statement: books/owner-identity-intern.lisp fn-oii-ocfg-prepare-identity (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-identity, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-identity-commit for every signed POST's, signed NNTP transit's and signed BP application's kind-4 composite and every keyring snapshot). Since the records flip the identity prepare's gate (fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity) admits the retained kinds only (fn-stxe-p, fn-stxk-p, fn-hstxa-p); the owner's composite (fn-pa-authorized-event) is a wire fn-stxa-p, so it was refused and every signed POST answered 441. The entry stages fn-oii-identity-row, the row fn-intern-event makes, at the arena's count under the Store's keyring and generation. fn-oii-identity-row-is-the-intern: at h = (fn-arena-count fn-arena) the row is (mv-nth 0 (fn-intern-event w k g fn-arena)); fn-oii-seal-is-the-intern-arena: the intern's arena is the arena with fn-oii-identity-payload sealed when fn-oii-identity-sealsp holds, else unchanged (the host seals exactly that, and only when the Store changed); fn-oii-composite-row-is-held: a composite whose article decodes interns to an fn-hstxa-p row carrying the composite unchanged (D25: the relayed octets, which the test book shows are the poster's post-injection octets). KEYSTONE fn-oii-ocfg-prepare-identity-is-intern-then-step (hypothesis fn-own-relation of the owner): the entry at the arena's count is (fn-ocfg-step oc (list :store (list :prepare-identity ROW)) fn-arena) for ROW the intern's row, by PRF-144's fn-ccar-ocfg-prepare-identity-is-ocfg-step-under-relation.
proofs.progress_note: Lane signed-post (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27). The regression: records-flip c5808cd72 (fn-sn-prepare-identity's gate to fn-hstxa-p) and flip-L3 d689ec388 (the same in fn-ccar-sn-prepare-identity) changed the gate; the host entry kept passing the wire composite, and owner-signed-post-tests hand-built its row (ospt-row), so no test crossed the host line. The test book's witness is the reachable served-POST trace of owner-signed-post-tests over a flipped owner: the wire composite is refused by the gate, the interned row is staged, and the completion records the signed verdict.

proofs.title: The store's history is an abstract stobj of columns whose logical value is the history list, and the store node's event index answers what it answers
proofs.statement: books/history-columns.lisp (lane history-columns, stage 1 of 3; the coordinator's decision on PKT-PRS-1's event-index half, PKT-PRS-3, PKT-PRS-4). defabsstobj fn-hist: logical value the true list of retained events (fn-sf-records, oldest first, sequence = position); executable fn-hist$c: a resizable rows column by sequence, the count, and a Message-ID table from a salted 32-bit FNV-1a hash of the Message-ID of an event's article (taken by digest-free shape, fn-hist-key-article) to the sequences carrying it, newest first; a lookup compares every candidate exactly (fn-cei-event-article, fn-held-p, equal), so no answer assumes Message-ID uniqueness or hash separation (PKT-774 worst case: an adversary who learns the salt puts all N articles in one bucket; a lookup is then N exact comparisons, an append stays O(1)). Correspondence fn-hist$corr: the object IS the fold of the history's appends from the empty object with its salt (supporters digest-free; :corr-fn-exists t). Exports refined by defabsstobj: fn-hist-count (len), fn-hist-at (nth), fn-hist-msgid-records (fn-cei-article-records-for), fn-hist-append (append one) and fn-hist-clear, all exec functions guard-verified. KEYSTONE fn-hist-load-is-the-history: the open's load (clear with a salt, one append per event) is the history. Bridges over the store node's index under its correspondence fn-cei-correspondencep (PRF-144): fn-hist-count-serves-cei-count, fn-hist-at-serves-cei-get (every natural sequence, the history within 2^32 events), fn-hist-msgid-records-serve-cei (every Message-ID). Stage 2a (books/history-columns-store.lisp): R(o, fn-hist) := fn-hist = (fn-sf-records (fn-sn-files (fn-own-store o))); fn-hist-sync appends the rows past the stobj's count (fn-sf-records-nth); KEYSTONE fn-hist-sync-after-run-is-the-history: under fn-own-relation, R before any fn-own-run implies the synced stobj is the history after it (by fn-own-run-records-prefix); fn-hist-sync-of-prefix-is-the-history. The store's carried folds from the stobj under R alone, for every cache: fn-hist-count-is-used (fn-sbud-used), fn-hist-bytes-carried-is-bytes-extend, fn-hist-debt-carried-is-debt-extend, fn-hist-usage-carried-is-usage-extend (the EXTEND specifications fn-sbud-bytes-carried, fn-scf-debt-carried, fn-scf-usage-carried meet under the index). Stage 2b path E (lane history-columns-2): host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-install-extended calls fn-hist-load on the installed store's history (every recovery: fn-owner-recover-from-store-open, -recover-rows, -recover-from-checkpoint), establishing R; fn-owner-record-octets, fn-owner-record-debt and fn-owner-carried-usage call fn-hist-sync on the owner store's files then fn-hist-bytes-carried, fn-hist-debt-carried and fn-hist-usage-carried (guard-verified), preserving R between installs by fn-hist-sync-after-run-is-the-history; the committed count the budget reads is fn-sf-records-count (fn-sf-records-count-is-used-by-definition), no longer the event index. Not yet switched (stage 2b remainder): the Message-ID readers (acceptance payload ref on the store node, the BP receiver's fast lookups), the consumer poll window, the owner completion refresh, the checkpoint tables and the in-book prepares' fn-sbud-count. Local policy; no RFC requirement.
proofs.progress_note: history-columns stage 1 2026-09-27: measured in an hbox ACL2 session over the same held rows, the structure's own live bytes per record: fn-hist 58.6 B (10k, 27-char Message-IDs), 56.8 B (10k, 47-char), 76.4 B (1k); the store node's index fn-cei-build 692 B, 1,429 B, 681 B. Stage 2 (switch the store node's index) and stage 3 (held-row strings into a byte pool) open.

proofs.title: The log kernel the host holds keeps the committed records' count, frames by guard-verified code, and every host transition over it, the pipelined commit's included, is the logical kernel's transition under the abstraction
proofs.statement: Subjects: the concrete kernel transitions host/native/io.lisp calls (fnn-log-open-kernel -> fn-lgc-open, fnn-log-prepare -> fn-lgc-t-prepare, fnn-log-take -> fn-lgc-phase / fn-lgc-take, fnn-log-ensure-extent -> fn-lgc-extension-needed-p / fn-lgc-extension-target, fnn-log-append -> fn-lgc-append-admitsp / fn-lgc-frontier / fn-lgc-append-octets / fn-lgc-append, fnn-log-fence (the syncer's fnn-log-sync-sealed-batch) -> fn-lgc-fence / fn-lgc-fence-failed, fnn-log-finish -> fn-lgc-finish-one, fnn-log-rotate -> fn-lgc-rotate-admitsp / -rotate-needed-p / -rotate, the open's catch-up, fnn-log-reserve and fnn-log-write-history -> fn-lgc-consume-to). The concrete kernel is (:lgc COUNT LAST FRONTIER NEXT-TXID BATCH INFLIGHT ACKED PHASE); fn-lgc-of replaces the logical kernel's COMMITTED by its length. KEYSTONE fn-lgc-run-refines-the-kernel (books/store-log-kernel-concrete.lisp): for every host operation sequence OPS -- prepare, take, consume-to, append, SEAL (the extension to fn-lgc-sealed-extent then the append: lane log-2's pipelined commit), fence, fence-failed, finish-one, rotate -- the concrete kernel reached from fn-lgc-open of the segment string is fn-lgc-of the logical kernel reached by the same OPS from fn-lgt-recover of its octets (the kernel fn-lg-recover-program-establishes-the-relation names), with no hypothesis. The pipelined commit's owner and syncer steps are each one operation under the log's kernel lock (fnn-log-with-kernel), so every interleaving is one OPS (a take behind the batch in flight is a :take between its :seal and :fence). So PRF-264's relation, crash and link theorems over fn-lgk-* are theorems about the kernel the host holds. Per transition: fn-lgc-prepare-refines, -t-prepare-, -append-, -fence-, -fence-failed-, -finish-one-, -consume-to-, -take-, -rotate-refines, fn-lgc-open-refines, and the observers (fn-lgc-observers-of-abstraction, -append-octets-, -append-len-, -fitsp-, -append-admitsp-, -extension-needed-p-, -extension-target-, -sealed-extent-of-abstraction). The extension: fn-lgc-extend-program-keeps-the-relation (fn-lg-extend-program run over the concrete kernel ends on the same kernel, R-related to the logical one, the segment NEXT long; fn-lg-extend-run-keeps-the-kernel), fn-lgc-sealed-extent-fits-the-batch (after the extension the seal's append fits, whole units, never shrinking; hypotheses: a positive unit, an extent of whole units). Execution (input-loop-2 section 6: *1* fn-lg-log recursed per octet and a 3 MiB POST exhausted the owner's stack): the fit and the fence's frontier use fn-lgc-log-len, guard-verified arithmetic over record lengths, equal to (len (fn-lg-log records prev unit)) with no hypothesis (fn-lgc-log-len-is-the-log-length); the append's octets and the fence's chain head use guard-verified twins fn-lgx-* (each equal to its logical function with no hypothesis) through fn-lgc-log-octets / fn-lgc-last-trailer (fn-lgc-log-octets-is-log, fn-lgc-last-trailer-is-last-trailer). Measured (hbox, 1,000 POSTs x 2 KiB, format 9): the kernel's retained COMMITTED was 38.8 KB per record (18 B per history octet) of live heap, and each fence copied it; after, 0 (planning/evidence/per-record-state-2026-09-27.md; lane kernel-concrete-2's re-measure there).

proofs.title: The Store prepares' field checks are ACL2's: the host calls one verdict per prepare, the metadata bound is exactly the record codec's, and every field the node generates for a POST is admitted
proofs.statement: books/post-fields.lisp. Subjects, each the function the host calls: fn-pfld-article-inputsp (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-buffer, fn-owner-prepare; host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-prepare), fn-pfld-retention-inputsp (fn-owner-prepare-retention, fn-store-sn-prepare-retention), fn-pfld-lookup-inputsp (fn-owner-existing-action, fn-owner-existing-action-buffer, fn-store-sn-existing-action), fn-pfld-group-name-requestp (fn-owner-reconfigure, fn-owner-declare-group), fn-pfld-bp-ingress-inputsp (host/bp-ingress-host.lisp fn-bpi-host-inputsp), fn-af-message-idp (fn-store-sn-lookup, -lookup-foundp, -verdict), fn-pfld-post-evidence (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-prov-post). The host predicates fn-store-text-octetsp, fn-store-msgid-octetsp, fn-store-msgid-validp and the host constant *fn-store-max-text* (512) are deleted. KEYSTONE fn-pfld-textp-is-a-record-metadata-field: an admitted field is fn-record-metadata-bytes-p of its string and its octets round-trip. KEYSTONE fn-pfld-textp-is-exactly-the-record-metadata-domain: over printable octets (33..126, hypothesis) the check IS the record's metadata domain, so no ceiling below the codec's (*fn-record-max-metadata* 256) remains; the deleted 512 admitted fields the record refuses. KEYSTONE fn-pfld-identity-text-is-admitted: fn-id-text of a nonempty octet identity of at most 128 octets (a SHA-256 identity is 32) is admitted. KEYSTONE fn-pfld-post-evidence-is-admitted: for a natural generation, the post evidence (wire form when fn-prov-durablep, legacy rendering otherwise; principal 'local' when no path identity) is admitted. fn-pfld-group-name-requestp-is-bounded-by-the-codec: a group-name request is within the group name's codec ceiling. Scope: the three metadata fields are node-generated, so their bound is a codec domain (STO-021's third class), not an admission limit or a profile field; the data a POST carries keeps its bounds where they are (RFC 5536 Message-ID, the profile's payload/group bound fn-sbud-post-boundary, the profile's header limits STO-030).
proofs.progress_note: Lane host-decisions (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27; prepare-served's host-decision list, item 1). Teeth: tests/acl2/post-fields-tests.lisp: REACHABLE witnesses over the identities and evidence the node builds for a POST (fn-id-subject-of-payload, fn-id-obligation-of through the digest attachment; fn-pfld-post-evidence with and without a path identity), each keystone's complete antecedent and conclusion; each conjunct of the article verdict removed refuses; BOUNDARY witnesses at 256/257/512 octets (the old host limit admitted 512, the record refuses it); the printable hypothesis needed (a space is a metadata octet the check refuses); the identity bound needed (129 octets renders 258); must-fail of the exactness keystone without its hypothesis and of the identity keystone without its bound.

proofs.title: A known abort of any staged deferred record (retention, identity, consumer, topic) resolves: the Store lands :ready with the live node advanced over the consumed transaction id, the relations kept
proofs.statement: books/store-node-resolution.lisp fn-sn-known-abort (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-known-abort: (:store (:known-abort)) through fn-owner-step, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-publish-prepared on a StoreError before the link; host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-known-abort for the standalone Store). fn-sn-known-abort-enabledp: a record phase (:record-staged or :record-data-durable) and, for a held article row, fn-sn-record-bindsp; for every other Store event (fn-store-event-p, not fn-held-p), that the event applies to the live node (consp of fn-replay-apply-record). The transition: the file kernel's known abort (fn-sn-known-abort-files, unchanged) and the node's aborted completion for a held row, fn-replay-advance-txid to the frontier for a deferred event. Before this target only the retention event had the deferred arm; a known abort of a staged identity, consumer or topic record was the identity, so the owner answered :fault and the host fenced (indeterminate) where the abort was known. KEYSTONE fn-sn-known-abort-preserves-relation (fn-snt-relation, no other hypothesis), fn-sn-known-abort-is-exact-node-abort (:ready and the node, per arm), fn-sn-known-abort-cannot-acknowledge. Configured level: fn-psrv-known-abort-preserves (fn-cst-relation and fn-cstp-carriedp) and fn-psrv-known-abort-preserves-invariant (fn-lgoc-invariantp of the owner after (:store (:known-abort))), every candidate. Crash points: the abort performs no syscall; its cuts are the record program's cuts before the link (books/byte-store-programs fn-bs-record-program: record-created, record-written, record-staged-durable), which are independent of the record's kind.

proofs.title: A lab host's raw clock reading becomes a clock observation in ACL2: units, the DTN epoch and whether the wall is usable are decided there
proofs.statement: books/clock-reading.lisp (prefix fn-clkr-). Subject fn-clkr-observation-of-ns, called by host/bp-ingress-host.lisp fn-bpi-host-observation (the lab BP ingress, Python bridge; fn-bpi-host-context). KEYSTONE fn-clkr-observation-of-ns-decides-the-wall, no hypothesis: every reading is a fn-clock-observationp; it has a wall exactly when the host claims one, the reading is a natural at or after the DTN epoch (2000-01-01, *fn-clkr-dtn-epoch-unix-ms*, equal to books/nntp-responses' *fn-nntp-unix-dtn-offset-ms*) and the error bound is a natural; then its wall is the reading's milliseconds past the epoch and its error the host's bound, each within the clock's range. The host's ns-to-ms arithmetic, epoch comparison and constant *fn-bpi-host-dtn-epoch-ms* are deleted. Served readings (assurance-hygiene-4/-5): the native host hands its raw readings to ACL2 and computes nothing: gettimeofday's seconds and microseconds to fn-otm-wall-reading, whose DTN epoch is ACL2's constant *fn-otm-dtn-epoch-unix-seconds* (KEYSTONE fn-clkr-wall-reading-is-the-ns-decision: for integer seconds and natural microseconds the reading has a wall exactly when its nanoseconds are at or after the epoch, and the wall is fn-clkr-ms-of-ns's milliseconds past it); SBCL's tick counter and rate to fn-otm-monotonic-ms (host/native/io.lisp fnn-monotonic-ms, called by fnn-owner-monotonic-ms, fnn-store-prepare-observation, fnn-bridge-config-initial, the admin clock, fnn-feed-now, fnn-tcl-now, fnn-pull-monotonic) and CLOCK_BOOTTIME's seconds and nanoseconds to fn-otm-boottime-ms (host/native/bp.lisp fnn-bp-monotonic-now) (KEYSTONE fn-clkr-monotonic-readings-are-the-ns-decision: each is fn-clkr-ms-of-ns of the reading in nanoseconds, the tick counter when a tick is a whole number of nanoseconds). The genesis's creation time (assurance-hygiene-6): gettimeofday's seconds and microseconds to fn-otm-wall-seconds (host/native/io.lisp fnn-genesis-created-seconds, called by fnn-genesis-octets) (KEYSTONE fn-clkr-wall-seconds-is-the-ns-decision: for integer seconds and natural microseconds it is the ns decision's wall floored to whole seconds, 0 when that decision has no wall). The host's encode-universal-time offset constant, its tick and boottime arithmetic and the genesis's floor to seconds are deleted.

proofs.title: The outbound feed sends the stored article's bytes, read through the arena, and a command word reaches the host only with octets: an unsendable offer is refused by name, never an owner stop
proofs.statement: books/owner-feed-article.lisp. Subjects: fn-ofa-feed-article (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-feed-octets passes it to fn-own-feed-port-observe-peer as the article of a 335 or 238; called by fn-owner-feed-reply-chunk, which host/native/feed-service.lisp fnn-feed-reply-step calls through fnn-owner-feed-arena-step) and fn-ofa-publication (the publication fn-owner-feed-octets and fn-owner-feed-tick return; feed-service.lisp fnn-feed-reply-step and fnn-feed-tick). KEYSTONES: fn-ofa-feed-article-is-the-feed-article-over-alpha (under fn-apr-store-at-restp of the owner's Store, the bytes are the payload of the octet-list model's feed article over ALPHA of the acceptance articles, books/store-intern.lisp fn-articles-wire-of: what fn-own-feed-article read before the records flip); fn-ofa-publication-command-words-have-octets (a publication whose word is :send or :offer has a non-empty command; otherwise its word is :unsendable, its sealed record plan is the port's, and it differs from the input only when the input was a command word without octets). fn-ofa-feed-article-is-an-octet-list: over an arena (fn-arena-p) the bytes are an octet list, never the handle. fn-ofa-publication-is-well-formed: the host's recognizer holds of the output. The attachment fn-arena-extent (books/payload-arena-extent.lisp) nests the paged arena (PRF-281) as a child plus an EXT array; an extent handle holds no octets; its relation fn-arena$xcorr is fn-arx-view of the child's logical value, and every {correspondence}/{guard-thm}/{preserved} obligation is proved (fn-arena-extent-get{correspondence} reads an extent handle through the realizer fn-durable-realize-octet, equal to the durable octet by A-DURABLE-EXTENT; fn-arena-extent-seal-extent{correspondence}). proofs.statement: books/owner-ack-after-barrier.lisp. The decision fn-oab-fence-before-change (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-statement-fence, called by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-statement-committed after every durable kind-4 composite fnn-owner-attempt-transit commits): an event whose authored source carries a key statement is fenced -- fnn-owner-statement-barrier commits the log's open batch, the statement and every member drained before it (fnn-log-commit-open-batch, awaiting a batch in flight first) -- before the statement-committed cut and the executor run. fn-oab-plan-only-after-the-fence (fn-ks-plan non-nil implies the fence), fn-oab-execute-only-after-the-fence, fn-oab-recovered-statement-was-fenced (fn-ks-pending, the open's recovery, acts only on such a record). KEYSTONE fn-oab-quantum-reports-after-its-barrier: over fn-oab-quantum, the host's schedule of one batch quantum (START's drain with the statement fence, cut and key-change take; SYNC's barrier when the word is :fenced; COMPLETE's deferred lines -- each member's outcome line and the executor's line naming the statement and its key change -- and the replies fn-ocs-member-releases names over fn-ocs-commit-step's action), fn-oab-reports-follow-fences-p holds: every cut, line and rendered reply names only records a barrier has fenced since their take. fn-oab-pipeline-reports-after-its-barriers: the same for a batch in flight and the next batch prepared behind its barrier (START-NEXT), a statement among them. fn-oab-every-kind-reports-after-its-barrier: for each of the fourteen record kinds in *fn-oab-record-kinds* (served and relayed articles, statements and their key changes in the quantum; the control post, BP applications, identity events, the key change at open, keys redecide, consumer, topic and retention events as a batch of one; configuration records and XREDEEM's publication through their own immutable publication), its route's trace reports only after its barrier; a kind with no route is unaccounted. proofs.title: A batch barrier is a request with a deadline and the disk's mode is ACL2's over recorded time: reads and status never wait on a pending barrier, a deadline never tells a member anything, and a POST arriving while the disk is slow is refused try-later with the reason exactly when health says so; past the stall deadline H every poster of the batch in flight is told uncertain, never accepted or refused, within H plus one committer wake (F4-W)
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-otm-next, fn-otm-observe, fn-otm-commit-event, fn-otm-committer-wake (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-gate-pick, fnn-owner-gate-leave, fnn-owner-commit-event, fnn-owner-commit-wake), fn-otm-disk-event (fnn-owner-disk-event: the committer's :issue at the syncer's start, :clock at each expiry of its timed wait, :return at the completion it observes; :clock on demand before a POST admission and a health/status render), fn-otm-wait-ms (fnn-owner-disk-wait-ms), fn-otm-admit-post (fnn-owner-disk-admit, in the served read quantum that queued a POST), fn-otm-disk-lines / fn-otm-health-lines (host/native-live-status-host.lisp). KEYSTONE fn-otm-barrier-reader-bound (books/owner-time-model.lisp): for S with the pipeline's phase :staged (the barrier pending) and every sequence WS of pick observations (W EVENT) with a reader waiting at every pick and the commit class waiting only when the committer's wake is :start-next (fn-otm-barrier-walk-okp), the quanta picked before the first :reader pick (fn-otm-barrier-walk) contain no control, poster or transit quantum, at most one :commit whose event is :next-started, and at most one more :inspect than :commit; EVENT is unconstrained and the device's latency is not a quantity of the walk. KEYSTONE fn-otm-disk-event-keeps-the-pipeline: every disk event leaves the pipeline's value unchanged (so fn-ocs-members-told-only-after-the-barrier and fn-ocp-complete-only-after-the-barrier hold of every run with deadlines: a deadline never tells a member anything). fn-otm-next-is-ocp-next, fn-otm-commit-event-is-ocp-commit-event, fn-otm-observe-keeps-the-disk: the pipeline's keystones (PRF-248, PRF-267, PRF-272, PRF-288) hold of the host's calls. fn-otm-recorded-time-is-monotone (the recorded time is the max of the readings; a lower reading increments the regression count and moves nothing); fn-otm-shed-only-past-the-deadline and fn-otm-past-the-deadline-sheds (a POST is shed exactly while a barrier is pending D or more at the recorded time); fn-otm-shed-iff-slow (shed iff the health/status disk line says disk slow); fn-otm-return-recovers, fn-otm-clock-event-never-issues (the completion is the recovery; no clock event re-enters slow without a new barrier); fn-otm-return-records-the-latency; fn-otm-wait-reaches-the-deadline (a clock event WAIT-MS after the recorded time finds the barrier past its deadline and enters :slow once); fn-otm-issue-only-when-none-pending, fn-otm-issue-is-pending-and-admits. Hypotheses of the wall-clock reading (stated, not proved): the store commits through the record log (format 9); the quanta admitted during a barrier contain no I/O wait (true of :inspect, :reader and START-NEXT; the inline barrier of :control/:poster/:transit quanta is not admitted in flight, PKT-825 (c)); the served read's octets are in memory; the committer thread is scheduled (its clock events can be late, never early). Slice 2 (lane time-model-2): the limits (D H C) are the live configuration's barrier-deadline-ms, barrier-stall-ms and clock-event-ms rows (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-barrier-limits; fn-otm-limits: defaults 5,000 / 30,000 / 1,000 ms, H read as at least D), carried by the barrier's :issue. fn-otm-disk-mode is :stalled past H; fn-otm-admit-is-the-mode (shed exactly in :slow and :stalled). KEYSTONE fn-otm-stall-tells-no-member-its-outcome: fn-otm-stall-releases (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-stall-release, called by the committer once per barrier when fnn-owner-disk-stalled-p) releases every member :own-uncertain, :uncertain-reply or :close, never :rendered, one per member; with fn-otm-disk-event-keeps-the-pipeline a member is told its own outcome only in a COMPLETE after a fenced barrier, and a member told at the stall is dropped from the COMPLETE's releases (fnn-owner-unreleased). KEYSTONE fn-otm-f4w-stall-within-h: from a pending barrier not past H (since at most the recorded time), committer clock events each at most its wait (fn-otm-wait-ms) plus LATE after the recorded time (fn-otm-clock-run-okp) enter :stalled at a reading at most since + H + LATE, and until one does every reading is before since + H; fn-otm-wait-stays-within-the-stall (the wait never reaches past H). fn-otm-return-after-a-stall-is-named (the completion after a stall answers :recovered-from-stall). Hypotheses stated, not proved: the committer is not blocked on the device (the syncer is); LATE bounds the scheduler's lateness of one timed wait; the committer appends a clock event at every wake while a barrier is pending (host). Not claimed: that the since-at-most-now hypothesis is needed (no counterexample found; the weakened statement is not yet proved).

proofs.title: QUIT ends the served fold: after the 205 no octet is framed or answered, whatever the read boundaries (RFC 3977 section 5.4)
proofs.statement: fn-served-step-stops-at-quit: for any connection CONN and octets LEFT and RIGHT, when the connection fn-served-step leaves after LEFT is quit (fn-served-quitp: its reader session is no longer open, which QUIT's 205 leaves), fn-served-step over LEFT ++ RIGHT has exactly the effects and the connection of fn-served-step over LEFT (the one hypothesis). fn-served-step-of-quit-connection-is-a-no-op: a read of a quit connection emits nothing and leaves it unchanged; fn-served-feed-of-quit-connection: the byte fold stops there. The fold stops on fn-served-haltedp (the handshake owed after 382, or quit) in fn-served-feed and in every twin the host executes (fn-served-feed-counted, fn-scar-feed-counted, fn-scar-feed-span, fn-scar-scan-span, fn-scr-feed-span, fn-scr-scan-span), each proved equal to the reference as before. Subject: fn-served-step, which books/owner.lisp fn-own-read calls once per socket read; the native owner calls fn-served-step-counted-fast (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span), equal to fn-served-step of its consumed prefix (fn-served-step-counted-fast-is-reference, fn-served-step-counted-result-is-step-of-consumed-prefix). With fn-served-run-is-the-concatenated-step every cut of LEFT ++ RIGHT into reads serves the same, which is the host's stop after the read that carried the close (fuzz-nntp F1).
proofs.progress_note: Covered scope: the host's stop after the read carrying the close (host/native/mux.lisp) is measured by the fuzz reproducers and the differential harness, not proved. host/native/mux.lisp's close-after-handshake case (STARTTLS and a close in one read) is deleted (lane served-leftovers): the host reads books/served-plan.lisp fn-splan-step-handshake-owed, the 382's handshake only when the step neither closes (after QUIT no 382 is emitted) nor meets the exposure's failed-login close, so the loop never holds both.

proofs.title: A transit article is bounded by the operator's profile before its verdict: the transit connection opens at the profile bound, the served run retains at most it, and the cut article is refused by name (437/439) and closed
proofs.statement: fn-tb-open-peer-body-limit-is-the-profile-bound: for an admitted profile and O2 the owner fn-osb-install leaves (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-install-profile, on every run path), a transit connection fn-own-open-peer opens (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-open-peer, at accept) has a wire body limit no larger than the profile's max-article-octets A, whatever the peer record's inbound-max-octets (peer add writes the codec ceiling, 4 GiB, there); fn-own-peer-body-limit-is-within-the-profile-bound: the limit fn-own-open-peer uses is positive and at most fn-own-body-limit. fn-tb-served-run-retains-at-most-the-body-limit: for any connection whose wire is a wire state (fn-wire-statep, which every open establishes) and any reads, the completed lines the wire retains after fn-served-run (its body size) are at most the body limit it opened with, and everything it retains (fn-wire-held-octets: the completed lines and the current line, in article mode the packed store of lane chunked-body) at most that limit plus the line ceiling (the opening line limit or the body limit plus one); fn-tb-served-step-keeps-the-body-limit / fn-tb-served-run-keeps-the-body-limit: no read changes the limit. fn-peer-transfer-unreceived-effects (called by fn-peer-step and its carried twin fn-pgc-transfer-step): an article the wire cut at the limit ((:reject :body-overlimit)) is refused 437 with the size's reason text (IHAVE, RFC 3977 section 6.3.2) or 439 echoing the Message-ID (TAKETHIS, RFC 4644 section 2.5.2), then closed; fn-peer-transfer-unreceived-effects-well-formed. Fuzz-nntp F2.
proofs.progress_note: Open (D27): the bound is on octets, not on the representation; the wire retains an article in flight as octet lists, so its heap cost is a constant multiple of A (measured in the record), as for POST. The concrete in-flight representation is input-loop-2's item 2.

proofs.title: Every group membership is charged to the history budget: the budget is the sum of the stored charges, a crosspost the budget cannot pay for is refused by name, and the heap figure's membership term is bounded by H
proofs.statement: ember's decision 2026-09-27 17:30Z (D27: no new crosspost cap). books/store-budget.lisp *fn-sbud-membership-octets* = 320 (the heap model's *fn-heap-membership-octets*: measured 137 octets of live heap a membership plus 45 for the group's name, 182, with the per-group index's doubling slack): fn-sbud-row-octets charges a held row its payload extent plus 320 per group (fn-sbud-row-memberships: a held row's groups, or the held article's inside an accepted-statement composite), so KEYSTONE fn-sbud-record-octets-pays-the-memberships: 320 x (fn-sbud-record-memberships records) <= (fn-sbud-record-octets records). books/store-budget-stored.lisp KEYSTONE fn-sbud-record-octets-is-the-stored-octets (restated): under fn-sbud-rows-extents-okp the budget is the sum of fn-sbud-row-stored-octets (extent + 320 per membership). books/store-budget-article.lisp: fn-sbud-article-figure p k = the record ceiling + 320 k, so every gate (article verdict, capacity vector, carried verdict) charges the memberships and the stored charge is within the figure (fn-cvec-held-row-within-its-figure). books/store-capacity-vector.lisp fn-cvec-article-refusal-word (host: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare and fn-owner-prepare-buffer, over fn-pout-prepare-article's word): KEYSTONE fn-cvec-article-refusal-word-names-the-memberships: the word is :memberships exactly when the prepare answered :unaffordable, k >= 1, the article budget was 0, and without the membership charge the count gate, the history gate and the vector would have admitted it; 441 posting failed; ... (memberships) (books/nntp-post.lisp), 436 to a feeding peer (books/peer-inbound.lisp). books/heap-store-figure.lisp: the state is arena(USED) + 48 N + 2 x 12,288 N + 2 x 320 M with M the memberships; the figure takes M = fn-heap-membership-bound = floor(H / 320) (KEYSTONE fn-heap-membership-bound-holds-the-charged-memberships; fn-heap-membership-term-is-at-most-twice-h), and fn-heap-store-figure-holds-every-store gains the hypothesis 320 M <= H. Figures (core 200 MB, 64 MiB nursery; full-store heap before -> after): small 1,052 -> 891 MB, development 7,326 -> 2,254, scale 172,841 -> 10,539, default 10,856,110,718 -> 120,789,633 (its T = 2^32 - 1 records at 12 KiB each), gate (scale, T 2^20, A 4096) 41,977,971 -> 37,107. Lane bp-retention-leftovers (membership-budget's two deferrals): the accepted-statement composite's gate charges its figure, fn-cvec-statement-figure k = the kind's publication ceiling 196,608 + 320 k (k the groups its article is filed in): fn-cvec-statement-verdict-at (count gate, history gate and vector at the figure; host: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-identity-publication-verdict through the carried twin fn-pvc-statement-verdict-carried, KEYSTONE fn-pvc-statement-verdict-carried-is-cvec-statement-verdict-at, asked by host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-identity-commit over the WIRE event, whose kind the row reading fn-store-event-kind answered NIL, so the preflight charged a composite nothing), and the history arm fn-cvec-record-admittedp admits an :accepted-statement row at that verdict with its stored charge within the figure. KEYSTONE fn-cvec-statement-admission-keeps-the-vector; KEYSTONE fn-cvec-statement-row-within-its-figure: for a retained composite row, its stored charge is within its figure exactly when its encoding is within the ceiling, whatever its group count; fn-cvec-record-keeps-the-vector restated over the new arm. The preflight's count fn-oii-publication-group-count is the interned row's (fn-oii-publication-group-count-is-the-rows). The developer store post names the membership refusal: fn-cvec-article-verdict-word (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-article-verdict-word, host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-post), :memberships exactly when the verdict refused, k >= 1 and the figure without memberships passes every gate (fn-cvec-article-verdict-word-by-definition).

proofs.title: The store's history as an FNADTSN2 image on the page store's pages: the decoder inverts it, the page store's page digest is the image's page-digest leaf, an append changes only O(K + columns) pages while no region doubles, and the open's header check and the row read the host calls (need-verdicts) answer the history over verified pages
proofs.statement: books/history-pages.lisp. The image of a history H (fn-hp-image H SALT) is adt-ser (the FNADTSN2 bytes, books/proto/adt-bytes.lisp) over the schema ((:u64) (:u64) (:octets)): per event MKEY (1 + fn-hist-hash of fn-hist-key-msgid, 0 when none), the length of its fn-scc-encode tree octets, and those octets zero-padded to a multiple of 8. KEYSTONES: fn-hp-decode-image (fn-hp-events-okp H, (len H) and (len (fn-hp-image H SALT)) below 2^64 => (fn-hp-decode (fn-hp-image H SALT) SALT) = (:ok H)); fn-hp-page-digest-is-leaf ((natp K), page K's words LE = page K of the image => (pgs-x-page-digest K ...) = the be-nat of leaf K of adt-page-digests, BLAKE3 of page K's octets: the page store's table-entry digest IS the image's per-page leaf, no second digest table); fn-hp-append-changes-only-dirty ((natp K), K not in (fn-hp-append-dirty H NEW SALT) => page K of (fn-hp-image (append H NEW) SALT) = page K of (fn-hp-image H SALT)); fn-hp-append-dirty-bound ((fn-hp-caps-same ...) => 16384 * |dirty| <= 11 * 16384 + 32 |NEW| + NEW's padded tree octets). Generic lemmas over any in-place region growth: fn-hp-body-page-same, fn-hp-ser-page-same, fn-hp-regs-of-append, fn-hp-body-dirty-in-pages, fn-hp-dirty-pages-bound. Named limit L-HP-DOUBLING: the canonical image places regions contiguously; a region that doubles is the writer's verdict (:grow R). Milestone 2 (books/history-pages-words, -exec, -read): the image as the page store's little-endian words (fn-hp-iw = fn-hp-pack8 of the image; fn-hp-words-le-octets-of-pack8, fn-hp-page-words-of-pack8); its header, cells and pool entries read back (fn-hp-w-header-of-image, fn-hp-w-row-of-image); the host-called reads return need-verdicts and never fill a page. KEYSTONES: fn-hp-x-header-is-image ((fn-hp-okp H SALT), NPAGES = (fn-hp-npages H SALT), (fn-hp-vhold 0 (pgs-v-length pgs-mem) pgs-mem (fn-hp-iw H SALT)): every verified page holds the image's words, and the header's verdict :ok => (fn-hp-x-header NPAGES pgs-mem) answers (:ok (len H) lens starts); another schema digest is refused :schema); fn-hp-x-at-is-nth ((fn-hp-okp H SALT), (natp SEQ), SEQ < (len H), the same fn-hp-vhold, verdict :ok => (fn-hp-x-at SEQ ...) answers (:ok (nth SEQ H))). The open reads page 0 only; the first read of a row pays at most its four cells' pages and its pool entry's pages. Milestone 3a (lane arena-store-3, books/history-pages-write, -write-exec, -write-keys): the writer the host calls, fn-hp-x-append EV SALT N LENS STARTS pgs-mem -> (mv VERDICT N2 LENS2 pgs-mem): six blocks (header words 6-17, one cell per column, the padded tree's words in the pool) written with fn-hp-x-put (each word's page marked dirty) only after every touched page is verified (fn-hp-x-blocks-ready: else the need-verdict, nothing written) and only while no region changes its cap (else (:grow R), nothing written). Model theorem fn-hp-iw-of-append1: (fn-hp-iw (append H (list EV)) SALT) = (fn-hp-wreps (fn-hp-iw H SALT) (fn-hp-blocks H EV SALT)) when no region's cap changes and the new header fields are u64. KEYSTONE fn-hp-x-append-refines: (fn-hp-okp H SALT), N = (len H), LENS = (fn-hp-lens H SALT), STARTS = (fn-hp-starts H SALT), (fn-hp-vhold 0 (pgs-v-length pgs-mem) pgs-mem (fn-hp-iw H SALT)) and the verdict :ok => (fn-hp-okp (append H (list EV)) SALT), N2 = (len (append H (list EV))), LENS2 = (fn-hp-lens (append H (list EV)) SALT), the starts do not move, (fn-hp-vhold 0 ... mem2 (fn-hp-iw (append H (list EV)) SALT)), and every page P it marks dirty is in (fn-hp-append-dirty H (list EV) SALT) and verified in mem2. Milestone 3b (arena-store-3): the image format is FNADTSN2 (books/proto/adt-bytes.lisp: magic FNADTSN2, version 2, the image's page count NPAGES after the region table; adt-decode and the history's open check fn-hp-w-header accept any placement adt-placement-ok (every region after page 0, inside NPAGES, apart from every other) and refuse any other :placement; FNADTSN1 is refused :magic; adt-decode-ser keeps the canonical round trip, adt-placement-ok-of-starts-l the canonical placement); every keystone above re-proved over the FNADTSN2 image; the decoder's acceptance of a moved region is witnessed in tests/acl2/proto-adt-2-tests.lisp. The placed image (books/history-pages-placed): fn-hp-piw H SALT STARTS NP, NP pages of zeros with the header page (naming STARTS and NP) and each region's padded words at its start; fn-hp-piw-canonical: at the canonical starts and page count it IS fn-hp-iw. KEYSTONES over ANY placement (adt-placement-ok STARTS (fn-hp-lens H SALT) NP): fn-hp-x-header-is-placed ((fn-hp-okp H SALT), (fn-hp-starts-okp STARTS), the placement, (fn-hp-vhold 0 (pgs-v-length pgs-mem) pgs-mem (fn-hp-piw H SALT STARTS NP)), verdict :ok => (fn-hp-x-header NP pgs-mem) answers (:ok (len H) (fn-hp-lens H SALT) STARTS)); fn-hp-x-at-is-nth-placed (the same over the placed image, (natp SEQ), SEQ < (len H) => (fn-hp-x-at SEQ ...) answers (:ok (nth SEQ H))); fn-hp-x-append-refines-placed (books/history-pages-append-grown; the writer takes NP and grows a region's cap in place when (adt-placement-ok STARTS LENS2 NP), else answers (:grow R C) and writes nothing: N = (len H), LENS = (fn-hp-lens H SALT), (fn-hp-starts-okp STARTS), the placement, the vhold over the placed image, verdict :ok => the appended history is an image, N2/LENS2 its header, the placement stays valid, every verified page holds the appended history's placed image, and every newly dirty page is in fn-hp-append-pdirty and verified). Model fn-hp-piw-of-append1 from generic facts: block replacements nest (fn-hp-wreps-nest) and commute (fn-hp-wreps-commute), books/history-pages-nest. GROWTH (lane arena-store-4): fn-hp-piw-caps-extend (the placed image viewed with larger caps that still fit the placement is the same image) and fn-hp-piw-of-append1-grown (the append model without cap equality: the new lengths fit the placement, the deltas word-aligned); fn-hp-piw-relocated (books/history-pages-grow: moving region R to page TT >= NP of an image grown to NPN pages is three block writes -- header words 6-18, R's old pages zeroed, R's words at TT); KEYSTONE fn-hp-x-relocate-refines (books/history-pages-relocate: the host's (fn-hp-x-relocate R C N LENS STARTS NP pgs-mem) answering :ok leaves every verified page holding (fn-hp-piw H SALT (update-nth R NP STARTS) (+ NP C)), the placement valid there, and every newly dirty page page 0, one of R's old pages or a new page, each verified; any other answer changes nothing); fn-hp-grow-then-append (books/history-pages-grow-then-append: after (:grow R C) and a relocation answering :ok, the next :grow names a later region, so an event relocates at most five times; -only-r: none when only R outgrew). Old logical pages become zero pages; their physical pages leave every new root at the next commit and are reclaimed (PRF-344); logical page 0 and the reserved physical page never move. RECORDS ON PAGES (m3c P1, ACL2 side; books/history-pages-step, -import, -view): KEYSTONE fn-hp-x-append-step-refines (the one call per committed event, fn-hp-x-append-step: the writer, relocating on (:grow R C) at most five times; never answers :grow; :ok => the vhold of the appended history's placed image at STARTS2 NP2 and its header answer; otherwise the history unchanged at the (possibly relocated) STARTS2 NP2); fn-hp-x-init-refines (the empty history's image on an empty page store); fn-hp-x-append-all-refines (the import fold: the first K2 events appended, all of them on :ok); fn-hp-records-at-is-nth (record I of the image's history followed by an in-memory suffix: an :ok answer is (nth I (append H SUFFIX)); below the end the answer is :ok or a need-verdict). The link from fn-sf-records to image + suffix is not proved yet.
proofs.pending_subject: No host function calls the image yet: the owner's open and snapshot through the page store (fnps-open / fnps-commit over the fn-hist image; fn-hp-x-header, fn-hp-x-at and fn-hp-x-append from the host) are lane arena-store-3's m4.
proofs.progress_note: Milestone 1: the image, its round trip, the one digest theorem and the region plan. Milestone 2: the words, the open's header check and the row read with need-verdicts over verified pages. Milestone 3a (arena-store-3): the writer, refining the append into the words, marking only the proved dirty list. Milestone 3b: the FNADTSN2 format (free placement, NPAGES); the header check, the row read and the writer proved over any placement. Open: the growth path (a region that outgrows its pages moves to new pages; the (:grow R) verdict), the store's E/R records on pages with fn-hist a view, host wiring, measurement at the store open.

proofs.title: The owner's snapshot as a copy-on-write page store with a two-level page table: commit-then-open, crash anywhere, fork isolation, complete fresh allocation, and reclamation that never frees a page a live root keeps
proofs.statement: books/pagestore.lisp (model), books/pagestore-keystones.lisp, books/pagestore-reclaim.lisp, books/pagestore-exec.lisp, books/pagestore-gc.lisp, books/pagestore-words.lisp, books/pagestore-words-blake3.lisp. Model: a commit record names a directory run whose entries name table pages of 341 entries, whose entries name data pages (PHYS TXID BLAKE3-256); growth appends logical pages; allocation from (FREE HWM). KEYSTONES over R-opens, dirty pages in order (pgs-lpages-ok) and the allocator invariant (pgs-alloc-inv): pgs-open-after-commit (the commit opens on the next txid and the state with the dirty pages replaced or appended); pgs-open-after-crash (any subset of the commit's data, table and directory writes with the record old, torn or new opens on the committed or the previous state, the previous one unless the record landed; takes pgs-writes-faithful, A-CRYPTO instantiated); pgs-crash-isolates-other-roots; pgs-fork-denotes; pgs-alloc-fresh (allocation always answers, distinct, fresh) and pgs-plan-commit-complete; pgs-tables-after-plan (rewriting only the touched table pages rebuilds the new table pages). Reclamation: pgs-keeps-after-commit, pgs-alloc-inv-after-commit, pgs-cycle-inv-start/-after-commit, pgs-invariants-after-fork, KEYSTONE pgs-reclaim-never-frees-live (the sweep of a mark-and-sweep cycle that commits may interleave with adds only addresses no valid record of any root keeps), pgs-sweep-split (bounded quanta). Executable: pgs-x-plan-tab-refines/-dir-refines (the O(dirty) plan over the pgs-t words is pgs-plan-ptab on the decoded table), KEYSTONE pgs-x-commit-refines (pgs-x-commit, what the host calls, is pgs-plan-commit's sequence), pgs-x-dir-verdict-is-model, pgs-x-table-verdict-is-model, pgs-decode-encode-table; pgs-g-sweep-all-is, pgs-g-mark-record-covers-encoded, pgs-g-reclaim-sound (the executable cycle keeps pgs-alloc-inv); pgs-x-words-digest-is-blake3 (the word digest the host calls, pgs-x-words-digest over the page store's octet buffer fn-octets-pg, is the big-endian natural of fn-blake3 of the words' little-endian octets, with hypotheses (natp BASE) (natp NB) only; fn-blake3 is fn-digest's attachment's value, fn-blake3-stobj-is-blake3; SHA-256 until 2026-09-28). Whole-disk refinement (books/pagestore-refine.lisp, lane arena-store-5): the abstraction pgs-x-abs-disk of the files (the model pages and each root's slot page) with the handle's slot words pgs-m[0,1024) bound first as the open root. Not yet: the open square (the host's open is a host loop of ACL2 steps and fills, and its lazy open is not the model's, L-PGS-LAZY-SHAPE), so the handle's agreement with the model's open is a hypothesis of both squares; the model pages are not yet derived from the page file through A-PGS-HOST-IO. proofs.title: init refuses by name a profile the machine's budget cannot hold, unless a target budget is named; a store init admitted always reopens on the same machine
proofs.statement: ember's decision 2026-09-27 17:30Z and the coordinator's release blocker (friend-path packet A: a 2 GiB node init said within-budget=yes, reservation 1,234 MB, and after 960 posts every start refused machine-cannot-hold-profile heap=2104 MB machine=2031 MB). books/heap-reservation.lisp: fn-heap-reserve-full-store-decide (was fn-heap-reserve-first-run-decide over the empty store) judges the run of the FULL store the profile admits (heap-figure's :run figure unobserved), and fn-heap-reserve-acceptsp and fn-heap-init-reservation-octets use it. KEYSTONE fn-heap-init-accepted-store-always-reopens: a profile (the admittedness hypothesis was removed after proving the weakened theorem) the full-store decision accepts within OBS is accepted by the launcher's :run decision (fn-heap-reserve-operation-decide) on the same OBS for every OBSERVED store and every owner bound. fn-heap-init-decide, for an operator's request (sizing :requested) this budget does not hold: written only when FN_INIT_BUDGET_MB names a target budget that holds its whole reservation (fn-heap-init-target-holdsp; the decision (:init REQUEST WORD MB BUDGET-MB :requested NIL TARGET-MB), the line `within-budget=no target-budget=N MB'), else refused :init-budget-cannot-hold-profile with the reservation and the budget (KEYSTONE fn-heap-init-decide-refuses-the-operators-request-past-the-budget; exit 1, fn-heap-init-refusal-exits-1), nothing written; unobserved machine memory is :machine-memory-unobserved. fn-heap-init-decide-honors-the-operators-request now holds when the budget or the named target holds the request. Host: host/native/operator.lisp init (fnn-heap-init-decision, host/native/heap.lisp), unchanged: it prints the line and exits with the decision's code. EXTENSION (batch AX fix init-budget, finding R1 of the public-node rehearsal, planning/evidence/public-node-rehearsal-2026-09-27.md): init run outside the service's memory limit sized the store for the whole machine and the service then refused machine-cannot-hold-profile. The named budget is FN_INIT_BUDGET_MB (there is no init option); it already caps the budget init sizes for. books/heap-reservation.lisp fn-heap-init-budget-note (decision physical limits budget-octets), called by host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-init-decision-noted (from host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-execute-init, on the same observation of the machine as the decision), is NIL or (:named-budget-below-machine NAMED-MB MACHINE-MB), MACHINE-MB the budget init observes without the named one (fn-heap-init-machine-octets: the physical memory less the OS's reserve and each limit). Init still writes (a warning, not a refusal: a named budget below the machine is how a store is made for a smaller limit, and the harness names one); the host prints fn-heap-init-budget-note-line on stderr after the init line: `warning init-budget-below-machine named-budget=N MB machine-budget=M MB: ...' telling the operator to run init under the service's memory limit. KEYSTONE fn-heap-init-budget-note-names-the-budget-init-sized-for: (implies (and (equal (car d) :init) (posp named) (< (floor named MiB) machine-mb)) (and (equal (car note) :named-budget-below-machine) (equal (nth 1 note) (nth 4 d)) (equal (nth 2 note) machine-mb) (< (nth 4 d) machine-mb))) with d the fn-heap-init-decide decision and note its fn-heap-init-budget-note: the note names the budget the store was sized for (the decision's) and the larger machine; fn-heap-init-budget-note-only-when-named-below-machine-by-definition: otherwise (no named budget, a named budget at or above the machine, a refusal) there is no note and init is as before; fn-heap-init-budget-is-the-named-below-the-machine. Not addressed: an init with NO named budget outside the service's limit still sizes for the whole machine silently (it cannot observe the unit's limit); the docs say to run init under the limit or name it.

proofs.title: The record log's open refuses damage by name and recovers only the torn tail of the one pending write
proofs.statement: Subjects: the calls host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-stream-segment makes after the stream's stop (fnn-log-probe-tail: fn-lgdm-start, fn-lgdm-done-p, fn-lgdm-q, fn-lgdm-header-len, fn-lgdm-entry-len, fn-lgdm-step; then fn-lgdm-verdict, fn-lgdm-effective, fn-lgdm-refused-p, fn-lgdm-refusal-text, fn-lgdm-report-text, fn-lgdm-repair-text), reached from fnn-log-recover (the writable open of the active segment; fn-lgdm-quarantine-name before a confirmed repair's truncation), fnn-log-open-read-only (status), fnn-log-scan-segments and fnn-log-read-closed-segment (closed segments), and fnn-command-recover's --repair truncate SEGMENT:OFFSET; and fnn-log-check-history-chain (fn-lgdm-chain-continues-p) in the history reads fnn-log-history-each and fnn-log-closed-records. KEYSTONE fn-lgdm-open-verdict-is-the-classification (books/store-log-damage.lisp): over the segment's octets C with no hypothesis, the verdict of the probe run from the stream's stopped state (the state fn-lgw-run-is-the-open names) is fn-lgdm-classify: the stop is the scan's frontier, the splice verdict is fn-lgs-chain-broken-p's, and the damage point is the least unit-aligned offset at or past the stop where an entry validates under the predecessor it claims (fn-lgdm-least-valid). KEYSTONE fn-lgdm-no-silent-prefix: the open's stop is the scan's frontier; when a valid entry starts at any offset P + k*UNIT below the extent the verdict is refused (:broken or :damaged), never a recovered prefix; and a :damaged verdict names a valid entry at or past the stop. KEYSTONE fn-lgdm-damage-lies-in-the-last-write: for C = a well-formed log of admitted records from a digest genesis, then octets Y, then zeros (a crash image of the one pending write at L's end has this shape with Y inside the write's range: fn-bs-crash-of-aligned-append), the stop is at or past L's end, a :damaged or :broken verdict points into Y, and with Y empty the verdict is not refused. fn-lgdm-repair-is-only-the-confirmed-damage: the operator's repair changes nothing but the :damaged verdict of the active segment of a writable open at exactly the confirmed SEGMENT:OFFSET, and keeps the stop. Scope: the torn-tail case is exactly the last incomplete write; damage confined to the LAST entry is indistinguishable from a torn tail and is recovered with a `log torn-tail' line (reported, exit 0); a frame embedded at a unit-aligned offset inside the torn write's own octets is refused (fail-closed). Record: planning/evidence/log-corruption-2026-09-27.md.

proofs.title: A payload handle is not octets: the retained article's and held row's payload is a handle by recognizer, disjoint from octets, and the host's every call into ACL2 refuses a wrong-kind argument or argument count by name before the entry runs
proofs.statement: books/payload-kinds.lisp. fn-payload-handle-p (a compound recognizer for natp) types the retained payload fields (books/acceptance.lisp fn-article-payload, books/held-record.lisp fn-held-payload). KEYSTONES fn-payload-handle-is-not-octets and fn-payload-octets-are-not-a-handle: no value is both a handle and fn-cbor-octet-listp octets, so a guard naming one kind refuses the other. The host entry guard (host/native/io.lisp fnn-entry-guard, run by fnn-call, the dispatcher every fnn-core* wrapper applies) evaluates, on the actual arguments, the entry's arity and exactly the conjuncts (R v) of the entry's own ACL2 guard with R in *fn-entry-guard-kinds* and v a non-stobj formal, and raises fnn-entry-guard-fault naming the entry, the position, the formal and the kind; it never evaluates another conjunct (no whole-state revalidation). tools/harness_check.py entry-guards: every dispatched entry's byte-carrying formal is covered by a kind conjunct (111), a body-first kind test (11) or a named exemption (16); tools/payload_kind_check.py: every definition that reads a retained payload declares its kind (fn-payload-kind :handle, :source or :wire) and the check has no waivers (lane entry-guards-2 closed the fourteen). The consumers it found: KEYSTONE fn-stx-index-of-store-without-a-keyring (books/stx-index.lisp; no hypothesis): with no keyring the statement index of ANY article list is (fn-stx-index-empty), so the keyring-less opens (books/config-observed.lisp, books/store-checkpoint-open.lisp twice, books/replay-identity-index.lisp; host fn-store-open-* through the owner's open) build the empty index and never walk the retained articles' handles. KEYSTONE fn-ofa-feed-article-is-the-owner-step-article (books/owner-feed-article.lisp; hypothesis fn-apr-store-at-restp): the bytes the book owner's feed step hands the feed (books/owner.lisp fn-own-feed-reply, now over fn-arena: fn-handle-bytes of fn-own-feed-article's handle) are the host entry's (fn-ofa-feed-article, host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-feed-octets). Reclaim: fn-rcl-verdict and fn-rcl-summary are the octet model (declared :wire), equal over ALPHA to the arena counts the host calls (fn-rcl-store-counts, PRF-088's fn-rcl-store-counts-is-the-model-over-alpha); fn-rcl-reclaimable is the standing verdict (fn-rcl-standing-verdict), which reads no payload: the log reclaim's context (books/store-reclaim-pack.lisp fn-rclp-ctx-reclaimable) tests the tombstone on the record's own octets and the counts through the arena (fn-rcl-verdict-in). Control status and HDR :fn-control read the article through the arena (lane matrix-reds, PRF-084/PRF-228).

proofs.title: The decision journal: every event the scheduler's disk-and-clock value takes is one journal entry, the journal reads back whole and replays to agreement from the run's start, and every decision the host asks of the value reads only what the journal determines
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-otm-disk-step (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-disk-event: every disk and clock event, the served read's :served reading included, fnn-owner-advance-clock), fn-otm-note-step (fnn-owner-journal-note: the stall's release, members told and queued POSTs shed), fn-otm-start-line (fnn-owner-journal-open), each rendering the entry (SEQ OP READING A B C WORD) with fn-otm-jline; the host offers it to the service-log writer thread (host/native/io.lisp fnn-journal-line), which appends it to STORE/decisions/decisions.fnj, never on the owner and never waited on, bounded by ACL2's sink (books/log-sink.lisp). fn-otm-disk-step-unfolds: the step's word and value are fn-otm-disk-event's. fn-otm-journal-read-of-jlines: a list of entries (naturals) rendered and read back is itself, the reader's status :whole. KEYSTONE fn-otm-journal-determines-the-decisions: for every run STEPS of the host's calls (fn-otm-run: disk events of the four kinds, notes, and the gate's fn-otm-next, fn-otm-observe and fn-otm-commit-event interleaved in any order; hypothesis fn-otm-run-okp: the host appends only :clock, :served, :issue and :return events), the journal it writes reads back :whole and fn-otm-replay from the run's start answers :agrees (every recomputed word equals the journaled one, no gap) at the run's disk and clock. fn-otm-decisions-read-only-the-journal-state: admission, mode, wait, the 441 and 440 reply lines, health's disk lines and the log lines read only the disk and the clock. fn-otm-wall-reading-shape (books/clock-wall-reading.lisp, N3 of lane proto-determinism): the wall reading's validity is ACL2's (host/native/io.lisp fnn-owner-wall-milliseconds). fn-otm-journal-report-of-a-run: the operator's replay (host/native/io.lisp `store ROOT journal' calls fn-otm-journal-report and fn-otm-journal-exit) of the journal of any such run from fn-otm-init reports status=whole replay=agrees. Not claimed: that the file on disk holds every entry (the sink drops by name under its bound: a gap replay reports as (:gap SEQ)); anything about the record log's fold (lane proto-determinism: deterministic); the served machine's own replay from the :served readings (the readings are journaled; the served transcript replay is not built).
proofs.progress_note: Lane time-model-2 (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-27). REPL-admitted on hbox (the book 4.6 s ACL2 time from source). Teeth (tests/acl2/owner-time-model-tests.lisp, prefix t2-): a reached run of nine interleaved host calls whose six entries are exact, read back whole and replayed to agreement; a tampered word (:diverged 3); a dropped entry (:gap 3); a run with an event kind the host never appends (:malformed 1, fn-otm-run-okp removed); two values with equal disk and clock decide alike and a different clock does not.

proofs.title: While the disk sheds a served read runs with posting not permitted and under the disk-slow posture, so a POST command is answered 440 with the disk's reason before its article, a peer's IHAVE 436 and CHECK 431, and the node's configuration is never changed by it
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-otm-read-span (books/owner-time-admission.lisp), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at calls with S, the gate's scheduler value at the read's recorded time (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-handle-chunk-read: fnn-owner-advance-clock's :served event, then fnn-owner-gate-sched-value; the admission is fn-otm-admit-post of S). fn-otm-read-span-when-admitted-unfolds: admitted, it is fn-orr-read-span (every reader-read theorem, PRF-288/PRF-296, holds of the host's call). KEYSTONE fn-otm-read-span-while-shedding: while shedding, connection ID's read is fn-orr-read-span over the owner with that connection's injection configuration's posting bit off (the served step reads the connection's snapshot, books/owner.lisp fn-own-served-conn; its effects are that read's), and afterwards the connection, when its record has the owner's shape, has the posting bit it had before; the owner's own configuration is never touched. fn-otm-closed-posting-never-awaits-an-article: under a configuration that does not permit posting, fn-scr-post-step from a session not awaiting an article leaves it not awaiting one (the POST is answered 440, RFC 3977 section 6.3.1, and no article is read). Mutating control (host/native/control.lisp: an operator post, a live configuration change, a moderation decision) is answered BUSY while fn-otm-admit-post sheds, at a clock event appended before it waits for the gate. Not claimed: the chain from fn-orr-read-span to fn-scr-post-step (the served machine calls it with the connection's injection configuration; stated, not proved here); IHAVE/CHECK during slow (PKT-862). EXTENSION (lane log-leftovers, 2026-09-27; the disk's reason on the wire and PKT-858). KEYSTONE fn-otm-read-span-while-shedding (restated): connection ID's read while fn-otm-admit-post S is :shed runs over fn-otm-shed-ocfg (posting bit off; the disk-slow posture's entry *fn-peer-shed-entry* at the front of the owner's refused-offer memory, so every peer session re-pinned with it by books/owner.lisp fn-own-conn-live-session is fn-peer-shed-p); its effects are that read's with each generic 440 and posting-disallowed 441 replaced by ACL2's fn-otm-post-command-reply S / fn-otm-shed-reply S exactly when the connection's posting bit was on before the read (fn-otm-disk-effects), and the read's own when it was off (the configuration refuses, not the disk); afterwards the connection has its posting bit back and the refused-offer memory is the read's with the posture's entries out (fn-otm-strip-shed; fn-otm-strip-shed-leaves-no-posture, fn-otm-strip-shed-of-marked). fn-otm-disk-effects-names-the-disk: with replacement lines that are not the generic ones (true of the host's lines at every reached slow and stalled state, test book), no generic 440 or 441 is left and the count of effects is kept; fn-otm-disk-effects-keeps-the-rest. proofs.statement: books/store-log-buffer.lisp: the host preads each log entry into its own octet buffer fn-octets-lg (an abstract stobj congruent to fn-octets) and calls fn-lgw-step-buf and fn-lgb-entry-places over it. KEYSTONE fn-lgw-step-buf-is-step: (fn-lgw-step-buf st unit max extent buf) = (fn-lgw-step buf st unit max extent), no hypothesis (the index decision fn-lgb-decide-fast runs under mbe behind the buffer's recognizer; its equality with the list decision is fn-lgb-decide-fast-is-decide over fn-lgb-decide-is-flat, the list step's closed form for an entry of at least 74 octets under a frame bound; shorter entries and other bounds take the list step on the buffer's octets). So fn-lgw-run-is-the-open (PRF-297) holds of the host's loop. KEYSTONE fn-lgb-entry-places-is-list-places: (fn-lgb-entry-places pos count unit buf) = (fn-arx-list-places buf pos count unit 0 0 nil 0 0 nil), no hypothesis. Host subject: host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-stream-segment. NOT done: the step's next-txid fold still decodes each record (fn-lgt-txid over fn-record-decode-exact-impl), and the records still reach the replay as octet lists.

proofs.title: A replay that stops at an article its configured capacity cannot hold refuses the open by name; any other stop stays a fault and names where it stopped
proofs.statement: books/store-open-replay-refusal.lisp: fn-sorr-stop finds the history item at the configured replay's fault position (the event whose sequence plus the configuration records fn-cpr-loop takes before it is the position). fn-sorr-refusal REPLAYED RECORDS CONFIGS answers (:refused :capacity TXID MSGID CHARGE RESERVED CAPACITY) when that item is an article whose charge exceeds the last good node's retention capacity less its reservation, else nil; it is nil unless the replay answered :fault (fn-sorr-refusal-only-on-a-stop), and its numbers are that retention state's with RESERVED + CHARGE > CAPACITY at an :event-refusal (fn-sorr-capacity-names-the-retention-state: fn-retain-admissiblep's capacity conjunct fails). fn-sorr-refusal-text renders the operator's line; fn-sorr-stop-text names any other stop (position, reason, txid). Host subject: host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-open-classified records the refusal (answering :refused, printed as the open's refusal by host/native/io.lisp) or the stop's text (answering :fault; fnn-replay-fault appends it to the fault's line, exit 4 as before). proofs.title: The full replay's log walk decodes each record once: the walk without its txid fold, and the fold from the replay's decode
proofs.statement: books/store-log-walk-once.lisp: fn-lgw-step-buf-nf is the buffer step keeping the stream's NEXT (fn-lgw-step-buf-nf-is-step-nf: EQUAL to fn-lgw-step-nf, the list step with NEXT kept, no hypothesis). KEYSTONE fn-lgw-run-nf-then-fold-is-run: from (fn-lgw-start GENESIS FLOOR), the run without the fold (fn-lgw-run-nf), its NEXT then set to (fn-lgw-next-fold RECORDS FLOOR) of the records it emitted (fn-lgw-set-next), IS fn-lgw-run, no hypothesis (the general form fn-lgw-run-of-set-next-is-run-nf holds from any state and NEXT); so PRF-297's fn-lgw-run-is-the-open holds of the host's composition. fn-lgb-decode-next RS NEXT answers (mv (fn-srs-decode RS) (fn-lgw-next-fold RS NEXT)) under mbe, its exec decoding each record once (fn-lgb-decode-next-exec-decode, fn-lgb-decode-next-exec-fold); the fold over any chunking is the fold of the concatenation (fn-lgw-next-fold-of-append). books/store-log-txid.lisp: fn-lgt-txid reads the record through the codec's seam (fn-record-decode-exact), as the replay's decode does. Host subject: host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-stream-segment under *fnn-log-stream-finish* (bound by fnn-recover-log's full replay) calls fn-lgw-step-buf-nf and, at the segment's end, fn-lgw-set-next with the fold fnn-recover-log-stream-flush took from fn-lgb-decode-next.
