proofs.title: Catching up from a peer: the XFNCATCHUP batch serves only what ARTICLE would, always progresses within its quantum, and the requester offers only verified batches, only through its own IHAVE verdict, and resumes at the last journaled batch
proofs.statement: Serve (books/peer-catchup-serve.lisp fn-cu-serve-reply, which books/nntp.lisp fn-nntp-command-pinned calls for XFNCATCHUP on the pinned, READ-restricted view; books/nntp-auth.lisp gates it with the archive readers): fn-cu-select-serves-only-retrievable: every article a batch serves is an entry of the view and fn-cu-servedp (a valid Message-ID in the view's trie, not reclaimed, CRLF-framed, held at a number in a group the wildmat admits: what ARTICLE <msgid> on the same view returns); fn-cu-select-makes-progress: a batch from FROM below the view's end answers NEXT > FROM; fn-cu-select-stays-within-the-quantum: for a natural quantum, the batch's article octets are at most the quantum or the batch is exactly one article (served whole, never cut); fn-cu-serve-reply-effects-well-formed (books/peer-catchup-effects.lisp, cited by books/nntp-pinned-effects.lisp): the reply is one well-formed response. Requester (books/peer-catchup.lisp; host/native/pull-service.lisp fnn-pull-round calls fn-cu-session-begin-pair, fn-cu-session-step-pair, fn-cu-session-close; fnn-pull-journal-append calls fn-cu-cursor-envelope; fnn-catchup-journal-open calls fn-cu-journal-scan and fn-cu-records-replay): fn-cu-step-keeps-offers-verified: fn-cu-step preserves fn-cu-verifiedp (while offering, the held batch chains from the committed chain to the peer's claim and what remains is a suffix of it; while waiting, nothing remains), and fn-cu-begin establishes it; fn-cu-on-end-refuses-a-digest-mismatch: a batch whose records do not chain to the claim ends the round :failed with (:close) only and the cursor unmoved; fn-cu-step-installs-only-through-the-verdict: every effect of a step that reaches the local node is the IHAVE of the record the round then waits on, or, only on the local node's 335 in phase :offer, that record's body; every journal record is the round's committed cursor with nothing of its batch left; fn-cu-records-replay-is-the-last-cursor and fn-cu-resume-asks-from-the-journaled-cursor: the open recovers the last journaled cursor of the peer and a round begun from it asks from exactly that position and chain; fn-cu-decode-of-encode: the FNCU record round-trips. The digest chain c' = SHA-256(c || SHA-256(article) || msgid) is a transport and completeness check, not an authentication of the peer. Not proved: positions are stable only while the view grows (a READ-rule change can skip entries on resume); the peer's claim is relative to the chain the requester presents.
proofs.progress_note: Slice 1. Open: an absolute peer digest at a position (needs an ordinal index), position stability across a view reshape, the concrete representation of the batch buffer (D27, as the pull's ARTICLE), the snapshot hook (design only, waits for arena-store).

proofs.title: A compressed record in the log expands to exactly the record it was sealed from; a compressed extent reads back, through the proved DEFLATE decoder, as the record's payload; the replay and the commit with compressed extents are the resident ones
proofs.statement: books/payload-lz-record.lisp (brief C2 of planning/evidence/article-compression-2026-09-27.md section 6; lane compression-extents). The record FRAME sits between the record codec and the log: Z = 'fn-z' head ++ u32 DICT-ID, K, N, |STUB| ++ STUB ++ C, STUB the record R without its payload span [K, K+N), C a raw DEFLATE stream (books/payload-deflate.lisp fn-pzd-decode, PRF-257) decoding to that span against the dictionary DICT-ID; fn-lzr-expand gives R back or refuses by name (:lz-frame, :lz-dictionary, :lz-decode); a record that is not a frame passes unchanged. fn-lzr-seal (the one producer of a frame) runs the proved decoder over the host's untrusted candidate and frames R only when it decodes to the span, the span reaches the profile's threshold MIN (0 never) and the frame is shorter (fn-lzr-compress-p); a record that begins with the frame head is framed with an empty span. KEYSTONE fn-lzr-expand-of-seal: for a table binding DICT-ID to DICT, a u32 DICT-ID and an octet record of u32 length, (fn-lzr-expand dicts (fn-lzr-seal dict dict-id min r k n candidate)) = (:ok r), whatever the candidate, threshold or span. fn-lzr-replay-reads-the-sealed-record (the D25 decision): for (fn-record-p w) the expansion of the seal of (fn-record-encode w) decodes to (:ok w), so the content identity, Message-ID comparison, signatures and Cancel-Lock -- all over the authored octets, computed before the seal -- are unchanged; the log's frame trailer covers the durable Z. Dictionaries: fn-lzr-dictsp (u32 id, at most 65,536 octets; the initial table is the shipped one, books/payload-lz-dicts.lisp, PRF-912), fn-lzr-dicts-add refuses a rebinding (fn-lzr-dicts-add-keeps-bindings). The compressed extent (FILE EOFF ELEN CPOFF CLEN TRAILER N DICT-ID) of a frame at its log place (fn-lzr-extent-of: C is Z's tail and decodes to the record's payload); KEYSTONE fn-lzr-extent-read-denotes: under the faithful read of Z at its place, fn-lzr-read of C's durable octets against the dictionary is (:ok payload). The arena (books/payload-arena.lisp, books/payload-arena-extent.lisp, books/payload-arena-extent-logic.lisp): exports fn-arena-seal-lz-extent / fn-arena-reseat-lz-extent (logic: the handle is fn-lzr-lz-value DICT (durable C) N, books/payload-lz-value.lisp), every {correspondence}/{guard-thm}/{preserved} obligation proved over the reference and the extent attachment (EXT entry an 8-tuple carrying the dictionary's octets); KEYSTONE fn-arena-seal-lz-extent-payload, KEYSTONE fn-arena-reseat-lz-extent-keeps-a-faithful-arena. The replay (books/payload-lz-replay.lisp): fn-lzr-intern-step (a frame whose C decodes to the record's payload sealed as a compressed extent, anything else the plain extent intern); KEYSTONE fn-lzr-intern-step-refines: under fn-arx-faithful-p it is fn-srs-intern-step. The commit: fn-lzr-commit-reseats; KEYSTONE fn-lzr-commit-reseats-keep-the-arena under fn-arx-commit-faithful-p. The served read of a compressed handle is the host realizer fn-durable-realize-lz (A-DURABLE-LZ): the extent realizer's trailer-checked read of C, then ACL2's payload decoder over pooled buffers (fn-pzd-decode-bufs; KEYSTONE fn-lzr-decode-bufs-is-the-lz-value), a failed decode refused by name (arena-extent-lz-decode). Host subject: host/native/extent.lisp fn-durable-realize-lz calls host/native/deflate.lisp fnn-pzd-decode, which calls fn-pzd-decode-bufs; the seal (POST), the replay step and the commit reseat have no host caller yet (the lane's continuation wires them: planning/evidence/compression-extents-2026-09-27.md).
proofs.progress_note: Batch AY (2026-09-27): books/payload-arena, payload-lz-record and payload-lz-replay re-certified afresh at the merged batch digests (--recertify), persvati certify-20260927T234217Z-3182383 (10 passed, 0 failed; no book over 10 s). Certified on hbox: the 656 affected roots (679 books, certify-20260927T213338Z-2661898, passed) and, after splitting the replay into books/payload-lz-replay.lisp, its 3 roots (certify-20260927T221728Z-2829003, passed, no book over 10 s). Teeth: tests/acl2/payload-lz-record-tests.lisp on codec-c1's real 1993 article and its liblz4-HC blocks (without and with a 2,749-octet dictionary): the seal frames the record (136 and 334 octets shorter), expands to it and replays to the record through the attached codec; per keystone a reachable witness, ground counterexamples (a missing or wrong dictionary, a non-u32 id, an improper record) and must-fails per hypothesis.

proofs.title: `store reclaim` records its instant before it rewrites, and the rewrite is a function of the pre-reclaim store and that record
proofs.statement: books/reclaim-instant.lisp. The reclaim's instant NOW (the clock's stamp the context reads, host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-reclaim-rule-and-stamp) is the configuration limit row `retention-reclaim-at` (CODE = NOW + 1, 0 for no wall reading), staged as the one delta fn-rci-delta by fn-store-reclaim-instant-record (host/checkpoint-host.lisp, over the configuration record path fn-store-cfg-peer-delta-record) and published, before any rewrite, by host/native/checkpoint.lisp fnn-reclaim-record-instant (through host/native/admin.lisp fnn-admin-publish-record: authorization, publication, read-back), called by fnn-log-reclaim-steps on the :reclaim decision. fn-rci-recorded-instant-reads-back: for NOW nil or a natural (fn-rci-instantp), the configuration the published record yields (fn-rci-recorded-config: fn-cfg-apply-record, what every open applies) records an instant, reads back NOW, and keeps the retention rule. KEYSTONE fn-rci-recorded-context-is-the-decided-context: the context a replay derives from that configuration (fn-rci-context) is fn-rclp-ctx of the rule and NOW the host decided under. KEYSTONE fn-rci-recorded-decision-is-the-decision: the decision over the recorded configuration (fn-rci-decide-stream; `store reclaim --recorded`, host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-log-reclaim-decide-recorded from fnn-log-reclaim-steps) is fn-lgr-decide-stream at that rule and NOW over the same store and fold, so with PRF-271 the history the host checkpointed is determined by the pre-reclaim history and the record. With no recorded instant `--recorded` is refused :no-recorded-instant (fn-rci-decide-stream's first arm). fn-rci-delta-is-a-delta: for a representable NOW the staged delta passes fn-cfg-delta-listp. The operator keystones: `store reclaim --recorded` is exactly the :reclaim-recorded native action (fn-native-operator-run-store-reclaim-recorded-is-the-reclaim-recorded-action, fn-native-operator-run-reclaim-recorded-action-is-only-store-reclaim-recorded). Not a store-format change: a :set-limit row of a slot no reader names is admitted by every image (books/config.lisp fn-cfg-limit-ceiling) and read by none; a new record-log kind would be (books/store-recover-stream.lisp fn-srs-decode refuses an undecodable record).
proofs.progress_note: Lane log-leftovers (sub-lane log-leftovers-reclaim), 2026-09-27: PKT-857 (N2 of lane proto-determinism; time-model-2's PKT-861). Open: a process death between the instant's record and the checkpoint's install leaves the instant recorded and the history unrewritten; `store reclaim --recorded` completes it, a plain rerun records a later instant (the open does not apply a recorded instant by itself). The hypothesis fn-rci-instantp is shown necessary for the context keystone (tests: :late); for the decision keystone no counterexample is claimed (the decision reads NOW only through fn-rcl-rule-permits' natp test).

proofs.title: A peer's feed queue holds undelivered obligations, never history: a final answer retires the entry, a full queue is the named refusal feed-queue-full, and health holds it
proofs.statement: fn-feed-done (fn-feed-observe on 235/239/435/438/437/439, host: fn-owner-feed-octets -> fn-own-feed-reply; replay at open: fn-own-feed-recover -> fn-feed-replay) removes the entry (fn-feed-queue-retire). fn-feed-queue-length-is-undelivered: for a driven journal (fn-feed-drivenp), the queue after fn-feed-replay has length start + enqueue/commit records - final outcome records. fn-feed-final-outcome-retires-for-good: a final outcome for a Message-ID with no later enqueue leaves it out of the queue after the fold. fn-feed-accepted-outcomes-bounded-by-enqueues: accepted outcomes for (peer, Message-ID) are at most the times it was owed; fn-feed-at-most-one-accepted-outcome: at most one when owed once (fn-feedp is implied by fn-feed-drivenp, fn-feed-drivenp-implies-feedp). fn-own-intent-refusal-word (host: host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-drain-one) names a :capacity intent :feed-queue-full: its own 441 line (fn-post-store-refusal-text), and 436 for transit (fn-peer-transit-code; fn-peer-full-feed-queue-is-a-retry-code-by-definition). fn-nh-feed-queue-full-intent-is-held: a :capacity intent (fn-own-submission-intent-result, the reference of fn-icar-submission-intent the host calls) holds unavailable-peer in fn-nh-verdict over the same feed table (fn-nh-saturated-peer-is-held, fn-nh-feed-queue-refusal-is-held). fn-feed-distinct-fast-is-distinctp: fn-feed-distinctp (the fn-feedp conjunct every transition and replayed record checks) executes one pass with a fast alist (mbe); 0.2 ms at 1,024 entries on hbox against 19 ms quadratic.
proofs.progress_note: Open: the owner-level theorem keeps fn-own-feed-tablep, which is probably redundant (no violating value found; the weakened theorem is not proved). The power-loss rig has no feeding workload yet; retirement writes no new record (the :feed-outcome record already was a cut), and the keystones hold over every driven prefix. max-queue is still 1024 from `peer add` (an admission limit on undelivered backlog; no operator verb sets it).

proofs.title: The running owner's report string and obligation lines are built with constant stack: `obligations` at 5,000 answers and the owner keeps running
proofs.statement: fn-nls-octets-string-is-record-octets-string: fn-nls-octets-string, a loop, equals fn-record-octets-string on every value. fn-nls-buffer (called by host/native-live-status-host.lisp fn-native-live-status-host-answer) builds the report text with fn-record-octets-string, which since PRF-345 executes by a loop itself (books/records-shape.lisp); before, its non-tail recursion exhausted the 1,024 KB control stack past about 50,000 octets. fn-nls-obligation-lines executes fn-nls-obligation-lines-rev (mbe; the equation is its guard).
proofs.progress_note: Closed at the cause by PRF-345 (lane thread-stacks, PKT-693): books/records-shape.lisp fn-record-octets-chars and fn-record-string-octets-aux execute an accumulator loop (mbe), so every caller of the two conversions runs in constant stack; fn-nls-buffer now calls fn-record-octets-string directly and fn-nls-octets-string stays with its equation and tests.

proofs.title: Octet text codecs over the octet buffer: decimal and hexadecimal naturals, hex strings and RFC 4648 base64 round-trip, base64 accepts only canonical text and refuses by name, case-insensitive equality is equality of case folds, and the bounded token split loses nothing
proofs.statement: books/octet-text.lisp. Each codec is a list model over octet lists with an in-place twin over the octet buffer (fn-octets, books/octets-stobj.lisp) and a boundary theorem equating the twin with the model on the buffer's slice; every executable function is guard-verified. fn-ot-nat-parse-of-nat-octets: parsing the printed natural (radix 2..16) under the caller's bound MAX gives it back; fn-ot-nat-parse-bounded: an accepted natural is at most MAX. fn-ot-hex-decode-of-encode and fn-ot-b64-decode-of-encode: decode of encode is the identity (RFC 4648 section 4 for base64). fn-ot-b64-accepted-is-canonical: an accepted base64 text is the encoding of what it decodes to (padding bits zero, the pad only in the last quantum); fn-ot-b64-refuses-outside-alphabet and the refusal kinds :b64-quantum, :b64-alphabet, :b64-padding-bits are named. fn-ot-ci-equal-is-downcase-equal: ASCII case-insensitive equality is equality of the case folds. fn-ot-split-wsp-loses-nothing: the tokens are the input's non-whitespace octets in order, at most LIMIT of them; more is the refusal :too-many-tokens, never a truncation. No function caps data: bounds are the caller's (D27).
proofs.pending_subject: No host function calls these codecs yet (lane shared-books built them as the shared library the wire books re-derived); each wire book that adopts one names its host caller then.
proofs.progress_note: Lane shared-books (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-28), id assigned at the batch AY merge. Certified on persvati: certify-20260928T025149Z-846867 (under 10 s). Teeth: tests/acl2/octet-text-tests.lisp with the RFC 4648 section 10 vectors. Proof-style findings in docs/proof-style.md.

proofs.title: The compressed append: ACL2 plans the payload span, decides the frame over the untrusted DEFLATE candidate with named outcomes, and every record the log hands out is read back through the proved decoder; the switch is a configuration row
proofs.statement: books/payload-lz-append.lisp (lane compression-extents-2, the host wiring of C2 over PRF-326). fn-lzr-append-plan MIN R: the payload span (K . N) of the article record R (the codec decodes R; the payload's place checked) when MIN (the `compress-min-octets' :set-limit configuration row, fn-lzr-config-min; no row is 0, off: fn-lzr-config-min-without-a-row-is-off, fn-lzr-append-plan-off) wants it (no ceiling of the plan's own: the span is the admitted article's payload, so the operator profile's article-size admission limit bounds one append's encoder and decoder work; the retired C encoder's 2^30 - 1 one-call limit is gone, lane compress-9). fn-lzr-append-decide DICT DICT-ID MIN R K N CANDIDATE runs the proved decoder over the host's candidate (zlib 1.3.2 raw DEFLATE over the current shipped dictionary, vendored, untrusted; host/native/deflate.lisp fnn-deflate-candidate) and answers (:framed Z), (:kept :lz-no-gain) (the named policy: no block within the cap, or the frame not shorter), (:kept :lz-span), or (:refused :lz-candidate). proofs.title: BLAKE3 in ACL2: the definition over octet lists and its executable twin over the octet buffer
proofs.statement: books/blake3.lisp defines BLAKE3 (the compression function over 64-octet blocks with seven rounds as a chain of multiple-value functions over declared 32-bit words, chunks of up to 1024 octets with CHUNK_START and CHUNK_END, the tree whose left subtree holds the largest power-of-two number of whole chunks shorter than the input, parents, and the root's first 32 output octets) in the hash, keyed_hash and derive_key modes, every function guard-verified, with the shape proved (fn-blake3-shape, fn-blake3-keyed-shape, fn-blake3-derive-key-shape: 32 octets for every object). Agreement with BLAKE3 is evidence, not proof: tests/acl2/blake3-tests.lisp evaluates all 35 official vectors (third_party/blake3/test_vectors, tag 1.8.7) in all three modes. books/blake3-stobj.lisp is the executable twin over a list prefix and a window of the octet buffer, conses nothing per block, and is proved equal to the definition level by level: fn-b3x-byte-is-nthx, fn-b3x-words-is-words, fn-b3x-chunk-is-chunk, fn-b3x-node-is-node, and the keystone fn-b3x-hash-is-hash (the buffer hash of PREFIX then the window [A, A+WN) is fn-b3-hash of the octets of their concatenation, for a window inside the buffer); its three entries fn-blake3-stobj (any object, copied once into a local buffer), fn-blake3-of-prefixed-buffer and fn-blake3-of-prefixed-range are equal to fn-blake3 (fn-blake3-stobj-is-blake3, fn-blake3-of-prefixed-buffer-is-blake3, fn-blake3-of-prefixed-range-is-blake3). books/crypto-attach.lisp and books/frame-digest-buffer.lisp attach them to fn-digest, fn-frame-digest, fn-frame-digest-buffer and fn-frame-digest-range. In the saved images host/native/digest.lisp replaces the three entries with the vendored C (lib/libfn-blake3) after checking it against the official vectors and fn-b3x-hash (A-CRYPTO-NATIVE). Collision resistance is A-CRYPTO: about 2^-128 per chosen pair (the birthday bound over 256 bits), not proved.

proofs.title: A POST the store refuses at its drain for capacity or input wrote nothing: it is told its named refusal at once and never waits for, or is told uncertain because of, another member's barrier; a START of only such refusals issues no sync
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-ocs-told-at-drain-p (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-commit-start-locked, per drained member of a START, START-NEXT or the inline quantum), fn-ocs-start-event (fnn-owner-commit-start-event), fn-ocs-commit-step (the inline quantum, fnn-owner-commit-queued-locked) and fn-ocp-commit-step (the committer, through fn-otm-commit-event). KEYSTONE fn-ocs-unstaged-start-tells-its-refusals (books/owner-commit-steps.lisp): for every list WORDS of drained members' outcome words observed certain, if every word is told at its drain (fn-ocs-all-told-at-drain-p: :unaffordable, :memberships or :malformed, the refusals whose prepare staged no record) then the batch keeps no member (fn-ocs-kept-count 0), the START's event is :started-none, and the step from an idle owner is :none with the owner idle: no barrier. fn-ocs-kept-member-starts-the-barrier: a START whose first member is not told at its drain names the barrier. fn-ocs-told-at-drain-p-by-definition: a told word is never :durable, :durable-key-change-refused, :uncertain, :duplicate, :conflict or :refused. fn-ocp-unstaged-start-issues-no-sync (books/owner-commit-pipeline.lisp): the committer's step names :none, leaves the phase :idle and opens no next batch. books/owner-ack-after-barrier.lisp: the drain model tells such a member at once with a report naming no record and the batch completes the members it kept; fn-oab-quantum-reports-after-its-barrier and fn-oab-pipeline-reports-after-its-barriers (PRF-267's reply keystones in the ack model) hold unchanged in statement over it. Scope: the words are ACL2's outcome words, which the host takes from the attempt (fnn-owner-attempt: the prepare's refusal after the refused reservation was consumed); that a refusal word means no record was staged is the prepare's property (books/owner-prepare-outcome.lisp), cited, not re-proved here. A capacity refusal reads the capacity unfenced members use: its reason may not hold after a failed barrier, its outcome (nothing stored) does. A refusal that names another record waits for the barrier as before (fn-ocs-member-release).

proofs.title: The collector's trigger while a store opens is sized to the history it reads: at least 8 MiB, at most 4 x the history on disk, never more than the figure's trigger, and the figure holds every store at it
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-heap-open-nursery-trigger (books/heap-open-nursery.lisp), which host/native/io.lisp fnn-open-nursery calls at the start of every open (fnn-recover: the owner's recovery and every offline verb that opens), over the launcher's own history observation (host/native/heap.lisp fnn-heap-history-octets: the log's segments, checkpoints/ and the state checkpoint; NIL when unreadable). KEYSTONE fn-heap-open-nursery-trigger-bounds: for every D, NURSERY and HISTORY, 8 MiB <= trigger <= (fn-heap-nursery-trigger D NURSERY), and for a natural HISTORY trigger <= max(8 MiB, 4 x HISTORY). fn-heap-store-figure-holds-every-store-at-the-open-trigger: under PRF-198's keystone's hypotheses the store's need at this trigger is within D (the figure's keystone at the figure's trigger, and fn-heap-store-need monotone in the trigger). Why (F1, lane f1-bisect): an open conses in proportion to its history (81.5 MB for a 1,000 x 2 KiB store of 4,388,380 octets on d5ab87aec, two thirds in the checkpoint's decode), so at the figure's trigger (a sixteenth of the dynamic space, 48.75 MiB at the small profile's 780 MB) the open's garbage reached the whole trigger before the first collection: the reopen's peak was the live heap plus the profile's trigger, whatever the store's size.

proofs.title: The free space is a recorded observation and a write is admitted only above ACL2's need: below it every POST is refused try-later by name before its article (440, or 441 for an article already sent), nothing stored, the owner stays up, and the next observation with room recovers
proofs.statement: Subjects: fn-otm-admit-post (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-handle-chunk-read after fnn-owner-advance-clock's :served and, when fn-otm-space-due-p, :space event; host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at feeds S to fn-otm-read-span, PRF-323), fn-otm-disk-event with kind :space (fnn-owner-space-event: the committer before every barrier's syncer, fnn-owner-sched-snapshot before every health/status render, fnn-owner-space-observe-if-due before a served read's admission; ARG (FREE NEED), FREE the statvfs observation of the store's filesystem or nil), fn-otm-space-need (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-space-need: PRF-129's fn-smr-reserve-octets + 2 x fn-olr-omax + the `disk-reserve-octets' row, default 64 MiB), fn-otm-shed-reply / fn-otm-post-command-reply (the reason), fn-otm-disk-step (journal op 6). KEYSTONE fn-otm-admit-keeps-the-space-need: admitted with the space observed, free >= need. fn-otm-full-sheds: observed below the need, every write is shed whatever the barrier. fn-otm-space-need-covers-two-batches: from an observation F >= need, two batches of at most OMAX octets leave the reserve and the extra (hypothesis: nothing else writes to the filesystem between the observation and the appends; the observation at every barrier's issue keeps that window to two batches). fn-otm-space-recovers: an observation with room admits unless the barrier is past D. fn-otm-space-of-event / fn-otm-full-p-of-other-event / fn-otm-space-event-keeps-the-disk: only a :space event moves the space and it moves nothing else (so fn-otm-disk-event-keeps-the-pipeline and the durability keystones hold). fn-otm-admit-is-the-mode: shed exactly in :slow, :stalled, :full. fn-otm-shed-iff-slow restated: shed exactly when the disk line says slow/stalled or the space line says `disk full:'. PRF-311's fn-otm-shed-only-past-the-deadline, fn-otm-return-recovers, fn-otm-clock-event-never-issues and fn-otm-issue-is-pending-and-admits carry the hypothesis (not (fn-otm-full-p s)). fn-otm-journal-determines-the-decisions holds with the fifth kind. Scope: statvfs unobserved is never :full (an append that then meets ENOSPC stays the recovery event it was); the space consumed between observations by another writer is outside the model.

proofs.title: The decision journal never keeps a torn line: a failed append is truncated back to the last whole entry, the next entry after a loss carries a mark the replay reads as a gap naming the first sequence number missing, a run's start cuts a torn tail, and so at every process-death and ENOSPC cut the journal reads whole or torn, never malformed, and replays to agreement or a named gap
proofs.statement: Subjects (books/owner-time-journal-writer.lisp): fn-otm-jw-init, fn-otm-jw-open-first, fn-otm-jw-open-step and fn-otm-jw-cut-line (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-journal-open, fnn-owner-journal-cut: the file read backwards in chunks of *fn-otm-jw-open-chunk* octets and cut to its last whole entry before the run's start entry); fn-otm-jw-drop, fn-otm-jw-plan, fn-otm-jw-after, fn-otm-jw-truncated and fn-otm-jw-closed-line (host/native/io.lisp fnn-journal-write, called by fnn-log-writer-loop through fnn-log-write-item; a :journal-gap item is the first journal entry queued after the sink dropped one, host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-offer). The writer carries (OFFSET OWE CLOSED); its plan is the entry's line, the mark line (0 7 0 0 0 0 0, *fn-otm-mark-entry*) first when an entry was lost since the last whole one, nil when closed; a non-written outcome asks for a truncation to OFFSET, and a truncation that fails closes the journal for the run. fn-otm-replay (books/owner-time-journal.lisp) reads the mark as (:gap N) and a sequence jump likewise, N one past the last entry replayed. fn-otm-jw-sim composes the host calls over ANY fates of the offered entries (written; dropped by the sink; failed after K octets landed, the truncation holding or not -- a process death mid-append is the last such fate). fn-otm-jw-sim-file: the file is the starting file, the lines of fn-otm-jw-whole, then fn-otm-jw-frag, a fragment with no LF (fn-otm-jw-frag-is-a-fragment). KEYSTONE fn-otm-jw-file-reads-agrees-or-gap: from a file of whole lines E0 that replays to agreement from R, and entries ES that replay to agreement after it, the file the writer leaves reads back with a status other than :malformed, as E0 followed by the entries that landed whole, and replays from R to :agrees when no entry was written after a loss, else to (:gap N), N one past the entries replayed before the first loss. fn-otm-jw-gap-is-the-first-lost: when the first entry lost is not a start entry, N is its sequence number (fn-otm-jw-gap-names-the-first-missing). fn-otm-jw-segment-agrees: a segment as the host offers it (fn-otm-start-line's entry, fn-otm-jw-start-line-is-the-start-entry, then any run of fn-otm-run-okp host calls from fn-otm-init) replays to agreement from any state, so the keystone applies to every segment. fn-otm-jw-open-step-is-the-cut: under the backward read's invariant (the octets after the chunk hold no LF), a :cut is the whole file's cut fn-otm-jw-open-cut and a :more keeps the invariant; fn-otm-jw-open-step-cuts-a-written-file: over a file the writer left (whole lines then a fragment), every :cut under that invariant is the length of the whole lines. Not claimed: that every entry is on the disk (a loss is named, and the tail lost by a death or by a journal closed until the run ends is not marked: the reader's status says torn when octets of it remain); anything about the record log.

proofs.title: A graceful stop drains the POSTs in flight: the fence comes only when every member was told its reply (240 after a fenced barrier) or, past the drain deadline H, told uncertain by the stall's rule, and the drain ends within H plus the send grace
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-osd-drain-next (books/owner-stop-drain.lisp: the step fn-osd-drain-step, fn-osd-drain-next-step-unfolds, and whether the release was made), which host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-drain-service calls once per observation after a SIGTERM (fnn-owner-run: the drain, then fnn-owner-stop-service), with S0 and S the gate's scheduler values after a clock event (fnn-owner-sched-snapshot) at the drain's start and at the observation, LIMITS the configuration's (D H C) (fn-owner-barrier-limits), AWAITING the connections registered for a completion plus the queued submissions, UNSENT the connections holding a completion's reply not yet written (host/native/mux.lisp fnn-mux-unsent), RELEASED whether its :release was acted on. KEYSTONE fn-osd-stops-only-when-nothing-is-owed: :stop only when fn-osd-quiet-p (no member awaits, no reply unsent, and no batch in flight unless released by this drain or by the stall, fn-otm-disk-stalled) or released and H + 10,000 ms have passed since S0. KEYSTONE fn-osd-releases-only-at-the-deadline: :release only unreleased, at or past H, and not quiet; the committer then answers every member of the batches in flight by fn-otm-stall-releases (fn-otm-stall-tells-no-member-its-outcome: uncertain, never accepted or refused) and sheds the queued POSTs (refused try-later, nothing stored). KEYSTONE fn-osd-drain-ends-by-the-deadline: unreleased, at or past H and not quiet is :release; released and past H + grace is :stop. KEYSTONE fn-osd-drain-stops-by-the-deadline (lane sigterm-hang): the host's composition of fn-osd-drain-next over two consecutive observations S1, S2 (the second call takes the RELEASED the first returned) at or past H + grace since S0, with ANY AWAITING and UNSENT at each (any number of connections mid-article, mid-commit or holding an unread reply) and any RELEASED carried in: the first answers :stop or the second does; with the host's 100 ms cadence on a clock that never goes back, the stop comes within H + grace + one poll. A connection mid-article is in neither count and never holds the drain; the fence closes it (nothing stored). The host reaches the drain at the SIGTERM in every accept mode (host/native/mux.lisp fnn-mux-serve-once returns at the SIGTERM; batch AZ's once-mode hang). fn-osd-deadline-is-past-the-slow-deadline: H is at least D. With fn-ocs-members-told-only-after-the-barrier (PRF-267) a member is told 240 only in the COMPLETE after its fenced barrier, which the drain lets run before the fence. Not covered: the fence (fnn-owner-stop-service, a :control quantum) waits for a barrier that does not return; a command read but not yet stepped at the SIGTERM is not answered (nothing stored).

proofs.title: The owner's records as an abstract stobj over the history image: the read with its one need-page retry loop answers the history's record, keeps the history, its faithfulness and the page file's relation, and never stops for fuel; append, load and the flush into the image keep the history faithful
proofs.statement: books/history-records.lisp. The abstract stobj fn-hrecs (defabsstobj: value (H . C), H the history as a ghost, C the concrete: the FNADTSN2 image of H's first N events on a nested page store then a suffix array; correspondence C itself). fn-hrecs-faithful ST: (fn-hrs-rel H C), H the image's events then the suffix's and every verified page of the nested store holding H's placed image (fn-hp-vhold of fn-hp-piw). KEYSTONES: fn-hrecs-at-is-nth ((fn-hrecs-p ST), faithful, SEQ natural: an :ok answer of (fn-hrecs-at SEQ ST) is (:ok (nth SEQ H)) below (len H) and (:refused :seq) past it; any other verdict is a need-verdict and SEQ < (len H)); fn-hrecs-read-is-nth (ST faithful and (fn-hrecs-disk-faithful FILE ST): the page file FILE holds, at the address the table names, the image's page for every page not verified; then (fn-hrecs-read SEQ FILE ST) keeps fn-hrecs-p, H, faithfulness and the page file's relation, answers :ok only with record SEQ as above, and never (:refused :fuel)); fn-hrecs-get-is-nth and fn-hrecs-get-fuel-enough (the loop with any fuel; fuel at least the number of pages not verified suffices); fn-hrecs-serve-keeps (one fill from fn-pgs-fill-realize, A-PGS-HOST-IO, keeps all three, whatever it answers); fn-hrecs-fill-keeps (a fill that writes the image's page when the page is not verified keeps H faithful, whatever it answers); fn-hrecs-flush-keeps (the oldest suffix event into the image, fn-hp-x-append-step, the empty image first: keeps H faithful, whatever it answers; over fn-hrs-loop-placement: a step's answer other than :ok leaves a valid placement); fn-hrecs-append-appends, fn-hrecs-load-is-events, fn-hrecs-count-is-len. Scope: not yet host-called; the store's readers still read the record list (fn-sf-records); the open's adopt of a committed image, the flush's retry over pages not verified and the commit are not stated.

proofs.title: The operator's obligations report is sent page by page with a version token: the owner renders one page per request from a cursor, and the pages a client joins at one version are the whole report (lane obligations-paged)
proofs.statement: Subjects: books/native-live-pages.lisp fn-nlp-answer, which host/native-live-status-host.lisp fn-native-live-pages-host-answer calls under the owner mutex (host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-pages-answer, FNLS request frame kind 4) with the owner's retention (fn-nlp-live-retention) and width *fn-nls-chunk-octets*; fn-nlp-client-step, which host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-live-pages folds every reply through (fn-native-live-pages-host-client-step); fn-nlp-offline-start and fn-nlp-offline-step, which host/native/io.lisp fnn-command-live-pages calls with no owner running. The report is fn-nlp-report (the header line and one line per obligation); fn-nlp-live-report-is-the-report: with no hypothesis it is fn-nls-live-report of kind :obligations, the whole report the owner rendered before. fn-nlp-take-cuts-the-stream: a page from a cursor (the unsent rest of a line and the obligations not yet rendered) is the next min(W, |rest|) octets of the rest, and the cursor it leaves is what follows. KEYSTONE fn-nlp-pages-join-to-the-report: for any owner cursors CACHE, retention RET, width W and fuel, if the composition of owner answers and client steps from version 0 page 0 (fn-nlp-run) reaches :done, the joined pages are (fn-nlp-report RET), the ledger the owner held at the first page. KEYSTONE fn-nlp-pages-reach-the-report: with 0 < W <= *fn-nls-chunk-octets* and L <= W * FUEL (L the report's length), the run reaches (:done (fn-nlp-report RET)). KEYSTONE fn-nlp-answer-keeps-other-versions: a request that neither names version V nor starts it leaves V's rest at PAGE unchanged or drops it (:none, answered version-gone, the client restarts). KEYSTONE fn-nlp-offline-pages-join-to-the-report: the offline pages from fn-nlp-offline-start, joined, are the report. Work and allocation per request: one page of at most W octets and at most W obligation lines, plus the ledger's length on the first page; the page and version counters wrap modulo 2^32, so no report length is refused. The whole-report exchange (FNLS kind 1) refuses :obligations by the name report-is-paged (host/native-live-status-host.lisp fn-native-live-status-host-answer).

proofs.title: The heap figure holds a pool of article credits and every served read admits a connection into article mode only within them, refusing the rest by name, and an admitted upload is never blocked (reserve-to-finish): concurrent large POSTs no longer exhaust the heap
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-oas-read-span (books/owner-article-slots.lisp), which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at calls for every served read with the slots host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-connection-budget installs from the store's profile (fn-heap-article-slots; one before any run: fn-owner-article-slots). THE POOL (books/heap-store-figure.lisp): the heap figure's base and need hold fn-heap-articles-octets = max(r, min(32 r, 64 MiB)), r = fn-heap-article-reserve-octets = 2 x 16 x (512 + A + HDR), what one admitted article retains at most (the body as wire lists within the body limit and a line; then its submission, the injected article within A and its groups within HDR, as lists; the collector's copy); fn-heap-article-slots = floor(pool / r) in [1, 32] (fn-heap-article-slots-bounds). KEYSTONE fn-heap-article-slots-are-held: k credits, k <= the slots, are within the pool. fn-heap-articles-octets-monotone: the pool grows with A and HDR (so fn-heap-store-base-octets-grows-with-the-profile and heap-reservation's fn-heap-figure-octets-grows-with-history-and-record gained the A hypothesis; its removal witness is in tests/acl2/heap-reservation-tests.lisp). THE ADMISSION: fn-oas-held counts the owner's connections in article mode, its queued submissions and the one submission in flight (fn-oas-inflight-count: 1 when the in-flight field holds a submission record, else 0) (the credit moves with the request and is released when the commit answers). A read is OVER (fn-oas-over-p) when the owner then holds more than the slots and more than before the read, or connection ID entered article mode in it; past the slots the host's call takes the first of three tiers the slots hold (fn-oas-tiers): (a) the read with ID's posting bit off and restored (a POST 440 at the command with the memory reason, as PRF-323's shed read), (b) that read with ID's wire closed, 400 and close (the article it entered dropped, what it completed kept), (c) the whole read refused, 400 and close, nothing taken; an admitted connection skips (a). fn-oas-read-span-held-step: after the host's read the owner holds at most the slots or at most what it held. KEYSTONE fn-oas-read-span-admits-within-the-slots (no hypothesis): a connection that is in article mode after the host's read and was not before leaves the owner holding at most the slots. fn-oas-read-span-when-held-unfolds: a read the slots hold is fn-otm-read-span exactly (PRF-323's theorems hold of the host's call). fn-oas-refusals-are-not-article: tiers (b) and (c) leave ID out of article mode. THE GAP CLOSED (lane admission-gap): the entry test alone let a read that enters article mode AND completes the article (a TAKETHIS, RFC 4644 section 2.5; a pipelined IHAVE or POST; a small article in one socket read) raise what the owner holds past the slots with ID back in command mode. books/owner-article-held.lisp, from the shape of every layer under the host's read (fn-scar-finish-read replaces or removes ID's record and enqueues at most one decision; the view, pin, posting-bit and memory exchanges touch nothing else): KEYSTONE fn-oah-read-span-keeps-held-within-the-slots (held <= slots before the read implies held <= slots after, for a read of any connection carrying anything); KEYSTONE fn-oah-read-span-leaves-the-others-article-mode (the frame: for id2 /= id the read leaves connection id2's record and article mode as they were; fn-oah-read-span-keeps-the-other-records: the connection list less ID is unchanged); KEYSTONE fn-oas-read-span-never-blocks-an-admitted-article (RESERVE-TO-FINISH, restated: a connection in article mode whose read completes its article or only continues it -- ID out of article mode after it, or the queue's length unchanged -- reads exactly as fn-otm-read-span, whatever the slots, so an admitted upload completes, or is refused by name past the body limit, 441, without waiting for any other); fn-oah-admitted-read-keeps-what-it-completed (for an admitted connection the host's call is that read or that read with the article it began closed: the whole-read refusal is unreachable for it). Not claimed: that the octet-list heap of a retained body is 16 octets an octet (a measurement, planning/evidence/rep-wave-d-2026-09-25.md); the queue's growth by the control channel and BP deliveries, which enter no article mode; the body in bounded pooled chunks (the credit's representation step, open); that the served fold yields after one submission (PKT-600) -- the theorems hold without it, and the never-blocks keystone's second hypothesis is therefore stated, not removed.

proofs.title: A configuration record's stamp is the owner clock's milliseconds, so an expired invitation's redeem is refused at admission and faults the replay
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-cfg-account-livep inside fn-cfg-delta-reason (books/config.lisp), reached by fn-cfg-record-acceptablep (host-called through fn-cnode-record-acceptablep: host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-cfg-peer-delta-record, the stopped node's records; books/owner-config.lisp the live owner's) and by fn-config-replay-loop (every open's configuration replay). A configuration record's stamp is the owner's clock observation in milliseconds (books/owner-config.lisp fn-ocfg-config-stamp; the stopped node's host/native/admin.lisp fnn-admin-clock-plan through books/native-admin.lisp fn-native-admin-clock-observation), each time a u64 codec item (fn-cfg-uitemp; fn-cfg-stampp is fn-clock-observationp); books/clock-unit.lisp *fn-clock-record-stamp-unit* is :milliseconds and fn-cfg-account-livep reads the stamp through fn-clock-reading-latest-milliseconds. KEYSTONE fn-cfg-record-redeeming-an-expired-code-is-refused-and-faults-replay: a record whose first delta is a well-formed :account-redeem of a pending row, stamped with no wall claim or with wall + error (ms) at or past the row's expiry (ms), has admissible-reason :account-expired, is not acceptable, and a replay reaching it faults. fn-cfg-account-livep-unfolds states livep in milliseconds. Before this, stamps were the seconds projection (uint32) and the check compared seconds with a millisecond expiry, so it never fired (LANEDUMP invite-clock). Also: fn-oag-group-fact-of dates a group by its stamp's wall directly (ms). Not claimed: stores written before this change (their seconds stamps read as milliseconds); every node redeploys fresh at 6.6.0, no migration (ember 2026-09-28). Not claimed: redeem records whose redeem delta is not the first of the record.

proofs.title: Memory admission by credits: an operation acquires its credit before it allocates, the credit follows the buffer (connection body, queued submission, the committer's take, the batch in flight), and the ledger M_base + M_cache + sum(credits) + E_completion + E_runtime <= B holds across every transition of the served path; the launcher's reservation is B
proofs.statement: books/memory-credits.lisp: the ledger (BUDGET BASE CACHE COMPLETION RUNTIME DRAWN OPS) and its transitions; fn-mcr-transitions-keep-funded (acquire, grow, retain, release, evict, overdraw: certified, not cited, since no host line calls those transitions; reach_check) and KEYSTONE fn-mcr-resize-and-move-keep-funded (lane credits, the transitions the host calls): fn-mcr-resize sets an operation's credit, never refused when it shrinks (reserve to finish) and admitted to grow exactly within the budget, refused :memory-budget-exhausted by name with the ledger unchanged (fn-mcr-resize-refuses-exactly-past-the-budget); fn-mcr-move moves credit between operations with the funded total unchanged (fn-mcr-total-of-move). THE SERVED PATH (books/owner-credits.lisp; lane credits, B5): the host keeps one ledger a run (host/owner-host.lisp global fn-owner-credits). Subject: fn-mca-read-span, which host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at calls for every served read over fn-oas-read-span (PRF-377): connection ID's credit (key (:conn . ID)) is resized to fn-mca-need, one reserve fn-heap-article-reserve-octets while it is mid-article and one per queued submission of it; past the budget the read is refused by name (a POST 440 at the command by fn-oas-refused-read, else fn-mca-shut-read: 400 and close, the read not run). KEYSTONE fn-mca-read-span-keeps-funded (hypothesis: a funded ledger only): the host's read never over-commits. KEYSTONE fn-mca-read-span-covers-the-connection: if ID's credit covered its buffers before the read it is exactly their need after. fn-mca-read-span-within-the-credit-unfolds / fn-mca-read-span-never-blocks-what-is-held: a read the credit holds, in particular one that needs no more than ID holds (an admitted article read on and completed into its queued submission), is fn-oas-read-span exactly. THE COMMIT: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-take calls fn-mca-take (one reserve from (:conn . ID) to :open), fn-owner-shed-outcome fn-mca-untake, and host/native/owner.lisp calls fn-owner-credits-seal after fnn-log-seal-open-batch (fn-mca-seal: :open to :sealed), fn-owner-credits-batch-done in COMPLETE after the barrier (fn-mca-batch-done), fn-owner-credits-settle after a synchronous write or a START that kept no member, fn-owner-credits-stop at the stop. KEYSTONE fn-mca-commit-steps-keep-funded; fn-mca-take-and-seal-keep-the-total (the same credit follows the buffer); fn-mca-seal-and-batch-done-move-the-batch. THE CLOSE: fn-owner-close and fn-owner-fault call fn-mca-close. KEYSTONE fn-mca-close-keeps-what-the-commit-owns: a close (client gone, idle timeout, a stall's uncertain answer, a fault) releases only the connection's own credit; the committer's :open and the batch in flight's :sealed keep theirs until COMPLETE, since the native pipeline feeds each member's outcome before the barrier and the syncer's fdatasync still owns the batch (GPT-6 2026-09-28: a timeout does not release memory a worker or submitted syscall owns). THE BUDGET: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-connection-budget installs fn-mca-initial of the store's profile, core and nursery. KEYSTONE fn-mca-initial-funds-exactly-the-articles: the budget is fn-heap-figure-octets (the reservation the launcher sized the dynamic space from), the open's terms are the completion reserve (funded, never admitted against), the collector's room the runtime reserve, and exactly fn-heap-articles-octets is free. proofs.title: Configuration admission refuses a record the codec cannot carry: an accepted record encodes within the decoder's whole-record limits (65,535 items, 65,538 octets)
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-cfg-record-fitsp inside fn-cfg-record-acceptablep (books/config.lisp) and inside the carried check the replay folds execute, fn-cnode-carried-acceptablep (books/node-config.lisp; PRF-186's fn-cnode-record-acceptablep-is-the-carried-check equates the two under fn-cfgp), host-called through fn-cnode-record-acceptablep (books/node-config.lisp; host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-cfg-peer-delta-record for the stopped node, books/owner-config.lisp for the live owner) and folded by fn-config-replay-loop. KEYSTONE fn-cfg-record-fitsp-is-the-decoder-limits: fn-cfg-record-fitsp r is exactly (len (fn-cfg-record-items r)) <= *fn-cfg-max-items* and (len (fn-cfg-encode r)) <= *fn-cfg-max-octets*, the two whole-record refusals of fn-cfg-decode-exact (:item-count, :limit), with no hypothesis; so no accepted record is one fn-cfg-decode-exact refuses for size. The check counts item by item (fn-cfg-record-item-count, fn-cfg-record-octet-count: each item encoded alone and only its length kept, every walk a tail loop), never building the record's octets, and each count equals the encoder's by fn-cfg-record-item-count-is-len-of-items and fn-cfg-record-octet-count-is-len-of-encode. The limits are codec widths (STO-021 (iii)), not data caps: fn-cfg-recordp alone admits records up to 64 deltas of 1,024 rows of 256-octet labels, which encode past them. Not claimed: that a record within the limits decodes (fn-cfg-decode-exact's round trip is witnessed on ground records, tests/acl2/config-field-max-tests.lisp, not proved for all records).

proofs.title: The owner's queue is fair under sustained POST load: a waiting control request is admitted within 22 counted quanta and six sealed batches
proofs.statement: Subjects fn-otm-next (host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-gate-pick), fn-otm-commit-event (fnn-owner-commit-event) and fn-otm-committer-wake (fnn-owner-commit-wake, which passes the gate's six waiting counts, and its recheck inside the START-NEXT quantum of fnn-owner-commit-pipeline). The rule: fn-ocp-wake answers :start-next only while no control, poster or transit request waits past the pass budget (*fn-ocp-pass-bound* = 4 :commit quanta in flight, counted by fn-ocp-next while one waits and reset at a pick where none does; fn-ocp-no-start-next-while-a-shut-out-class-waits, fn-ocf-start-next-while-control-waits-is-within-the-budget). KEYSTONE fn-ocf-control-waits-at-most-the-bound: from ANY scheduler value, for every sequence of picks ITEMS (each the gate's waiting counts and, for a :commit pick, the events its quantum reports) satisfying fn-ocf-okp -- a control request waits at every pick, and each :commit quantum takes one of the host's shapes (outside flight a START; in flight a START-NEXT, :next-started only at a :start-next wake with that pick's counts, or a COMPLETE: the barrier's word then :completed) -- before the first control pick or the owner's stop at most 22 quanta run that are not :inspect, not a :reader in flight and not a START-NEXT that took nobody (fn-ocf-delay-at-most-the-potential with fn-ocf-potential-at-most-twenty-two), and at most 6 batches are sealed (fn-ocf-seals-at-most-the-seal-potential, fn-ocf-seal-potential-at-most-six). Proof by a potential: the four classes' distance to the control slot (PRF-248's measure) + 3 x whether a START can still be due + the batches left to complete + 3 x the passes the budget still allows. Not counted and bounded elsewhere: :inspect alternates (PRF-267); readers during a barrier run while the fdatasync runs and a waiting COMPLETE goes first (fn-ocs-in-flight-commit-before-reader); an empty START-NEXT is an owner quantum without I/O. The wall-clock reading takes the disk's barrier time, which books/owner-time-model.lisp bounds by H before the stall answers. Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-commit-fairness-tests.lisp (a reached walk from fn-otm-init: next batch open, control arrives, two COMPLETEs, control admitted, delay 2, seals 1; the starvation counterexample under the pre-lane wake: 12 batches sealed, 24 counted quanta, control never admitted; the budget spent: one START-NEXT allowed, then the wake stops the pipeline and control is admitted; hypothesis removal: no control waiting, a :commit quantum outside the host's shapes). Native: tests/test_native_owner_scheduler.py test_a_control_request_is_admitted_under_sustained_post_load (SCN-195).

proofs.title: An acknowledged BP custody is delivered within one quiet read timeout of an open session, never held until the session ends (PKT-873)
proofs.statement: Subjects fn-tcl-delivery-plan and fn-tcl-delivery-plan-progress-p (books/tcpcl-delivery.lisp), which host/native/tcpcl.lisp fnn-tcl-act calls on every completed inbound transfer; fnn-tcl-session marks the custody when the plan names the progress point and calls *fnn-tcl-progress* at its first quiet read timeout after it (at most max(1, keepalive/4) s; a session the peer ends first is delivered by the between-sessions pass), and host/native/bp-node.lisp fnn-command-bp-node binds it to fnn-bpnode-dispatch-pending. KEYSTONE fn-tcl-acknowledged-custody-is-progressed-in-its-turn: if the plan's released messages carry the transfer's final END XFER_ACK, the callback's result was (:accepted PATH) (kind-5 custody durable, spec 9.2) and the plan names the progress point; fn-tcl-unaccepted-delivery-names-no-progress: a refusal, an uncertain publication or a fault names none. Crash scope: the in-session turn adds no durable write; a process death between the ACK and the delivery is the existing kind-5 cut, recovered by the open's delivery pass. Teeth: tests/acl2/tcpcl-delivery-tests.lisp (fn-tcl-complete's held END ACK with (:accepted nil): final ACK released, progress named; removal of the final-ACK hypothesis by a refusal, an uncertain publication and a fault: no progress). Native: tests/test_native_source_corpus_bp.py (B SIGKILLed mid-receive; the relay restarted after B keeps its session open; the verdict precedes that session's end).

proofs.title: The adopted F4 bars in the owner: an unresolved request's late completion is consumed exactly once into its own generation (every member answered once, no second reply, the I/O-owned batch kept until the completion applies); a read's late page is a named 403, never absence; a restart forgets the previous run's clock domain
proofs.statement: Subjects (books/owner-time-bars.lisp): fn-otb-issue, fn-otb-answer-early and fn-otb-complete, which host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-commit-pipeline calls at each barrier's issue (the syncer carries the generation), at the stall's uncertain release and every stop's release, and, at the COMPLETE after the syncer's join, through fn-oqw-receipt (PRF-1245, books/owner-queued-work.lisp: its applying receipt carries fn-otb-complete's answer and ledger, fn-oqw-receipt-outcomes-are-distinct; the host faults on :stale and :consumed). The ledger is (GEN OPEN TOLD). KEYSTONE fn-otb-a-member-is-answered-once: from a ledger open at G, any early answers and then the completion for G over members CIDS (no duplicates): it applies; the early-told are fresh and each told once; the completion answers only members, none already told; every member is told before, early or by the completion. KEYSTONE fn-otb-a-late-completion-is-consumed-once: a completion applies iff open at its generation; one that does not apply answers no one and changes nothing; after one applied no completion applies again, and after the next issue every earlier generation's completion is :stale. KEYSTONE fn-otb-a-deadline-keeps-the-io-owned: early answers keep OPEN and GEN; an issue is refused while open. KEYSTONE fn-otb-a-late-page-is-unavailable-never-absent: fn-otb-dependency-step is :unavailable iff the page has not completed and the declared deadline (the read-dependency-ms row, default 5,000 ms) has passed, :serve whenever it completed, and its wait ends exactly at the deadline; fn-otb-unavailable-line's code is 403, not 430 or 423 (the interface row A4's asynchronous page fault calls; no host call site yet). KEYSTONE fn-otb-a-restart-forgets-the-previous-clock-domain: when a run's segment E1 replays to agreement, E1 then the next run's start entry (fn-otm-start-entry WALL USABLE: the wall observation, no monotonic origin) then E2 replays exactly as E2 from fn-otm-init (fn-otm-replay, called by the operator's `store ROOT journal' through fn-otm-journal-report and fn-otm-journal-exit).
proofs.progress_note: Lane time-bars (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-28). REPL-admitted on hbox against certified dependencies. Teeth: tests/acl2/owner-time-bars-tests.lisp (prefix otbt-): a reached pipeline of ledgers (a normal completion; a stall telling the batch in flight and the next; the late completion answering no one; the successor answering only its untold member); per keystone a reached positive witness of the whole antecedent and conclusion, hypothesis-removal witnesses (a consumed ledger; a member listed twice; a stale then a fresh completion; a regressed dependency reading; a tampered earlier segment), a must-fail for the open hypothesis, and the splice tooth (run 2's readings on run 1's domain do not replay as run 2). Native: tests.test_native_slow_disk test_the_adopted_default_bars_classify_an_unresolved_write.

proofs.title: The store's records over the committed history image: the records field may be based on a committed image the page file holds; its list is the image's decode (defined through the host's page fill, no new assumption) followed by the suffix, and is H followed by the suffix when the page file holds H's image and the decode is clean
proofs.statement: books/history-records-disk.lisp, books/store-records-field.lisp, books/store-files.lisp. HANDLE = (:hrs-handle FILE REC SALT N LENS STARTS NP). fn-hrs-disk-history HANDLE: over a fresh fn-hrecs$c, the page store opened from the root record REC (the directory run and every table page from FILE through fn-pgs-fill-realize, A-PGS-HOST-IO, each checked by pgs-x-open-dir / pgs-x-open-table-page :eager), the header adopted, rows 0..N-1 by the retry loop fn-hrc-get (fn-hrc-get-is-hrecs-get: the concrete loop is fn-hrecs-get over (cons X C) for every ghost X); exactly N rows (fn-hrs-disk-history-len); a decode that is not clean signals history-image-fault. KEYSTONES: fn-hrs-disk-history-is-image ((fn-hrs-handlep HANDLE), (fn-hrs-disk-holds HANDLE H): the open lands and over the state it leaves fn-hrecs-faithful (cons H C) and fn-hrecs-disk-faithful FILE (cons H C); the decode clean: then (fn-hrs-disk-history HANDLE) = H); fn-sfr-list-of-fn-sfr-based-is-image (the based field's list is H then the suffix's); fn-sfr-list-of-fn-sl-of (an unbased field built from a list reads it back); fn-sfr-list-of-fn-sfr-snoc (the commit's snoc is the append, for every value); fn-sfr-count-is-len, fn-sfr-last-is-last, fn-sfr-nth-is-nth (the O(1) readers, for every value). store-files: fn-sf-records = (fn-sfr-list (fn-sf-records-field s)); fn-sf-remake, fn-sf-record-dir-result's commit and fn-sf-emit-success keep the fields in the logic (fn-sf-records-of-fn-sf-make-fields-kept / -snoc). Scope: no path builds a based field yet (the served open's adopt is milestone (c)); the readers still read the whole list (a based field's list costs one decode).
proofs.progress_note: Lane arena-store-7 milestone (b1), 2026-09-28, the coordinator's decision on arena-store-6's Ask 2. Host-called: fn-sf-records and its O(1) readers (fn-sf-records-count/-last/-nth) read through fn-sfr-*; the host realizer of fn-pgs-fill-realize is host/native/extent.lisp (and the extraction's a-pgs-fill-realize). Teeth (tests/acl2/history-records-disk-tests.lisp): LIVE-RUN witnesses, not ground defthms: the page file is an alist attached to fn-pgs-page-words / fn-pgs-fill-realize (a proof cannot evaluate an attachment), a 40-event history flushed and committed (pgs-x-commit) into it; positive (every part of fn-hrs-disk-holds executed, clean, the history is H); removal of disk-holds (another image's handle: clean, the file does not hold H's pages, the history is not H); removal of the clean decode (a table entry naming a digest the page lacks, tables/directory/record consistent: disk-holds holds, the decode refuses, the history names the fault); a corrupted page (refused); fn-sfr-* over a based field (list, count, last, nth, snoc). Ground: fn-sl-of never builds a based value.

proofs.title: A local article number or transaction id, once issued, is never issued again across crashes
proofs.statement: books/number-durability.lisp. A number is ISSUED when a party outside the owner can observe it; every observation is of the completed (fenced) prefix (books/owner-reader-view.lisp fn-ocvm-reader-view-is-the-completed-prefix; replies, log lines and feed resolutions in COMPLETE). KEYSTONE fn-ndur-replay-extension-keeps-every-number: the configured replay (fn-cst-replay-node) of any history extending XS holds every (group . number) of XS's replay with the same Message-ID, below its next number. KEYSTONE fn-ndur-recovery-keeps-every-visible-number: for a live configured owner whose view (fn-ocl-view-historyp) is at a version no later than the fenced count, the host's open (fn-cpo-open-observed, the function fn-store-sn-recover-rows reaches through fn-rii-sco-extend-open) of any history extending the fenced prefix keeps every number the view shows, below the recovered next number; the log's crash theorem (fn-lg-batch-crash-is-a-prefix-under-a-crypto-trailer) gives that extension at every crash image, the decode keeps it (fn-ndur-decode-of-a-scanned-prefix). KEYSTONE fn-ndur-prepare-never-allocates-below-the-watermark: fn-accept-prepare stages no number below the state's next number. KEYSTONE fn-ndur-crash-trace-never-reissues-a-number: over any crash trace of epochs, each extending the previous one's visible prefix, a number issued in the first epoch is held by the same Message-ID in the last and below its next number. A number held only in memory by an unacknowledged, lost POST is not issued and may be given to the next article (RFC 3977 section 6: the next sequential unused number). KEYSTONE fn-ndur-recovery-never-reissues-a-logged-txid (PKT-835): every record of the fenced prefix the recovered history extends has a txid below the recovered next txid (the open's frontier); the first prepare stages it (fn-ndur-prepare-stages-the-next-txid). A txid named only by a durable FNFD feed intent whose record was never logged is not issued: the open decides the intent without its txid (PRF-269, fn-own-feed-intent-reuse-is-a-fresh-intent). books/number-durability-handles.lisp (PKT-886): the premises are over rows, which carry payload HANDLES a live arena may number differently from the open's fresh intern; fn-ndh-events erases them, the configured replay commutes with the erasure (fn-ndh-cpr-loop, fn-ndh-cst-replay-node), and KEYSTONES fn-ndh-replay-extension-keeps-every-number and fn-ndh-recovery-keeps-every-visible-number restate the two keystones with the extension premise up to handles (exact extension implies it, fn-ndh-prefixp-of-prefixp).
proofs.progress_note: Lane durability-bugs (row I3 item 2), 2026-09-28; PKT-886 closed by correctness-i4-2 (2026-09-29): books/number-durability-handles.lisp proves the configured replay commutes with erasing payload handles (fn-ndh-cpr-loop, fn-ndh-cst-replay-node), so both numbering keystones hold with the extension premise up to handles (fn-ndh-replay-extension-keeps-every-number, fn-ndh-recovery-keeps-every-visible-number); the rows of a live arena that sealed a refused POST's payload first are not a prefix of the fresh intern and are one up to handles (teeth). Teeth: tests/acl2/number-durability-tests.lisp. The extension premise is a hypothesis here; at a crash it is T2's conclusion (fn-lg-batch-crash-is-a-prefix-under-a-crypto-trailer, under A-CRYPTO-TRAILER) on a device that honours its flushes (A-DURABILITY; the power-loss rig's model)

proofs.title: SCRAM-SHA-256's server half: HMAC-SHA-256 and PBKDF2 execute as their RFC text, an honest client is accepted, and a final message bound to another exchange's nonce or channel binding is refused before any key is read
proofs.statement: books/hmac-sha256.lisp: fn-hmac-sha256 is RFC 2104's text and fn-pbkdf2-sha256 is RFC 8018's first block (RFC 5802's Hi) as an mbe whose :exec runs from the two key-block states (fn-sha256-of-block-prefix-is-from-state, fn-hmac-from-states-is-hmac, fn-pbkdf2-chain-fast-is-chain). books/scram.lisp: KEYSTONE fn-scram-honest-proof-verifies (a proof derived from the password, salt and count fn-scram-keys enrolled is accepted for every AuthMessage); KEYSTONE fn-scram-finish-refuses-another-nonce and fn-scram-finish-refuses-another-binding (a client-final whose nonce is not the exchange's, or whose channel binding is not the gs2 header plus, under tls-exporter, this connection's exporter value, never :accept); fn-scram-finish-accepts-only-a-valid-proof. Forgery resistance is A-CRYPTO. Teeth: tests/acl2/scram-tests.lisp runs RFC 7677's exchange byte for byte and refuses each one-change variant; tests/acl2/hmac-sha256-tests.lisp checks RFC 4231 and RFC 7914 vectors.

Increment 2 (lane sasl): the served AUTHINFO SASL arm calls it through books/sasl.lisp, and the events are cited.

proofs.title: The push feed's restart forgets the previous process's back-off deadline: a restarted feed does not depend on it, has none, and admits the new process's first observation
proofs.statement: Subject fn-feed-restart (books/peer-feed.lisp), reached at every open through host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-feed-restart (books/owner-feed-port.lisp fn-own-feed-port-restart-fold, the :restart event of fn-feed-live-next) and in the model's reopen (books/owner.lisp fn-own-reopen, fn-own-feed-restart-all). KEYSTONE fn-feed-restart-forgets-the-previous-clock-domain (books/feed-restart-domain.lisp): for a feed and any natural deadline B, the restart of the feed with B in place of its deadline is the restart of the feed; the restarted feed's deadline is 0; so the back-off conjunct of fn-feed-selection holds at every observation. The attempt counts (the semantic observation) are kept and set the next back-off.
proofs.progress_note: Lane time-bars (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-28). Found by the restart clock-domain audit: fn-feed-restart kept backoff-until, a reading of the previous process's monotonic clock rebuilt by the replay of :feed-retry/:feed-lost, and fn-feed-with-backoff never lowers it, so a peer backing off at the stop was not fed for about the previous run's uptime. Teeth: tests/acl2/feed-restart-domain-tests.lisp (prefix frd-): a feed backed off at 259,200,000 ms (three days up), restarted, offers again at 1,500 ms; the same through the replayed journal; the defect as a tooth (no restart: nothing offered); a non-feed keeps its deadline (the feedp hypothesis).

proofs.title: The per-group expiry policy: what the operator sets reads back, the age instant honours Expires: within keep and purge, the walk is its specification, a group that keeps an article keeps it, and expiry releases no held article
proofs.statement: Subject: the reclaim context host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-reclaim-context = books/expiry.lisp fn-xpy-ctx (called by host/native/checkpoint.lisp fnn-log-reclaim-steps), whose sixth element is fn-xpy-expired-set, read per record by books/store-reclaim-pack.lisp fn-rclp-ctx-reclaimable through fn-xpy-releasablep. fn-xpy-rows-policy-after-expire-set: staging fn-xpy-deltas through fn-cfg-apply on any value reads back the policy's four fields (no hypothesis); fn-xpy-rows-policy-of-other-target-after-expire-set: other targets unchanged; fn-xpy-group-policy-without-rows-keeps-forever (D03). fn-xpy-age-instant-is-within-the-bounds (keep at most purge: never before stamp+keep days, never after stamp+purge days); fn-xpy-age-instant-honours-expires-within-the-bounds (an Expires: instant within them is the instant exactly); fn-xpy-age-instant-without-expires; fn-xpy-no-age-rule-never-expires-by-age. fn-xpy-expired-set-is-the-spec: membership in the set the walk builds (one running octet sum per group) is membership in fn-xpy-spec, which recomputes each size window from the articles accepted at or after the article. fn-xpy-a-group-that-keeps-it-keeps-it: an article one of whose groups does not expire it is not expired. fn-xpy-releasablep-is-rule-or-expired-and-unheld: released iff the rule releases it, or the policy expired it and no authorship verdict needs its payload and no obligation of fn-rcl-obligations names it; fn-xpy-expired-verdict-is-the-policys; fn-xpy-held-article-is-not-expired; fn-xpy-releasablep-without-expiry (no policy: the rule's verdict). fn-rclp-events-never-touch-a-held-article (PRF-119) over the expiring context. fn-xpy-classes-partition-the-articles: the six classes the verb reports sum to the article count. fn-xpy-rci-recorded-context-is-the-decided-context: `store reclaim --recorded` derives the same expiring context from the recorded configuration.
proofs.progress_note: Lane expiry (2026-09-28). Open: expiry while serving (the owner's checkpoint publication); GROUP/LISTGROUP exclusion of reclaimed articles; transaction capacity (Q11: needs history compaction under D13).

proofs.title: LIST COUNTS carries LIST ACTIVE's status for every group: m for a moderated group, n for a read-only one, y otherwise
proofs.statement: RFC 6048 section 2.2.2: the last field of a LIST COUNTS line is LIST ACTIVE's status (RFC 3977 section 7.6.3; RFC 6048 section 2.1.1). books/nntp-responses.lisp fn-nntp-counts-summary-line renders fn-nntp-closed-status of the group under the connection's CLOSED list (the reader environment's, books/nntp-post.lisp fn-post-reader-env-closed: the read-only groups, the moderated entries, a moderator's approver entries), the list LIST ACTIVE's status reads; the reference fn-nntp-list-counts-command, the pinned bucket arm fn-gidx-list-counts-command (books/nntp.lisp) and the catalog arm fn-nntp-list-counts-command-cat (books/served-catalog.lisp) take (fn-nntp-env-closed env) from their dispatchers. KEYSTONES: fn-scat-counts-lines-status-is-the-active-status (the host's arm: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at -> fn-scr-command -> fn-nntp-archive-command-cat -> fn-nntp-list-counts-command-cat -> fn-scat-counts-lines), fn-gidx-counts-lines-status-is-the-active-status, fn-nntp-counts-lines-status-is-the-active-status (books/nntp-list-counts.lisp): line I of the LIST COUNTS lines over GROUPS and CLOSED ends with the octet line I of LIST ACTIVE's status lines over the same GROUPS and CLOSED ends with, for any archive, buckets and catalog; fn-nntp-counts-summary-line-status names that octet (fn-nntp-closed-status-octet). The served equations to the archive fold (fn-nntp-list-counts-command-cat-is-archive, fn-gidx-list-counts-command-is-the-archive-fold, fn-served-dispatch-list-counts) carry CLOSED. Before PKT-703 the field was the constant y.

proofs.title: A POST refused for a header line longer than 998 octets is refused by that name; a header field of any length folded within the line bound is never so refused
proofs.statement: RFC 5322 section 2.1.1 (a MUST: a line is at most 998 octets without its CRLF; RFC 5536 section 2.1 applies RFC 5322 to articles) bounds a LINE, not a field: a header field of any length is carried folded (section 2.2.3), up to the store profile's header limits (PRF-230). books/injection.lisp fn-inj-decide refuses a source the parser refuses :limit with the reason :line-length (fn-inj-parse-refusal), answered `441 posting failed; a header line is longer than 998 octets (RFC 5322 section 2.1.1); fold it' (books/nntp-post.lisp fn-post-refusal-line; logged reason=line-length, books/owner-log.lisp); every other parse refusal stays :unparsable. KEYSTONE fn-inj-decide-line-length-is-a-long-header-line (no hypotheses): a :line-length refusal's source has, among the header lines the parser reads, a line of at least 999 octets before any CR or LF (books/article-line-bound.lisp fn-alb-long-header-linep); by contraposition a header whose every line is within the bound is never refused :line-length. It rests on fn-article-parse-under-limit-is-a-long-header-line (within the codec ceiling, a parse refused :limit met such a line, under any header limits) and fn-article-next-line-limit-is-a-long-line. Subject: fn-inj-decide, run by every POST (books/nntp-post.lisp fn-nntp-post-step on the served path from host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at) and the operator's article. PKT-506: before it the refusal read `the article is not valid syntax'. The peer path (row I5) names the same bound: books/peer-inbound.lisp fn-peer-decide-transfer refuses a transferred article whose parse is refused :limit within the article ceiling (fn-peer-parse-limitp) with the intrinsic reason :line-length, answered `437 transfer rejected; a header line is longer than 998 octets (RFC 5322 section 2.1.1); fold it' (TAKETHIS: 439 with the Message-ID, RFC 4644 section 2.5); KEYSTONE fn-peer-decide-transfer-line-length-is-a-long-header-line (books/peer-refused-offers.lisp, no hypotheses), subject fn-peer-decide-transfer, run by every IHAVE and TAKETHIS transfer. A field body may begin on a continuation line (RFC 5322 section 2.2.3: `References:' CRLF ` <id>'); books/article.lisp fn-article-field-closedp refuses a field still empty when closed (RFC 5536 section 2.2).

proofs.title: A read-restricted session's view is prepared once per pin and every command reads it; the reply is the per-command view's

KEYSTONES fn-gacc-prepare-keeps-okp, fn-gacc-view-of-prepare (the prepared key is answered with the view) and fn-gacc-view-is-the-view-entry (an answer under fn-gacc-okp is the view of the key). The host: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-chunk-span-at prepares the connection's entry (books/served-catalog-chain.lisp fn-scr-prepare-access, KEYSTONE fn-scr-prepare-access-keeps-okp; fn-scr-prepare-access-serves-the-pin) from its global fn-owner-access-cache (nil at start, fn-gacc-okp-of-nil; written only there) and passes it to the read (fn-oas-read-span ... cache ...); fn-scr-auth-delegate's restricted arm reads the view (fn-scr-cached-view, fn-scr-cached-view-is-the-view) and builds it per command only when no entry is keyed to the pin. fn-scr-auth-delegate-is-scar-auth-delegate-pinned and the chain up to fn-scr-ocfg-read-span-is-reference-under-ocl-relation carry (fn-gacc-okp cache). Work: a restricted command at a prepared pin builds nothing; a prepare after k acceptances does O(k) cuts and path copies plus the configuration-sized group cut; a build happens at a restart, a withdrawal or a new rule. proofs.title: A running owner gives the disk blocks of the files a checkpoint publication dropped back while serving: every live payload the installed checkpoint holds is reseated at its frame without changing the arena, and a dropped file's descriptor closes only when no extent and no log member in flight names it and no off-mutex reader pinned before that was found still runs
proofs.statement: Subject: host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-release-extents (called by fnn-owner-publish-captured after a durable install) calls books/extent-retire.lisp fn-xrt-reseat-checkpoint-frame per payload frame the arena run wrote (host/native/io.lisp fnn-checkpoint-write-arena-steps records each frame's entry offset and fn-xrt-step-handles), then, in one owner-mutex hold, fn-xrt-quiet-files over the concrete arena's file count column (one read per retired file, never a walk of the extent column; lane composed-owner-4's fn-arx-file-count), the quiet files pending at a fresh arena-reader stamp S (host/native/io.lisp fnn-arena-stamp, books/arena-reader-pins.lisp PRF-941); host/native/extent.lisp fnn-extent-close closes a pending group once fnn-arena-clear-p S answers that no other off-mutex reader is pinned at or below S. fn-xrt-reseat-frame-keeps-the-arena (KEYSTONE): when the file durably holds, at the frame entry's offset, the octets the buffer holds (A-DURABLE-EXTENT's faithful file), the reseat leaves the arena (every handle's payload) unchanged; each payload is the commit's reseat (PRF-309 fn-arx-commit-reseat) with R the payload's own octets, so a wrong pairing reseats nothing. fn-xrt-quiet-files-are-unnamed (KEYSTONE): under the arena's correspondence (fn-arena$xcorr, kept by every export), a quiet file is retired, named by no log member in flight, and named by no extent entry at any handle, so a reader pinned after S never reaches it; a reader pinned at or below S may hold an older entry and the close waits for it (fn-arpn-clear-through-p). Before this every extent descriptor was held for the process's life, so the online compaction (PKT-868) freed no disk until restart. Scope: the realizer file table and descriptors are host state; the reseat's progress (every checkpoint payload found in its frame) is observed by the native (df shrinks), not proved.

proofs.title: `store reclaim`'s per-record step and rewrite read an article index, never the Store's article list
proofs.statement: Subject: fn-rcls-step (host/checkpoint-host.lisp fn-store-reclaim-step) and fn-rclp-event (fn-store-log-reclaim-event), called once per record by host/native/checkpoint.lisp fnn-log-reclaim-steps, under the context fn-rclp-ctx-expiring builds (fn-store-reclaim-context via books/expiry.lisp fn-xpy-ctx). fn-rclp-article-index-finds-the-article: the index (the context's seventh element, a fast alist) binds each Message-ID to the article fn-find-article's walk finds, for every article list, no hypothesis. fn-rcls-step-reads-no-article-list and fn-rclp-event-reads-no-article-list: replacing the context's article list (its fifth element) with anything changes neither the step nor the rewrite, for every accumulator, record and context. Scope: a record's step is its decode, one hashed article lookup, one hashed expiry lookup and, when the rule permits a release, the holders and verdict tables (linear in those tables, not in the Store's article count); before (row A8) each step walked the article list, 485 s at 100k for `store reclaim --dry-run`. A hashed lookup's cost is the ACL2 image's fast alist; an extracted core that runs hons-get as hons-assoc-equal walks the index instead.
