proofs.title: The owner carries RFC 3977 section 6's article-number bound: the Store node's watermarks and in-flight allocation, and the view's watermarks
proofs.statement: books/owner-number-bound.lisp (fn-onb-). fn-onb-node-boundp node: every watermark of the node's acceptance is within RFC 3977 section 6's bound (fn-nntp-nexts-boundedp) and a pending allocation's groups fit at them (fn-snb-groups-fitp). fn-onb-store-boundp s is it of fn-sn-node s and fn-onb-inflight-fitp s (a staged or completing record that is not a held row fits at the node); fn-onb-boundp o is the store's and fn-nntp-nexts-boundedp of the view archive's watermarks. KEYSTONE fn-onb-node-boundp-of-replay-apply-record: a record that fits at the node (fn-snb-record-fitp) keeps the node bound; with it the retention, identity-neutral, completion, txid-advance and prepare steps (fn-onb-node-boundp-of-*). The Store: fn-onb-store-boundp-of-prepare / -of-spc-prepare / -of-prc-spc-prepare (a fitting record staged), -of-io (the node and the candidate are untouched; the record directory's :ok makes the candidate the completion record, fn-cstp-completion-record-after-dir), -of-finish (no hypothesis: a held row completes its pending allocation, any other record fits by fn-onb-inflight-fitp), -of-ccar-prepare-identity (a fitting composite staged). The owner: fn-onb-boundp-of-refresh (the refreshed view's archive carries the node's watermarks, fn-ctl-visible-state-of-fields), fn-onb-boundp-of-same-store-and-view (the frame), and KEYSTONE fn-onb-boundp-at-owner-prepare-buffer: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-buffer calls fn-pout-prepare-article, whose owner is fn-psrv-prepare's (fn-onb-boundp-of-psrv-prepare): the admission stages only a record fn-psrv-event-numberedp admits (PRF-921), so from fn-onb-boundp before, the carried parse recognizer and the view's index recognizer, fn-onb-boundp after. KEYSTONE fn-onb-boundp-at-owner-prepare-identity: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-prepare-identity calls fn-pout-prepare-identity, whose owner is fn-psrv-prepare-identity's (fn-onb-boundp-of-psrv-prepare-identity). THE OPEN: KEYSTONE fn-onb-boundp-when-open-okp: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-install-extended installs a recovered owner only when fn-onb-open-okp (O(groups): the node's and the view's watermarks, the pending allocation, no transaction in flight) holds, refusing it by name (:article-numbers-damaged; the native owner refuses the store) otherwise; fn-onb-open-okp-is-boundp-outside-a-transaction says the test refuses exactly the out-of-bound stores. THREADED (books/owner-number-bound-join.lisp, fn-onbj-): the bound at every host entry that carries the catalog join, one KEYSTONE per fn-sjh-okp-at-X over the same host-called function: the configured owner step's events (fn-onbj-boundp-of-ocfg-step-owner-event; begin, declare-group, observe, unstage, node-secret, install-profile, outcome, open-peer), the store's io (log-reserve, log-order, with no premise: the io step keeps the node and the candidate), the opens (open, open-captured -- also -carried's owner --, exposure-open), read-step, the served read (chunk-span, -carried, -fully-carried, under fn-sjh-okp's premises: the serve keeps the store and the view by fn-sjh-rd-orr-keeps), the abandoned transaction (known-abort, refuse-reservation: the Store back at :ready), the completions (fn-onbj-boundp-at-owner-finish over fn-rix-ocfg-complete: finish-no-row's and finish-identity's owner; host-article-finish; finish-submission), the article prepare (fn-onbj-boundp-at-owner-prepare-buffer: the view's identity-index premise from fn-ocl-relation and fn-sjh-okp), the identity prepare (fn-onb-boundp-at-owner-prepare-identity, no premise: -sealed's and -unsealed's owner), the configuration's completion (fn-onbj-boundp-at-owner-reconfigure-complete: the carried configure keeps every watermark and starts a new group at 1, fn-onbj-extend-nexts-bounded), the host-name corollaries (-at-owner-unstage, -outcome, -finish, -finish-submission) are in the book, not cited: their content is fn-sjh-okp-at-owner-unstage's frame, fn-onbj-arm-acar-outcome, fn-onbj-boundp-of-ccar-ocfg-complete and fn-onbj-boundp-at-host-article-finish, and the opens' install (fn-onb-boundp-when-open-okp; KEYSTONE fn-onbj-open-okp-is-boundp-when-idle: at an idle store -- fn-sjh-okp-at-install's premise -- the host's check is exactly the bound). proofs.title: The Message-ID table, executable: the reader over the table stobj's page-store words (whole home page, the run of full pages after it, candidates ascending by construction, the BLAKE3 tag) confirmed against the rows is the ascending walk of the rows carrying the Message-ID (lane paged-history-2, row P2)
proofs.statement: Subjects: books/msgid-pages-exec.lisp fn-mpxt-seqs (the executable paged reader: fn-mpxt-confirm over fn-mpxt-candidates of fn-mpxt-tag, the first eight octets of fn-digest of the Message-ID's octets floored at 1; the table a defstobj fn-mpxt of u64 words in 2048-word page-store pages, 1,024 two-word slots (TAG, SEQ+1) a page, 0 the empty slot) against fn-mpxt-spec-from 0 (the walk: the sequences of the rows whose fn-record-msgid is the Message-ID, ascending). KEYSTONE fn-mpxt-seqs-is-spec-from: under fn-mpxt-faithful (fn-mpxt-okp: every slot's SEQ word in 1..the row count; fn-mpxt-faithful-from 0: every row's own sequence among its tag's candidates) the reader equals the walk, for every table and every key. Structure by construction: fn-mpxt-candidates-ascending and -nat-listp (each match is inserted into an ascending list, fn-mpxt-ins), fn-mpxt-candidates-below (under okp), fn-mpxt-faithful-from-complete; the refinement fn-mpxt-confirm-is-the-spec (an ascending, below, complete candidate list confirmed is the walk). The reader scans the tag's home page whole and continues only past a FULL page, so no placement invariant is assumed: the page need is one page plus the run of full pages (expected one at the writer's load of at most 1/2; correct and bounded by the page count in every store, design B.3's L-MPX-OVERFLOW). The writer (fn-mpxt-put at the first empty slot of the first non-full page of the run; fn-mpxt-add grows at half the slots, doubling and re-placing every entry) is guard-verified with its shape lemmas; its preservation of fn-mpxt-faithful is the row's next READY. The consumers the host calls are each equal to their reference over the buffer's value: fn-ars-lb-ocfg-gate-is-reference (fn-lb-ocfg-gate, the served POST's login gate), fn-ars-filing-plan-is-reference (fn-pa-filing-plan, C1), fn-ars-carrier-form-is-reference (fn-pa-carrier-form), fn-ars-current-plan-is-reference (fn-pa-current-plan); every keystone about the references applies to the host's verdict. proofs.title: The local-control frame is opened in place from the octet buffer, and the host site's dispatch over the buffer is the dispatch over the octet list
proofs.statement: books/frame-buffer.lisp: fn-frb-decode DIGEST MAX fn-octets reads the header's fields by index, compares the trailer in place and answers fn-frame-decode's result with the payload LOCATED by its length (KEYSTONE fn-frb-decode-is-frame-decode: under fn-octets-p, the buffer's invariant, the twin equals fn-frb-of the reference decode of the buffer's value; fn-frb-payload-is-window: the reference's payload is the buffer's window of that length after the 10-octet header, an error's the empty one). books/native-control-buffer.lisp: fn-frb-open-with DIGEST KIND fn-octets is fn-nctrl-open with the digest as an argument (KEYSTONE fn-frb-open-with-is-nctrl-open-with, against fn-frb-nctrl-open-with, which fn-nctrl-open is by definition with the trailer of its protected prefix); fn-frb-open-payload-with lifts it to the reference's exact result, the payload copied out of its window (one cons of the payload, never of the frame); fn-frb-open and fn-frb-open-payload compute the digest ONCE as frame-digest-buffer's window digest of the protected prefix (fn-frb-open-is-nctrl-open, fn-frb-open-payload-is-nctrl-open). The open is generic over the frame FAMILY (magic, version, payload bound, refusal): fn-frb-open-as / fn-frb-ref-open-as (KEYSTONE fn-frb-open-as-is-ref-open-as; the lift fn-frb-open-payload-as-is-ref-open-as), FNCT (fn-nctrl-open-by-definition) and FNLS (books/native-live-buffer.lisp, fn-nls-open-by-definition, fn-frb-nls-open-payload-with-is-nls-open-with) its instances. fn-frb-control-decode is the FNCT dispatch of host/native/control.lisp fnn-control-handle-client (reasoned flag, request, admin, moderation, topic, consumer; the kinds and the order the host used) from one digest, equal to fn-frb-control-reference, the same dispatch over the octet list through the reference decoders (fn-frb-control-decode-is-reference); fn-frb-site-decode (books/native-live-buffer.lisp) is the whole site, that tuple then LIVE (fn-cev-any-request-decode answers :live-status) and PAGES (fn-nlp-request-decode answers :page), FNCT and FNLS from the ONE digest, equal to fn-frb-site-reference (fn-frb-site-decode-is-reference). The FNLS decoders fn-nls-request-decode, fn-nlp-request-decode and fn-cev-request-decode are split as the FNCT ones are. The reference decoders fn-ncl-request-decode, fn-cwait-request-decode, fn-ncr-request-decode, fn-thlc-request-decode and fn-native-control-moderation-decode are each the open followed by a payload grammar over the opened frame (-payload-decode), which both they and the buffer entry call. Every executable is guard-verified. host/native-control-host.lisp fn-native-control-host-decode-frame (fn-frb-site-decode) is the entry, over the control service's own buffer fn-octets-ctl (congruent to fn-octets; the owner's buffer is filled under the owner mutex, a control worker decodes before it takes that mutex), called by fnn-control-handle-client under the control buffer lock after fnn-octets-ctl-fill of the frame: no list of the frame is built for the FNCT decoders, and the frame is digested once per request instead of once per decoder.

proofs.title: The Store's resume from a carried pause: the paused-node verdict and the tries carried across extend, O(|Q|) beyond the folds with no whole-node pass
proofs.statement: books/store-finalize-incremental.lisp section 4 (fn-sfi-, row A9). Subject: fn-sfi-extend-open-carried (c ix configs suffix frontier count next), the served open's fused extension-and-open from a carried pair, and fn-sfi-cpr-resume-carried (r configs events ix), the resume of the configuration fold from a carried pause; the host's function today is fn-rii-sco-extend-open (host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-recover-from-checkpoint), whose resume fn-rii-sco-cpr-resume checks the paused node (fn-cnode-statep) and rebuilds its tries (fn-rii-ix-of) at every extension: two whole-node passes. Invariant fn-sfi-cpr-carriedp (r ix): r paused, its node configured, the tries under fn-rii-okp with it. KEYSTONE fn-sfi-cpr-resume-carried-is-sco-cpr-resume: under the invariant (car (fn-sfi-cpr-resume-carried r configs events ix)) = (fn-sco-cpr-resume r configs events) for every configuration list and suffix, with neither pass. KEYSTONE fn-sfi-extend-open-carried-is-rii-extend-open: under the invariant on (fn-sco-cpr c) and ix, the carried verdict ((fn-sn-open-kind (fn-sco-finalize c configs f0)) = :ok, f0 free), count = (len (fn-sco-records c)) and next = (fn-sf-next-lower (fn-sco-records c) 0): (fn-sfi-extend-open-carried c ix configs suffix frontier count next) = (list (fn-sco-extend c configs suffix) IX' (fn-rii-classified-open (fn-sco-extend c configs suffix) configs frontier)), the host's two components (fn-rii-sco-extend-open-is-extend-then-open). Corollary fn-sfi-extend-open-carried-finalizes-the-extension (the swap's shape, :rule-classes nil). PRESERVATION: fn-sfi-cpr-prefix-carried-keeps-carried, fn-sfi-cpr-resume-carried-keeps-carried, fn-sfi-extend-open-carried-keeps-carried (the invariant over the extension's pause and tries); fn-sfi-extend-open-carried-count-and-bound (count' = count + |Q|, next' = (fn-sf-next-lower Q next), each O(|Q|)); fn-sfi-carry-is-carried (the open's one node pass establishes the invariant); fn-sfi-carried-msgid-trie-is-the-rebuilt-trie (the carried Message-ID trie is fn-rii-ix-of's; the id trie is related by the defun-sk fn-rii-known-okp, not equal). THE BOUND fn-sfi-cpr-resume-carried-steps-bounded (:linear): the steps twin fn-sfi-cpr-resume-carried-steps, which walks the fold's path, is at most |configs| + |Q|; no term names the node. What an iteration costs is the trie step fn-rii-ix-next (the changed articles, one id; its fallback rebuild only where the retention change has no recognized shape) and the node step; fn-node-statep on a configuration record is the fold's own per-config check (few). The invariant is the entries' verified guard and is not executable (fn-rii-known-okp is a defun-sk), exactly as the twin fold's own guard is: an obligation the caller keeps, as PRF-946's NEXT and verdict are (the pair comes only from fn-sfi-carry or the previous call; the :program host calls the entries raw, as the served image does). An abstract stobj whose recognizer is the invariant is refused by ACL2 (stobj-attachment-restrictions: fn-cnode-statep reaches fn-digest, attached in books/crypto-attach.lisp). Not changed: the record list copy in fn-sco-extend (append, len over (fn-sco-records c): O(|P|) list work, D27's rows and header count remove it), and the fault branch fn-rii-sco-store-open. Every executable function guard-verified. Teeth: tests/acl2/store-finalize-incremental-tests.lisp, the entries run raw through :program wrappers (the served path).

proofs.title: The COMPRESS DEFLATE inflater is total, bounded per call and resumable: host calls over whatever reads and quanta arrive are one run over the concatenated stream, and malformed streams are refused by name
proofs.statement: books/deflate-inflate.lisp (lane compress, RFC 8054 over RFC 1951). The host entry fn-zin-feed B ST START END LIM fn-octets fn-zin-win fn-zin-tab fn-zin-out decodes the raw DEFLATE octets in cells [START, END) of a buffer (the host's private fn-octets$c per connection), with the 32 KiB history ring fn-zin-win, the Huffman tables fn-zin-tab (two octets per entry) and the scalar state stobj fn-zin-st, and answers (mv STATUS B2 IP ST win tab out): :more (all input taken), :full (output reached LIM), :yield (budget B of actions spent), or (:refused R), R one of the named malformations (fn-zin-refusal-text). Stored, fixed and dynamic blocks (zlib's puff, a bit at a time). fn-zin-feed-unfolds: once the buffers are ready the entry is fn-zin-loop. KEYSTONE fn-zin-feed-out-bound: the output only grows, never past max(LIM, its length). fn-zin-loop-stops: :more means every octet up to END was read, :full that LIM was reached. KEYSTONES of resumption: fn-zin-loop-split-budget (a :yield resumed with more budget is the call with both), fn-zin-loop-split-input (a :more resumed on a later END is the call over all of it), fn-zin-loop-out-free (the output is written, never read: a :full resumed on a cleared output is one call), fn-zin-loop-is-run (a call over any buffer cells is the list model fn-zin-run over exactly those octets: the D27 representation boundary), fn-zin-run-append (a :more run of A resumed on B is the run of A ++ B).

Witnesses from zlib (fixed, dynamic and stored blocks; every two-read cut of a session; 7-action quanta; 10-octet output bounds) and one hand-built stream per refusal; removal witnesses and must-fails for each resumption hypothesis. proofs.title: A DEFLATE decompression bomb is refused by name: a COMPRESS stream never produces more than 256 times the octets it read plus 64 KiB
proofs.statement: books/deflate-inflate.lisp. fn-zin-st counts the octets read (TOTAL-IN, field 7) and produced (TOTAL-OUT, field 6); fn-zin-emit refuses (:bomb) the octet that would make TOTAL-OUT exceed *fn-zin-ratio* (256) x TOTAL-IN + *fn-zin-slack* (65,536). KEYSTONE fn-zin-feed-bomb-bound: from a state within the bound (fn-zin-bomb-okp; fn-zin-reset-okp: the initial state is), a call stays within it, the octets it appends to the output are exactly what it adds to TOTAL-OUT and the octets it reads (IP - START) exactly what it adds to TOTAL-IN, so the bound is about the plaintext actually handed to the served step. Witness: 1 MiB of zeros in 1,037 zlib octets is refused at exactly 256 x read + 65,536 octets.
proofs.progress_note: Lane compress (Opus 5.5, 2026-09-28). The hypothesis (natp start) was proved redundant and removed; the bomb-okp removal witness is a state already past the bound.

OCTETS)); fn-lzr-dicts-initial is that table (fn-lzr-dicts-initial-dictsp); fn-lzd-table-current: the current ID resolves to baseline 1. proofs.title: The payload decoder's window frame: it writes only ring cells below min(TOUT, 32 KiB) and never the preset half
proofs.statement: books/deflate-frame.lisp (lane compress-3). KEYSTONE fn-zfr-loop-ahead-frame: from any state whose ring position W satisfies fn-zfr-posp (W below 32 KiB, and W = TOUT while TOUT is below 32 KiB), fn-zin-loop-ahead (the store's payload decoder, with its fast path) returns a state that satisfies it again, does not decrease TOUT, and a window equal to its input from cell min(TOUT', 32768) on: the preset half is never written and the ring only below the octets produced. Per-function frame lemmas for emit, copy, match, lits, lit-loop, act, step, f-copy, f-sym, fast and ahead-fast. Subject of PRF-949's pool invariant.

proofs.title: The served read's pooled payload decoder: fn-zpl-decode-bufs is fn-pzd-decode over a window kept across payloads, and keeps its pool invariant
proofs.statement: books/deflate-pool.lisp (lane compress-3). The host keeps, with each buffer set, ACL2's POOL value (DICT H DIRTY) or NIL; fn-zpl-pool-okp: the window is DICT's ready window (fn-zin-payload-ready's) from cell DIRTY on, H its preset length. fn-zpl-decode-bufs re-zeroes only the DIRTY cells and remakes the table when the pool names the same dictionary (an equal that is eq for the shared table entry), else makes the buffers whole. KEYSTONES fn-zpl-decode-bufs-is-decode (under fn-zpl-pool-okp: the answer's status is fn-pzd-decode's, on :ok the output buffer holds its octets, and the returned pool satisfies fn-zpl-pool-okp; fn-zpl-pool-okp-of-nil: the host's starting pool does) and fn-zpl-decode-bufs-is-the-lz-value (an :ok answer's octets are fn-lzr-lz-value, the value A-DURABLE-LZ names). Host subject: host/native/deflate.lisp fnn-pzd-decode calls fn-zpl-decode-bufs (the realizer host/native/extent.lisp fn-durable-realize-lz). Witnesses: tests/acl2/deflate-pool-tests.lisp (two reads over one buffer set, the second through the reuse branch; a forged pool without the invariant answers other octets; must-fail without fn-zpl-pool-okp). Measured (hbox, load ~18, same session, held-out 9,733 20news articles): 223 us median vs 497-526 us for fn-pzd-decode-bufs, 0 mismatches; measure at convergence.

proofs.title: The COMPRESS command (RFC 8054): only DEFLATE starts, only after a login or for a configured peer; the capability block withdraws COMPRESS, STARTTLS and AUTHINFO once a layer is active; the layer is established by the host's event without changing the session
proofs.statement: books/nntp-compress.lisp (fn-zc-, lane compress) and the COMPRESS arm of books/nntp-auth.lisp (the session's seventh field, compress; lane sasl's SASL context is the eighth). fn-zc-decide STATE MAYP ARGS answers :start only for DEFLATE from no layer when MAYP (fn-zc-decide-starts-only-deflate); fn-auth-compress-mayp: an authenticated session or a configured peer (local policy stronger than RFC 8054 section 2.2.2, against CRIME-style length leaks, section 7). fn-zc-capability-lines-withdraw: once active, no STARTTLS, no AUTHINFO label and no COMPRESS label. KEYSTONE fn-auth-established-starts-the-owed-compression: after the 206, the host's established event makes the layer active, releases the hold and keeps the TLS flag, the login, the pending name and the base. fn-auth-compress-preserves-consistentp keeps the session invariant. proofs.title: The wire dictionary negotiation's decisions (NNT-055): a stored payload goes to a peer as it is stored exactly when the peer holds the frame's shipped dictionary
proofs.statement: books/nntp-compress-dict.lisp (lane compress-4). fn-zdn-choose (Z, the stored payload-lz-record frame; DIGESTS, the BLAKE3 digests an XFN-ZARTICLE request lists): KEYSTONE fn-zdn-choose-stored-only-shared: a (:stored D) answer has a frame that parses, D the digest the shipped table records for the frame's DICT-ID, and D one the peer listed; KEYSTONE fn-zdn-choose-complete: a parsed frame whose recorded digest the peer listed is always answered stored; every other payload (DICT-ID 0, not a frame, a dictionary the peer lacks) is :decoded. fn-zdn-request-shape: a parsed XFN-ZARTICLE names a message-id and one 32-octet digest per hex token. fn-zdn-capability-line: XFN-DICT and the shipped digests, newest first. proofs.title: BP fragment reassembly as a job carried across scheduling steps reads as the whole reassembly; the reassembled image is refused past the profile's limit by name
proofs.statement: books/bp-node-fragment-job.lisp (Q4a; PRF-250 hosted; PKT-646; D27). A job is (CELLS TOTAL SWEEP) over bp-fragment-resume's sweep state: fn-bpfj-start makes it from the machine state's family (fn-bpnf-fragment-cells of fn-bpnf-active-set, the anchor's total ADU length); fn-bpfj-step runs at most QUANTUM positions of the sweep (fn-bpfj-step-is-bounded: exactly min(QUANTUM, left) positions consumed); fn-bpfj-finishedp reads the positions left. The invariant fn-bpfj-wf is the executable fn-bpfj-currentp (the job's cells and total are the family's now) and the sweep's resumption equal to the sweep from the start; fn-bpfj-start-is-wf establishes it, fn-bpfj-step-preserves-wf preserves it (through fn-bpfr-step-resumes). KEYSTONE fn-bpfj-query-is-the-query: under the invariant a finished job's reading, fn-bpfj-query (fn-bpfr-finish over the job; (:stale :job) for a job that outlived its family, (:pending :job) for an unfinished one), is fn-bpnf-fragment-query, the foundation's whole reassembly inside one step. fn-bpfj-plan is fn-bpnf-family-plan over the job under a LIMIT (the profile's held octets, fn-bpnpf-held-octets; received-fragment wire size remains bounded independently by fn-bpnpf-bundle-octets) in place of the *fn-bpnf-max-held-image* cap: KEYSTONE fn-bpfj-plan-refuses-past-the-limit-by-name (an image past the limit answers (:refused :bundle-beyond-profile), before any record, whatever the capacity checks would say) and KEYSTONE fn-bpfj-plan-is-the-plan-within-the-limit (within the limit, the limit within the codec's width as an explicit premise, the plan is fn-bpnf-family-plan). fn-bpfj-plan-at, fn-bpfj-apply and fn-bpfj-apply-at equal fn-bpnf-family-plan-at, -apply and -apply-at under the same hypotheses. The job lives in host memory only: a process death loses bounded work, never a decision (every reading is a function of the durable rows the job was started from). NOT bounded here: the whole-bundle encode (fn-bpb-encode of the reassembled bundle) is one step's work, once per plan, until PKT-585.

proofs.title: The Message-ID table resists crafted Message-IDs (ember's PKT-774 ruling, row W2b; GPT-6's structural bound): the tag is keyed BLAKE3 under a per-generation purpose key of the node secret; a lookup reads at most the home page and its overflow and confirms at most 2,048 exact Message-IDs, for every tag, key known or not; a home page whose overflow is full is INDEX-SATURATED, refused by name with the table unchanged, never a dropped insert or a scan; the next generation is built beside the old (lane paged-history-3)
proofs.statement: Subjects: books/msgid-pages-exec.lisp sections 0, 4 and 6. THE KEY: the stobj fn-mpxt carries 32 key octets (fn-mpxt-key-octets reads them); fn-mpxt-set-key installs a key into an emptied table (a key change empties the table); fn-mpxt-key-of-entry entry = fn-ns-purpose-key entry "fn/msgid-index/v1" (books/node-secret: BLAKE3 derive_key over the node-secret entry, the same derivation as the cancel-lock and posting-account keys, from which its label differs by definition, fn-mpxt-key-info-separate-by-definition); every writer keeps the key (the -key clauses of the frame theorems; fn-mpxt-add-key, fn-mpxt-grow-shape, fn-mpxt-copy-key-copies). One key per index GENERATION (GPT-6): stable across ordinary checkpoints, never per checkpoint; a generation changes only by a controlled rebuild (fn-mpxt-grow-into, the next generation beside the old) or on compromise, and a key derived from a compromised secret restores nothing (a rotation is a fresh node-secret epoch and a rebuild); the persisted index (row P8) binds the key identifier into its manifest. THE TAG: fn-mpxt-tag msgid key = the first eight octets of fn-ns-mac key octets (BLAKE3 keyed_hash of the Message-ID's octets) as a little-endian word floored at 1. THE STRUCTURAL BOUND: fn-mpxt-reach np = min(2, np); the reader fn-mpxt-candidates scans the home page and, only when it is full, its overflow page, never further; fn-mpxt-run-counted is the reader's run returning its candidates and the pages it read (fn-mpxt-run-counted-is-run), fn-mpxt-candidates-pages the lookup's page need (fn-mpxt-candidates-counted-is-candidates). KEYSTONE fn-mpxt-candidates-page-need: for every table and every natural tag, the need is at most two pages and at most the page count, and the candidates -- each confirmed against the row's EXACT Message-ID by fn-mpxt-confirm (PRF-969) -- number at most 2,048 (fn-mpxt-run-len, fn-mpxt-scan-len, fn-mpxt-ins-len): no hypothesis restricts the tag beyond its type, so the bound holds with the key known. THE FOURTH OUTCOME: fn-mpxt-put places on the home page or its overflow, else not at all, the table unchanged (fn-mpxt-put-run-unplaced-unchanged, fn-mpxt-put-unplaced-unchanged); fn-mpxt-saturatedp tag = the home page and its overflow both full; fn-mpxt-put-places-iff-not-saturated. fn-mpxt-add tag seq fn-mpxt fn-mpxt2 returns :placed or :mpx-saturated, and :mpx-saturated counts nothing and leaves the table literally unchanged unless a generation was adopted first (fn-mpxt-add-saturated-keeps-the-table; that the adopted generation holds every mapping is the grow's preservation theorem, the next READY): never a false absence, a dropped insert or a fallback scan. The admission limit -- 2,049 Message-IDs whose tags share a home page cannot be admitted however empty the rest is -- is an implementation limit stated here and refused by name before durable acceptance (the catalog's key-argument export at THE SWITCH, row P2); under an unpredictable key it is a Poisson tail (two pages of 1,024 entries where the mean is 512 at the writer's load of at most 1/2), so the outcome is evidence of crafted tags under a leaked key: rebuild under a fresh node secret. GROW BESIDE: fn-mpxt2 is a congruent stobj (fn-mpxt2p-is-fn-mpxtp); fn-mpxt-grow-into doubles the pages into it with the same key (fn-mpxt-copy-key) and re-places every entry (fn-mpxt-put-all-checked, ok only when every one landed); fn-mpxt-adopt copies the generation in only then (fn-mpxt-grow-shape: not ok means the table is unchanged). Under the table condition fn-mpxt-no-adjacent-fullp (no page and its successor both full) no tag is saturated (fn-mpxt-no-saturation-under-the-condition). What this does not prove: unpredictability of the tags (BLAKE3 keyed_hash as a PRF is A-CRYPTO; the theorems hold for every key), the Poisson occupancy figure (prose), secrecy of the key file, or the grow's preservation of fn-mpxt-faithful (the next READY: put-all-checked ok gives a faithful generation). Teeth tests/acl2/msgid-pages-exec-tests.lisp (structural fixtures with direct tags, not claims about BLAKE3): on a 520-row table (two pages) the counted reader's pages equal the need, at most the page count and at most two, the condition holds and no tag is saturated; 2,048 entries under one tag in four pages fill the home page and its overflow: the tag is saturated, its need is two pages, the condition fails, the next placement is refused and the table unchanged; 1,000 entries under one tag are not saturated; the key witness: two entries' keys and tags differ, the key differs from the cancel-lock key. The 10k crafted-collision native (Message-IDs colliding under the old table's hash) exercises the served path and ships with THE SWITCH (row P2).

proofs.title: The TLS handshake is an admission ACL2 decides before SSL_accept: a per-source token bucket, a node-wide in-flight and per-second bound (PKT-639, W2a)
proofs.statement: books/tls-handshake-decision.lisp and books/tls-handshake-budget.lisp (fn-hsb-). fn-hsb-admit s hl trustedp address now queuedp decides :admit ID, :wait or :refuse (:handshake-budget or :busy) for a source (an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /64) under the operator's rows tls-handshakes-per-source-per-minute (N), tls-handshakes-in-flight (L), tls-handshake-ms (D). KEYSTONE fn-hsb-steps-keep-the-bound: from fn-hsb-okp (at most L in flight, at most L started in the tick, at most 32L waiting) every admit, done and leave keeps it. KEYSTONE fn-hsb-admits-per-tick-are-bounded: over any event sequence from any state, the admissions in one one-second tick are at most the largest L they were decided under. KEYSTONE fn-hsb-source-admits-are-bounded: from any state, over events with nondecreasing times in [T0,T1] decided at source KEY's own rate N (fn-hsb-source-rate: the operator's override for KEY, else the row), one untrusted source is admitted at most N + N(T1-T0)/60000 handshakes. KEYSTONE fn-hsb-buckets-are-bounded: over any events decided under limits whose L is at most LMAX, the per-source accounting table holds at most max(its start, 64 x LMAX) rows (a new source past 64 x L after the prune is refused :sources-full; no row is evicted). fn-hsb-mapped-address-is-one-source: an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (::ffff:a.b.c.d) is its IPv4 source. The CGNAT overrides: the policy row tls-handshake-source-overrides (ADDRESS=N or ADDRESS/64=N, comma-separated, or none) is parsed by fn-hsb-overrides-of-word (books/tls-handshake-source.lisp), admitted by the administrative plan (books/native-admin.lisp fn-native-admin-plan, `policy set tls-handshake-source-overrides WORD`) exactly when that parse lists it, else refused :override-address or :overrides-full; fn-hsb-overrides-of-word-is-bounded: every admitted list holds at most the profile's tls-handshake-source-overrides (64) entries. fn-hsb-scratch-within-the-machine-term: the handshakes in flight under the host's limits hold at most L x *fn-cbud-handshake-scratch-octets* (128 KiB, stated) of native scratch, exactly the term books/connection-budget.lisp charges to the machine's base (fn-cbud-handshake-octets; PRF-223's run decision and live reconfiguration, fn-cbud-deltas-refusal-keeps-the-machine-held), and at most the scratch of any held slots at least L; fn-hsb-lim-in-flight-is-the-charged-slots: the L the host's limits resolve is the L the run charges. THE PROXY HEADER on a trusted path (books/tls-proxy.lisp, item 4): KEYSTONE fn-pxy-direct-unless-trusted: fn-pxy-begin answers (:direct) -- nothing is read for a header -- exactly when the transport peer is in none of the policy row tls-proxy-trusted-peers' ranges, and otherwise (:read 6 WHY) with WHY a listed range matching the peer. KEYSTONE fn-pxy-step-reads-within-the-bound: fn-pxy-step, over any octets read so far, asks for at least one and at most 528 - read more (so the header is never over-read and at most 528 octets are read for it), answers a header only as exactly the octets read, and otherwise refuses by name (:proxy-malformed, :proxy-oversize, :proxy-unsupported). KEYSTONE fn-pxy-handover-keeps-the-bound: fn-pxy-handover (the proxy's handshake done, the asserted source's admitted, charging its own per-source budget) keeps fn-hsb-okp; it is two events of the event language (fn-pxy-handover-is-two-events-by-definition), so every bound over any event sequence covers both charges. Books: books/tls-handshake-source.lisp (the source key and the override list, split by lane tls-handshake-budget-3 so native-admin admits the row without the decision's closure), books/tls-handshake-decision.lisp (the decision, the step bound, the scratch term) and books/tls-handshake-budget.lisp (the bounds over any event sequence), split by lane tls-handshake-budget-2. Host subjects: host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-proxy-begin, fn-owner-proxy-step, fn-owner-proxy-handover (called by host/native/mux.lisp fnn-mux-proxy-or-admit, fnn-mux-proxy-readable, fnn-mux-proxy-handover), fn-owner-handshake-limits (reads the override row), fn-owner-handshake-admit, fn-owner-handshake-done, fn-owner-handshake-leave (called by host/native/mux.lisp fnn-mux-begin, fnn-mux-request-handshake, fnn-mux-start-waiting-handshake, fnn-mux-finish). The captured PROXY deadline is computed by fn-pxy-deadline from monotonic clock ticks, the admitted handshake milliseconds and the clock frequency. Host fn-owner-proxy-step and fn-owner-proxy-timeout-line call fn-pxy-observe before/after reads and at timer observations. KEYSTONE fn-pxy-observe-keeps-the-read-bound preserves the framing bound and permits a header only on natural clock observations strictly before its captured deadline; a complete header at or after it refuses :proxy-timeout, invalid observations refuse :proxy-clock. Byte progress never refreshes the header deadline. Clock fidelity and scheduling remain host assumptions; this is not a hard real-time wall-clock guarantee.

proofs.title: The event history keeps every acceptance through reclamation, and an acceptance records its commitment
proofs.statement: fn-hkn-reclamation-never-forgets-an-acceptance: for the host's rewrite fn-rclp-events (fn-store-log-reclaim-event per record), the knowledge fn-hkn-knowledge of any Message-ID over the rewritten history is :not-accepted, :outcome-unresolved or :history-unavailable exactly when it was over the original, :accepted-reclaimed stays, and :accepted-retained becomes one of the two accepted states. fn-hkn-acceptance-records-subject-principal-and-undertaking: when fn-replay-apply-record accepts a plain article record, the node binds the record's Message-ID to (msgid, content-subject, obligation-id) and holds the pin (obligation-id, content-subject, :archive, release-evidence, charge), with nothing staged. proofs.title: Reclamation is a logical release the continuation language cannot distinguish, except by the freed charge
proofs.statement: Over fn-hkn-release (the node with the article's payload at the tombstone, fn-rcl-reclaim-state, and its pin's charge at the history unit): a retry of the same Message-ID with any payload and any groups is refused after as before (fn-hkn-retry-refused-after-release-as-before); a receipt or release discharges the same obligation or none over an obligation list (fn-hkn-release-discharges-the-same-obligation); every obligation id is known after as before (fn-hkn-release-keeps-every-known-id); the stage and the bindings are unchanged; the reserved sum drops by exactly the content charge less the history unit (fn-hkn-release-frees-exactly-the-content-charge); and a request refused before and admitted after was refused for capacity alone and fits the freed charge (fn-hkn-release-enables-only-what-the-freed-charge-affords). The naive equivalence of every continuation is FALSE at the capacity refusal: must-fail in the teeth.

proofs.title: Replay binds the recorded evidence, never the replay's policy
proofs.statement: fn-hkn-replay-binds-the-recorded-evidence-not-the-policy: when fn-replay-apply-record accepts a plain article record from any node (any groups, any capacity), the evidence of the pin it holds under the record's obligation id is the record's release-evidence. Observed evidence (the record's release-evidence, a fn-provp value), the authorized decision (the binding) and the obligation (the pin) are three fields of the same acceptance; replay copies, it does not derive. Open: the revocation half (preserved historical authorization confers no current authority) is books/replay.lisp's fn-replay-apply-revoked-verdict (PRF-098) for identity verdicts; no theorem yet states it for retention authority.

proofs.title: The extent reader decides IDENTITY, not self-consistency: the descriptor carries the entry's commitment and every read is decided against it
proofs.statement: GPT-6's second review (warranty-quality-proof-engineering.md section 2): host/native/extent.lisp fnn-extent-entry ignored the descriptor's trailer, checked a read against the trailer it had just read, and keyed its cache by file and offset only, so a different well-formed same-sized entry (E1, T1) at the extent's offset was accepted; and the descriptor's trailer field was 0 at every construction site (fn-arx-extent-of, fn-arx-commit-extent, fn-lzr-extent-of). books/payload-extent.lisp: fn-arx-trailer-nat OCTETS (fn-bch-pack, books/packed-octets.lisp) is the commitment of the entry's 32 trailer octets, injective on octet lists (fn-arx-trailer-nat-injective); fn-arx-attach-trailers attaches each record's place its entry's commitment (START N ROFF RLEN TRAILER), and fn-arx-extent-of, fn-arx-commit-extent (books/payload-commit-extent.lisp) and fn-lzr-extent-of (books/payload-lz-record.lisp) carry it into the descriptor; books/extent-retire.lisp fn-xrt-reseat-one reads the frame's commitment from the buffer after the prefix (fn-arx-trailer-nat-at-buffer). books/payload-extent-read.lisp: fn-arx-entry-verdict-buffer EXPECTED READ BUF answers :ok, :trailer (the trailer recorded after the prefix is not the descriptor's: another entry at this offset, a wrong offset, an entry of another store or generation) or :digest (the prefix's frame digest is not its trailer); KEYSTONE fn-arx-entry-verdict-buffer-ok-is-the-commitment: :ok exactly when READ is 32 octets whose commitment is EXPECTED and the buffer's frame digest is READ; KEYSTONE fn-arx-entry-verdict-buffer-ok-digest-is-the-recorded-trailer, the boundary composed with the descriptor: when EXPECTED is the commitment of the entry's durable recorded trailer, an :ok verdict means the frame digest of the buffer the host serves from IS that recorded trailer (the octets handed to the model are the octets whose digest the accepted extent committed to; the pessimistic gap is a BLAKE3 collision, 2^128 work); fn-arx-entry-verdict-buffer-of-durable: a faithful read of an intact entry is :ok; fn-arx-attach-trailers-buffer-is-attach-trailers: the by-index attachment over the open's entry buffer is the list one. proofs.statement: Subjects: books/msgid-pages-exec.lisp section 7 (fn-mpxt-settle, the put-first fn-mpxt-add, fn-mpxt-first-page, the stuck bit). (1) fn-mpxt-add-places-iff-not-saturated: the add's outcome is :placed exactly when fn-mpxt-saturatedp of the tag is false in the table BEFORE the add (so the served POST can decide the refusal without mutating anything; from no pages the first page is made in place). (2) fn-mpxt-grow-preserves-faithful: for every wf table and buffer, fn-mpxt-faithful rows table implies fn-mpxt-faithful rows (mv-nth 1 (fn-mpxt-grow table buffer)) -- an adopted generation holds every mapping (fn-mpxt-grow-into-faithful over the entries list: a candidate is a slot's entry, fn-mpxt-candidates-entry; the checked re-placement finds every entry of its list, fn-mpxt-put-all-checked-finds, and keeps every candidate, fn-mpxt-put-all-checked-keeps-candidate; the fresh generation satisfies the slot invariant, fn-mpxt-fresh-okp, and re-placing entries below N keeps it, fn-mpxt-put-all-checked-keeps-okp), and a generation that could not be built leaves the table (the stuck bit set; never retried before a rebuild). (3) fn-mpxt-add-preserves-faithful: faithful rows table and a :placed add of row H at seq (len rows) give faithful (append rows (list H)) of the result. (4) THE FOLD fn-mpxt-build key rows (the fold of fn-mpxt-add from (fn-mpxt-set-key key (create-fn-mpxt)); fn-mpxt-build-unplaced its unplaced count): KEYSTONE fn-mpxt-build-faithful -- unplaced 0 implies fn-mpxt-faithful rows (fn-mpxt-build key rows); fn-mpxt-build-append -- the fold over one more row is one more add (the catalog's commit step); fn-mpxt-build-nil. The reader-projection congruence fn-mpxt-same-pages-faithful (the reader reads only the pages' words: count, stuck bit and buffer are never read) carries the count and stuck updates and the adopt. Scope: the logical fold; the catalog's correspondence clause table = fn-mpxt-build key rows and the served :mpx-saturated refusal are THE SWITCH (row P2, open in the LANEDUMP NEXT). Hypotheses: fn-mpxtp and fn-mpxt-wfp of the table, fn-mpxtp of the buffer, true-listp rows, (< (+ 1 (len rows)) 2^64) (the seq word).

proofs.title: Live limits keep three values: the requested policy, the funded limit the running process admits under, and the representation ceiling; a recorded change never funds
proofs.statement: books/limits-live.lisp (GPT-6, planning/review-2026-09-29-gpt6-decisions.md section 7). KEYSTONE fn-lim-funded-after-decide: for every live decision D = fn-lim-decide FIELD N VALUES USE RUN-MB CORE NURSERY OBSERVATIONS OBSERVED and candidate C = fn-lim-apply-row VALUES FIELD N, the profile the owner serves afterwards (fn-lim-funded-after D FUNDED C) is FUNDED unless D is :applied, and on :applied it is C, admitted (fn-bs-profile-admittedp), with the store's use at most N, N at most the ceiling (fn-lim-ceiling FIELD) and D's heap figure at most RUN-MB. KEYSTONE fn-lim-resource-refusal-is-the-reservations: D's refusal class (fn-lim-refusal-class) is :resource exactly when FIELD is live, N is within the ceiling and the use, C is admitted, and the launcher's run reservation (fn-heap-status-decide C ...) answers no heap; policy (not live, below use) and representation (past the ceiling, invalid profile) refusals are never resource ones. fn-lim-decide refuses N past fn-lim-ceiling (the configuration delta's u32, fn-cfg-deltap; T also the txid width, A the article codec) by name, :above-representation-ceiling, before the profile or the machine is consulted, and the operator's parser takes any decimal natural for a live field (books/native-admin.lisp fn-native-admin-naturalp), so that refusal is what `policy set' answers past the ceiling (exit refused, never a usage line); fn-lim-decide-accepted-keeps-use-within gains N <= the ceiling. Host: host/native/admin.lisp fnn-owner-limit-serialized installs (fn-lim-funded-after D FUNDED C) with FUNDED the owner's served profile and replies fn-lim-reply-line (the decision sentence; then `limit FIELD requested=R funded=U ceiling=C'); fnn-admin-execute-limit replies it with funded=none; host/native/heap.lisp fnn-lim-print-values prints fn-lim-values-lines for the three fields on an offline `status' (host/native/operator.lisp fnn-operator-status-once, :offline route). The running owner carries (REQUESTED . FUNDED) (host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-limit-carry: both the history's effective profile at its open, fn-owner-install-profile; fn-lim-carry-after after each accepted, published `policy set', fn-owner-limit-decided) and decides the live `policy set' over it; its `status' and `health' append fn-lim-report-octets of the carry (host/native-live-status-host.lisp fn-native-live-status-host-answer), no history walk. KEYSTONE fn-lim-reported-triple-is-the-decisions: for a live FIELD with VALUES and FUNDED given, the reply fn-lim-reply-line FIELD N D OPEN-MS VALUES FUNDED is the decision sentence, `; ', then fn-lim-values-line FIELD of the carry after D (fn-lim-carry-after FIELD N D (VALUES . FUNDED)), and that line is a member of the report's lines (fn-lim-report-lines) over that carry. KEYSTONE fn-lim-carry-after-is-the-history: when the carry's requested profile is fn-lim-effective SEALED RECORDS and FIELD is live, after D it is fn-lim-effective SEALED over RECORDS with the verb's record (fn-cfg-record-make S TX GEN (fn-lim-deltas FIELD N) STAMP) appended when D is accepted, and fn-lim-effective SEALED RECORDS when refused. Scope: the start's own refusal is the launcher's reservation refusal (heap-reservation.lisp fn-heap-reserve-report-line), the same words this class names :resource. Local policy, no RFC requirement.

proofs.title: The history image adopted from its committed root and bound to the exact log prefix: adoption ESTABLISHES the history's faithfulness (header from page 0, the root's tables, a narrow digest bound instead of the unestablished disk-faithful relation), the binding identifies the prefix by the log's chain value (not its count), a page request's late completion is refused by name, eviction respecting pins keeps faithfulness and progress
proofs.statement: books/history-image-binding.lisp. ROOT-HOLDS fn-hib-root-holds H C: every entry of the loaded table names the digest of H's placed image page. DISK-BOUND fn-hib-disk-bound FILE H C: the page file holds no BLAKE3 second preimage of an image page at the address the table names (the narrow cryptographic-failure hypothesis on the actual file; collision bound 2^-128 per pair). KEYSTONES: fn-hib-fill-rel (a fill of the words the file holds keeps fn-hrs-rel with ROOT-HOLDS and DISK-BOUND, no fn-hrecs-disk-faithful); fn-hib-get-keeps (the retry loop fn-hrc-get keeps them; :ok is record SEQ); fn-hib-hrecs-get-fuel-enough (fn-hrecs-get never stops for fuel with the open pages as fuel, with no relation to the disk); fn-hib-adopt-establishes (fn-hib-adopt: the page store opened at the root, page 0 filled and checked, the header read from page 0, its count checked; when it lands and the root is H's image under the digest bound, fn-hrs-rel H, ROOT-HOLDS and DISK-BOUND hold and the count is (len H)); fn-hib-open-binds-prefix (fn-hib-open accepts a binding (:hib NODE CODEC COUNT TRAIL REC SALT) only when TRAIL is the log's chain value at the prefix: with the snapshot's TRAIL the chain of its entries EW, the log's that of its entries EL, and fn-hib-chain-distinct (the narrow chain bound), EW = EL); fn-hib-open-is-log-prefix (the adopted concrete holds the snapshot's history HW, of exactly the log's prefix); fn-hib-replay-extends (replaying the suffix Q holds HW ++ Q); fn-hib-complete-keeps / fn-hib-complete-stale (a page request (:page-request OP ROOT P PHYS DIGEST) completed with the file's words keeps the relations; a late completion -- root or entry changed -- changes nothing and is refused :stale-root / :stale-page); fn-hib-evict-keeps, fn-hib-undone-evict, fn-hib-complete-progress (eviction of an unpinned page keeps the relations; an operation's measure fn-hib-undone is bounded by the page count, unmoved by evictions respecting its pins, dropped by each of its completions). Scope: not host-called yet (the served checkpoint writes no image, the served open adopts none); the eviction frees no memory in this representation.
proofs.progress_note: Lane composed-owner, 2026-09-29 (rows A2-A4 of build/coordinator/COMPLETE-BEFORE-6.6.0.md; GPT-6's review of 2026-09-28). Teeth (tests/acl2/history-image-binding-tests.lisp): LIVE-RUN witnesses over committed page files (an alist attached to fn-pgs-page-words / fn-pgs-fill-realize; two histories of equal length, the first committed in two generations): positive (every hypothesis of fn-hib-open-is-log-prefix executed; every row reads H); removal of root-is-image, of the binding's trail and of the log's trail (each conclusion fails); row A3: equal-count image/binding swaps (:root-absent, (:dir-damaged 1), (:refused :prefix 40)), another store / salt / codec, a count mismatch ((:refused :count 40 39)), an old root over a newer table generation ((:table-damaged ...); copy-on-write keeps the old root readable), a late fill after the root changed ((:refused :stale-root 1 2), nothing changed, the new root answers), a stale entry at the same txid ((:refused :stale-page P)), a crash between the two publications (old root selected and read; out of order :root-absent), damage at first touch ((:page-damaged P PHYS), never an answer or absence), page 0 damaged (adoption refused), eviction (pinned refused, evicted page asked for again, the row still read). No removal witness for the digest bound or the chain bound: removing either while keeping the rest needs a BLAKE3 collision or second preimage.

proofs.title: Readers of the history image by access pattern: one paged fold, proved once over a constrained step and instantiated per reader, that reads without filling, stops at the first unverified row with its cursor and accumulator (so the page is served outside the owner) and resumes; the composed runs fold exactly the rows read
proofs.statement: books/history-image-fold.lisp. fn-hif-run I U ACC C: rows [I, U) of the concrete read with fn-hrc-at (no fill, no I/O), the constrained step fn-hif-f applied to each while it reads (:ok); answers (mv VERDICT CURSOR ACC). KEYSTONE fn-hif-run-is-foldl: over a concrete that holds H (fn-hrs-rel, fn-hrc-wfp) and U <= (len H): I <= CURSOR <= U; ACC is fn-hif-foldl of H's rows [I, CURSOR) (fn-hif-seg); VERDICT is :done exactly when CURSOR = U; any other VERDICT is a need-verdict. fn-hif-run-resume: a run stopped at J with A, resumed at J with A, folds H's rows [I, K). fn-hif-def-fold NAME STEP FOLDL instantiates the run and its keystone per reader by functional instance (two instances in the book, witnessed by tests/acl2/history-image-binding-tests.lisp). Patterns: indexed = fn-hrc-get (PRF-920 fn-hib-get-keeps), count = fn-hrc-count, fold / bounded cursor = this run. Scope: no served reader calls it yet (the served open does not adopt the image).

proofs.title: The live arena's off-mutex readers pin a generation; a retirement is released only when every live reader pinned after it (row A6, the generation pin)
proofs.statement: Subject (books/arena-reader-pins.lisp): fn-arpn-step, which the host calls for every event of the arena readers' generation state (host/native/io.lisp fnn-arena-pins-step under its own lock; fnn-arena-pin/-unpin around a checkpoint publication's thread, host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-maybe-publish and fnn-owner-publish-captured; fnn-arena-retire and fnn-arena-release-due in the COMPLETE's reseat, fnn-log-reseat-fenced; fnn-arena-stamp/-clear-p for the installing reclaim pass). The state is (CUR PINS PEND): the current generation, the live pins as a strictly ascending table of (G . N) with every G <= CUR (fn-arpn-okp, established by fn-arpn-initial and preserved by every event: fn-arpn-step-preserves-okp), and the pending retirements (S . ITEMS). A :pin answers CUR (fn-arpn-pin-answers-the-generation); a :retire stamps CUR, which is at or above every live pin, and advances the generation (fn-arpn-retire-stamp-covers-every-live-pin; fn-arpn-step-generation-never-decreases). KEYSTONE fn-arpn-release-postdates-every-live-pin: every retirement :release answers was pending and its stamp is below every live pin, so no reader live at the retirement is live at its release; fn-arpn-release-keeps-every-covered-retirement: a retirement some live reader is pinned at or below stays pending. Generalizes the single off-mutex reader count (*fnn-arena-off-mutex-readers*, removed): an old retirement is released as soon as the readers older than it end, whatever newer readers run.

proofs.title: The Store open from a checkpoint is the twin's open from the publication's two facts (the composed boundary of the incremental finalize); the F row carries NEXT
proofs.statement: books/store-finalize-published.lisp (fn-sfp-, row A9) and books/store-checkpoint-tables.lisp (the F row). Subject: fn-store-sn-recover-from-checkpoint (host/store-node-host.lisp) calls (fn-sfi-extend-open checkpoint configs rows frontier next) with NEXT read from the F row (fn-store-sco-decode-finish keeps it in the global fn-store-sco-next): the whole-history finalize fn-rii-sco-extend-open is no longer on the open from a checkpoint (the full open fn-store-sn-recover-rows keeps it). The F row (fn-sct-f-row s frontier revision log next) carries NEXT = (nfix (fn-sct-next-lower records 0)), the prefix's transaction bound, beside S; fn-sct-next-lower-is-next-lower equates the guard-t fold to fn-sf-next-lower; fn-sct-next-of-tables-of-capture and fn-sct-next-of-tables-is-bound-of-loaded-records say the F row's NEXT of any capture's tables is the (nfix of the) bound of the records the load means. Both publish paths (host/native/io.lisp state-checkpoint, host/native/owner.lisp auto and reclaim) build the F row inside ACL2 (fn-sct-tables-of-capture from owner-checkpoint-writer / -pipeline / store-checkpoint-arena-writer), so the field lands on both with no host change there. KEYSTONE fn-sfp-open-from-publication-is-the-twin: whenever the captured history opens :ok at the publication frontier ((fn-sn-open-kind (fn-cpo-open-observed configs frontier records)) = :ok), the tables (fn-sct-tables-of-capture (fn-ock-next-checkpoint base configs records) frontier revision log) of the publication, loaded by fn-sct-capture-of-tables and opened by fn-sfi-extend-open with the F row's NEXT over any suffix at any frontier f, equal fn-rii-sco-extend-open's open, with the same CONFIGS on both sides (the publication's and the open's). From fn-sfp-published-capture-finalizes-ok (the published capture finalizes :ok at the publication frontier: fn-ock-next-checkpoint-is-the-capture, fn-ock-finalize-of-extended-capture over the empty suffix) and fn-sfp-published-next-is-the-bound (NEXT = (fn-sf-next-lower records 0), a natural of every observed history: fn-sfp-next-lower-natp). What connects the tables to the bytes the open verified is fn-scka-load-of-written-file (the writer's file loads to its tables) plus the trust row A-CHECKPOINT-PUBLICATION (books/assumptions-publication.lisp: encapsulate fn-assume-checkpoint-publishedp / fn-assume-checkpoint-publication, constraint fn-assume-checkpoint-publication-is-a-publication: a verified file's tables are a publication's of a history that opened :ok under the open's configuration at the F row's frontier), under which fn-sfp-open-under-checkpoint-publication is the host's open. Pessimistic figure with its scope: A-CRYPTO-TRAILER's collision bound over one 256-bit trailer, about 2^-128 per chosen pair of frames, not the second-preimage figure; the row is also operational (a foreign store's verifying checkpoint is a publication of another history: the lineage check of row A10 refuses it by name before this open). Every process-death cut of the publication is a crash point of fn-bs-scp-program (books/byte-store-state-checkpoint-program.lisp fn-bs-scp-program-crash-is-old-or-new): the open sees the old checkpoint or the new one; a torn new one fails its chain before any table is read. NOT established here: that the owner's live history opens :ok at every publication frontier -- the theorem takes it as its antecedent and the row names it (the owner's live-history relation, PRF-083/PRF-144 territory).

proofs.title: The carried pair's invariant made decidable: fn-sfk-carried-check's :ok establishes fn-sfi-cpr-carriedp and its :wrong-msgid-trie refutes it; the trust row A-CARRIED-PAIR
proofs.statement: books/store-finalize-carried-check.lisp (fn-sfk-, row A9 item (2); lane incremental-finalize-3). fn-sfi-cpr-carriedp (PRF-968) is a verified guard the evaluator cannot run (fn-rii-okp's fn-rii-known-okp is a defun-sk) and ACL2 refuses an abstract stobj holding the pair (fn-cnode-statep reaches the attached fn-digest), so the :program host keeps it. fn-sfk-carried-check (r ix), guard t and executable (one node pass, fn-rii-ix-of; never on a served path), answers :ok, :wrong-msgid-trie, :not-paused, :node-not-configured, :not-a-pair or :uncertain-id-trie, kept distinct. KEYSTONES: fn-sfk-check-ok-is-carried (:ok implies fn-sfi-cpr-carriedp, via fn-sfk-check-ok-facts: :ok is the three conjuncts with IX exactly fn-rii-ix-of of the paused node, and fn-rii-okp-of-ix-of); fn-sfk-check-wrong-msgid-trie-is-not-carried (fn-sfi-carried-msgid-trie-is-the-rebuilt-trie: under fn-rii-okp the Message-ID trie is canonical, so a different one refutes the invariant); fn-sfk-check-shape-answers-are-not-carried (the three shape answers refute it by the invariant's own conjuncts); fn-sfk-carry-checks-ok (the open's own pair, fn-sfi-carry, checks :ok). :uncertain-id-trie decides nothing: fn-rii-known-okp is extensional and a structurally different id trie may still satisfy it; the check says so instead of guessing. Trust row A-CARRIED-PAIR (books/assumptions-publication.lisp: encapsulate fn-assume-carried-pairp, constraint fn-assume-carried-pair-is-carried; theorem fn-sfp-carried-open-under-carried-pair = PRF-968's keystone under the row): a host that carries the pair across extensions relies on passing the pair fn-sfi-carry produced or the previous carried entry answered, which the preservation theorems keep carried; nothing on a served path calls the carried entries at this revision (the open calls fn-sfi-extend-open, PRF-992), the row is the contract of the swap wiring that will. Item (3) decided here: fn-rii-sco-cpr-prefix-is-sco-cpr-prefix (and PRF-968's keystones) need NO fn-rii-okp hypothesis -- they equate logical values and the tries enter only through mbe :exec, whose faithfulness is the guard obligation of the twin's inner functions (fn-rii-okp is that guard); a wrong trie is a guard violation visible only on the raw path, which the tooth shows (the wrong pair admits a duplicate Message-ID the right pair refuses) while the check names it :wrong-msgid-trie. Adding the hypothesis would weaken a true theorem for nothing; the decidable check is what the boundary lacked.
proofs.progress_note: Lane incremental-finalize-3 (Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-09-29): REPL-green on persvati (every theorem under 400 steps). Teeth: the open's pair and a carried round's answered pair both check :ok (so on the test history the carried id trie IS structurally the rebuilt one); the empty node's tries check :wrong-msgid-trie and on the served path (raw) admit a duplicate Message-ID the right pair refuses; the three shape answers; :uncertain-id-trie reached with the right Message-ID trie and a foreign id trie.

proofs.title: A checkpoint the open accepts shares the log's lineage: every segment K >= 2 opens with a rotation entry chained from the closed segment's last trailer, the F row's GENESIS is its trailer, and the open decides over segment K's head before it scans -- a fork's checkpoint (a restored backup that diverged, the same store identity, an equal count, an empty suffix) is refused :foreign-lineage by name
proofs.statement: books/store-log-lineage.lisp (lane store-lineage, row A2's last piece: composed-owner-6's G1 finding). The rotation entry fn-lgl-rotation-frame P K: an FNLG frame of kind 3 (*fn-lg-rotation-kind*) over P (the closed segment's last trailer, the claimed predecessor) and K as u32, no records; fn-lgl-open K G HEAD T0 MAX: the open's lineage decision over the F row's (K G) and segment K's head -- nil, or (:refused :foreign-lineage) when the head is a readable rotation entry naming K whose trailer is not G, (:refused :segment-head-damaged) when it is not a readable rotation entry, (:refused :segment-misnamed) when it names another index; segment 1 must carry T0. KEYSTONE fn-lgl-open-of-rotated-segment: over segment K as the rotation wrote it from P (the entry, then anything -- records or nothing) the open accepts (K G) exactly when G is the entry's trailer. fn-lgl-fork-refused: with G the trailer of a rotation entry from another chain value Q, the open refuses :foreign-lineage, under the per-pair hypothesis fn-lgl-trailer-distinct (two rotation entries naming K with equal trailers continue from the same value; its failure is a BLAKE3 collision between the two frames, the pessimistic figure 2^-128 per pair). fn-lgl-accepted-shares-lineage (the composed statement over publish, recover and open): with P the chain value of the segments the log held below K and Q that of the segments the checkpoint's capture covered, an accepted checkpoint covered exactly the log's segments, under fn-lgl-trailer-distinct and fn-lgl-chain-distinct (fn-hib-chain-distinct's shape over segments). Scope at READY 1: the model; the host's rotation and open follow it in READY 2 (books/store-log.lisp kind 3, fn-lgc-rotate KS K, host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-rotate / fnn-recover-log).

proofs.title: fn-tcl-encode is the canonical TCPCL wire form: the encoding of every message kind the host sends decodes back to it with the rest untouched, and an accepted buffer is the encoding of its parse
proofs.statement: books/tcpcl-octets.lisp; host/tcpcl-host.lisp's fn-tcl-host-encode is an exact alias (a checked :delegates fn-tcl-encode, the generated equation fn-tcl-host-encode-is-fn-tcl-encode-by-definition), called by host/native/tcpcl.lisp's send path. KEYSTONES: fn-tcl-decode-message-of-encode-{init,segment,ack,refuse,term,reject,keepalive} and fn-tcl-decode-contact-of-encode: for a message M of that kind with (fn-tcl-messagep M mru) (for the contact header: an octet version and octet flags; for term and reject no hypothesis at all, since their two fields are single octets written and read verbatim -- the recognizer was proved redundant there), (fn-tcl-decode-message (append (fn-tcl-encode M) rest) mru) is (fn-tcl-parse-ok M rest), so a peer reads exactly M and consumes exactly the encoding; fn-tcl-accepted-message-is-canonical and fn-tcl-accepted-contact-is-canonical: an octet buffer the decoder accepts equals the encoding of its parse followed by its rest, so no second octet form is accepted for a message. proofs.title: THE SWITCH: the catalog's Message-ID column is served from the paged table (lane paged-history-5, row P2): fn-cat-msgid-seqs reads a nested fn-mpxt whose logical value is the fold fn-mpxt-build of the rows under the table's own key; the served refusal fn-cat-msgid-saturatedp is the fold's outcome for one more row
proofs.statement: Subjects: books/catalog.lisp, the concrete stobj fn-cat$c with the paged Message-ID table fn-cat$c-mpx (a nested fn-mpxt, books/msgid-pages-exec), its next generation fn-cat$c-mpx2 and the unplaced count fn-cat$c-unplaced, replacing the hash fn-cat$c-msgids; the abstraction relation fn-cat$corr-base states EQUALITY: (nth 2 c) = fn-mpxt-build key rows, (nth 9 c) = fn-mpxt-build-buffer, (nth 10 c) = fn-mpxt-build-unplaced, key = fn-cat-key-of c (the table's own key octets). Host caller: every served Message-ID finder calls the abstract export fn-cat-msgid-seqs (served-columns fn-scol-find-row, served-catalog fn-scat-msgid-article, served-catalog-owner); its logic fn-cat$a-msgid-seqs is unchanged (design B.6, the 5u method: no served book changes). proofs.title: OVER/XOVER of a range answered in bounded windows is the unbounded reader's reply, for every window width
proofs.statement: books/served-catalog.lisp (the section "OVER/XOVER of a range answered in bounded windows") and books/over-window.lisp. The served step answers an OVER/XOVER range with a CURSOR: fn-ovw-start (session v token legacyp fn-cat) parses and clamps the range once (no number probed) and answers a cursor (group k top v legacyp owedp), or the 412 reply with no cursor; the -cat dispatcher's OVER/XOVER range arm fn-nntp-over-range-ovw (called by fn-nntp-archive-command-cat, the host's served read through books/served-catalog-chain.lisp fn-scr-command) emits that cursor as the step's one effect (:over-cursor CUR). A cursor effect MEANS the complete reply of its range (fn-ovw-cursor-octets: the lines K..TOP of GROUP in the pinned view V, the status line owed); fn-ovw-expand replaces every cursor effect of an effects list by that reply and keeps everything else, and the chain's readers of an effects list see through it (fn-ovw-offeredp-of-expand, fn-ovw-submission-of-expand, -submission-login-, -submission-account-, fn-ovw-selectedp-of-expand: the expansion begins with its own status line 224/423/420). KEYSTONE fn-nntp-over-range-ovw-expands-to-over-range-cat, no hypothesis: the arm's session is unchanged and its expanded effects are (cdr (fn-nntp-over-range-cat session v token legacyp fn-arena fn-cat)), the unbounded reader's reply. From fn-nntp-archive-command-cat-is-pinned up every -cat = pinned equation of books/served-catalog-chain.lisp (through the keystone fn-scr-ocfg-read-span-is-reference-under-ocl-relation) is stated on the results' components -- session / connection / consumed count / submission / owner / re-pin flag equal outright -- with the effects of BOTH sides expanded (the pinned reference builds no cursor: fn-ovw-cursor-effect has the one call site; stating the equations symmetrically keeps them free of that structural fact about the whole pinned dispatcher, which is not proved). The host's continuation (books/over-window.lisp): fn-ovw-step (cursor w fn-arena fn-cat) probes the window k..hi, hi = min(top, k+W-1), builds its NOV lines, sends the 224 status line before the first line, the stuffed lines, and on the last window the dot (or 423 / 420 when no line was ever sent), and answers the next cursor or NIL. proofs.title: The Message-ID index as a linear-hashing table (stage 7, the index part): a root-carried round modulus N and split pointer S, address TAG mod N re-addressed by TAG mod 2N below S, a split that moves one home's movers to one new page, a lookup of at most the home page and its flagged next page; the reader is the specification under the faithful relation and a split preserves it
proofs.statement: Subjects: books/msgid-linear.lisp. THE TABLE (fn-mpxl-tabp): pages (FLAG . ENTRIES) with entries (TAG . SEQ) in slot order, root (N S) with 0 <= S < N and N + S pages; fn-mpxl-addr tag n s = h = tag mod n, or tag mod 2n when h < s (fn-mpxl-addr-below: below N + S; fn-mpxl-mod-double: tag mod 2n is h or h + n). THE READER fn-mpxl-records msgid tab rows = fn-mpx-confirm (layer A of books/msgid-pages, reused unchanged) over fn-mpxl-cands: the home page's seqs and, when the home page's flag is set, the next page's, inserted ascending (fn-mpxl-ins). KEYSTONE fn-mpxl-records-is-the-records-for: under fn-mpxl-tabp and fn-mpxl-faithful (fn-mpxl-okp: every seq below the length; fn-mpxl-faithful-from 0: every held row's seq among its tag's candidates) the reader equals fn-cei-article-records-for, by fn-mpx-confirm-is-the-records-for with fn-mpxl-cands-nat-listp / -ascending / -below and the completeness lemma; fn-mpxl-records-is-hist-msgid-records restates it against fn-hist$a-msgid-records. THE WRITER fn-mpxl-put: the entry onto its home page when it has room, else onto the next page with the home page's flag set, else NOT AT ALL (fn-mpxl-put-places-iff-not-saturated: placed exactly when not fn-mpxl-saturatedp; fn-mpxl-put-unplaced-unchanged): fn-mpxl-put-finds (the placed seq is a candidate of its tag), fn-mpxl-put-keeps-candidate (every candidate of every tag survives), fn-mpxl-put-okp, fn-mpxl-put-preserves-faithful (a held row's entry at (len rows) keeps the table faithful to the rows with that row appended; fn-mpxl-faithful-append-not-held for a row that is no article). THE SPLIT fn-mpxl-split (Litwin): of the entries on page S and on S + 1 those whose address under mod 2N is N + S (fn-mpxl-moverp; fn-mpxl-mover-home: their home is S) move to the new page N + S, appended with flag clear; S advances, and at S = N the round ends (N doubles, S = 0); refused with the table unchanged when the movers exceed *fn-mpxl-cap* (fn-mpxl-split-refused-unchanged). fn-mpxl-addr-after-split-same-round / -next-round: the movers' address is the new page and every other tag's is unchanged. fn-mpxl-page-of-split-pages: only pages S, S + 1 and the new page differ (the bounded-work frame, D27). KEYSTONE fn-mpxl-split-keeps-candidate (stated on candidate membership for every tag, so every row model inherits it; proved over the root's variables as fn-mpxl-split-pages-keeps-candidate) and KEYSTONE fn-mpxl-split-preserves-faithful: fn-mpxl-tabp and fn-mpxl-faithful give fn-mpxl-faithful of the split table, taken or refused (the success hypothesis REMOVED by proof after the 2026-10-01 review, from -when-taken and fn-mpxl-split-refused-unchanged; fn-mpxl-split-keeps-candidate-always likewise) (with fn-mpxl-split-tabp, fn-mpxl-split-okp, fn-mpxl-faithful-from-of-split). The one representation change against books/msgid-pages-exec: the reader follows the home page's OVERFLOW FLAG, not its fullness, because a split empties slots and would otherwise orphan overflow entries. What this does not prove: the executable twin (books/msgid-linear-exec, PRF-1219), the catalog's switch, anything about the tag's distribution. Teeth tests/acl2/msgid-linear-tests.lisp: the colliding tag (FNV mod 3) attached; the four-row history placed by fn-mpxl-put into N = 2 pages, the keystone's complete antecedent and conclusion (two records in history order, one, none); the split of page 0 (ok, S = 1, three pages, every mover's address under mod 4 is 2, the count conserved) and the round's end (N = 4, S = 0), tabp and faithful and the reader's answers after each; the refusals (1,025 movers refused with the table unchanged, 1,024 taken; a put onto a full home page lands on the next page with the flag set and is found, a put with both full is refused with the table unchanged; the flag is what the reader follows); a MUTATED SPLIT on a reachable table (N = 2, S = 0, 1,024 tag-2 entries, then tag 0 at seq 1024 overflowing to page 1 and flagging page 0): the book's split keeps the flag and the row, a split that drops the flag loses seq 1024 (faithful fails, the reader misses it); hypothesis removal: faithful-from dropped (an entry missing: the conclusion fails); fn-mpxl-okp and fn-mpxl-tabp have no removal witness (their redundancy is a proof task on layer A, not a counterexample).

proofs.title: The linear-hashing Message-ID table, executable: typed fixnum words (u61: a 60-bit keyed tag, SEQ + 1, the overflow flag in bit 60 of slot 0's seq word), inlined slot accessors, a scan that allocates nothing; the stobj abstracts to the logical table and the word reader is the logical reader of the abstraction; the reader is the catalog's walk under the faithful relation; the writer, the split (refining fn-mpxl-split), the add (one split per step) and the fold the catalog's correspondence needs
proofs.statement: Subjects: books/msgid-linear-exec.lisp (fn-mlh-). THE STOBJS: a page fn-mlg is a FIXED array of 2,048 (unsigned-byte 61) words, the table fn-mlh a two-level directory of table pages (fn-mlt, 64 page slots each) grown ONE page at a time (fn-mlh-grow = fn-mlh-fresh-page at the page count: the table page's slot array grown by one, at most 63 pointers copied, the directory 256 wide doubling past its width and widened once at open by fn-mlh-reserve; fn-mlh-word reads a slot never taken as 0; fn-mlh-word-of-put-word / -of-fresh-page / -of-reserve are the read-after-write equations; the hot loops fn-mlh-scan-pg / fn-mlh-find-empty-pg equal fn-mlh-scan / fn-mlh-find-empty) -- no page ever copied and no per-split copy of the page pointers (Codex r42 F1 / r48 F3; one add touches at most five data pages), so a step allocates one page and at most 63 pointers within the reserved width (D27; MEASURED hbox 2026-10-01, 3.67M adds to 8,193 pages: worst add 49,408 B, mean 96 B, vs 114,752 B / 168 B for the one-array predecessor); slot J: tag word J, seq word 1024 + J holding SEQ + 1 below 2^60; bit 60 of slot 0's seq word the page's OVERFLOW FLAG, fn-mlh-ovf), the root fn-mlh-n / fn-mlh-s beside the page count (fn-mlh-rootp: no pages, or N + S pages with 0 <= S < N), the count, the 32-octet key, the stuck bit; fn-mlh-tag msgid key = the keyed BLAKE3 word of books/msgid-pages-exec reduced mod 2^60, floored at 1 (fn-mlh-tag-below). The slot accessors fn-mlh-tag-at / fn-mlh-seqw / fn-mlh-seq-at / fn-mlh-ovf are defun-inline over the typed array, so every read is a fixnum. THE READER fn-mlh-candidates: the home page (fn-mpxl-addr of the tag under the root) scanned whole by fn-mlh-scan (tail recursive, (unsigned-byte 60) compares, fn-mpxt-ins) and, under the home page's flag, the next page -- at most two pages by construction; fn-mlh-seqs msgid rows = fn-mpxt-confirm over it (the catalog's shape). THE ABSTRACTION fn-mlh-abs: the pages as (flag . entries-in-slot-order) by fn-mlh-pe with the root (fn-mlh-abs-tabp; fn-mlh-page-of-abs-pages); fn-mlh-scan-is-seqs (the scan is fn-mpxl-seqs of the page's entries, via fn-mlh-pe-upto) and THE BRIDGE fn-mlh-candidates-is-cands: the word reader IS fn-mpxl-cands of the abstraction, for every positive tag -- every theorem of books/msgid-linear transfers. KEYSTONE fn-mlh-seqs-is-spec-from: under fn-mlh-faithful (fn-mlh-okp: the logical okp of the abstraction, every seq below the row count; fn-mlh-faithful-from 0: every row's sequence among its keyed tag's candidates) the reader equals fn-mpxt-spec-from 0, by fn-mpxt-confirm-is-the-spec with fn-mlh-candidates-nat-listp / -ascending / -below and fn-mlh-faithful-from-complete. THE WRITER fn-mlh-put: the first empty slot of the home page (fn-mlh-find-empty), else of the next page with the home page's flag set (fn-mlh-set-ovf), else nil with the table unchanged (fn-mlh-put-places-iff-not-saturated against fn-mlh-saturatedp; fn-mlh-put-unplaced-unchanged); fn-mlh-write-slot keeps the flag part of the seq word; the accessors after the writes (fn-mlh-tag-at/seqw/seq-at/ovf-of-write-slot and -of-set-ovf), the entries after the writes (fn-mlh-pe-of-write-slot-other/-above, fn-mlh-seqs-pe-of-write-slot: the seqs of a page gain the seq exactly when the tags agree), and the membership facts fn-mlh-put-finds and fn-mlh-put-keeps-candidate. MEASURED (persvati, proof_repl mlx, sb-ext:get-bytes-consed around 10,000 lookups on 10,000-entry tables, one candidate each): fn-mpxt-candidates 6,364 bytes consed per lookup (7,548 of 10,000 old tags at or above 2^62), fn-mlh-candidates 16 bytes per lookup (the result list's one cons; the scan allocates nothing). THE SPLIT (section 7, lane msgid-linear-hash-2): fn-mlh-count-movers (= len of fn-mpxl-movers of the page's entries, fn-mlh-count-movers-is-len) and fn-mlh-move (slot order, each mover written to the new page at a cursor and cleared on its page keeping the flag part; fn-mlh-pe-of-move-source: the page keeps its stayers; fn-mlh-pe-of-move-dest(-whole): the new page receives the movers; fn-mlh-accessors-of-move / -pe-of-move-other / -ovf-of-move: the frame); fn-mlh-split: m = movers of S plus of S + 1, refused unchanged above a page, else grow, move S then S + 1, advance the root. KEYSTONE fn-mlh-abs-of-split: for fn-mlhp, fn-mlh-wfp and a page, fn-mlh-abs of the split is mv-nth 1 of fn-mpxl-split of fn-mlh-abs, taken or refused (fn-mlh-split-taken-iff; by fn-mlh-split-page and list extensionality), hence fn-mlh-split-keeps-candidate and KEYSTONE fn-mlh-split-preserves-faithful from books/msgid-linear. THE ADD (section 8): fn-mlh-put-preserves-faithful (fn-mlh-put-okp, fn-mlh-faithful-from-of-put-append); fn-mlh-add = first page when none, the put, then fn-mlh-settle (count + 1 and, at 2 count >= 1024 N with no split refused, ONE split; a refused split sets stuck): fn-mlh-add-places-iff-not-saturated, fn-mlh-add-saturated-keeps-the-table, KEYSTONE fn-mlh-add-preserves-faithful. THE FOLD fn-mlh-build key rows (defun-nx over fn-mlh-build-from from fn-mlh-set-key of the creator; a row past the word limit counted unplaced): KEYSTONE fn-mlh-build-faithful (no row unplaced: faithful), fn-mlh-build-append (one more row is one more add), fn-mlh-build-nil, fn-mlh-build-append-unplaced-iff (placed exactly when not fn-mlh-saturatedp of the table as it is and the sequence space has room), fn-mlh-clear-is-build-nil / fn-mlh-create-is-build-nil / fn-mlh-set-key-canonical / fn-mlh-key-octets-of-set-key, fn-mlh-build-of-update-nth-same-msgid, and the executable projections fn-mlh-build-saturatedp / fn-mlh-build-health with -is-the-build and fn-mlh-build-saturatedp-is-the-outcome -- the catalog's correspondence's shape, the fn-mpxt2 rebuild gone.
