proofs.title: Recovery refinement: at every crash point of the composed store the recovery holds a prefix of the committed-then-in-flight records that holds every acknowledged record, and the composed open is the full open of it
proofs.statement: books/recovery-refinement.lisp (lane recovery-refinement, 2026-10-01; specs/recovery-refinement.md; design 2026-10-01 stage 7). Argosy's shape as DFSCQ's tree sequence: fn-rr-tree-sequence-memberp RECOVERED COMMITTED INFLIGHT says RECOVERED is COMMITTED followed by a prefix of INFLIGHT. KEYSTONE fn-rr-recovery-refines-a-prefix-with-every-acknowledged-record: over a related state (fn-lgk-relp BS KS, the log relation R every cut of the served log programs keeps: fn-lg-append/fence/reserve/order/extend-program-keeps-the-relation, fn-lg-recover-program-establishes-the-relation), any admissible crash image (fn-bs-crash-imagep), A-CRYPTO-TRAILER's premise on the tear past the frontier (fn-lg-platform-tears-p), and any image the medium holds bound to the capture of the first S committed records (S at most the committed count): (1) the records the log's recovery holds (fn-rr-recovered-records: fn-lgk-committed of fn-lgk-recover over the image's segment) are a tree-sequence member; (2) the composed open fn-rr-open (the selection under K, then the open from the image over the suffix it leaves, else the full open) is the medium's full open of those records; (3) every record among the first ACKED of COMMITTED (the kernel's acknowledged prefix, R's conjunct; the owner batch layer's fn-owb-acked members by fn-owb-alignedp and fn-lgu-acknowledged-record-is-committed) is among them, and a composed open that succeeded (fn-rr-medium-open-okp) HOLDS it (fn-rr-medium-holds; the medium's third constraint fn-rr-medium-full-open-holds-its-records, added for the Codex review of 2d1b10ed7 F2: without it the opened state was unconstrained beyond its equation to fn-rr-medium-full-open). Composed from fn-lgk-crash-of-related-state-is-a-prefix with fn-lg-no-forgery-under-a-crypto-trailer (fn-rr-log-crash-image-in-flight-recovers-a-tree-sequence-member), fn-bs-crash-keeps-fenced-content with fn-lg-scan-of-complete-append and fn-lg-scan-of-zeros (fn-rr-log-crash-image-quiet-recovers-committed), and the medium's interface (fn-rr-open-is-the-full-open-of-the-recovered-records: one hypothesis, the binding). The medium is the encapsulate fn-rr-medium-capture/-open/-full-open/-select/-open-okp/-holds whose constraints are PRF-083's keystone shape (fn-rr-medium-open-of-capture-is-the-full-open), the selection's bound (fn-rr-medium-select-bounds-the-sequence) and holding (fn-rr-medium-full-open-holds-its-records); books/recovery-refinement-store.lisp instantiates it with fn-sco-capture, fn-sco-open, fn-cpo-open-observed and fn-sco-select, the functions host/store-node-host.lisp fn-store-sn-recover-from-checkpoint and fn-store-sn-recover call, with the log's records decoded by fn-srs-decode (host fn-store-decode-records). MODEL-LEVEL, not a served-path claim (the Codex review of 2d1b10ed7, F1): no host file calls fn-rr-open or fn-rrs-open. The served open is host/native/io.lisp fnn-recover-log (fnn-log-recover: fn-lg-open-kernel, fn-lg-open-kernel-is-the-recovered-kernel), then fn-rii-sco-extend-open (books/replay-identity-index.lisp) or fn-sfi-extend-open (books/store-finalize-incremental.lisp) or the full replay; the claim becomes one about the served path only with the store instance admitted AND a named theorem equating fn-rrs-open to the host-called open (both in pending_subject). No host-called ACL2 function composes the two layers (the open square is host code, as PRF-344 records for the page store). Teeth: tests/acl2/recovery-refinement-tests.lisp (the ground two-record log with a third in flight at log-written under every per-unit tear and at log-fenced; the ground medium instantiated into fn-rr-open at S = 0, 1, 2, past K and absent; MUTATION: the image whose segment drops the acknowledged r2 is no admissible image and the conclusion fails on it; hypothesis removal: the binding (a non-prefix capture), the relation (a misplaced pending write)).
proofs.pending_subject: MODEL-LEVEL until two things land: (a) books/recovery-refinement-store.lisp (the instantiation with the store's open and fn-srs-decode, and the holding obligation: a successful fn-cpo-open-observed of EVENTS holds every member of EVENTS in fn-sf-records of fn-sn-files) is WRITTEN, NOT ADMITTED: its include chain reaches the node tower, red at dev 896c48c16 (books/store-events-carried.lisp fn-evc-consumer-shape, books/store-node-traces.lisp fn-snt-record-directory-preserves-relation); (b) a named theorem equating fn-rrs-open to the opens host/native/io.lisp fnn-recover-log calls (fn-rii-sco-extend-open, fn-sfi-extend-open). The generic book's chain stops at the byte model and the log kernel and was REPL-admitted on hbox (0 refused) from the cache.
proofs.progress_note: Open: PRF-1214 (a crash point inside a publication while a batch is in flight: R's pending conjunct names the segment's write alone), PRF-1215 (the page store as the medium). The sequential half of the checkpoint program's cuts is PRF-1216. Teeth after the Codex review of 2d1b10ed7: the keystone instantiated over the ground medium (rrt-keystone) with a reachable positive witness asserting its complete antecedent and conclusion at the exact tear and the quiet cut (F4); the relation witness removes exactly R (F3). The torn-write applicability of A-CRYPTO-TRAILER's premise rests on the assumption's own witness, which admits only the exact tear (F4, open against books/assumptions.lisp, not this row).

proofs.title: The checkpoint reserve: two image generations fit a format-time reserve of twice the reader's file bound at every cut of the publish program
proofs.statement: books/checkpoint-reserve.lisp (lane recovery-refinement, 2026-10-01; specs/recovery-refinement.md section 4; KeyKOS's format-time checkpoint reserve, Landau 1992). KEYSTONE fn-ckr-two-generations-fit-the-reserve-at-every-cut: from the quiet store the publication asks for (fn-bs-scp-inputp), with the new image's octets within BOUND and the old image's durable content within BOUND, every state of fn-bs-run over fn-bs-scp-program (fn-ckr-all-fit: the pairs after every step, the five cuts included) has the two generations' octets through the view, pending writes included (fn-ckr-generations-octets: the old inode's and the staged inode's), at most 2 * BOUND. The reserve fn-ckr-reserve-octets is twice fn-sccr-file-read-bound (the bound the open refuses a file past; the capture budget fn-ock-capture-budget is that bound over the profile, the equality fn-rrs-reserve-is-two-capture-budgets and the decision theorem fn-rrs-funded-reserve-never-defers-for-space over fn-ockp-decide are in books/recovery-refinement-store.lisp, written and not admitted while the node tower is red). The forcing half is PRF-083's fn-ock-publication-duep and fn-ock-not-due-keeps-the-checkpoint-open (the owner publishes at K/2). Host subject: host/native/io.lisp fnn-checkpoint-write-steps through fn-bs-scp-program's cuts (tests/campaign/native_cuts.py STATE_CHECKPOINT_CUTS). Teeth: tests/acl2/checkpoint-reserve-tests.lisp (the ground run of ten states at bound 3, the first publication without an old image; a new image past the bound and an old image past the bound each refused).
proofs.progress_note: Retiring the statvfs observation from fn-ockp-decide under the format-time reserve is a served host change outside this lane (MODE 2026-10-01 section 2). The page-store generation sized by K (the dirty pages of at most K commits) is PRF-1215. OPEN JOIN (Codex review of 2d1b10ed7, F5): the theorem bounds fn-bs-scp-program's OCTETS; the host writes through fnn-state-checkpoint-write -> fnn-history-image-write and fnn-checkpoint-write-steps (host/native/io.lisp) with no refinement of those writes to OCTETS, so funded space is an assumption of the join: PRF-1222.

proofs.title: The log relation R lifted to the segment's own pending operations: the composed recovery at every crash point of the checkpoint publication with a batch in flight
proofs.statement: books/recovery-refinement-concurrent.lisp (lane recovery-refinement-2, 2026-10-01; specs/recovery-refinement.md sections 3 and 5). fn-rrc-relp is fn-lgk-relp with (fn-bs-ops-for-ino (fn-bs-pending bs) ino) in place of the whole pending list; fn-lgk-relp-implies-fn-rrc-relp. THE PROJECTION fn-rrc-crash-content-is-the-projected-crash-content: a crash image's content at an inode is the content of the image of the projected store (fn-rrc-project: the store whose pending list is the inode's own operations) under the projected choices (fn-rrc-choices-for-ino), because fn-bs-crash-select tears each write by its own selectors and entry operations touch no inode; so the projected image of an admissible image is admissible with the same segment content (fn-rrc-projected-image-is-admissible-with-the-same-segment) and the projected store of a lifted-related store is related (fn-rrc-projection-is-related). KEYSTONE fn-rrc-recovery-refines-a-prefix-with-every-acknowledged-record: PRF-1212's statement, conjuncts (1) to (3) including holding, with fn-rrc-relp for fn-lgk-relp (by the transfer through the projection: fn-rrc-log-crash-image-recovers-a-tree-sequence-member). THE CONCURRENT CUTS fn-rrc-checkpoint-crash-point-refines-with-a-batch-in-flight: from a related state (fn-lgk-relp, a batch in flight or not) and the publication's input without its quiet conjunct (fn-rrc-scp-inputp), at every state of fn-bs-run over fn-bs-scp-program and for every admissible crash image of it, the keystone's three conclusions: the program keeps the segment's presence, content, unit and own pending operations (fn-rrc-scp-run-keeps-the-segment, local), which keeps the lifted relation (fn-rrc-keeping-the-segment-keeps-the-lifted-relation). The old-or-new of the image under concurrency is not restated (PRF-1216's fn-bs-scp-program-crash-is-old-or-new asks for the quiet store); the finish and stage-cleanup rows of the cut table cite the step lemma with their keep-the-segment proofs owed under PRF-1221. Host subject as PRF-1212 (MODEL-LEVEL): host/native/io.lisp fnn-state-checkpoint-write off the owner mutex while fnn-log-append holds a batch at log-written; the open after the crash is fnn-recover-log. Teeth: tests/acl2/recovery-refinement-concurrent-tests.lisp (the publication run from the ground log at log-written: at every state after the first step fn-lgk-relp FAILS and fn-rrc-relp holds; the conclusions under three choices at all ten states; rrct-concurrent-keystone, the literal theorem over the ground medium, with a reachable positive witness of its complete antecedent and conclusion at the staged-durable and durable cuts under the exact tear; MUTATION: the recovery that drops the acknowledged r1 is no tree-sequence member and loses r1; hypothesis removal, exactly the lifted relation: a second segment write pending inside the publication recovers r1 r2 r3 r4, no member, every other hypothesis kept).

proofs.title: The page store's generation: a root commit writes at most 2|DIRTY|+1 pages, and two generations of K records fit the format-time reserve
proofs.statement: books/recovery-refinement-pages.lisp (lane recovery-refinement-2, 2026-10-01; specs/recovery-refinement.md section 4; design 2026-10-01 stages 5 and 7). On the page store a checkpoint is a root commit (pgs-plan-commit, books/pagestore.lisp): the dirty pages copy-on-write to fresh addresses, the table pages they touch, the directory run, the record to the other slot. KEYSTONE fn-rrp-commit-writes-within-the-generation: a planned commit's write list has at most fn-rrp-generation-pages (len dirty) = 2 * |DIRTY| + 1 entries (fn-rrp-page-writes-count one per dirty page, fn-rrp-touched-count at most one table page per dirty page since pgs-touched emits each touched table once, fn-rrp-table-dirty-count, the directory). fn-rrp-two-generations-fit-the-reserve: two planned commits over dirty sets of at most K * D pages each write at most fn-rrp-reserve-pages K D = 2 * (2KD + 1) in all: KeyKOS's two-generation reserve in pages, K the suffix bound the due rule forces the checkpoint by (fn-ock-publication-duep at K/2, PRF-083), D the pages one record dirties. NOT in this row (PRF-1220): the page store as an instance of books/recovery-refinement.lisp's medium (no host path opens the owner's state from a root yet, design stage 5), the binding of |DIRTY| to K * D on the host (the due rule and a per-record dirty bound from the profile), and the root record's log position. The page store's own crash keystone pgs-open-after-crash (PRF-344) is the medium's-own-ordering row of the spec; the snapshot program's cuts (*pgs-snapshot-cuts*, pgs-cut-crash-point: KEEP a prefix of the writes, the slot old, torn or new) map onto it in the spec's section 4 table. MODEL-LEVEL as PRF-1212: the host's commit is pgs-x-commit (books/pagestore-refine.lisp, pgs-x-commit-refines-plan equates its plan to pgs-plan-commit), so the bound is about what fnps-commit writes through that square. Teeth: tests/acl2/recovery-refinement-pages-tests.lisp (the ground store of tests/acl2/pagestore-tests.lisp under the toy digest: one dirty page plans exactly its generation of 3, two dirty pages plan 4 within 5, two such commits fit the reserve for K = 1, D = 2; hypothesis removal: a dirty set past K * D exceeds the reserve; MUTATION: a commit writing its pages twice is past its generation).

proofs.title: The checkpoint program's crash points recover exactly the committed records under an old-or-new image
proofs.statement: books/recovery-refinement.lisp section 8 (lane recovery-refinement, 2026-10-01). fn-rr-checkpoint-crash-point-recovers-committed-under-old-or-new: over a related state (fn-lgk-relp) with nothing in flight and the quiet store the publication asks for (fn-bs-scp-inputp; the segment inode below the allocation mark), at every state P of fn-bs-run over fn-bs-scp-program and for every crash choice, the crash image recovers exactly COMMITTED (fn-rr-recovered-records equals fn-lgk-committed) and holds the OLD image or the NEW one (fn-bs-scp-old-or-newp, by fn-bs-scp-program-crash-is-old-or-new). The program never writes the segment: fn-rr-all-keep-segment over the run (fenced, durable content and unit unchanged at every state). These are the five state-checkpoint cuts of tests/campaign/native_cuts.py (state-checkpoint-created, -written, -staged-durable, -replaced, -durable), the sequential half of the composition; the concurrent half is PRF-1214. Teeth: tests/acl2/recovery-refinement-tests.lisp (the ten states from the recovered ground store under the lose-everything and land-everything choices).
proofs.progress_note: The five cuts are the program's outer operations; the host's write loops have process-death points inside the single :write-all (fnn-checkpoint-write-steps' per-step fault kill, fnn-history-image-write's page writes; the Codex review of 2d1b10ed7, F6): their mapping to model crash points is PRF-1223. The concurrent half (a batch in flight during the publication) is PRF-1214's fn-rrc-checkpoint-crash-point-refines-with-a-batch-in-flight.

proofs.title: OPEN: the host's state-checkpoint write joined to the reserve (fn-his-file-octets within the capture budget, and a reservation invariant in place of the free-space observation)
proofs.statement: OBLIGATION (lane recovery-refinement-2, 2026-10-01; the Codex review of 2d1b10ed7 F5, restated after r10). PRF-1213 bounds the OCTETS of fn-bs-scp-program's one :write-all. The staged file the host writes is fn-his-file-octets (host/store-node-host.lisp: fn-his-region-octets of the history image's page count plus the stream the checkpoint steps write), produced by host/native/io.lisp fnn-history-image-write then fnn-checkpoint-write-steps; it is not the table estimate fn-ockp-decide plans against, and no fn-sct-encode exists. Two obligations, neither a byte equality: (a) the length of what the two loops write is fn-his-file-octets of the image's page count and the steps' stream, within fn-ock-capture-budget (the reader's bound the old image is held to, fn-sccr-file-read-bound), so the two generations are what fn-ckr-two-generations-fit-the-reserve-at-every-cut bounds; (b) a RESERVATION invariant: the reserve's octets are set aside at format time and each publication draws on them, so fn-ockp-decide's statvfs observation can be retired (a served host change, MODE 2026-10-01 section 2). Until both land, the funded-space premise of fn-rrs-funded-reserve-never-defers-for-space is an assumption of the join.

proofs.title: OPEN (registered, not resolved): the checkpoint write loops' intra-batch process-death cuts have no model crash point
proofs.statement: OBLIGATION (lane recovery-refinement-2, 2026-10-01; the Codex review of 2d1b10ed7 F6, confirmed open by r10; AGENTS: every process-death cut is a model crash point). STATUS: registered only. books/byte-store-state-checkpoint-program.lisp fn-bs-scp-program is still one :write-all, tests/campaign/native_cuts.py is unchanged, and the intra-batch SIGKILL points of host/native/io.lisp (fnn-checkpoint-write-steps' per-step kill under fnn-checkpoint-batch-fault; fnn-history-image-write's header, pad and page writes) have no model crash point. To do: split the :write-all into the batch's writes, each a cut (k fn-bs-write steps to the staged inode; fn-bs-step has no :write-at kind, so either add one or run the writes through fn-bs-write), prove every state's crash images recover COMMITTED under the OLD image (the root entry is untouched until the rename; PRF-1216's conclusion), and add the cut rows so native_program_check ties them to io.lisp. PRF-1216 covers the five outer cuts only. PROGRESS (fable-deputy-2, 2026-10-01): the split is in the model. books/byte-store-programs.lisp gains the step kind (:write-at dir name offset octets) (fn-bs-stepp, fn-bs-step through fn-bs-write at OFFSET, D1 and D2 treat it as a :write-all); books/byte-store-state-checkpoint-program.lisp defines fn-bs-scp-batched-program (one :write-at per batch at the running offset, each followed by the cut "state-checkpoint-batch"; fn-bs-scp-chunksp, fn-bs-scp-octets), its D1-D3 ground checks, and fn-bs-scp-write-at-zero-is-write-all-by-definition (fn-bs-scp-program is the one-batch shape). Teeth: tests/acl2/byte-store-state-checkpoint-program-tests.lisp evaluates every state of a three-batch run under per-state generated, fn-bs-crash-choicesp-checked lose-everything and land-everything vectors (nil versus one :new per touched unit for writes, :drop versus :apply for entries): old or new at all 15 states, the old entry at the 11 states before the rename, and the batches exactly in the durable inode; land-everything also yields all six staged bytes in a crash before file fsync. The labelled offset-0 mutant yields a third content under both vectors; the labelled non-:ok positive-offset mutation witness checks :eio, stopping and the pending/view bytes (1 2 3), and must-fails on the mutant's (3 2). STILL OWED: the keystone fn-bs-scp-batched-program-crash-is-old-or-new at every state (plan: a quiet predicate through the write phase for the old arm, the sequential-splice content of the fenced staged inode for the new arm, fn-bs-run over append as store-import-publication's fn-bs-imp-run-of-append); PRF-1216's conclusion over the batched run in books/recovery-refinement.lisp; the native_cuts.py row for "state-checkpoint-batch" tied to fnn-checkpoint-write-steps (host side, after stage 0). Open joins for the batched keystone's host tie (r22): the host writes the history-image region before fnn-checkpoint-write-steps (host/native/io.lisp fnn-history-image-write ~3306, call ~3436), so the chunk mapping must include that prefix; a batch step may issue no write (io.lisp ~3364: nil frames still count a fault step), so chunks must admit empty elements or the refinement must stutter.

proofs.title: OPEN: the page store as the image medium (the root's pages decode to the capture of the first S records; the open from a root as fn-rr-medium-open; |DIRTY| bound by K records)
proofs.statement: OBLIGATION (lane recovery-refinement-2, 2026-10-01; specs/recovery-refinement.md sections 1, 4 and 5; design 2026-10-01 stage 5). books/recovery-refinement.lisp's medium is six constrained functions; the page store discharges them only once fn-hist lives on pages (stage 5): (a) the capture of a committed prefix is the dirty page set of its full open and the root record carries S (the log position), so that a root's pages decode to the capture of the first S records (the analog of fn-sct-decode-file-of-file-is-the-capture, PRF-199); (b) the open from a root over the log's suffix is fn-rr-medium-open and equals the full open of prefix ++ suffix (PRF-083's shape), with fn-rr-medium-open-okp and fn-rr-medium-holds over the opened pages; (c) the old-or-new of the root under a crash (pgs-open-after-crash, PRF-344) binds the image the open reads to the capture of S_old or S_new committed records; (d) the host's open from a root (PRF-344's open square: no ACL2 function composes fnps-open) named as the subject; (e) |DIRTY| <= K * D on the host: the due rule fn-ock-publication-duep forces the checkpoint by K/2 records and a per-record dirty-page bound D comes from the profile, discharging fn-rrp-two-generations-fit-the-reserve's hypotheses (PRF-1215). Until then PRF-1215 is the model's generation bound alone and the page store is not an instance of the recovery-refinement keystone.

proofs.title: OPEN: the native cut table's remaining cuts under the lifted relation (finish, stage cleanup, segment rotation and drop, import, export, init)
proofs.statement: OBLIGATION (lane recovery-refinement-2, 2026-10-01; specs/recovery-refinement.md section 3, the cut table). PRF-1214's fn-rrc-keeping-the-segment-keeps-the-lifted-relation turns 'this program's run keeps the segment's presence, content, unit and own pending operations' into fn-rrc-relp at every state, and the keystone covers every crash image there. The keep-the-segment proof exists for fn-bs-scp-program only (fn-rrc-scp-run-keeps-the-segment, local). Owed, one per program, over the programs tests/campaign/native_cuts.py names: fn-bs-finish-program and fn-bs-recover-stage-cleanup-program (entry operations only; K0's fn-bs-k0-finish-program-preserves-relation is the octet half), the segment programs fn-lgs-spare/-rotate/-rotate-durable/-drop (books/store-log-segments.lisp: cuts rotate-created, rotate-fenced, rotate-renamed, rotate-headed, rotate-durable, drop-unlinked, drop-durable; these change which inode is the active segment, so the relation's INO moves with the rotation: their own theorems in books/store-log-segments.lisp and books/store-log-lineage.lisp are the citation to make), the import, export and init publication programs (import-*, export-*, init-* cuts: other inodes and directories), and the statement cut (fn-ks-cut). Each is a crash point of the composed store; none is covered by PRF-1212/1214/1216 until its keep-the-segment theorem is cited by name in the spec's table.

proofs.title: The page fill crosses the trust boundary in place: fn-pgs-fill-frame (A-PGS-HOST-IO's frame form) is the put of the page's words, and every fill the history image performs is its list form at the realizer's words
proofs.statement: books/assumptions-pgs-host-io.lisp (A-PGS-HOST-IO, now a part of books/assumptions.lisp by inclusion), books/history-records.lisp, books/history-records-disk.lisp, books/history-image-binding.lisp. The host's page fill `fn-pgs-fill-realize' answered a true list of 2048 words per 16 KiB page (fn-pgs-page-words-shape), so every fill consed the list, boxed every word at or above 2^62 and put the list into the stobj word by word (measured on hbox, SBCL 2.2.9, 10,000 fills: 155,622 bytes consed and 120.7 us per fill). proofs.title: The resource vector and the bank: funded preserved by every transition, settle once, refusal keeps the slack, destroy returns exactly the unsettled draws
proofs.statement: books/resource-vector.lisp: the resource vector (a fixed-arity list of naturals, one coordinate a class of *fn-rv-coordinates*: resident, disk, descriptors, workers, read-ids, txids, config-gens, conn-ids, work; the first five Codex's fn-prs vector) with coordinate-wise plus, the order fn-rv-below and the truncated difference, split by the reusable mask into reusable and spent coordinates; the bank (BUDGET DRAWN SLOTS) with the drawn vector carried in state and direct-index rows (PHASE GEN . DEMAND), phase 0 idle, 1 drawn, 2 a sub-bank whose demand is its whole budget (sub-banks partition their parent), GEN the slot's generation raised by every charge and answered as the draw's completion token, which every later step on the slot names (:stale otherwise); the transitions draw, open, settle, refund, grow, destroy and the root fn-rv-install (slot 0 the owner's baseline, slot 1 the maintenance reserve as a sub-bank, before any user's slot). KEYSTONE fn-rv-step-keeps-okp: from an okp bank (funded; the reusable part of drawn exactly the reusable part of the outstanding rows; the spent part of the rows within the spent part of drawn) every transition's result is okp, admitted or refused; fn-rv-run-keeps-okp over sequences. KEYSTONE fn-rv-step-refused-keeps-the-bank: a refused step returns the bank itself, so fn-rv-refusal-keeps-slack and fn-rv-refused-run-keeps-the-bank. KEYSTONE fn-rv-draw-admits-exactly-within-the-budget (the check precedes every effect; fn-rv-draw-charges-exactly-the-demand). KEYSTONE fn-rv-settle-once. KEYSTONE fn-rv-replayed-completion-is-stale (Codex review r06 F2: the first draw's token, any run, a second admitted draw of the slot; the replayed token is :stale and leaves the bank; fn-rv-run-never-lowers-a-gen, fn-rv-charge-raises-the-gen). KEYSTONE fn-rv-step-keeps-the-other-slots and fn-rv-user-steps-keep-the-reserve (the reserve is never drawn by a user's step). KEYSTONE fn-rv-install-reserves-the-owner-first. KEYSTONE fn-rv-destroy-returns-exactly-the-unsettled-draws: destroying a sub-bank returns exactly its budget less what it spent, which covers the reusable part of every draw it still held. books/resource-vector-tree.lisp, a node's accounting as ONE state (ROOT SUBS), the sub-bank living in its parent's slot: KEYSTONE fn-rt-step-keeps-okp (and fn-rt-run-keeps-okp, fn-rt-step-refused-keeps-the-tree); KEYSTONE fn-rt-sub-bank-steps-keep-the-root (the partition); KEYSTONE fn-rt-destroy-revokes-the-sub-bank (r06 F2: after an admitted destroy, any run, and whatever the slot holds then, every step addressed to the destroyed sub-bank's token is :stale and leaves the tree; fn-rv-token-retiredp inductive over steps). Not claimed: which operation may draw which coordinate, any tariff, any served path (definterface :operation, specs/resource-vector.md); the refusal path's own transient allocation (the operation layer's, specs/resource-vector.md item 4).

proofs.title: K6: one transit decision for the NNTP and BP carriers
proofs.statement: MODEL-LEVEL. A BP transit delivery that fn-own-bp-transit-submit-result submits is, after the enqueue and the owner's take, the in-flight TAKETHIS record of the same peer, Message-ID and octets under the control id, and fn-tsd-drain-decision (a model of the fn-pta-decide call host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-transit-decide makes) gives it the gate's byte decision, :want. An NNTP IHAVE/TAKETHIS in flight with the same peer, Message-ID and octets over the same store, clock and header limits gets the same byte decision. Neither needs a string-peer hypothesis: a submitted delivery names a configured peer (fn-tsd-submitted-names-a-string-peer). Where they differ is named: the principal (NNTP's session peer vs fn-bpaj-ingress-peer) is an input; under fn-ocfg-statep an open connection's pinned configuration is never the control id's (nil), and the BP submission's authority verdict is :ungoverned or :none. Whole-decision equality is not claimed: its equal-pin premise fails while the NNTP connection is open. OPEN (Codex r36 F1): no carried invariant ties an in-flight or queued submission's id to an open connection; the tests witness only that fn-ocfg-close drops the connection's in-flight submission.

proofs.title: A BP receipt regenerates byte-identically after a crash of the record log, when the receiver acted only on acknowledged Store records (PKT-217 restated over format 10's crash model)
proofs.statement: books/bp-receipt-log-crash.lisp KEYSTONE fn-brlc-receipt-regenerated-after-log-crash: from a receiver whose state is the replay of its journal (fn-bprr-replay, host fn-bprj-install), run any live trace (fn-bpr-live-run); let the record log be at any crash point of its served programs (fn-lgk-relp BS KS), take any admissible crash image (fn-bs-crash-imagep) under A-CRYPTO-TRAILER's premise on the tear (fn-lg-platform-tears-p); the open interns what the log's recovery holds as the HOST'S FULL-REPLAY OPEN does (host/native/io.lisp fnn-recover-log, full replay: fnn-recover-log-stream-take/-flush; fnn-bridge-recover-begin seeds fn-ssr-seed (fn-stxk-initial-context 0); each chunk decoded by fn-lgb-decode-next, whose :logic first value is fn-srs-decode, and interned by fnn-bridge-recover-step = fn-ssr-intern-step :resident, the statement keyring, generation and identity cursor carried between records; -extents/-lz equal :resident under fn-arena-p and a faithful placement, fn-ssr-extent-step-refines-resident, fn-ssr-lz-step-refines-resident): fn-brlc-rows, with fn-brlc-chunks-are-one-step (any chunking gives the same rows); then opens as fnn-bridge-recover-end does (fn-store-sn-recover-rows: fn-rii-sco-extend-open on the empty capture, installing the classified answer's second element; fn-brlc-host-classified), which fn-brlc-host-open-is-the-observed-open equates with fn-cpo-open-observed whenever it is a Store (fn-rii-sco-extend-open-is-extend-then-open, fn-rii-classified-open-is-classified-open, fn-rii-sco-extend-is-sco-extend, fn-sco-store-open-of-extended-capture with PREFIX = NIL); run the recovery barriers to :ready; then the journal's replay is the live receiver state and fn-bpr-receipt-adu is byte-identical. The premise that replaces the per-file image predicate fn-sf-crash-imagep: the live Store's history is a prefix of the rows of the log's ACKNOWLEDGED records (the first fn-lgk-acked of fn-lgk-committed). The decode of the recovered records is no longer a hypothesis: fn-brlc-open-ok-implies-decoded proves an :ok open implies it (removed after that proof). Steps: fn-brlc-recovered-is-the-acknowledged-prefix-and-more (from fn-rr-log-crash-image-recovers-a-tree-sequence-member, over fn-lgk-crash-of-related-state-is-a-prefix), fn-brlc-rows-of-prefix-is-a-prefix (fn-srs-decode-of-append, fn-ssr-resident-step-of-append, fn-brlc-ssr-rows-grow), fn-brlc-acknowledged-rows-are-a-prefix-of-the-recovered-rows, then fn-sonb-live-receipt-regenerated-from-related-open. Hypotheses NOT discharged here, named (OPEN): (1) THE PREMISE'S PRODUCER: nothing yet proves, for a log the host wrote, that the live Store history is a prefix of the rows of the acknowledged records (that every row the Store holds came from a record the log fenced and the owner acknowledged through fn-lgk-finish-one, in order): the join between the owner's commit path and the log kernel; (2) the open's success (fn-sn-open-okp of the host open; under the log it is the store instance's obligation, books/recovery-refinement-store.lisp, PRF-1212/PRF-1213, written, not admitted; a refused open serves nothing); (3) fn-sonb-configured-before-eventsp (a store reconfigured after an event needs the receipt over fn-cst-relation, PKT-217's first follow-up); (4) the single FN-ARENA through which the replay reads payloads, as in PRF-007. Scope: the full-replay open; the checkpoint opens (fnn-recover-log-from-state-checkpoint, fnn-recover-log-from-log-checkpoint) are not covered. MODEL-LEVEL as PRF-1212. Teeth: tests/acl2/bp-receipt-log-crash-tests.lisp on the live trace of bp-receiver-evolving-tests, its two rows held by the log as their host encodings (the rows the host's replay makes of them ARE the live rows), each witness asserting the keystone's hypothesis vector (all but the image predicate, which is asserted by fn-bs-crash-imagep-suff or refuted by a theorem). POSITIVE reachable and WRITER-BUILT: r1 r2 prepared, written (P-LOG-APPEND), fenced (P-LOG-FENCE) and acknowledged (fn-lgk-finish-one) on a fresh store's log; every hypothesis and both conclusions. REMOVALS (every other hypothesis holds, the omitted one fails, the conclusion fails): the replay agreement (CORRUPTED receiver state ahead of its journal), fn-lgk-relp (CORRUPTED kernel over a fresh log's bytes), fn-bs-crash-imagep (the fresh log's bytes, refuted by brlct-fresh-bytes-are-no-crash-image-of-the-written-state), the phase :ready (no barriers), the acknowledged-prefix hypothesis (a writer-built log that acknowledged a different first article). NOT WITNESSED, with reasons: fn-csi-full-relationp (its fn-snt-relation conjunct is refuted where it works, bpre-teeth-live-extension-without-relation; the receipt reads no consumer or identity conjunct), fn-lg-platform-tears-p (T when nothing is in flight; its failure with a batch in flight lies outside A-CRYPTO-TRAILER's constrained premise and is not evaluable), fn-sn-open-okp (no refused open reaches :ready), fn-sonb-configured-before-eventsp (not shown necessary: a log reconfigured after an event, fn.letters removed at txid 2, opens and regenerates the receipt). MUTATION (labelled): a recovery that drops the receipted record r1 is no tree-sequence member, the host's replay refuses it (identity cursor) and no open over it is a Store.

proofs.title: The unfunded cold line: every issued page read pins its file generation until its I/O actually completes, runs on a bounded persistent worker, and settles once by its observation (success, error, timeout, late or duplicate delivery)
proofs.statement: books/page-read-direct.lisp (lane cold-read-ownership; Codex r31 F1/F2; GPT-6's first fallible-I/O row). Host subjects: host/native/extent.lisp fnn-extent-issue-direct calls fn-pio-direct-admit (from host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-cold-issue-locked, owner mutex held, before retirement can run) and fnn-extent-direct-settle calls fn-pio-direct-settle (from fnn-owner-cold-transfer-result-locked, owner and extent locks held, only after the worker's actual return is observed). KEYSTONES: fn-pio-direct-admit-binds-an-idle-worker-to-the-issued-identity (an admitted read binds an idle fn-pxe worker to an fn-pio row whose token is exactly (id cid file eoff elen trailer), the file being a process-local incarnation never reused; with no idle worker the read is refused by name, :read-resources-unavailable, nothing issued: fn-pio-direct-admit-without-an-idle-worker-is-refused); fn-pio-direct-cancelled-read-still-pins-its-file (the row, cancelled by a timeout or not, makes fn-pio-file-clear-p false for its file, so fnn-extent-close keeps the descriptor); fn-pio-direct-settle-publishes-only-the-issued-identity (publication only for an :issued, never cancelled, row of exactly that token with a verified read and a worker that returned that job); fn-pio-direct-settle-observes-every-outcome (a failed read is (:fault V) whether or not its request timed out; a verified late read after a timeout is :cancelled and inserts nothing; the row settles, releasing the file, and the worker idles); fn-pio-direct-settle-stale-changes-nothing (a foreign token -- another request, a reused worker's next job, another generation -- a settled row or an unreturned worker leaves row and worker unchanged); fn-pio-direct-settle-happens-once (a second delivery is stale). The worker count is fn-pio-direct-workers, the profile-limits row :cold-workers, counted in fn-heap-thread-count. The global bound (at most that many reads in flight) is the host's fixed worker set (fnn-extent-direct-start) plus admission requiring an idle worker and only a non-stale settlement idling one; it is not a theorem over the worker set. Host thread/mutex/table fidelity is A-HOST.

proofs.title: Holding as a declared relation: a holder table's late holder is refused by name, a key's count over any run is its holds less its drops, and a duplicate drop never takes another holder's hold
proofs.statement: Subject: books/def-holder.lisp fn-hd-keyed-step (the keyed step over the arena readers' table of books/arena-reader-pins.lisp: :hold K / :drop K / :count K / :quiet K, any other event refused) and fn-hd-ident-step (the identified step: a token per holder). HOST: the generic that every def-holder instance's host-called entries thread (the first instances: books/handle-holds.lisp over the arena generation table, and the cold read's file table, in progress). fn-hd-drop-of-unheld-is-refused (KEYSTONE): a :drop of a key nobody holds, or of a non-natural key, answers :refused and leaves the table as it was -- the late holder's outcome, distinct from :dropped. fn-hd-run-count-is-holds-less-drops (KEYSTONE): over any run of keyed events a key's count is what it was plus its holds less its drops answered :dropped; fn-hd-quiet-from-empty-means-every-hold-was-dropped: from the empty table a quiet key is one whose every hold was dropped. fn-hd-ident-duplicate-hold-is-refused and fn-hd-ident-drop-of-absent-token-is-refused (KEYSTONES): a hold by a token already holding the key and a drop by a token not holding it are refused and change nothing, so a duplicate drop by one holder can never take another's hold (consultation c05). def-holder is an ACCOUNTING component: it authorizes no forget or close by itself; a release is licensed by an instance's root theorem over every root, this accounting, physical custody ended and the durable ordering (a :physical effect's release cut must follow the durable replacement in the declared cut list, else the declaration is refused). Scope: the table's counts and tokens; which host functions hold is the declaration's and tools/holder_check.py's (the raw host, both ways); no claim about a copy of a key the declaration does not name.

proofs.title: The arena's forget: a handle the served history no longer names is emptied while the owner serves, its file's count falls by one, and only what the generation release answers is forgotten
proofs.statement: Subject: books/payload-arena.lisp fn-arena-forget (the generic's export; the attached implementation's is books/payload-arena-extent.lisp fn-arena$x-forget) and books/arena-forget.lisp fn-arf-apply-released, fn-arf-retire-event, fn-arf-changed-handles. HOST: NOT WIRED YET (host/native/io.lisp fnn-log-reseat-fenced's release loop and host/native/owner.lisp fnn-owner-reclaim-pass are the call sites; the wiring waits for the root fact below). fn-arena-forget-payload (KEYSTONE): for a natural H the forgotten handle reads the empty payload, every other natural handle keeps its payload, the count is unchanged (no handle is reused) and an arena stays an arena; no existing :logic definition changed. fn-arx-forget-file-count (KEYSTONE): under fn-arena$xcorr, for a handle inside the arena, the count of the file its entry named falls by exactly one and every other file's count is unchanged; with PRF-930's fn-xrt-quiet-files-are-unnamed a dropped file whose handles are all reseated or forgotten goes quiet. fn-arf-apply-released-payload (KEYSTONE): applying the generation step's :release answer (PRF-941) empties exactly the handles tagged (:forget H) in it; a plain handle is a staged page's release. fn-arf-changed-handles-are-unnamed (KEYSTONE): when the old rows' handles are pairwise distinct and the new rows are a rewrite of them (each changed row names no old handle), no new row names a handle the pairwise walk answers. OPEN, not proved: (1) the root fact, that the served history's handles are pairwise distinct and that the reclaim's interned rows are such a rewrite; (2) the liveness theorem composing rows, generation pins and whole-arena leases (DEF-HOLDER's payload-handle instance); (3) a resident payload's octets in the paged child are not returned by the forget. Scope: a read of a forgotten handle answers the empty payload through no realizer and no descriptor; the named refusal on the read path is not built.

proofs.title: Off-owner jobs: the commit's batch effects run in ACL2's order with no owner lock, and the job's receipt is consumed once into its own generation with distinct outcomes
proofs.statement: books/owner-queued-work.lisp. Subjects fn-oqw-start, fn-oqw-step, fn-oqw-receipt, fn-oqw-outcome-of-final, host-called in host/native/owner.lisp: fnn-owner-run-job (the syncer thread's body through fnn-owner-batch-job, and the bound submission's inline quantum) executes exactly the phase fn-oqw-step names; fnn-owner-commit-pipeline consumes the job's end through fn-oqw-receipt (fnn-owner-complete-generation) on the time-bars ledger (PRF-384) it issued the job under; fnn-owner-commit-queued-locked maps an inline job's end through fn-oqw-outcome-of-final. KEYSTONE fn-oqw-batch-effect-order: from the :batch job's first phase, under any answers, the log's append runs only after the FNFD intents and the extension returned, the barrier only after the append returned, an FNFD resolution only after the barrier returned, and the job is :done iff all five phases returned, having run exactly :intents :extend :append :fence :resolutions in order. fn-oqw-a-failed-effect-ends-the-job: fn-oqw-step after a non-terminal phase that answered other than :ok is the terminal :uncertain (an uncertain word) or :fault, and a terminal never steps again. KEYSTONE fn-oqw-receipt-outcomes-are-distinct: the receipt is one of :fenced :failed :fault :stale :consumed; :fenced iff open at its generation and the job ran every phase, :failed iff it ended uncertain, :fault for any other end; :stale iff another generation's; stale and consumed answer no one and leave the ledger unchanged; the job's own receipt closes the ledger with fn-otb-complete's answer.

proofs.title: An FNFD journal written in the old batch order (intents N, intents N+1, resolutions N) replays exactly as one in the new order (intents N, resolutions N, intents N+1)
proofs.statement: books/feed-journal-order.lisp. The open replays each FNFD frame through the host-called host/owner-host.lisp fn-owner-feed-journal-scan into two folds: the unresolved-intent set (fn-own-feed-intent-apply) and the peer's offerable feed (fn-feed-replay via fn-owner-feed-replay-counted and fn-own-feed-port-replay-peer). KEYSTONE fn-fjo-an-intent-moved-past-another-resolution-replays-alike: for any prefix XS and suffix YS, an intent frame I moved past a resolution frame R (:feed-commit or :feed-abort) of a different intent key leaves both folds unchanged. Since lane owner-offlock the batch job writes a batch's resolutions before the next batch's intents, so a journal a running node wrote under the old order is read alike at its upgrade (no migration). Helpers: fn-fjo-intent-commutes-with-another-resolution, fn-fjo-feed-replay-ignores-an-intent-unfolds (an intent is a no-op in the offerable feed).
